author: ryakel
body:
Fifth of the seven PRs in `wiki/Settings-Design-Language.md` §9 — and the largest single pocket of the problem this rebuild exists to fix: **seven collapsed sections on one screen, every one folded by default.**

```
‹ Settings
Notifications

CHANNELS
Push                 ⓘ              (off)
Email                ⓘ              (off)
Pushover             ⓘ              (off)
QUIET HOURS
Quiet hours          ⓘ              (off)
From                        (dimmed) 22:00
Until                       (dimmed) 08:00
Bypass label         ⓘ    (dimmed) wake-me
MORE
Event pings          ⓘ                   ›
Morning digest       ⓘ              On   ›
Critical mode        ⓘ              Off  ›
Deep links           ⓘ         Not set   ›
Email deliverability ⓘ         Not set   ›
Test channels        ⓘ                   ›
History                                  ›
```

## The collapse machinery is gone

`openSections`, `isCollapsed`, `toggleCollapsed` and the local `SectionHeader` — **the biggest of the seven parallel collapse implementations** the original audit found.

With `SettingsSection` already deleted in PR4, the collapse machinery this rebuild exists to remove is now **entirely out of `SettingsModal.jsx`**.

## Quiet hours was a second framed card

It had been a framed block, which would have quietly made PR4's claim — *"the danger card is the ONE framed element in the surface"* — **false**. It's plain rows now, with its three dependent rows dimming rather than vanishing.

Worth flagging because that's exactly how a design rule dies: not by being argued down, but by a second exception nobody noticed.

## One place I did NOT follow the plan

§9 says *"flatten the per-type cards into grouped ToggleRows"*. **I didn't.**

The per-type × per-channel grid is genuinely two-dimensional — five types against three channels. Flattening it means five captions and **fifteen toggle rows** to say what a grid says at a glance. Rows are a one-dimensional form and this isn't one-dimensional data.

What actually made it a problem was its *length on the main screen*, and moving it to its own page fixes that without pretending a matrix is a list.

Flagging rather than doing it quietly — if the grid reads badly on a narrow phone, say so and I'll flatten it.

## Verification

Driven in a real browser against a live server:

- **0 old section headers, 0 `▸` glyph chevrons**
- All **seven** sub-pages title correctly with a "‹ Notifications" back affordance, and back returns to Notifications every time
- The four value-bearing NavRows show real state (`On` / `Off` / `Not set`)
- No page errors

ESLint 0 errors, build ✓, `npm test` 134/134 + smoke, `npm audit` clean.

History loses its own collapse toggle — on a dedicated page it's simply open.

## Next

PR6 — Integrations (per-integration sub-pages, delete the name-toggle expander family; Labels rows re-cut in the same PR), then PR7 teardown.

author: jdc308
body:
## Problem

On the Updates tab, the Live progress panel opened with output from the *previous* action (e.g. a just-finished self-update) before the new run's lines appeared.

## Cause

On a successful upgrade/downgrade request the client optimistically flips status to "Backing up" and mounts the live-log component, which opens the SSE stream and reads `progress.log` from the top. But the updater only truncates `progress.log` once it *claims* the request (its poll interval later). In that gap the stream replays whatever the last action left in the file.

## Fix

Truncate `progress.log` in the app when it writes the request (`resetProgress()`, called from the upgrade, downgrade, and self-update writers). The POST handler writes the request before responding, so the log is already empty by the time the client opens the stream. The updater's own reset stays as a backstop.

Added tests asserting each of the three writers clears the log. Full gate green (typecheck, lint, 2741 tests, build, docs; no api.ts drift).

Note: jsdom can't prove the visual behavior, so this wants an eyeball on a real upgrade.

author: takasek
body:
## Summary

Closes #587. #580 introduced coverage measurement but deliberately deferred two decisions: whether to gate CI on a threshold, and whether to exclude the vscode-extension's vscode-API glue layer from the denominator. This PR makes both decisions and implements them.

**Decision record (work-cycle 適用点1):**

- **CI ゲート化**: 前提「baseline を閾値として固定運用せず、当面は測定のみに留めることが許容される」を否定する案（=ゲート化する）を採用。却下した「測定のみ継続」案の却下理由はプロダクトオーナー判断（ユーザーに AskUserQuestion で確認、baseline を floor として敷く方針を選択）。
- **除外対象**: 前提「vscode API 直結層込みの数字のまま閾値管理することが許容される」を否定する案（=除外する）を採用。除外しない案の却下理由も同様にプロダクトオーナー判断。除外対象ファイルは `import ... from "vscode"` を持ち、対応する `*-logic.ts` にロジックが分離済みで実測 0% だった 15 ファイルを機械的に特定（`analyze.ts` 等ロジックを含み部分的にテストされているファイルは除外していない）。

**実装:**

- `vitest.shared.ts`: `mergeConfig` が配列フィールドを merge でなく置換する挙動を踏まえ、`sharedCoverageExclude` を named export 化。ビルド設定 `**/*.config.mjs` も除外に追加（`esbuild.config.mjs` が数字を歪めていた）。
- `packages/vscode-extension`: vscode API 直結 glue 15 ファイルを coverage 対象から除外（31.9% → 98.81% stmts）。
- 各パッケージの実測 baseline を `coverage.thresholds` として設定: core (99/91/99/99), metadata-exporter (100/97/100/100), graphviz-exporter (88/90/91/88), preview-engine (100/100/100/100), cli (98/87/97/98), vscode-extension (98/86/92/98) — stmts/branches/funcs/lines。
- 各パッケージの `test` スクリプトに `--coverage` を追加し、既存の CI エントリポイント `pnpm -r test` がそのまま閾値ゲートとして機能するようにした。`coverage` スクリプトは `test` と同一コマンドになったため `test` へのエイリアスに整理（`/simplify` 指摘）。

**対象パッケージ層**: テスト/CI 設定層（全 6 package の `vitest.config.ts` / `package.json`、ルートの `vitest.shared.ts`）。プロダクションコードの変更なし。

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -r test`（= CI エントリポイント）が全パッケージ PASS することを確認
- [x] `core` の閾値を意図的に実測値超えへ引き上げ、vitest が非ゼロ終了することを確認（ゲートが実際に機能する検証）→ 確認後に正しい値へ復元
- [x] `pnpm -r typecheck` / `make lint` PASS
- [x] `pnpm --filter @pfdsl/vscode-extension typecheck` PASS
- [x] `node scripts/gate-check.mjs --base main --no-artifact` 全項目 PASS/SKIP（#587 は `flow:exempt`、roadmap 出力 artifact なし）
- [x] `/simplify` 実施（角度: reuse/simplification/efficiency/altitude）。共通指摘（test/coverage スクリプト重複）を適用。html reporter の CI 上の無駄な書き出しと glue ファイル個別列挙の将来メンテナンス性は、スコープ超過・実害軽微と判断しスキップ

body:
## 무엇을

rate-limit 파서에 **카운트다운/타이머 콜론 형식**을 인식하는 새 순수 패턴 `countdown-duration`을 추가했습니다.

- `try again in 1:30:00` → `H:M:S` = 지금부터 1시간 30분
- `resets in 45:00` → `M:S` = 지금부터 45분

## 왜

기존 파서는 `relative-duration`(단위 문자 `d`/`h`/`m` 필요)과 `clock-time` 계열(절대 벽시계 `at`)은 다루지만, **라이브 진행바·카운트다운 타이머**가 남은 시간을 `HH:MM:SS`/`MM:SS`로 렌더하는 흔한 실사용 형식은 어떤 패턴에도 걸리지 않아 리셋 시각을 놓쳤습니다. 관련 BACKLOG 항목(§8 무한 개선, 파서 실사용 갭)을 이번 세션에 발굴·구현했습니다.

## 어떻게 (구현)

- `packages/core/src/parser.ts`에 순수 `countdown-duration` 패턴 추가, `relative-duration` **앞**에 배치해 콜론 형식을 먼저 잡습니다.
- 정규식: `(?:try again|resets?|retry)\s+in\s+(?:(\d{1,3}):)?(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\b`
  - 세 필드형 `(H:)?M:S`, 두 필드형 `M:S`로 해석.
  - **초는 0–59, 3필드형의 분도 0–59로 검증** → `in 12:99`·`in 1:99:00` 같은 잘못된 타이머 필드는 매치 거부.
  - `in 0:00`은 미래 리셋이 아니므로 `null`.
  - 두 필드 `M:S`의 분은 타이머가 `90:00`을 정당히 표시할 수 있어 상한 없음.
- 사전필터(`resets?\s+(at|in)`·`try again`)가 이미 커버하므로 필터 변경 0줄.
- **새 CLI 코드 0줄** — 기존 `agentrelay parse`와 run 감지 경로가 자동으로 노출합니다.
- `BACKLOG.md`에 항목 `[x]` 기록, `PROGRESS.md`에 세션 46 로그 한 줄 추가.

## 어떻게 테스트했나

- 로컬 `pnpm install` → `pnpm build`(Next.js 대시보드 포함) 클린, `pnpm ci:lint`(Biome) 무경고, `pnpm test` 전 패키지 통과.
- core parser 테스트 **33 → 41 (+8 신규)**: `H:M:S`, `M:S`, 초 포함, `90:00` 허용, 초·분 범위초과 거부, `0:00` 거부, `2h`는 `relative-duration` 유지 회귀.
- 실제 빌드된 CLI e2e(mock 아님):
  - `parse "try again in 1:30:00."` → `countdown-duration`, now+1h30m
  - `parse "resets in 45:00."` → now+45m
  - `parse "try again in 12:99."` → 미감지
  - `parse "resets in 2h"` → `relative-duration` 유지

## 관련 BACKLOG

§8 무한 개선 백로그 — "파서: 카운트다운/타이머 형식의 콜론 구분 상대 시간 인식" (👷 클로드 코드)

body:
ドキュメント 2 件。コードの変更はありません。

## `docs/EVIDENCE.md` — 日本語で全面書き直し

旧版は **854 tests / 11 files** と記載していましたが、実測は **974 / 15** です。キャプチャ表もプレイヤーが未描画だった時期のもので、内容が現状と合っていませんでした。すべて測り直しました。

このコミット時点の実測値:

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| ユニットテスト | 974 passed / 974、15 ファイル（ファイル別内訳を追加） |
| `tsc --noEmit` / `vite build` | クリーン |
| ショーケース検証 | 0 errors / 0 warnings、被覆率 98.7% |
| コースカメラ構図検査 | 35 件中 1 件が不合格（`cam9`） |
| キャプチャ | 14 / 14、ハッシュ全相異 |
| 性能 | 描画数・三角形数のみ有効、**fps は測定不能** |

構成上の主な変更:

- **§3「検査ツール自身が誤っていた記録」を新設。** このプロジェクトで最も繰り返した失敗なので独立させました — 明るさは中身ではない／ジオメトリも被写体ではない／投影は可視性ではない／推論で決めた閾値はすべて緩すぎた／自分の書いたテストが空虚だった／自動化が偽陽性を作っていた、の 6 件を経緯付きで記録
- **§4 で `explore-quiet` が現行基準（3.0 m）を満たさないことを表内と注記の両方に明示。** 平均奥行き 1.99 m の壁のフレームで、良好例として引用されないようにするため
- **§7 の未解決欠陥を 9 件に整理。** `reload` / `light` 系 / `stamina` / `blur` の 4 件は「なぜ直さないか」まで記載

## `CLAUDE.md` — 新規

このリポジトリで作業するエージェント向けの指針です。中心に置いたのは機能一覧ではなく、**実際に繰り返し起きた失敗**です:

| パターン | 実例 |
|---|---|
| 書かれているのに繋がっていない | `Player` がシーンに未追加、USE の効果が未消費、マップを開く呼び出しが不在 |
| テストが通ることと正しいことは別 | 「撃つとダメージが入る」の直後で例外が出ていた |
| 同じ表を 2 箇所に持つとズレる | 回転オフセット表が 3 箇所にあり 1 つだけ転置されていた |
| 静かに失敗させない | 握り潰した catch と黙って捨てる `?? null` が最も高くついた |

作業ルールとして次を明記しています:

- **新しい回帰テストは、必ず修正を戻して失敗することを確認する**
- 閾値は推論ではなく実測した良例・悪例の分布から決め、実測表をソースに残す
- テスト対象が関数の奥に埋まって到達できないなら純粋関数として切り出す
- このコンテナに GPU は無いので **fps を主張しない**

## 検証

記載した識別子・パス・コマンドはすべて実在を確認しました:

- 定数 — `CELL` 4.0 / `NAV_RES` 0.25 / `PUNCTUAL_INTENSITY_SCALE` 4π

author: nrdptel
body:
Both are derived from the velocity, so they go the same way it does. Where the analysis judges a speed physically impossible it withholds both headlines, `lib/explore.ts:146` stops offering the curves and `lib/compare.ts:147` stops drawing them — but `analyzedDataCsv` computed them per sample regardless. So the one artefact a flyer pastes into a spreadsheet or a cert document was the one place the withheld figure came back.

### Measured over the corpus

**10 of 46** flights have their speed withheld on screen, and **all ten** exported a Mach and a dynamic pressure:

| flight | CSV max Mach | CSV max Q |
|---|---|---|
| `eggtimer sta-carl2` | **362.4** | 1.79e+8 kPa |
| `eggtimer seb-earlydeploy` | 4.1 | 8.42e+3 |
| `genericcsv swiss-cheese-L1` | **1.7** | 187 |
| `genericcsv the-gardener-L1` | **1.6** | 182 |
| `perfectflite sg1.2 booster` | **1.3** | 126 |
| …and 5 more | | |

The loudest reads Mach 362 and 179 million kPa, which nobody would believe. The dangerous ones read **1.7, 1.6 and 1.3** — which anybody would, on flights where Debrief refuses to say "supersonic" on every other surface.

### What changed

Both columns are omitted **entirely** rather than blanked, so the header says what the file actually contains. The velocity column stays, exactly as its trace stays on screen, so a mis-scaled column can still be seen and diagnosed.

### How it was verified

- Swept all 46 fixtures through `analyzedDataCsv` and parsed the emitted columns back: 10 offenders before, **0 after** — no `mach` or `dynamic pressure` column is emitted for any of them.
- A new test builds a flight with an impossible speed, asserts the analyzer really does withhold it, then asserts the CSV header carries neither column while keeping `velocity` — and that a flight whose speed stands keeps both.
- **Falsified**: restoring the columns unconditionally fails with `no mach column: expected 'time (s),altitude (m AGL),velocity (m…' not to contain 'mach'`.
- Gate: `npm test` 52 files / 662 tests · `npm run build` exit 0 · `npm run test:e2e` 172 passed.

author: mbayard-sorp
body:
Phase 1, workstreams OS-1.5 (admin panel extensions) and OS-2.6 (daily owner report). Built on the ticket lifecycle from #346: everything here consumes `team.server.ts` exports rather than adding queries to it.

## 1. Admin ticket queue (`app/routes/admin.homepage-team.tsx`)

The flat suggestions list becomes a work board.

- **Open set** is now `proposed | approved | in_progress | pr_open | in_review | verified | blocked`, ordered by priority then age. A ticket in the middle of the lifecycle used to be invisible to the owner.
- **Columns**: assignee, priority (an inline 1-5 select with Set), age, attempt count (coral at 3).
- **last_error** is one muted line, truncated, with the full text in the `title` attribute.
- **Refs from `suggestion_links`** render as labelled links (`pr (open)`, `deploy (ready)`, `issue (open)`), fetched in one `inArray` query for the rows on screen, not one query per ticket. `note` rows are skipped: they are transition reasons, not destinations.
- **Filters** by status, kind, assignee, held in the query string so a filtered board is shareable and refresh-stable. Kind and assignee options come from the table itself.
- **New intents**: `suggestion-unblock` (blocked to approved, via `transitionSuggestion` so the transition map stays the single arbiter and the claim fields are cleared the same way agents get) and `suggestion-priority` (a plain re-prioritisation, guarded off terminal rows).
- **No regression**: Approve and Dismiss still call `decideSuggestion` on `proposed`, Retire still calls `retireSuggestion` on `approved`. Same functions, same guards.

### `release_engine_enabled` toggle
Added to the strategy tab valve list with the daily merge cap beside it. The copy states plainly what OFF does, because that is what a tired owner needs at 2am: nothing auto-merges, you merge every PR by hand exactly like before this shipped, everything else keeps running.

Both keys are added to the action's allowlisted-key guard. Without that the toggle renders and silently does nothing. They are read directly from `pipeline_settings` (the pattern already used for video frame review) rather than added to `VALVE_KEYS`, because `team-keys.ts` is a protected path for the release engine and the digest enumerates that constant.

### Mobile
`ResponsiveTable` with a `min-w-[860px]` floor, stat grid `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4`, filters `flex flex-col gap-3 md:flex-row`. The table is a table, not cards. Measured at 375px: body `scrollWidth` 375 against `clientWidth` 375 while the wrapper is 970, so the table scrolls inside its wrapper and the page body never scrolls sideways. The page shell moved from `max-w-4xl` to `max-w-5xl` so all nine columns fit on a laptop without scrolling.

## 2. Owner digest (`app/lib/owner-digest.server.ts`)

Five sections added around the existing ones.

- **Escalations**, placed first: protected-path PRs waiting on the owner (`suggestion_links` in a `needs-owner` state) and tickets that exhausted their attempts. When both are empty it says "Nothing needs you today", which is the most valuable sentence in the email. The count also reaches the subject line.
- **Shipped**: `pr`/`commit` links in a merged state in the last 24h, unioned with tickets that reached `applied` in 24h so agent-editor's legacy `apply_ref` path is not invisible. PR titles are not stored anywhere, and a cron must not block on a GitHub round-trip, so the ticket text is the title, with the PR number parsed from the ref.
- **Homepage now**: hero handle and headline, rail titles, and tile headlines read from the live storefront blob (`readHomepagePayloadB`), plus the render-truth verdict with the theme and freshness gates. When no render-truth result exists it says so, explicitly "this is not a pass", and any live `render:*` tickets are listed. The reader is tolerant by design: render-truth is a separate workstream, so this probes candidate KV keys and parses defensively rather than importing it.
- **SEO**: unchanged, still the `seo_coverage_daily` diagnosis from #342.
- **Tickets**: opened, closed, and blocked counts by kind, the oldest `approved` row with its age, and everything sitting at attempt 3. The legacy status-count line is preserved inside it.

Every gatherer swallows its own failures and degrades to "not reported", because a digest that does not send is worse than a digest with one thin section.

### Verification note
The once-a-day KV guard is untouched and is keyed on the UTC date, so triggering the cron to test it would consume the day's slot and suppress the real 13:00 UTC send. The cron was deliberately **not** triggered. Instead all five section builders are pure functions with 22 unit tests covering the empty cases, the escaping, the pluralisation, and specifically that an absent render-truth result never renders as a pass.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean
- `npm test` 619 passed, 34 files (22 new in `app/lib/owner-digest.server.test.ts`)
- `npm run build` exit 0
- Admin page rendered and screenshotted at 375px and at desktop width via a jsdom render of the route with stubbed loader data against the built CSS. Not reached through the live preview: `/admin` sits behind Neon Auth and there was no session to use.

author: zackees
body:
Implements **#1838 Phase 1** for the highest-impact wait.

A compile dispatched to the daemon blocks in `read_frame_sync` for up to 30 minutes (`SOLDR_COMPILE_REPLY_TIMEOUT_SECS`) and, until now, said nothing for the whole of it. #1838 states the problem precisely:

> three daemon-lifecycle defects all presented to the user the same way — **the build stopped making progress, and nothing said why until a multi-minute backstop expired**

The bound is not the bug. The silence is.

## What this does

`WaitHeartbeat` reports every 60 s while the wrapper is blocked, naming the **operation, elapsed time, active deadline, and controlling env var**:

```
soldr: daemon compile reply still waiting after 60s (deadline 1800s from
SOLDR_COMPILE_REPLY_TIMEOUT_SECS); if this is a wedged cache rather than a slow
compile, `soldr --no-cache cargo ...` or ZCCACHE_DISABLE=1 bypasses the daemon
```

That shape is deliberately identical to the cargo front door's existing heartbeat, which #1838 calls out as prior art to reuse rather than reinvent. It is *not* shared code, because `soldr-daemon` cannot depend on `soldr-cli` — the dependency runs the other way. Same 60 s cadence, so there is one rhythm to learn rather than two.

The remedy is inline, which is #1838's Phase 2 point: the corrective action belongs where the stall is visible, not only in `CLAUDE.md`. Someone watching a wedged build is not reading the repo docs.

## Design choices worth the review time

**A watchdog thread, not a shorter socket read timeout.** The obvious alternative — shorten the read and loop — changes IPC semantics: `read_frame_sync` starts returning `WouldBlock`/`TimedOut` mid-frame, and every caller then has to distinguish "no reply yet" from "the daemon died". A thread that only prints leaves the transport untouched, so **a heartbeat can never turn a healthy slow compile into a failed one**.

**Silent on the happy path.** Nothing prints unless the wait exceeds the first interval. A warm compile returns in milliseconds and is unaffected, so this does not add noise to normal builds.

**Stderr**, leaving `--json` modes on stdout intact (#1838 explicitly asks for this).

**The guard joins its thread on drop**, so a heartbeat cannot outlive the operation it describes and report on a compile that already finished — worse than silence.

## Verified it fires, not just that it formats

A probe with a 120 ms interval over a 500 ms wait emitted **3 heartbeats** with the expected text. Probe reverted before committing. Four unit tests cover the message contents, the inline remedy, happy-path silence, and drop-joins-thread.

## Scope

Phase 1 for the **compile reply** — the 30-minute wait, and the one users actually hit. The other long waits #1838 lists (cache flush at 5 min, graceful shutdown at 300 s) are the same pattern and can reuse `WaitHeartbeat` directly; I left them out to keep this reviewable and because the compile path is where the reported pain is.

Phases 2–5 (failure classification, unified timeout registry, telemetry, runbook) remain open on the issue.

## Validation (Windows host)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `-p soldr-daemon --lib` | **154 passed**, 0 failed |
| clippy `-p soldr-daemon --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| `--test timed_test_lint` | pass |
| fmt (per-crate) | clean |

author: zancas
body:
## Summary

**`mobile-adaptation-shipped`** — zingo-mobile already consumes this head: the pin rides `price_sources` at `47e44b79e` (zingo-mobile `4c8f3168`), and the race is wired into the price surface with a source-naming payload (zingo-mobile ADR 0006).

zingo-mobile's testers lose the price whenever Gemini is unreachable, because Gemini was the only source. This PR gives zingo-price two more and a race.

## The sources

`PriceSource` names the three operators, each carrying its URL and a pure parser over the response text:

- **Gemini** keeps its recent-trades endpoint and exact behavior; the median-of-eleven contract is untouched, and `fetch_current_price` still means "Gemini alone" for existing callers.
- **Kraken**'s public recent-trades endpoint (`pair=ZECUSD&count=11`) is a real USD pair with trades, so the same median contract transfers unchanged. Its in-band `error` array lands in a new typed arm (`SourceReportedError`) carrying the source's own words.
- **CoinGecko**'s simple-price endpoint is an aggregator's spot value with its update time — a different failure domain and trust model, serving as the diversity leg. There are no trades to take a median of.

Structurally alien bodies land in a second new arm (`UnexpectedShape`) naming the missing piece. The HTTP leg is shared by all sources and keeps the 20-second request bound from #2568, so every leg settles inside the single-fetch contract the mobile 25-second watchdog assumes.

## The race

`race_current_price` runs all three concurrently on a `FuturesUnordered` (no runtime dependency enters the lib) and returns the first success as a `RacedPrice` naming its source; the losing legs cancel by drop. When every source fails, `PriceRaceFailure` carries each source's typed error, and its rendered report walks every cause chain, so a total outage is diagnosable per operator. The sequential order (`PriceSource::next`) remains for a caller that prefers one source at a time.

## Testing

Seven parser and rotation tests (Kraken median, in-band error, shape refusal; CoinGecko spot, non-finite refusal; rotation cycle) plus two hermetic race tests against local stub servers: a healthy source wins beside a garbage server and a silent one, and an all-fail names all three sources. 14 of 14 zingo-price tests pass; check, clippy, and fmt are clean.

## Stacking

Based on `attach_retune` (#2569), which stacks on `socks5_typed_timeout` (#2568) → `netutils_time` (#2567) → #2561; the diff is this single commit and the PR auto-retargets as its base merges.

body:
## Summary

Wires this repo up to the Supabase project (`project_ref` `kgodwfbpgqndniepobbm`) in two ways:

1. Registers the hosted **Supabase MCP server** via a project-scoped `.mcp.json`, so the config is version-controlled and shared across everyone who works in the repo.
2. Adds **Prisma ORM** configured to connect to the Supabase Postgres database.

## Changes

**MCP server** — new `.mcp.json` at the repo root registering the `supabase` HTTP MCP server (URL scoped to the project ref; features: `docs`, `account`, `database`, `debugging`, `development`, `functions`, `branching`). Generated with:

```
claude mcp add --scope project --transport http supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=kgodwfbpgqndniepobbm&features=..."
```

**Prisma ORM**
- Added `prisma` as a dev dependency.
- New `prisma/schema.prisma` with a `postgresql` datasource: `url` = `DATABASE_URL` (transaction-mode pooler, port 6543, `pgbouncer=true`) and `directUrl` = `DIRECT_URL` (session-mode pooler, port 5432, used for migrations).
- Documented `DATABASE_URL` / `DIRECT_URL` in `.env.example` (commented, with `[YOUR-PASSWORD]` placeholder). Real credentials stay in gitignored local env files — nothing secret is committed.

author: jtvargas
body:
Part 10: the new-message pill, message rendering, and Lato.

## The pill

`↓ Latest` is removed rather than hidden — the `.latest` case, the `LatestPill` view, the `isFarFromBottom` state and its two bindings, and the half-viewport distance band the scroll scaffold projected to feed it. That band was the only distance the shell measured that no scroll decision depended on, so removing the pill removes one arithmetic-on-estimates path from an engine whose content metrics are known to be unreliable.

What remains is `N new messages`, appearing only because something arrived. Plain glass instead of `.glassProminent` — the tint bought clarity against a sibling that no longer exists — at Slack's size: caption text, `.controlSize(.small)` for the button style's own insets, and a 28pt floor rather than a fixed height so an accessibility text size grows the capsule instead of clipping it.

## Rendering

Measured against the Buzz mobile client's renderer (`gpt_markdown` 1.1.6), construct by construct.

**New:** GFM tables, horizontal rules, task and radio items. **Parsed but never drawn, now drawn:** strikethrough, `<u>`, and code spans. **Fixed:** the code block's language label was an overlay printing *through* the first line of code whenever that line ran the full width.

Tables are a horizontally scrolled `Grid`. A `ScrollView` adopts the width it is offered rather than its content's, so a wide table never widens the message row; the axis is horizontal only, with `scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize)` so a table that already fits claims no gesture from the conversation. Cell width is capped by a custom `Layout` rather than `frame(maxWidth:)` — inside a horizontal scroll view the content is offered an unspecified width, so a `Text` lays out on one line however long it is and a frame then clips it. Measured: `frame(maxWidth: 260)` gives 16pt of height for a long string (one line, clipped); the layout gives 144pt (nine lines, all visible).

Deliberate divergences from upstream, all toward not losing text: a delimiter row is required before two pipe-bearing lines are treated as a table; only the empty cell an *outer* pipe makes is dropped; oversize tables fall back to complete plain text. Upstream's `[1]` citation badge is **not** implemented — its regex matches anywhere outside code, so `list[0]` in ordinary text would render as a circled `0` with the authored `[0]` gone.

## Lato

Six cuts under the OFL, registered through `UIAppFonts`, with the system font as fallback. 88 call sites converted.

The reason this is more than a swap: **a static font family silently drops a weight asked for by trait.** `Lato-Regular` asked for semibold returns `Lato-Regular` — no error, no warning. Three separate places would have shipped wrong because of it:

- `RichTextStyle` set every mention, channel reference and link with `base.weight(…)`, so **every entity in every message** would have drawn at body weight, carrying only the tint.
- The new table renderer set its header row with `.fontWeight(.semibold)`, so header cells would have been indistinguishable from body cells.
- Headings, and the sidebar's unread cue — **every channel row would have read as read.**

Same shape one layer down for code: `Text` renders an `inlinePresentationIntent.code` run by asking the run's font for the fixed-width member of its own family, and Lato has none, so an inline `` `--flag` `` would have set in proportional Lato. The monospaced face is now named rather than requested.

SF Symbols stay San Francisco by name (`hiveSymbol`) — a symbol is a glyph from the system's symbol font, and handing it Lato costs the weight and gains nothing.

## Validation at `7eaa546`

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| SwiftLint `--strict` | 0 |
| Package tests (release) | 556 — 293 NostrCore + 263 BuzzKit |
| App tests | 406 in 51 suites |
| Conversation shape gate | 32 readings, `allowance=311` on all 8 shapes, 0 failures |

The shape gate reading is stated because it can be vacuous: this run also caught the app test bundle **crashing** rather than failing. `TypographyTests` handed an already-scaled font back to `UIFontMetrics`, which UIKit answers with an exception — and an uncaught exception in a test bundle takes the whole run down and reports the totals from earlier launches, so the suite printed `5 tests in 2 suites passed` over a run that had aborted 361 tests earlier. Fixed by giving `uiFont` an optional `compatibleWith:` (default `nil`, so no app call site changes).

## Only a device can judge

Nothing in a test renders type or a table. Worth eyes on: Lato's colour and rhythm at body size, table borders and the h1 rule, checkbox baseline alignment, the new inter-block spacing (constants all live in `RichTextSpacing`), and the pill's size against Slack's.

## Not in this PR

Custom emoji (`:shortcode:`) and inline media are both in the mobile client and both need the event's tags at the renderer — the same plumbing. They belong with Part 11 (images), already tracked as gaps in `PARITY.md`.

body:
## Linked issue

- Closes #1607

## Description

`icalendar.enums.VALUE` enumerates the value types from :rfc:`5545` section 3.2.20, but it omitted `BINARY`, the first value type in that list. `BINARY` is used by the library itself: `vBinary.default_value` is `"BINARY"` and serializes as `VALUE=BINARY`, and `IMAGE` accepts `VALUE=BINARY`. Despite that, `VALUE.BINARY` raised `AttributeError`.

This PR:

- adds `BINARY = "BINARY"` to `VALUE` (in RFC order, before `BOOLEAN`);
- adds `BINARY` to the class docstring's `Attributes:` list;
- adds tests that `VALUE` matches the RFC 5545 section 3.2.20 value-type set, that `VALUE.BINARY == "BINARY"`, and that `vBinary.default_value` is a `VALUE` member.

There is no behavioural change to parsing or serialization; this completes the public enum so it matches the RFC and the library's own use of `VALUE=BINARY`.

body:
Closes #20 — the final slice. Written by a delegated Opus agent from the merged design + probe addendum; hardened through the full review discipline before this PR was opened (adversarial code review + functional review against live opencode 1.18.7 + coordinator verification), with all findings fixed in-branch.

## What it is
`GUILD_APPROVE=off|write|all` (default **off**) arms per-call approval on the delegate path: gated tools get an `ask`-tier rule injected via `POST /session`'s permission ruleset (probed: merges last-match-wins onto the def's resolved array). `GUILD_APPROVE_EGRESS` offers the same on `webfetch`/`websearch` for the read paths — the one opt-in spend of the ratified egress harness difference (provenance in AGENTS.md). Approval reaches the human via MCP elicitation (raw request — the SDK helper is blocked by Claude Code's bare capability) and/or `modelguild watch --approve`, which replies directly to the serve port; first reply wins, opencode arbitrates.

## Security properties (all adversarially probed)
- **Never-widen, enforced at the wire:** rulesets may only contain `ask`, and only for tools in the allow-set **parsed from the agent def in force** (`parseAgentPermissions` — the hard-coded mirror a review probe defeated is deleted; an unparseable def refuses the call). A user-hardened def can no longer be re-opened by the bridge.
- **Fail-closed everywhere:** timeout (120s default) ⇒ reject; headless elicitation auto-cancel ⇒ *abstain* when a watch terminal is live, reject when sole; mid-turn stream loss rejects open requests and reports `degraded`; armed-with-no-channel refuses up front, before any evidence-log entry; `GUILD_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` remains the outer bound.
- **Honest receipts:** counters record evidence-backed outcomes only (2xx or opencode's own `permission.replied`; 404 ⇒ `contested`, transport failure ⇒ `undelivered`). Prompt text is control-character-sanitized at write *and* render — a model-chosen command string cannot repaint the approval prompt.
- **Honest bound, stated everywhere:** an approved `bash` is an approved shell; the loopback reply path is not an authentication boundary (SECURITY.md). Visibility, not containment.

## Proven live on opencode 1.18.7
An `ask` ruleset genuinely blocks a real model turn (timeout resolved at exactly the configured deadline); approve via a real `watch --approve` TTY, reject (model receives it verbatim, turn continues), timeout, up-front refusal (1ms, zero log entries), `off` sends no ruleset (wire-verified via session echo), read paths under `all` gate nothing (intersection rule), and the egress knob works end-to-end. Quirk recorded: opencode's `edit` permission key gates the write/patch family (`write` is inert) — a module-load assertion keeps `edit` in every non-off tier.

## Review record
Adversarial review: 3 highs (terminal ANSI spoof, elicitation pre-empting the watcher, the def-mirror widening), 4 meds (wire-boundary gap, counter honesty, mid-turn blindness, subset read-back), 5 lows — all reproduced with probe scripts, all fixed, fixes re-verified by the coordinator. Functional review: 9/9 checks PASS. Parity audit: with the knob off (default) the asymmetry runs permissive; armed, it reaches Claude Code's own subagent-gating default without exceeding it; no new harness difference claimed.

Still human-unverified: whether the interactive Claude Code TUI renders the elicitation prompt (headless auto-cancels; the design never depends on it).

author: anko9801
body:
Supersedes #128 (same first commit, message corrected — see below).

## The problem

The parallel test runner LPT-bin-packed the file list into one **fixed chunk per worker**. That is optimal only if the per-file cost estimates are right, and measured on CI they cannot be: the same file's time swings **±30 % run to run** (runner speed, cache state, JIT order). Over four green CI runs the makespan sat **8–21 % above the perfect-balance floor** — one worker still grinding while the others had nothing left they were *allowed* to touch.

## What I tried first, and what it actually bought

Commit 1 re-fits `_COST` from measured CI medians (the table had 26 entries against ~250 files; the two heaviest per-push files were carrying the 3.0 s default while actually costing **91.5 s** and **84.2 s**).

Measured on CI as makespan / perfect-balance floor — that ratio normalises out runner-speed variance, which is ±40 % between runs:

| tier | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `oracles` | 1.212 | **1.143** (~10 s, below all four before-runs) |
| `fast` (critical path) | 1.091 | 1.084 (~1.5 s — **inside run-to-run noise**) |

An offline simulation had predicted ~25 s on both. It was wrong: it could not reproduce Julia's unstable `sort` tie-breaking across the ~90 files sharing the 3.0 default, so it packed different chunks than the runner did. #128's title claimed that number; this PR carries the corrected message.

The estimate was never the real problem. **Pre-assignment was.**

## The fix

Commit 2: the workers pull. The parent writes the file list (heaviest first) to a temp dir and starts N identical workers; each takes a file by atomically creating `claim_<i>` with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and moves on when it loses the race. The kernel does the mutual exclusion — no lock file, no IPC, no parent-side scheduler. `_COST` survives only as the hand-out order, where being wrong is cheap.

Measured, same machine, same 149 files, `tier=fast`:

| | per-worker totals | makespan / ideal |
|---|---|---|
| static | 432.5 / 426.2 / 396.8 / 456.7 s | 1.067 |
| on-demand | 255.1 / 255.1 / 258.2 / 262.0 s | **1.017** |

On CI's four-worker runner the recovered 7–19 % lands on the critical path.

## Safety

The one failure mode an on-demand queue has that static assignment does not is a worker dying **between** claiming a file and running it — the file would simply not run, and the suite would go green having skipped a test. So a worker writes `done_<i>` only *after* the file returns, and the parent errors loudly on any index with no `done_` marker.

## Verification

- `tier=fast`, 149 files, **all passed**; every file claimed exactly once (`claims == done == n`).
- 3-worker concurrency test on a 6-file queue: each file runs exactly once, all workers exit 0.
- Tier-membership meta-test green (enforces every `_COST` key names a real file).
- Clean under JuliaFormatter 2.5.0.

Tier lists are untouched.

author: huanghaoyuanhhy
body:
## Summary

`l0compact` fails on every backup taken from Milvus 2.5 with:

```
Error: l0compact: unmarshal extras: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go value of type string
```

The descriptor extras of a v1 binlog are not a string-to-string map. Milvus writes `nullable`
as a bool next to string entries such as `original_size`:

```go
// milvus internal/storage/binlog_writer.go, NewInsertBinlogWriter
// store nullable in extra for compatible
descriptorEvent.AddExtra(nullableKey, nullable) // bool
```

so the JSON is `{"original_size":"12345","nullable":true}`, while `envelope.go` decoded it into
`map[string]string`. `ReadInsertPK` reaches that decode for every `KindV1` segment, so the
command is unusable against 2.5. Milvus 2.6 stores insert logs as bare parquet and takes the
`KindV2` branch, never touching the v1 envelope parser — which is why only the 2.5 matrix
failed.

Typing the field as `map[string]any` is what the wire format actually carries. The sole
consumer compares `Extras["version"]` against `MULTI_FIELD`; comparing an `any` to a string is
still an equality on the dynamic value, so that keeps working.

This has broken the nightly `test-backup-restore-api (2.5, L2)` job on every run since
2026-07-17 — all 8 `test_l0compact.py` cases, never green since the feature landed.

## Changes

- envelope: decode descriptor extras as `map[string]any`, with a note on why they are mixed
- envelope: `BuildV1Envelope` takes the same type, keeping the writer symmetric with the reader
- test: cover extras carrying a bool, and a `version` marker sitting next to one

Both new tests fail on `main` with the exact error above and pass with the fix.

author: cmloegcmluin
body:
The resumed state stopped short of these two, on the reasoning that nothing
on disk brings them back: a lock is repeat-one in an mpv process that has
been replaced, and the sound level is re-seeded to full because Nau and the
audio companion each launch unattenuated.  Both are true about the
mechanism and neither is a reason to forget the setting -- there is no more
reason for the sound or a lock to reset overnight than for the clip on
screen to.  So carry them, and put the world back to match.

The level: seed_startup_states already wrote the volume file at startup, so
it now writes the session's level rather than MAX_VOLUME, and tells the
other sink too -- Nau gets SET_VOLUME <level> <muted> on its command
channel, drained on its first tick.  That is the answer to the old
docstring's worry that a resumed mute would be "a silence with nothing on
screen to explain it": Nau draws the level and the mute it is given.  Both
sinks go through one publisher (audio_volume.publish_audio_level) that
startup and every live volume command share, so the two spellings of the
same state -- zero for the companion, level-plus-flag for Nau -- cannot
drift apart.

The lock: queued back to the locked side's command file before the
satellites launch, so the player drains it on its very first tick, by which
time its session has loaded the clip the resume put at the top of the
playlist -- the clip the lock was on, locked again before a frame of
anything else plays.

Reading the carried state has to precede the seeding now, so the resume
block moves above it in both apps.  The desktop's start_core_session grows
nau_cmd_file, which the manifest already carries; FunTimeVR's primary role
reads that same file and handles SET_VOLUME, so it gets the level too.

selection still reset: those genuinely do not survive, and the HUDs are
right to show them off.

author: westbridgeinc
body:
## Phase 1 · Taxi — S2: nearest-candidate cap is now tunable + the straight-line/ETA seam is documented

**Problem.** `findCandidates` keeps the 50 movers with the smallest great-circle
`ST_Distance` (`ORDER BY ST_Distance … LIMIT 50`), then `rankCandidates`
re-sorts the survivors by **real road ETA**. Great-circle nearest ≠ road-ETA
nearest in a real network (rivers, one-ways, the single Demerara bridge). With
**>50 movers in range**, a car that is ETA-closest but straight-line #51 is
truncated *before scoring sees it*. SWIFT-142 guaranteed "nearest 50" only in
the straight-line sense.

**Fix (proportionate, cost-aware).** The `50` — previously hardcoded in two
places — becomes an env-tunable cap read per call:
`DISPATCH_NEAREST_CANDIDATE_CAP` (default **50**, unchanged behaviour). The
comment now documents the seam honestly:

- the cap is **straight-line**; the **ETA re-rank happens after** it;
- at **launch fleet density** the candidate pool rarely reaches the cap, so ETA
  truncation is **not a live risk today**;
- a **dense market raises the cap** to shrink the truncation window, at a
  bounded maps-provider cost (the ETA batch already handles N destinations).

We deliberately do **not** blindly 2× the default — in prod the maps provider
(Google Distance Matrix) bills per element, and doubling the pool doubles that
bill for a divergence that can't occur below cap-many candidates. Tunable is the
right lever; ops sizes it per city.

**Test.** With the cap overridden low and more movers than the cap in range, the
pool is exactly the nearest-N by distance — proving the cap is applied and
configurable.

No schema change. Phase 1 taxi backend S2 (#4 of 4 — closes the taxi backend
work). tsc + eslint + full suite green.

author: appcraft008-dev
body:
## Summary
三馆预热实战踩的三个坑,固化成契约纪律(纯文档)。

### 纪律⑨ 多步批任务用 `&&` 不用 `;`
`;` 连接的命令链**中间崩了后面照跑、末尾照打完成标记** —— "打印了完成标记"≠"全部成功"。

实测:三馆预热六条命令用 `;` 串起来,Joconde 崩掉 orsay/orangerie 两步,链条仍打印 `PREHEAT_ALL_DONE`;**第二次加了分步标记 `STEP_*`,用的还是 `;`,同样无效** —— 同一个坑踩两次,两次都靠**核验数据**(件数没涨)才发现。

### 纪律⑩ 判进程认执行体,不认编排它的外壳
`sh -c "A && B && C"` 外壳的 cmdline **包含整条链的字符串**,A 的进程早退出了外壳仍匹配 → 误判"还在跑"。后果:自动切换没触发,本该被拦截的橘园全量任务跑了 7 件。

附:**容器里没有 `ps` / `pgrep` / `pkill`** —— 判活用宿主 `docker top`,容器内定位/终止用 `/proc` + `os.kill`。

### 纪律⑪ 小馆 `popularity` 排序失真
橘园**睡莲六联作 popularity 全是 0**(同一作品拆成多条目,各自 sitelink 都少),而《保罗·纪尧姆肖像》是 6 —— 按 `--limit N` 预热**招牌反排最后**。

对策:小馆按**"有图"筛选或显式列 qid**("有图"=可拍照识别=用户魔法时刻入口,比热度更贴近真实价值)。

### 配方章补 Joconde 现状
**API 返回法语 HTML 而非 JSON,即不可用**,预热期间跳过 49+ 次。内容靠 Wikipedia+Wikidata 仍接地合格,只是材料薄一点。新馆现在配 `joconde` 意义不大;待恢复后可 `--force` 补材料。这也是纪律①"单源失败跳过继续"的实战来源。

## 预热最终成果(供对照)
| 馆 | ready | en | zh | fr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| louvre | 303 | 303 | 303 | 302 |
| orsay | 268 | 268 | 256 | 266 |
| orangerie | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18(**有图 15 件 100%**) |

**成本 ~$6.7**(预估 $11)。

author: charlessavage90
body:
## What this is

The record of the **Gate 2 → 3 boundary review** you commissioned: architect, security, quality, and frontend, each with the code open, read-only. The graph analyst was deliberately not staffed — no scoring question is open and path quality is PAUSED.

Findings doc: `docs/superpowers/findings/2026-07-27-gate2-gate3-team-review.md`. It owns no path-quality figures; the performance numbers are the reviewers' own, labelled, with the dev-laptop-not-container caveat stated.

## Headline

**Four blocking findings across three reviewers are one underlying issue**, and it is currently held back only by the password Gate 3 removes:

- Pathfinding is GIL-bound at a hard **~1.5 req/s for the whole internet**; at 40 concurrent requests `/health` takes 22 s against a 5 s timeout, so latency turns into instance replacement and the outage cycles. ~40 open sockets do it.
- The clip endpoint is an unauthenticated outbound proxy — every request hits Deezer/iTunes from one shared IP — and under throttling it **triples its own outbound rate** while the user sees a card silently revert.

Plus two untested wiring paths — `build_default_app` and `sync_frontend.main` — where every guard is tested but the code that arms them is not (delete the graph-checksum check, the clip cache, or the deploy ordering and all 448+58 tests stay green). And an iOS audio finding no test can reach: `play()` is never called in the tap's synchronous turn, which is the thing iPhone Safari refuses.

**One irreversible item:** every shared link is pinned to the auto-generated `*.cloudfront.net` domain, which can never be recreated. A custom domain is near-free now and impossible to retrofit for links already out there.

## Suites

Re-run green from `C:\dev`: builder 115, api 195, infra 58, frontend 80, + 5 Playwright e2e (new — the last closeout did not cover it).

## Owner's calls vs mine

Laid out in §6. Yours: the custom domain, telemetry retention + a privacy notice, whether to borrow an iPhone for ten minutes (an ordered script is included that settles the iOS finding on the first tap), and whether Gate 3 proceeds on this timeline. Mine (made, not tabled): nothing warrants reopening the closed list, and the sequencing recommendation — run the live-origin load test before planning remediation, because it decides whether the top finding is a rate-limit rule or a rearchitect.

## Note

**§7 is a placeholder** — it holds the result of that live load test, which the review names as its own pivot. Filling it in a follow-up commit to this branch, then this is ready to merge.

author: duongnad
body:
A desktop world left running grew the Rust process by **14 MB every minute** — 2 GB in 75 minutes, 19 GB projected over a day. This is most of it.

`simulation_loop` pre-fills the inference recycle pool with 16 batches and says why: *"to ensure zero heap allocations in the hot path"*. Nothing enforced the number. When the worker had not yet returned a batch, `sensory_system` allocated a fresh one — and since every batch is **recycled rather than dropped**, that allocation joined the pool permanently. A tick loop outrunning the inference worker grew the pool by one batch per tick, for as long as the run lasted.

An empty pool now means "the worker is behind", and the answer is to skip this tick's inference rather than buy memory. The system was already built for it: an agent that does not think keeps its last CPG parameters and goes on moving, eating and metabolising — the same tolerance the LOD tiering beside it relies on. Bounding the request side bounds both pools, since batches in flight can never exceed the pool.

**Measured** — headless (no webview, no emit, no evolution, 10 agents), 30 s to 182 s of a three-minute run:

| | 30 s | 182 s | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 211.8 MB | 233.3 MB | **8.5 MB/min** |
| after | 188.2 MB | 201.9 MB | **5.4 MB/min** |

A third of the growth removed and the floor 23 MB lower — **and a second source remains**, steady at 5.4 MB/min and not decelerating. This PR does not close that, and the commit says so rather than calling the leak fixed.

**Also corrected:** this was *not* the unbounded lineage growth `STATE_OF_THE_PROJECT.md` §3.15 predicts. That path writes nothing unless evolution is running, and evolution was off for every measurement above. §3.15 remains true about lineage; it was simply not what this run was doing.

**The test asserts the invariant, not a byte figure.** A memory threshold would depend on the allocator and the machine's load — the kind of gate that fails on a busy runner and teaches people to re-run CI. Verified in both directions: it fails on the unfixed code with `1 batch(es) were created out of nothing`, and it proves the skip is not permanent damage by returning one batch and watching the next tick think again.

`cargo test --features desktop`: **892 passed, 0 failed** across 87 targets (891 before, +1). fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean.

author: schubydoo
body:
The re-review on #1129 spent its denials probing for `uv run pytest`, then closed with:

> One thing I could not do: run the test suite here — `uv run pytest` was denied by the runner sandbox

That frames a design choice as a limitation. It shouldn't be trying.

## Why not simply allow it

The runner has **no virtualenv**, so a real run means `uv sync --extra dev` plus the suite — minutes of quota per review to reproduce what CI already runs on **three OSes × four Pythons**, on every PR, for free.

And for this PR specifically an Ubuntu run couldn't settle the claim anyway: the number that matters is the **Windows 3.11** leg. A Linux box cannot answer a Windows wall-clock question — a lesson this repo has paid for more than once.

The reviewer's fallback was already right: it verified six things statically (patch surface, marker coverage, `--strict-markers` safety, the WAL size guard, no open handle at copy time) and named CI as the measurement. This makes that the *instruction* rather than the consolation prize.

## The second-order reason

#1140 made a non-zero `permission_denials_count` raise a warning that the review may have been blocked from **publishing**. Routine, expected denials from probing for pytest would fire that warning on **every run** and train it to be ignored — the same decay the doc-pair guard had to be rescued from an hour ago. Removing the attempts keeps the signal meaningful.

## Effect

Instructions are fetched from the default branch at run time, so this takes effect **on merge, with no workflow change**.

`markdownlint` and `scripts/lint-docs.sh` pass. File is 160 lines.

## Description

### Problem

The TokenSpeed source-build pin (`815f50c`, 2026-07-20) trails upstream main — flagged by the engine-watch automation in #1980.

### Solution

- `scripts/ci_install_tokenspeed.sh`: `TOKENSPEED_REF` → `0f68676069141857a605b8805c13131d9f53e901`, the merge commit of Kimi K3 integration (tokenspeed#822). The window brings MiniMax M3 support (+ Eagle3.1 draft checkpoints, NVFP4 mixed precision, FP8 KV cache), Kimi K3, DeepSeek EAGLE MLA / Kimi K2.7 Code EAGLE3.1, GDN flashinfer decode + MoE/MSA/attention kernel optimizations, and properly declared runtime dependencies (tokenspeed#783).
- Torch co-pin unchanged: TokenSpeed's `pyproject.toml` still requires `torch==2.11.0` at this ref, so `torch==2.11.0+cu130` stays.
- No other pin sites: the release workflow and `docker/engine.Dockerfile` receive the commit via inputs; upstream's `tokenspeed-smg-grpc-*` dists (bumped upstream in tokenspeed#824) are uninstalled by this script in favor of source installs, so they don't constrain the pin.
- `UV_INDEX_STRATEGY=unsafe-best-match`: tokenspeed-kernel at this ref pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.15.post1` (needs `packaging>=24.2`), and uv's default first-index strategy resolved `packaging` exclusively from the cu130 extra index (stale, <=24.1) — upstream's pip-based installer merges indexes best-version, so this restores the semantics upstream relies on. `torch` still resolves from the cu130 index via its `+cu130` local-version pin.
- Dropped the pin comment's stale reference to the EPD package promotion (tokenspeed#743) — included in any ref newer than the previous pin.

Closes #1980

## Test Plan

- Static: every `tokenspeed` import statement across `grpc_servicer/smg_grpc_servicer` (22 sites, including lazy in-function imports) resolves against the `0f68676` tree — modules and symbols verified by ast scan.
- Real validation: `e2e-1gpu-chat (tokenspeed)` and `e2e-4gpu-epd (tokenspeed)` legs on this PR build the pinned ref from source and run the full suites.

author: kapumota
body:
### Objetivo científico

Este PR implementa la Fase 6 del Paper 1 y reemplaza los modelos formales de una sola transferencia por modelos concurrentes acotados con múltiples sesiones, mensajes, votos de validadores y mutantes científicos versionados.

Se reutiliza la infraestructura reproducible de la Fase 5, pero se eliminan los controles negativos generados temporalmente. Cada defecto estudiado se representa ahora mediante un modelo mutante persistente y trazable.

### Cambios principales

#### Modelo TLA+ multisesión

`CrossShardCommit.tla` representa el estado mediante funciones indexadas por transferencia:

* `status`.
* `sourceShard`.
* `targetShard`.
* `locked`.
* `receiptOwner`.
* `receiptUseCount`.
* `destinationCredit`.
* `fundsReleased`.
* `messages`.
* `votes`.

Los shards origen y destino se seleccionan dentro del bound declarado y deben ser diferentes.

Se agrega una acción `Stutter` explícita para evitar deadlocks espurios en estados terminales.

#### Configuraciones TLC

Se incorporan seis configuraciones válidas:

* `2shards-1transfer.cfg`.
* `2shards-2transfers.cfg`.
* `3shards-3transfers.cfg`.
* `duplicate-receipt.cfg`.
* `delayed-message.cfg`.
* `timeout-race.cfg`.

#### Mutantes TLA+

Se agregan cinco mutantes científicos versionados:

* `NoReplayProtection.tla`.
* `CreditBeforeReceipt.tla`.
* `CommitAfterAbort.tla`.
* `TimeoutWithoutRelease.tla`.
* `QuorumBypass.tla`.

Cada mutante posee una configuración que selecciona la propiedad que debe fallar.

#### Modelo Alloy con estados ordenados

El modelo Alloy utiliza:

```alloy
open util/ordering[State]
```

Se modelan explícitamente:

* `State`.
* `Transfer`.
* `Receipt`.
* `Shard`.
* `Validator`.
* `Message`.
* transiciones entre estados consecutivos.

Las transiciones utilizan `nextState` para representar el estado posterior.

#### Mutantes Alloy

Se agregan cinco mutantes equivalentes:

* ausencia de protección contra replay;
* crédito antes de validar el recibo;
* commit después de abort;
* timeout sin liberación;
* bypass de quorum.

#### Propiedades verificadas

* `NoReceiptReplay`.
* `DestinationCreditRequiresValidReceipt`.
* `DecisionConsistency`.
* `EventuallyReleasedAfterTimeout`.
* `QuorumRequired`.

`EventuallyReleasedAfterTimeout` se interpreta como una garantía acotada de estado. No se presenta como una demostración ilimitada de vivacidad.

#### Ejecución científica

`make formal-research` ejecuta:

* seis configuraciones válidas TLA+;
* cinco mutantes TLA+;
* un modelo Alloy válido;
* cinco mutantes Alloy.

En total se generan diecisiete reportes estructurados.

#### Contraejemplos

Los contraejemplos se almacenan en:

```text
results/formal/counterexamples/
```

La matriz experimental se registra en:

```text
results/formal/mutant_matrix.csv
```

#### Integración continua

El workflow formal:

* instala versiones fijadas de TLC y Alloy;
* ejecuta la matriz multisesión;
* verifica los modelos corregidos;
* comprueba los diez mutantes;
* valida el manifiesto;
* publica resultados y contraejemplos como artefactos.

### Correcciones identificadas mediante ejecución real

Durante la validación se corrigieron:

1. asignaciones funcionales no aceptadas dentro de archivos `.cfg`;
2. deadlocks espurios por ausencia de stuttering explícito;
3. uso del identificador inválido `s'` en Alloy;
4. una prueba Java que todavía exigía la estructura formal de la Fase 5.

### Validaciones realizadas

* `bash scripts/run_tests.sh`.
* `bash scripts/run_security_checks.sh`.
* `bash scripts/run_formal_checks.sh`.
* `make validate`.
* `make formal-research`.
* `git diff --check`.
* ejecución directa de TLC.
* ejecución directa de Alloy 6.2.0 con `sat4j`.
* validación del recibo JSON de Alloy.
* comprobación de 17 reportes.
* comprobación de 10 contraejemplos.

Todas las validaciones finalizaron correctamente.

### Resultados

El modelo Alloy corregido no produjo contraejemplos para las cinco propiedades dentro de los bounds declarados.

Cada mutante produjo el resultado negativo esperado.

El manifiesto final quedó con estado `passed`.

### Alcance y limitaciones

Los resultados corresponden a verificación acotada.

La ausencia de contraejemplos no demuestra corrección ilimitada para cualquier número de shards, transferencias, validadores, mensajes o estados.

La conformidad automática entre Java y los modelos formales queda reservada para la Fase 7.

author: johnshew
body:
Three failures earlier in this session were diagnosed by hand because
the logs did not carry the fact that settled them, and a fourth was
unreadable because of how it was printed. This closes those four gaps.

## Piped log output is ASCII (#186)

The query tool drew its table with box characters, and a Windows
console decodes a captured pipe at its own codepage, so the sanctioned
way to read runtime state turned to noise exactly when the reader was a
program. A terminal still gets the drawn table; anything else gets
column rules, one row per line, a row count, and cells flattened so a
row cannot span lines. `--format` now names csv and jsonl as the forms
to parse.

## A timeout says how long it actually took (#183)

The error carried the configured limit, which the operator already
knew. The elapsed time and the attempt count, which distinguish a slow
link from a wedged one, were not written down at all. Both are now on
every retry warning, on the terminal error, and on the agent phase of a
successful run, and `AgentTimeoutError` carries them for a caller that
has to explain itself.

## The smoketest names a host limit (#185)

An agent that exhausted its retries failed the run with the same shape
as a broken contract, so a link that was merely slow read as a defect
in the tool. The verdict names the limit, quotes the attempts and the
timeout each one hit, and records a category that the health check
reports alongside the reason. It reads the category off the exception
class that raises it rather than a literal, so producer and consumer
cannot drift.

## A capability probe that refuses or drags is recorded (#183)

Every host-mutating command asks the pre-dispatch gate whether the host
can do what it is about to be told to do, and the answer left no trace,
so a slow probe looked like a slow command. A refusal, and any probe
over five seconds, is now written to the admin log with the capability,
the operation that needed it, the elapsed time, and why it said no. A
fast pass stays silent: a row per invocation would bury the interesting
one.

## Verification

- Suite: 470 tests, OK, 9 skipped, on Windows. Eleven are new.
- The suite now installs the query tool's own dependency, in its PEP
  723 header and in the CI step, so its output is asserted rather than
  described.
- `pre-release-audit.py`: 73 files, no issues.
- `agents-live smoketest` against this worktree: PASS, 14 of 14, real
  agent tokens.

Fixes #186
Fixes #183
Fixes #185

author: sthbryan
body:
Curie only managed global skills. This adds per-project scopes: keep an AWS skill in `don_camaron` and a github-pages skill in `mi_taquito.com` without either landing globally.

## Scope lives in the URL

`/installed` is global, `/p/don_camaron/installed` is the project. The screen and the install destination are decided by the same string, so they cannot desync — no hidden "active project" to forget about. Back/forward work, and `AnimatePresence` already animates the switch.

The `skills` CLI supports this natively: omitting `-g` makes it operate on the process cwd. So the backend needed `current_dir` and a conditional flag, not new filesystem logic.

## What changed

- **`Scope`** (`src-tauri/src/skills/scope.rs`) resolves an optional project path to a cwd and a CLI flag. `canonicalize` rejects deleted folders, normalises `..`, and resolves symlinks in one step.
- **`project_path: Option<String>`** on the eight scoped commands. Tauri deserialises an omitted key to `None`, so this is backward compatible.
- **Project registry** at `~/.curie/projects.json` — plain `std::fs` + `serde_json`, atomic write. Project paths are data, not UI preferences, so they do not belong in localStorage. The active scope is not persisted at all; the app opens global.
- **`/projects`** lists folders as cards with a skill summary, added through `tauri-plugin-dialog` (`dialog:allow-open` only).
- **Four guards against installing into the wrong place**, cheapest to most expensive to miss: a scope chip in the header, an accent hairline, a scope banner on the discovery pages, and `INSTALL → DON_CAMARON` on the button itself.
- **A staleness token in `loadSkills`.** Without it a slow global response resolving after a scope change paints global skills under a project breadcrumb, and the next remove-all targets the wrong scope.

## Verified

439 vitest, 68 rust, no warnings. The scoped path was exercised against the real CLI (`cargo run --example scope_probe`): a project with one skill reports `global: 0` / `project: 1, scope=project`, and a missing folder is rejected before anything runs. The staleness test was mutation-tested — it fails with the guard removed.

## Known limitation

**Update checking does not work in project scope.** The global lock is v3 with `skillFolderHash`; the project lock is v1 with `computedHash` — a different field with different semantics. Every project skill comes back `checkable: false`, so the UI shows nothing rather than something wrong. Fixing it means replicating the CLI's hashing.

## Also fixed in passing

- Three navigations dropped you back to global silently (`explore→find`, `find→marketplace`, the installed empty state).
- `remove.rs` fell back to the literal "Removed every global skill", a lie in project scope.

author: adithyan-ak
body:
## Summary

- make explicit-directory and configured no-path `rules validate` / `rules test` report per-file YAML load failures and exit nonzero while still processing valid siblings
- propagate parse, validation, and compilation failures retained by `Engine.LoadFailures()` through the command result
- reject fingerprint tar entries larger than 1 MiB instead of parsing a truncated prefix
- preserve intentional partial-bundle behavior so valid sibling entries still load
- add regression coverage for both command forms and exact/oversized archive boundaries

## Root cause

The explicit-directory loader printed parse errors but discarded their failure state, allowing the command to exit successfully. The initial fix preserved those failures for explicit directory arguments, but the documented no-path branch built the configured engine and discarded its retained `LoadFailures()`. Both command forms now feed load failures into the same reporting and exit-status path.

The tar loader used `io.LimitReader` at exactly 1 MiB and parsed whatever prefix it read, so a larger entry with a valid 1 MiB prefix could be accepted and executed.

## Impact

Rule validation and testing now produce truthful nonzero results for every candidate YAML that cannot be loaded, including rules discovered through `AGENTHOUND_RULES_DIR` or the default custom-rule directory. Oversized fingerprint entries are recorded through the existing partial-load failure channel and cannot enter the effective rule set.

## Validation

- retained mixed valid/malformed fixture: no-path `rules validate` and `rules test` both report `[FAIL]` and exit 1
- `go test ./collector/cli ./sdk/rules -race`
- `gofmt -l .`

- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./... -race`
- `golangci-lint run ./...`

Local `go-licenses` could not evaluate dependencies because the installed tool rejects Go 1.25 standard-library packages as lacking module metadata; this change adds no dependencies.

author: yitian-chen
body:
## 背景

PR #5 已合并到 master，但合并提交 `30b653d` 只包含到 `936e067`（坐标直传）为止，**缺少 force 模式修复** `8f873fa`。本 PR 补齐该修复。

## 问题

战术层 `sendIdleWait` 在队列空时发 60s `wait` 占用 UE busy guard，手动 `move_to` 等破坏性命令被 UE busy 拒绝：

```
HTTP 502 {"ok":false,"error":"ws.Call failed: action rejected: busy with Wait (1 game-min remaining)"}
```

## 方案

`handleDebugAction` force 模式（默认开启）依次执行：

1. 设 `agentContext.debugOverride=true` 暂停 worker dispatch（防止 stop 后 worker 立刻补新 idle wait 重新占用——关键竞态）
2. 对 `currentActionID` 发 `SendStopAction` 清 UE busy
3. 等 100ms 让 UE 处理 stop（fire-and-forget）
4. 发手动 action
5. defer 清 `debugOverride` 并 signal worker 恢复正常 dispatch

`debugOverride` 是必要的：没有它，stop 触发的 `action_completed` 会唤醒 worker，worker 在我们发手动 action 前就补一个 idle wait，重新 busy。

## 改动

- `main.go:57` 增加 `debugOverride` 字段；worker 循环检测到时 `continue`
- `main.go:1078` `handleDebugAction` 新增 `lookupAgent` 参数 + `Force *bool` 逻辑
- `web/debug.html` 增加 force 复选框（默认勾选）
- `docs/DebugAction_Tool.md` 新增 §3.2 `force` 字段说明
- 新增 2 个测试：`TestDebugActionRequest_ForceDefault`、`TestAgentContext_DebugOverrideLifecycle`

## 验证

- `go build ./...` 通过
- `go test ./...` 全部通过
- cherry-pick 自 `8f873fa`，无冲突

author: danybgoode
body:
## Why

**PR #119 shipped an endpoint that could not do its job.** Applied against production it returned `HTTP 400` for all 71 keys:

```
Cannot delete api keys that are not revoked - apk_01KRVSMVVM5PKSDZZ7G9VVJPR1, apk_01KSK11ADMKV2CXTGZ3MKPHPG1, …
```

**Nothing was deleted** — verified immediately after: still 72 keys / 70 dangling links. The module guard held, and the route surfaced the error rather than reporting success, so there is no partial state to unwind.

The more serious defect is the other one: **the dry run had confidently predicted `delete: 71`** — an outcome the apply could not deliver. A dry run that promises something the apply cannot do is a false green, and it is exactly the failure mode `AGENTS.md` rule 5 is about.

## The precondition, cited rather than paraphrased

`@medusajs/api-key/dist/services/api-key-module-service.js` → `deleteApiKeys_` rejects any key matching:

```js
$or: [ { revoked_at: { $eq: null } }, { revoked_at: { $gt: new Date() } } ]
```

Note it **compares** — a future-dated `revoked_at` still counts as unrevoked. Restating this as "has a `revoked_at`" would be a permissive fork of the real rule, which is the recurring defect in this codebase's history.

## What

1. **`isRevoked()`** mirrors that predicate exactly — null, future-dated, and unparseable all resolve to *not revoked* — with the source location in its comment.
2. **The plan carries it**: a per-key `revoked` flag and a plan-level `requires_revoke` count, so a dry run now states how many keys must be revoked before anything can be deleted.
3. **The apply path runs `revokeApiKeysWorkflow`** over the not-yet-revoked members of the DELETE set, then `deleteApiKeysWorkflow`. Only keys already destined for deletion are revoked — the kept storefront credential is never touched.

The two steps are **not atomic**, and the code says so: a failure between them leaves unused orphans revoked-but-present, and re-running completes the job because the second pass sees them already revoked. Those keys have no live sales-channel link by construction, so a revoked orphan is inert either way.

## Verification

Local gate green: build + `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` (**0 errors**) + `npm run test:unit` → **500/500 across 48 suites** (was 493 — 7 new).

**All 7 new specs observed RED via deliberate mutation**, covering: null treated as revoked, a null-check replacing the comparison (the permissive fork), the `<=` boundary, garbage input claiming revoked, `requires_revoke` counting outside the delete set, and the `revoked` flag hardcoded.

## Rollout

Merge → ~12 min deploy → dry run (expect `keep 1 / delete 71 / requires_revoke 71 / refuse null`) → apply → re-run `GET /internal/backfill-sales-channel` expecting `publishable_keys_skipped_links: 0` → storefront smoke against the pre-recorded baseline (home renders 16 distinct `/l/` listings, sample PDP 200).

Same review-axis gap as #119: orchestrator-authored and orchestrator-verified, no cross-family reviewer dispatched. Stated so it is not mistaken for a reviewed diff.

author: youknowone
body:
## What

Follow-up to #846. That slice hoisted the symmetric-difference merge loop into `set_symmetric_difference_storage` and, in doing so, dropped the `push_roots()` + `pin_root(d_new)` that the removed `pyre_object::setobject` helper carried.

`d_new` (the fresh result set from `w_set_new()`) is reachable only from the merge's Rust frame. The GC sees roots via the shadow stack only — the two operands are rooted through the interpreter frame, but `d_new` is not. A probe `eq_w` that triggers a collection therefore sweeps the in-progress result body; the next insert or the return then touches freed storage.

- interpreter path: `GC BUG: invalid type_id` crash
- JIT path: `AttributeError` type-confusion (freed storage reused)

Both reproduced on the merged slice, then fixed here.

## Fix

Wrap the merge in `push_roots()` and `pin_root(d_new)`. The set body is old-gen (non-moving) so it keeps its address across a collection — the pin prevents the sweep and needs no reload. `+7/-2` in `typedef.rs`; the traced-loop shape (matching `set_intersect_update`) is unchanged, so the census head stays retired.

## Why not re-residualize the helper

Restoring the deleted `#[dont_look_inside]` + `jit_fnaddr` helper (the #846-slice-1 pattern) **revives** the census head: the helper returns `Result<PyObjectRef, SetUpdateError>`, and the annotator cannot decode the custom enum across the residual boundary (`map_set_update_error() takes exactly 1 argument (0 given)`), regressing phaseA 321→322. Void residuals and null-niche `Option<PyObjectRef>` residuals cross the boundary; custom-enum-`Result` residuals do not. So the pin-only path is the census-clean fix.

## Test

Extends `set_symdiff_raising_eq.py` with:
- a `HashBoom` raising-`__hash__` case (the error must surface before any probe),
- return-type annotations on the `__hash__` methods,
- a `Collect` class whose `__eq__` runs `gc.collect()` — this is the pin guard; without the pin it crashes as above. The collect loop is kept small because a full collection per single-bucket probe is O(heap).

## Verification

- census A/B: head-neutral (phaseA 321 before ≡ 321 after; `comm` diff empty both ways)
- `check.py --backend dynasm,cranelift`: dynasm 326/326, cranelift 326/326, bit-exact
- `cargo test` pyre-object / majit-translate / pyre-interpreter (dynasm,host_env): green
- snippet passes under JIT, interpreter, and CPython oracle

Note: `set_intersect_update` shares the same live-read shape (a pre-existing class deviation, PyPy `_intersect_unwrapped` / `_symmetric_difference_unwrapped` both unerase once); restoring capture-once for both jointly is a separate follow-up, out of scope here.

author: alifzakuan
body:
Add dedicated device tree support for the Terasic DE-25 Nano board, which is based on Agilex5.

Following Terasic's Linux device tree for DE-25 Nano configuration in which UART and MMC mode differs from Altera SoCDK boards - enable UART1 instead of UARTT0 and using SDR50 instead of SDR104 mode for MMC. The device tree is also tweaked to enable the 16MB QSPI flash to store U-Boot image in a single partition for QSPI boot.

New files added:
- socfpga_agilex5_de25_nano.dts: Main device tree
- socfpga_agilex5_de25_nano-u-boot.dtsi: U-Boot specific additions
- configs/socfpga_agilex5_de25_nano_defconfig: Board configurations

Build system integration:
- Add build target in Makefile for DE25 Nano device tree binary file

Please do not submit a Pull Request via github.  Our project makes use of
mailing lists for patch submission and review.  For more details please
see https://u-boot.readthedocs.io/en/latest/develop/sending_patches.html

The only exception to this is in order to trigger a CI loop on Azure prior
to posting of patches.

author: janineteetz88-dev
body:
## Was

Root-Cause-Fix + Pipeline-Guard für den wiederholt live gerutschten Bug aus der Notion-Karte **„[Check][MITTEL] Interner Platzhaltertext 'Meta (für Blog-Engine & Freigabe)' live in Artikel-Meta + Blog-Kachel"** (mehrfach bestätigt in `blog/verben-mit-praeposition-franzoesisch/`, `blog/unregelmaessige-verben-franzoesisch/` u.a.).

**Root Cause:** `firstHeadIntro()` (`scripts/lib/notion-adapt.mjs`) dient als Fallback für die Meta-Description, wenn im Notion-Entwurf kein `Meta-Description:`-Bullet existiert. Die Funktion übersprang dabei zwar `Slug:`- und `Meta-Description:`-Zeilen, nicht aber ihre **eigene** `**Meta (für Blog-Engine & Freigabe)**`-Kopfzeile. Fehlte zusätzlich ein echter Intro-Absatz vor der H1, fiel die Funktion auf genau diese Kopfzeile zurück — der interne Platzhaltertext landete wörtlich in `meta[name=description]`, `og:description`, `twitter:description` und dem JSON-LD-`description`-Feld sowie in der Blog-Kachel-Vorschau.

**Fix:**
- `scripts/lib/notion-adapt.mjs`: `firstHeadIntro()` überspringt jetzt zusätzlich die Meta-Header-Zeile selbst (`isMetaHeaderText`-Check, dieselbe Funktion, die auch `blocksToMetaText()` zum Finden des Blocks nutzt).
- `scripts/lib/render-guard.mjs`: zwei neue **harte** Gates in `auditRenderedHtml()` — unconditional, unabhängig vom `STANDARD_LINT_STRICT`-Flag (das den Gold-Standard-Linter nur optional blockend schaltet). Diese Gates verhindern, dass die beiden bekannten Platzhalter-Leaks jemals wieder live gehen, egal über welchen Pfad sie entstehen:
  - `"Meta (für Blog-Engine"` irgendwo im HTML (deckt meta/og/twitter-description + JSON-LD in einem Rutsch ab)
  - `"Cover-Bild: beim Veröffentlichen"` im sichtbaren Fließtext (der zweite, mit derselben Ursachenklasse verwandte Fund aus der Karte — Editor-Hinweis statt echtem Cover-Bild)
  
  Das entspricht dem „Verschärften Vorschlag" auf der Notion-Karte: „einen Pipeline-Lint-Check ergänzen, der vor dem Publish-Schritt … prüft und den Build abbricht, statt live zu gehen." `auditRenderedHtml()` wird in `publish-from-notion.mjs` bereits genau so genutzt (kaputte Artikel werden nicht geschrieben) und läuft zusätzlich im CI-Pre-Deploy-Gate (`render-selftest.mjs`, `sync-notion.yml`).

**Out of scope (bewusst):** Die bereits live falsch gerenderten Artikel brauchen weiterhin eine echte, artikelspezifische Beschreibung in der Notion-Quelle — das ist ein Content-Fix in Notion, kein Code-Fix, und bleibt auf der Notion-Karte offen.

## Warum

Der Bug tritt laut Nightly-Check-Historie bei **jedem neuen Artikel** erneut auf, sobald die Notion-Quelle keinen echten Beschreibungstext liefert (zuletzt bestätigt 23.07.2026, neue Instanz). Kaputt sind dadurch: Google-Suchergebnis-Snippet, Social-Share-Vorschau (OG/Twitter), das strukturierte Datenschema und die Blog-Kachel für echte Nutzer. Der Guard verhindert jetzt strukturell, dass das nochmal passiert.

## Wie getestet

- `npm test` (39/39 grün) — inkl. 2 neuer Regressionstests in `scripts/lib/meta-block.test.mjs`: einer testet `firstHeadIntro()` direkt gegen die Bug-Situation, einer testet end-to-end über `blocksToMetaText()` + `parseMetaBlock()`.
- `node scripts/render-selftest.mjs` (CI-Pre-Deploy-Gate) grün — inkl. 2 neuer Guard-Selbstkontrollen, die verifizieren, dass `auditRenderedHtml()` beide Platzhalter-Muster tatsächlich erkennt.
- `node scripts/_preview/test-pipeline.mjs` zur Kontrolle mitlaufen lassen: 182/189 grün, dieselben 7 vorbestehenden (unrelated) Fehlschläge wie auf `main` vor diesem Branch (TL;DR→„Kurz gesagt"-Normalisierung, stale gegenüber der aktuellen „Das Wichtigste in Kürze"-Konvention — bestätigt per `git stash`-Vergleich, nicht Teil dieses Fixes).

author: ruvnet
body:
## Summary

Closes #1456 (follow-up documentation gap tracked from #1401). Two new operator-facing docs, both grounded in the actual Rust source (not ADR aspirational prose) — every specific number/threshold below is cited with a file:line and was spot-checked against source before this PR was opened.

### `docs/calibration-guide.md`
- The empty-room baseline has a **hard, enforced minimum of 600 frames** (`DEFAULT_MIN_FRAMES`, `wifi-densepose-signal/src/ruvsense/calibration.rs:48`) — `calibrate` fails outright below it, it doesn't degrade silently.
- Documents the real per-anchor quality gate thresholds used by `enroll` (`AnchorQualityGate`), and that `train-room` only requires a non-empty anchor list — a partial anchor set silently produces a bank missing whichever specialists lacked their prerequisite anchors.
- **Pets**: honest finding — `PresenceSpecialist` has no size/species discrimination at all, purely amplitude-variance/mean-shift thresholding. Documented as an open limitation, not glossed over.
- **Baseline conditions**: explains why a *steady* interferer (HVAC, fan) gets correctly absorbed into "empty" via Welford statistics, but also flags that ADR-135's described `drift_score`/`BaselineDrift` staleness system **does not exist in the actual code** — only a cruder `baseline_id`-mismatch check in `bank.rs` is real.

### `docs/trust-and-engine-errors.md`
- Traces `engine_error_count` and the separate, non-sticky `demoted` flag to their exact trigger conditions in `engine_bridge.rs` / `wifi-densepose-engine`.
- Confirms `/health/ready` and `/api/v1/status` share a handler and expose a `trust` block, but plainly states the real diagnostic gap: no per-cause error breakdown is exposed over the API — the rate-limited log line is the closest thing today.
- Documents the real recovery path for persistent clock-drift demotion (`WDP_GUARD_INTERVAL_US`, from issue #1049) and that `engine_error_count` has no reset besides a process restart.
- On the reporter's Hugging-Face-converted-model angle: states plainly that `--convert-model` and the engine/trust cycle are separate code paths with no call-through found — no invented causal link.

Both docs are added to the README documentation table.

## Test plan
- [x] Docs-only change — confirmed via `git status`/diff that nothing outside `docs/` and `README.md` was touched.
- [x] Spot-checked the load-bearing claims (`DEFAULT_MIN_FRAMES = 600`, `engine_error_count` increment/no-reset, `WDP_GUARD_INTERVAL_US`, `demote_one`/`self.demoted = trust.demoted`) directly against source before opening this PR.
- [ ] No code changes, so no test/build impact expected — CI should be green on docs alone.
