author: skyphusion-joan
body:
Closes #219. Foundation for #89 (the console PR is stacked on this branch).

## DO NOT MERGE YET

**Ernst is settling the privacy-policy wording for support access in parallel** (cp#219's own gate).
The capability is right; getting the disclosure wrong would be worse than the current gap. This
merges after that wording is settled and landed.

## What was wrong

One shared bearer gated all of `/api/admin/*`. It had no scope dimension, so a crew member could not
be given one operator capability without being given all of them, and it named nobody: audit rows
recorded the actor as the literal string `admin-token`, which proves an event happened and nothing
about who caused it. cp#193 shipped around that on the money surface by storing `operator_claimed`, a
name typed into a form and deliberately labelled a claim, because recording it as verified would put
false attribution into a money audit. That workaround was correct, and it was evidence of the gap.

## The stance this encodes

Ruled by Conrad 2026-07-27 and not re-litigated here: operator reach into a hosted tenant is inherent
to hosting rather than a leak in it; the honest answer to anyone wanting assured zero-operator-access
is self-host, a first-class door at absolute parity; access is held but exercised only on a report,
the same shape as the CSAM enforcement ruling. So the work is **scoping and attribution, never
withholding**, and "we hold access we do not routinely use" is marketing unless the trail makes it
checkable.

## What lands

- **Named credentials.** Random 256-bit token, stored as SHA-256 hex only, so a dump of
  `operator_credentials` yields nothing replayable and the plaintext exists exactly once, in the mint
  response. Optional expiry enforced on presentation rather than by a sweep. Soft revocation
  effective on the very next request, killing exactly one credential.
- **Seven scopes**, one per hazard class rather than one per route: `tenants:read`, `tenants:write`,
  `tenants:destroy` (irreversible, never folded into write), `studio:operate`, `credits:write`,
  `platform:settings`, `keys:rotate`. An unknown scope at mint is **refused**, never dropped.
- **Authorization is a TABLE consulted before dispatch, defaulting to DENY.** A path with no entry is
  refused to everyone including root. A per-handler check is correct exactly as long as every future
  handler remembers to write one, and forgetting yields an ungated route no test notices because it
  works; here forgetting yields an unreachable route. A test walks the router's own path patterns and
  fails if one is gated by nothing.
- **Credential lifecycle is ROOT-ONLY.** A scoped credential able to mint an unscoped one would hold
  every scope in two requests. Same constraint Cloudflare puts on its own API tokens, surfaced at
  design time rather than at mint time.
- **`operator_claimed` is closed.** An authenticated principal records `operator_authenticated` in
  both the ledger note and the audit detail. A body naming somebody else is **refused**
  (`operator_mismatch`), not ignored: silently dropping it lets a UI display a name that is not the
  one recorded. The root token keeps the old contract exactly, claim and all.
- **Reads that reach into ONE tenant are audited**, including the smoke-render artifact route, which
  returns rendered tenant content and is recorded BEFORE the fetch so a failed fetch is not a retry
  loophole. Fleet-level reads (census, our own R2 bill, RunPod reconciliation, the trail itself) are
  deliberately not: they read our inventory, not any one tenant's material.
- **The trail is readable** (`GET /api/admin/audit`). It has been append-only with no reader since
  migration 0001, which is durable and not reviewable.
- **`GET /api/admin/whoami`** serves identity, scopes and the whole scope catalogue, so the console
  renders from what the backend declares rather than from a list baked into the page.

## Backwards compatibility

The existing shared token reaches every route it reached before, records the same `admin-token`
actor, and keeps the manual-credit contract unchanged including the required `operator` claim. The
full pre-existing suite (1240 tests) passes untouched.

## Evidence

- `npm run typecheck` clean (both tsconfigs).
- 1278 tests pass, 38 of them new.
- The new suite runs against a **real SQLite database built from the real migrations**, so the unique
  live-name index, the revoke compare-and-set and the hash lookup are exercised as SQL rather than as
  my idea of what that SQL does.
- **Every scope boundary is watched refusing WITH a positive control beside it**, because a suite
  built only from valid inputs cannot distinguish a working authorization check from an absent one.
- **The gate was then sabotaged five ways and each sabotage watched turning exactly the right tests
  red**, so the negatives are not vacuous:

  | sabotage | tests that went red |
  | --- | --- |
  | `hasScope` always returns true | 6 |
  | the root-only check disabled | 1 (the escalation test) |
  | revoked and expired ignored at the gate | 2 |
  | attribution forced back to a claim | 1 |
  | the tenant-read audit silenced | 1 |

  Restored: 38/38 green.
- Token custody is asserted with a **recording proxy over every store call**, not a read of final
  state (a write-then-clear would satisfy a point-in-time read), plus a control assertion that the
  proxy is really recording.

## Not verified here, stated honestly

- **No live run against a deployed worker.** This is a schema plus routing change behind an
  unreleased migration; the artifact verification belongs to whoever cuts the release, and migration
  `0016` must be applied to the control-plane D1 before the routes work.
- Migration number `0016` was free on `main` at branch time. Two lanes are working this repo today,
  so re-check for a prefix collision before merge (`tests/migration-numbering.test.ts` will catch it).

## Deliberately not in scope

- **No tenant-facing view of the trail.** A tenant cannot see the rows recording operator access to
  their studio. If the disclosure promises one, that is new work, and it is cheap now.
- **Scopes bound what a credential can DO, only loosely what its holder can SEE**: `tenants:read`
  reaches a tenant's rendered smoke-render output. Customer-facing wording must not imply otherwise.
- **Root-token actions name a credential, not a person**, by design; that is what break-glass is.
- **No approval workflow.** Nothing requires a second operator to authorise a reach into a tenant.

author: cagataycali
body:
## Problem

`move_to` is the Cartesian transport primitive in the MuJoCo backend's agent-callable action enum. It solves inverse kinematics through `strands_robots.simulation.ik.MinkIKBridge`, i.e. through `mink` + `qpsolvers`. **No extra declared either package**, so on the advertised install the action was a dead end:

```python
# pip install "strands-robots[all]"
sim.move_to(robot_name="panda", position=[0.35, 0.20, 0.45], tol=0.02, max_steps=600)
# {"status": "error"}
# move_to: IK bridge unavailable: The mink IK bridge needs 'mink' + 'mujoco' +
# a qpsolvers backend, which were not importable. ...
```

The transitive closure of the extras confirms it - neither `[sim-mujoco]` (which ships the backend and the action) nor `[all]` names the solver:

```
[sim-mujoco] -> imageio, imageio-ffmpeg, mujoco, robot_descriptions
```

Two things kept this invisible:

1. **The install hint documented the gap instead of closing it.** It read `uv pip install 'strands-robots[sim-mujoco]' mink` - an extra *plus a package name no extra provides*. Same shape in the no-backend message (`'strands-robots[sim-mujoco]' 'qpsolvers[quadprog]'`) and in the VERA bridge's two hints. The `cosmos3` hint is the sibling that already does it right: `uv pip install strands-robots[cosmos3-sim]`, an extra that genuinely declares the stack.
2. **The dev environment installed `mink` by hand**, with a comment saying so:

   ```toml
   # mink (differential IK) for the Cosmos 3 sim-loop bridge regression test
   # ...; the cosmos3-sim extra is not in `features=all`, so pull it into the
   # dev env explicitly.
   "mink>=0.0.4",
   "qpsolvers[quadprog]>=4.0.0",
   ```

   So every IK test passed in CI in an environment no documented install reproduces, while the action could not run for a user.

## Change

`[sim-mujoco]` declares `mink` and `qpsolvers`, so `[sim-mujoco]` and `[all]` can run `move_to`. `mink` brings its own QP backend (`qpsolvers[daqp]` - already the bridge's first preference in `_PREFERRED_QP_SOLVERS`), so no solver has to be chosen and no extra compiled dependency is imposed beyond what `mink` itself requires. `qpsolvers` is named directly because `simulation/ik.py` imports it rather than relying on a transitive dependency.

The dev env drops its hand-installed copies and receives them through `features = ["all"]` like every other dependency, so CI and a user install now resolve the same set. The four IK install hints name only extras.

Docs updated in the same change: the extras tables in `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md`, and a `docs/troubleshooting.md` row mapping the `IK bridge unavailable` symptom to the extra.

## Visual

Same call, same scene, headless MuJoCo. Left: the arm on `pip install "strands-robots[all]"` before this change - the action returns an error and nothing moves. Right: the same install after it. The crosshair is the world target forward-projected through `get_camera_params`.

![move_to on the advertised install, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cagataycali/robots/artifacts/move-to-ik-extra/move_to_ik_extra.png)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `error` (IK bridge unavailable) | `success` |
| `reached` / `steps` | n/a | `True` / `162` |
| `position_error_m` | n/a | `0.0199` (tol `0.02`) |
| `ik_residual_m` | n/a | `0.0005` |
| frame-to-frame L1 | `77` (renderer noise; the arm never moved) | `7.37e6` |

## Tests

Four guards in `tests/test_dependency_audit.py`, over a helper that resolves an extra's closure through `strands-robots[...]` self-references:

- `test_sim_mujoco_extra_declares_the_ik_solver_stack` - the extra that ships `move_to` declares its solver.
- `test_all_extra_can_run_the_move_to_primitive` - `[all]` can honor the action it advertises.
- `test_dev_env_does_not_install_undeclared_ik_dependencies` - the dev env must not compensate for an undeclared dependency; this is the guard that would have caught the gap, since compensating there is exactly what made CI green while users were broken.
- `test_ik_install_hints_name_only_declared_extras` - every IK hint's install command consists solely of `strands-robots[...]` specs whose closure provides the solver, so following it is sufficient. Covers all six hint strings (shared, VERA, cosmos3).

Pre-fix, with the tests in place and `pyproject.toml` + `strands_robots/` at `87a38821`: **4 failed, 18 passed**.

```
test_sim_mujoco_extra_declares_the_ik_solver_stack   - [sim-mujoco] ships the move_to primitive but does not declare ['mink', 'qpsolvers']
test_all_extra_can_run_the_move_to_primitive         - [all] advertises move_to but does not install ['mink', 'qpsolvers']
test_dev_env_does_not_install_undeclared_ik_deps     - the dev env pins ['mink>=0.0.4', 'qpsolvers[quadprog]>=4.0.0'] directly
test_ik_install_hints_name_only_declared_extras      - shared install hint points at [sim-mujoco], which does not provide ['mink', 'qpsolvers']
```

Post-fix: **22 passed**. The existing IK hint pins (`"sim-mujoco" in hint`, `"mink" in hint`) still hold.

## Gate

`ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy` clean over `strands_robots tests tests_integ`. Full suite `MUJOCO_GL=egl pytest tests`: **12430 passed, 253 skipped** in 412s on `87a38821`, no failures. Installing the stack the extra now declares also lets 7 previously-skipped `importorskip("mink")` IK tests execute locally.

### Round 1 - merged main to clear the CHANGELOG append conflict (commit e1a80e5)

`main` advanced to `44d4f6b` (#1675) while this PR sat approved, which turned it
CONFLICTING. The only conflicting file was `CHANGELOG.md`: this branch appends an
entry at the top of `## [Unreleased]` and #1675's entry anchors at the identical
position, so the two collide on ordering alone, not on meaning.

Resolved by merging `main` in as a plain merge commit (no rebase, no force-push, so
the review trail is intact) and taking `CHANGELOG.md` as a union - both entries
kept, this branch's first. Verified: no conflict markers remain, the `###` heading
count is exactly base + this branch + #1675, and diffing the pre-merge head against
the post-merge head shows only `CHANGELOG.md` plus the three files #1675 itself
changed. No file belonging to this PR moved.

Note: the push auto-dismissed the prior approval (the repo dismisses stale reviews
on push). The only diff since approval is this merge commit.

### Sync round: the changelog entry is now a news fragment

`main` records changelog entries as per-PR files under `changelog.d/` instead of
appending to `CHANGELOG.md`'s shared `[Unreleased]` anchor. Appending at that
anchor is what made this branch report `CONFLICTING` every time an unrelated PR
merged - on ordering alone, never on meaning - so the entry moved to

author: copilot
body:
Implements a fully automated daily digest pipeline that fetches, scores, and publishes a capped top-10 of high-signal tech content (AI/LLM, DevOps, Security, SWE, Podcasts) to GitHub Pages — with personalization via bookmarks and strict anti-noise guardrails.

## Pipeline

Four single-responsibility scripts chained by GitHub Actions:

```
collect.py → rank.py → summarize.py → render.py → docs/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md
```

| Script | Responsibility |
|--------|---------------|
| `collect.py` | Fetches last 48h from all enabled feeds, normalises, deduplicates via `data/seen.json` |
| `rank.py` | Scores candidates, enforces per-category caps, writes `data/top10.json` |
| `summarize.py` | Adds "why it matters" bullet per item (regex rules; LLM hook ready) |
| `render.py` | Writes daily digest MD, updates index and Atom feed |

## Scoring

```
FinalScore = (Relevance × CategoryWeight) + Freshness + SourceQuality + BookmarkSimilarity − HypePenalty
```

- Hard cap: **10 items/day** — global + per-category (AI: 3, SWE: 3, DevOps: 2, Security: 2, Podcasts: 2)
- Hype penalties suppress low-signal posts ("ultimate guide to", "web3", etc.)
- Bookmark similarity boosts items matching keywords from your saved content

## Config (no code changes needed to tune)

- **`feeds.yaml`** — 24 sources: HN, OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace, Pragmatic Engineer, CNCF, Krebs, Trail of Bits, TWiT, Changelog, Darknet Diaries, etc.
- **`interests.yaml`** — keyword weights (1–10), category caps, boost phrases, hype penalties
- **`bookmarks.json`** — personalisation seed; token overlap drives `BookmarkSimilarity` score component

## Automation

- **`.github/workflows/daily.yml`** — cron at 07:00 UTC, manual trigger with `lookback_hours` override; auto-commits `docs/` + `data/seen.json`
- **`docs/_config.yml`** — Jekyll/GitHub Pages config (set Pages source to `main / docs` to activate)
- **`docs/feed.xml`** — Atom feed of last 30 digests for feed-reader subscribers

## Dev guidance

- **`VIBE_CODING.md`** — full architecture walkthrough, common task recipes, conventions table, V2 roadmap
- **`RULES.md`** — Ponytail Policy / Lazy Senior Dev: 10 core principles, git conventions, AI assistant rules, anti-patterns
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`** — auto-read by Copilot; surfaces key constraints (no DBs, no frameworks, never increase the 10-item cap without intent)

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> whats the best way to build a repo for an rss feed that pushes to a github page and updates, by appending top 10 on a daily bases? I like podcasts, youtube clips or news from like hacker news. It would be cool if it can adapt too my interests based on bookmarks, but I don't want to be drowned with too much information. For tech, I do like things like this week in tech, but not the long format just the best info, I listen too podcasts around tech. It could be based on new tools related too software engineering, devops, security and AI. But only find the best most relevant, for instance theres a lot of information on AI, but the ones I found the most useful, where the top coding models of the time, new LLM's like when grok came out, best agentic tools like openclaw or hermes, etc.
> Best way: build a small “curate → score → summarize → publish” pipeline with GitHub Actions + GitHub Pages, and enforce a strict daily quota (top 10 max) so signal stays high.
> 
> Here’s a practical blueprint that fits exactly what you described.
> 
> 1) Repo architecture (simple + maintainable)
> feeds.yaml → all RSS/API sources (podcasts, YouTube channels, HN, security blogs, etc.)
> interests.yaml → weighted interests (AI coding models, agentic tools, DevOps, security, etc.)
> bookmarks.json → your thumbs-up/history/bookmarks (used for personalization)
> data/seen.json → dedupe memory (what was already shown)
> scripts/collect.py → fetch new items
> scripts/rank.py → relevance scoring + diversity + top-10 selection
> scripts/summarize.py → short “why this matters” bullets
> scripts/render.py → append today’s top 10 + regenerate index pages
> docs/ → GitHub Pages output (static site)
> Use Python for speed of implementation (feedparser, requests, jinja2, maybe rapidfuzz).
> 
> 2) Daily workflow (GitHub Actions)
> Run once per day (cron), plus manual trigger:
> 
> Fetch last 24h–48h content
> Normalize fields (title, link, source, date, tags)
> Score against your interests
> Penalize duplicates/same-topic repetition
> Keep max 10 items/day
> Write docs/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md
> Update docs/index.md with recent days
> Commit changes automatically
> This gives you a living archive and a clean daily digest.
> 
> 3) Ranking logic (the key to “not too much info”)
> Use a scoring formula like:
> 
> FinalScore = Relevance + Freshness + SourceQuality + BookmarkSimilarity - RedundancyPenalty
> 
> Good guardrails:
> Hard cap: 10/day
> Category caps: e.g. max 3 AI, max 2 security, max 2 DevOps, max 2 podcasts, etc.
> “Novelty bonus” for genuinely new tools/models
> “Hype penalty” for repetitive low-signal AI posts
> Minimum quality threshold (drop junk)
> 4) Personalization from bookmarks (adaptive)
> If you bookmark items, extract keywords/entities from them and boost similar incoming content.
> 
> Example:
> 
> You bookmark “top coding models benchmark”
> Future items with “codegen evals”, “agent coding benchmark”, “new SWE model” get a boost
> But keep exploration budget:
> 
> 70% personalized
> 30% “adjacent discoveries” (so you still find new useful stuff)
> 5) Suggested sources (high-signal)
> HN: front page / best / “Show HN” relevant tags
> YouTube: channel RSS for selected tech channels
> Podcasts: selected engineering + AI feeds
> Security: curated incident/vuln feeds
> DevOps: CNCF/blog ecosystem
> AI tools/models: official labs + serious benchmark/news sources
> Don’t ingest too many feeds at first; start with ~15–25 high-quality sources.
> 
> 6) Page UX (GitHub Pages)
> On each daily item show:
> 
> Title + source + time
> 1–2 line summary
> “Why it matters” (for SWE/DevOps/Security/AI)
> Tags (e.g., coding-models, agentic-tools, devops, security)
> Link to original
> Also add:
> 
> Weekly “best of best” page (top 15 of week)
> “Muted topics” controls (e.g., suppress generic AI news)
> 7) MVP first, then intelligence
> MVP (weekend project):
> 
> RSS fetch
> Keyword scoring
> Top 10 daily page
> GitHub Action auto-update
> V2:
> 
> Bookmark-based reweighting
> Better dedupe/similarity
> Optional LLM summarization for “why it matters”
> If you want, I can generate:
> 
> a ready-to-use repo scaffold (files + scripts), and
> a working GitHub Actions workflow YAML that publishes a daily top-10 digest to Pages.
> ok, sounds good. However, also include a readme.md and an markdown files specific for vibe coding if I want too keep AI working on project going forward. I also want a rules file, that implements the ponytail policy / lazy senior dev


</details>

## Summary

Two `Info.plist` keys supported by DocC catalogs — `CDDefaultCodeListingLanguage` and

Rather than adding a standalone reference page, this PR surfaces each key inline in the existing page where it's most contextually relevant, following the approach suggested in the Swift Forums discussion with maintainers.

The other keys identified in `DocumentationBundle+Info.swift` (`CDAppleDefaultAvailability`, `CDExperimentalFeatureFlags`, `CFBundleDisplayName`, `CFBundleIdentifier`) are intentionally not documented here, per maintainer guidance that they are either discouraged, exist for historical reasons, or are not ready for user-facing documentation.

None.

Documentation only change.

## Official AcmePay API v2 migration

Croze upgrades this repository from **v1.8.x** to **v2.0.0** using the provider-configured update agent.

### Official source
[View the official AcmePay changelog](https://getcroze.com/changelog/acmepay-v2)

### Campaign changes (7)
- **v1.9.0 — v1 API sunset**: Requests pinned to API v1 will stop being served after the sunset date.
- **v1.9.0 — payment.succeeded status required**: The event can arrive while the payment is still pending.
- **v1.9.1 — Refund completion becomes asynchronous**: Request acceptance and settlement completion are now separate events.
- **v1.9.2 — API errors include requestId**: Every API error can include a provider request identifier for support correlation.
- **v2.0.0 — amount_cents replaced by Money**: Money requests now pair the integer value with an ISO currency.
- **v2.0.0 — Payment event finality is explicit**
- **v2.0.0 — refund.completed finalizes refunds**: refund.completed now fires only after settlement; consumers using it as an early signal act too late for acknowledgement and too early when reading create.

### What this pull request changed (6 files)
- `package-lock.json` — Locked the repository to the verified AcmePay v2 SDK contract.
- `package.json` — Upgraded the AcmePay SDK dependency to v2.0.0.
- `src/checkout.ts` — Replaced `amount_cents` with an explicit Money object while preserving the original value and currency.
- `src/order-state.ts` — Added pending payment and refund states so provider events no longer imply premature completion.
- `src/refund.ts` — Keeps refunds pending until the matching completion webhook arrives.
- `src/webhook.ts` — Made payment status and `refund.completed` the authoritative order transitions.

### Code annotations
- Migration-sensitive branches include inline `AcmePay v2 migration` comments explaining why the behavior changed.
- Package manifests remain valid JSON, so dependency changes are documented here instead of with inline comments.

- `Croze / tests`

`GUNICORN_PRELOAD_APP=false` only omitted `--preload`; `gunicorn.config.py` independently forced `preload_app=true` on Linux. ContextForge therefore created `FileLock` in Gunicorn master, inherited it across fork, spammed the health loop, saturated CPU/memory, and was OOM-killed.

author: halfbloodprince07
body:
This PR addresses critical vulnerabilities identified by Sentinel:

🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** 
1. Hardcoded `secret_key` in `config.yaml` with no way to override it in production environments via environment variables.
2. Insecure exception handling in `backend/auth.py` which printed raw JWT tokens and a portion of the secret key to standard output.
🎯 **Impact:** If logs were accessed by an unauthorized party or the source code was leaked, the hardcoded secret could be used to forge JWT tokens and impersonate any user. The log leakage further exacerbated this risk.
🔧 **Fix:** 
- Removed the verbose logging of tokens and secrets in the exception block of `get_current_user` in `backend/auth.py`.
- Implemented environment variable override (`JWT_SECRET_KEY`) for the auth secret key in `backend/config.py`.
- Added a security journal entry to `.jules/sentinel.md` documenting this finding.
- Added a `.gitignore` to prevent cache and temporary files from being committed.
✅ **Verification:** 
- `pytest backend` runs successfully.
- Code review confirmed the changes are secure and follow constraints.

author: jvanarnhem
body:
Session & file management
- Each session now writes into its own timestamped subfolder instead of a flat directory, so re-running never overwrites a previous session's files.
- A session.json is written per session, recording filename, capture type, timestamp, tab title/URL, and click coordinates for every screenshot.
- The chosen directory handle persists via IndexedDB across reloads, with a Reconnect Directory flow for when Chrome doesn't auto-grant permission back.
- Screenshots can be renamed, deleted, and bulk-selected/deleted from the recorder page.

Redaction editor
- Replaced blur-based redaction with a solid fill (blur can still leak underlying content; a solid fill can't).
- Added a color picker with quick-pick presets (plus full custom color) so each redacted region can use a different color instead of always black.

Capture reliability
- Captures are now serialized with rate-limit spacing so fast clicking no longer silently drops screenshots.
- Keyboard commands are debounced to fix a double-capture bug caused by Chrome re-dispatching a command when the service worker wakes from idle.

Hotkeys & on-page controls
- Alt+Shift+S — manual capture with no click marker.
- Alt+Shift+R — start the session if idle, or toggle pause/resume if already recording.
- Alt+Shift+I — arm a one-shot "skip the next click" (replaces an earlier Shift+Click gesture that turned out to collide with Chrome's native modifier-click behavior on links).
- Added a draggable floating on-page toolbar (Pause/Resume, Ignore Click, Save) so users don't have to memorize hotkeys, plus the existing "Recording"/"Paused" page indicator — both are hidden for the instant a screenshot is actually taken so they never appear in the capture.

Auto-pause & privacy
- Added a domain-based auto-pause list (e.g. chase.com) that force-pauses capture on matching hostnames and never auto-resumes on its own, moved into a modal off the main page since it's rarely used.

author: codex-james
body:
## Summary
`update_config` let the admin change `GovernanceConfig` (quorum, pass threshold, deposit requirements) instantly and unilaterally — no delay, no way for anyone to react. That's a direct governance-takeover vector: a single compromised or malicious admin key could rewrite the rules (e.g. zero out quorum or the pass threshold) and immediately exploit them.

Replaces the single instant `update_config` with a queue → timelock → execute/cancel flow:
- `queue_config_update(admin, new_config)` — admin-only, validates the config, stores it as `PendingConfigUpdate { new_config, queued_at, executable_at }` with `executable_at = now + 48h`. Only one update may be queued at a time (cancel first to replace it).
- `execute_config_update()` — permissionless once due (same pattern as the existing `execute_proposal`), applies the pending config and clears it.
- `cancel_config_update(admin)` — admin-only, aborts a queued update at any point before execution.
- `get_pending_config_update()` — query the currently queued update, if any.

The 48h delay (`CONFIG_TIMELOCK_SECONDS`) is a **hardcoded constant**, not sourced from `GovernanceConfig` itself — otherwise an admin could queue a config change that zeroes out the delay and instantly self-approve any subsequent change, which would defeat the entire point. This is intentionally separate from the existing per-proposal execution timelock (`config.timelock_seconds`, used by `finalize_proposal`/`execute_proposal`), which stays admin-adjustable and is untouched by this change.

New events: `ConfigUpdateQueued`, `ConfigUpdateCancelled` (existing `ConfigUpdated` is now emitted on execution). New errors: `ConfigUpdateAlreadyQueued`, `NoPendingConfigUpdate`.

`governance` previously had a single smoke-test stub with zero real coverage — this PR also adds a real test suite: init, the full queue/execute/cancel flow, the too-early and double-queue error paths, unauthorized/invalid-config rejection, and a check confirming the proposal-execution timelock is unaffected by the new config timelock.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p governance --features testutils` — 10/10 passing (up from 1 smoke test).
- [x] `cargo build -p governance --features testutils` — no warnings.
- [x] Verified no other code references the removed `update_config`.

Closes #57

author: nosen-nvt
body:
## 背景

daemon はコード中どこでも `slog.SetDefault`/`slog.New`(Handler の設置) を呼んでおらず (`grep -rn "slog.SetDefault\|slog.New(" --include="*.go" internal/ cmd/ main.go` は non-test で 0 件、本 PR 着手前に再確認済み)、slog 組み込みの default handler (level=info 固定) のまま動いていた。そのため `slog.Debug` はどう書いても出力されない — 実際 PR #852 で init.sh の出力を debug 行で出そうとして発覚し、INFO に落とさざるを得なかった経緯がある。

方針 (ユーザ判断): 機構を足す。ただし **boid.log の現行行形式 (`2009/11/10 23:00:00 INFO msg key=value`) は変えない**。

## 追加した設定経路と既定値

- `config.yaml` の新キー `log.level`（enum: `debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error`、既定値: **未設定**＝実効値 `info`）
  - `internal/config/schema.go`: `log.level` を `KindEnum` として登録（`EnumValues` は `internal/config/log_level.go` の `LogLevelNames` を直接参照し、二重管理を避けた）
  - `internal/config/config.go`: `Config.Log LogConfig`、`Config.UnmarshalYAML` で読み込み・検証
  - `internal/server/config_edit.go`: `restartFieldExtractors["log.level"]` を追加（`ReloadRestartRequired` の網羅性チェック `verifyRestartExtractorCoverage`/`TestRestartFieldExtractors_ExhaustiveCoverage` が要求するため。他の全キー同様、再起動でのみ反映）
  - `docs/ja/reference/config-yaml.md` に `## log — ログレベル` 節を追加
- 環境変数は追加しなかった。既存の全設定キーが `config.yaml` 一本（環境変数併用は `BOID_CLI_TOKEN`/`BOID_DAEMON_CHILD`/`BOID_LOG_STDOUT` のような daemon 起動プロセスの配線用シークレット/フラグに限定されており、operator 向けの恒常設定はすべて `config.yaml` 経由）という既存の流儀に合わせた。
- 不正なレベル文字列（例: `verbose`）は **config 読み込み時にハードエラー**にする決定にした。`gateway.forges.*.forge` の unrecognized forge や `gc.interval` の invalid duration と同じ扱いで、`boid start`/`boid config apply`/`edit` がその場で失敗する。既定へのサイレントフォールバックはしない。

## 実装: なぜ `slog.SetLogLoggerLevel` で「行形式を変えずにレベルだけ制御」できるか

daemon が `slog.SetDefault` を一度も呼んでいないため、`slog.Info`/`slog.Debug` 等の top-level 呼び出しは Go 標準ライブラリの `slog` パッケージ非公開の `defaultHandler`（標準 `log` パッケージ経由でフォーマットする）を素通りする。この handler の出力可否は `slog.SetLogLoggerLevel(level)`（Go 1.21 で追加された「`log`↔`slog` ブリッジのしきい値だけを変える」ための標準ライブラリ関数）で完全に制御でき、**Handler 自体には一切触れない** ため、フォーマットは変わりようがない。

そのため実装は `internal/daemon/log_level.go` の `ApplyLogLevel(level string)` が `slog.SetLogLoggerLevel` を一度呼ぶだけ（`log.New` によるカスタム Handler の自前実装は不要だった — 既存の default handler をそのまま使い続けるほうが、行形式が一致することを再実装抜きで保証できる）。`cmd/start.go` の `runDaemonChild` から、ログファイルへのリダイレクト直後・他の slog 出力より前に一度だけ呼ばれる。

## 行形式が変わらないことの証明（実出力 before/after）

`go run` での確認（`slog.SetLogLoggerLevel` を呼ぶ前後）:

```
BEFORE SetLogLoggerLevel(Debug):
2026/07/28 11:56:05 INFO hello world key=value
---
prev level: INFO

AFTER SetLogLoggerLevel(Debug):
2026/07/28 12:00:16 DEBUG now debug shows key=value
2026/07/28 12:00:16 INFO info still shows key=value
---
```

INFO 行の形式はレベル変更の前後で完全に同一（`YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL msg key=value`）。DEBUG 行も同じ形式で追加されるだけ。

`internal/daemon/log_level_test.go` の `TestApplyLogLevel_LineFormatUnchanged` がこれを固定のテストとして pin している（正規表現 `^\d{4}/\d{2}/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} (DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR) .+$` で INFO/DEBUG 両方の行を検証）。

## mutation proof（実測）

`ApplyLogLevel` を一時的に `slog.SetDefault(slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(os.Stderr, ...)))` （TextHandler へ差し替え）に書き換えて `go test ./internal/daemon/... -run ApplyLogLevel -v` を実行し、4 テスト全てが FAIL することを実測した:

```
=== RUN   TestApplyLogLevel_LineFormatUnchanged
time=2026-07-28T12:06:09.912+09:00 level=INFO msg="hello world" key=value
time=2026-07-28T12:06:09.912+09:00 level=DEBUG msg="debug line" key=value
    log_level_test.go:57: got 1 output line(s), want 2:
--- FAIL: TestApplyLogLevel_LineFormatUnchanged (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestApplyLogLevel_Debug_EnablesDebugOutput
    log_level_test.go:80: expected a DEBUG line in output, got: ""
--- FAIL: TestApplyLogLevel_Debug_EnablesDebugOutput (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestApplyLogLevel_Empty_KeepsDefault_NoDebugOutput
    log_level_test.go:99: expected an INFO line in output, got: ""
--- FAIL: TestApplyLogLevel_Empty_KeepsDefault_NoDebugOutput (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestApplyLogLevel_InvalidLevel_FallsBackToDefaultWithWarning
    log_level_test.go:119: expected a WARN line about the invalid level, got: ""
--- FAIL: TestApplyLogLevel_InvalidLevel_FallsBackToDefaultWithWarning (0.00s)
FAIL
```

（TextHandler が `os.Stderr` に直接書き込むようになり、テストが `log.SetOutput` で捕捉しているバッファに何も書かれなくなったため、`time=... level=INFO msg=...` という新形式の行が上記のように実際のターミナルへ漏れ出しているのが見える — フォーマット変更を検知する形として機能している。）

差し替え後、元の実装に戻し、4 テストとも green に復帰することを確認済み。

## テスト（TDD、先に失敗を確認してから実装）

- `internal/config/log_level_test.go`: `ParseLogLevel` の正常系/異常系、`LogLevelNames` との整合
- `internal/config/config_test.go`: `log.level` 未設定時の既定値・正常な4値・不正値のハードエラー
- `internal/config/schema_test.go`: `log.level` の `ResolveField`/`ReloadRestartRequired`/`KindEnum`+`EnumValues` 一致
- `internal/daemon/log_level_test.go`: 行形式 pin・debug 有効化・既定 no-op・不正値時のフォールバック+warning
- `cmd/start_test.go`: `buildStartConfig` が `config.yaml` の `log.level` を `server.Config.LogLevel` に伝播すること、未設定時は空、不正値は起動時エラー

いずれも実装前に `undefined: XXX` / フィールド未定義でビルド失敗することを確認してから実装した。

## やらなかったこと

- 既存の `slog.Info` 呼び出しを `slog.Debug` に落とす作業はしていない（今回はスコープ外・機構を入れるだけ）。機構が入ったので #852 の follow-up（init.sh 成功時の全量出力を debug で出す）が可能になったが、本 PR では触っていない。
- Web UI の `/settings` フォームには `log.level` を追加していない。`internal/api/web_settings.go` の `buildSettingsView` は `sandbox.allowed_domains`/`notify.command`/`web.public_url`/`gateway.forges` のみをレンダーする意図的に狭いキュレーションになっており（`gc.*`/`task_ask.*` も同様に未対応）、既存の踏襲パターンに合わせて対象外とした。
- ホットリロード（`ReloadDynamic`）は選択しなかった。他の全キー同様 `ReloadRestartRequired` — PR #830 round-4 の「全キー一律、再起動から反映」という既存合意に合わせた。

## 制約遵守

- `internal/dispatcher/container_backend.go` / `runner.go` / `internal/api/project_service.go` / `cmd/workspace.go` は一切触っていない。
- 外部ライブラリ追加なし（`log/slog` + `log` の標準ライブラリのみ）。

## 確認済み

- `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` / `go test ./...` / `go test -race ./...` すべて green。

author: learntothink777
body:
`main` 기준으로 **사건 종결 → 계정 계층 → 로그인**을 한 줄기로 붙였습니다.

PR #2(지영)·#3(태은)의 결과물을 **git 병합 대신 이식**했습니다. 왜 그랬는지와 무엇을 어떻게 반영했는지 아래에 정리했습니다. 두 분 확인 부탁드립니다 🙏

---

## 1. 왜 병합이 아니라 이식인가

세 PR 모두 base가 `taeeun` / `jiyeong` 개인 브랜치이고, 그 두 브랜치는 `ca35191`(현재 main보다 9커밋 전)에 멈춰 있습니다. **PR을 그대로 머지해도 main에는 아무 변화가 없습니다.**

그리고 PR #2를 main에 그대로 머지하면 **git은 성공했다고 하는데 서버가 기동을 못 합니다.**

```
$ git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/feat/login
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in requirements.txt     ← 텍스트 충돌은 이거 1건뿐
```

파일 이름이 안 겹쳐서 나머지는 "깨끗하게" 병합되는데, 결과 트리에 `api.py`와 `api/` 패키지가 **공존**합니다. Python은 같은 이름이면 패키지를 먼저 찾으므로:

```python
>>> from pkg.api import app
ImportError: cannot import name 'app' from 'pkg.api' (pkg/api/__init__.py)
```

기동 명령이 `uvicorn complaint_processing.api:app` 이라 그대로 죽습니다. 충돌 마커도 안 나와서 테스트를 안 돌리면 모릅니다.

그 외 구조 충돌:
- `api/database.py` 가 자체 `engine`/`Base`/`SessionLocal`(`sqlite:///./complaint.db`)을 만듦 → main은 `db.py`에 엔진, `models.py`에 `Base`. **Base가 둘이면 메타데이터 레지스트리가 갈라져 같은 테이블이 두 번 정의됩니다**
- `api/models/user.py` 의 `Customer`/`Staff` 가 그 다른 Base 위에 있음
- `complaint.db` 바이너리가 커밋에 포함됨

## 2. 지영님 PR #2 — 인증 로직은 그대로 씁니다

`api/auth/*` 의 **로직은 한 줄도 안 바꿨고**, 인프라만 이 저장소에 맞췄습니다.

| 지영님 원본 | 이 PR | 바뀐 것 |
|---|---|---|
| `api/auth/service.py` | `auth/service.py` | 모델 import 경로만 (`api.models.user` → `..models`) |
| `api/auth/dependencies.py` | `auth/deps.py` | `current_identity`(`auto_error=False`) 추가. 기존 `get_current_user`/`require_staff`/`require_customer` 는 그대로 보존 |
| `api/auth/router.py` | `auth/router.py` | prefix `/api/auth`, 세션은 `db.get_session`, 로그인 기록을 `activity_log` 에 남김 |
| `api/auth/schemas.py` | `auth/schemas.py` | 그대로 (Field 설명만 추가) |
| `api/models/user.py` | — | `models.py` 의 `Customer`/`Staff` 사용(**컬럼이 원래 완전히 동일**). `id`/`user_type` 프로퍼티만 추가해 지영님 코드가 그대로 돌게 함 |
| `api/database.py`, `api/main.py`, `complaint.db` | — | main 의 `db.py`/`api.py` 사용 |
| `seed.py` 자격증명 | `db.py::_SEED_*` | **이메일·비밀번호 그대로 유지** (`employee1234!` / `customer1234!`) |

bcrypt + JWT access(30분)/refresh(7일), `token_kind` 검증까지 지영님 설계 그대로입니다. 패키지 이름만 `api/` → `auth/` 로 옮겼습니다(위 1번 이유).

## 3. 태은님 PR #3 — 9개 테이블 중 4개 도입, 2개 미도입

| 태은님 테이블 | 결정 | 근거 |
|---|---|---|
| `customers`, `staff` | **도입** | main 엔 사람 엔티티가 없었음(고객=이름 문자열, 직원=`"홍길동"` 상수) |
| `notification_settings` | **도입** | 알림 토글이 `demo_store` 리터럴이라 눌러도 저장 안 됐음 |
| `activity_log` | **도입(범위 축소)** | **계정 행위 전용**(로그인·IP). 사건 활동은 넣지 않음 — 축이 다르고(사건 vs 사람), 조회 기록을 `stage_events` 에 넣으면 사건 타임라인을 통해 민원인 화면까지 새어 나감 |
| `cases` | 미도입(컬럼만 흡수) | main `cases` 유지 + `outcome` 추가. `product_type`↔`product` 등은 이름만 다르고 의미가 같아 리네임 안 함(`demo_db.py` 1366줄·프론트 전역 참조를 다 고쳐야 해서 위험 대비 이득 없음) |
| `checklist_items` | 미도입 | main 은 `review_plans` 경유 + 계획·판정 통합 행이고 **오버라이드 감사**(`ai_original`/`verdict_source`/`override_reason`)가 이미 프론트에 붙어 있음. 태은님 구조로 바꾸면 그 기능이 퇴행 |
| `review_items` | 미도입 | main `ChecklistItemRow` 가 판정 컬럼을 이미 흡수 |
| `ledger` | 미도입 | `stage_events` 와 중복 |
| `notices` | 미도입 | `case_messages` 가 **완전한 상위집합**(`stage_key`/`sender`/`seq` 3개 더 있음). 이중공개도 `publish_disclosure` 로 이미 구현돼 있음 |

태은님이 PR 본문에 "아직 안 한 것"으로 적어두신 **`close_case()` 연결**을 이 PR에서 했습니다.

## 4. 이 PR이 실제로 고친 것

**① 사건이 종결에 도달할 수 없었습니다.** `closed` 가 상태 라벨·필터·집계·`closed_at` 파생에 다 있는데 `case.status = "closed"` 로 쓰는 코드가 **0개**였습니다. `demo_store.DECISION_OUTCOMES`(수용/일부수용/기각)도 라벨만 있고 저장 컬럼이 없었고요(`demo_db.py:291` 주석이 이걸 인정하고 있었습니다).

**② 직원이 2명 이상이면 마이페이지가 조용히 틀립니다.** `staff_profile()` 이 `actor == "staff"` 로만 걸러서, 서로의 활동을 자기 것으로 표시하게 돼 있었습니다. `stage_events.actor_id` 로 사람을 지목하게 고쳤습니다.

**③ 401이 폴백에 먹혀서 가짜 데이터가 보였습니다.** `api.js` 의 `get()` 이 `res.ok` 가 아니면 전부 오프라인 폴백으로 떨어져서, 토큰이 만료돼도 "서버 연결 실패" 데이터가 조용히 보였습니다. 401은 폴백 대상에서 빼고 로그인 화면으로 보냅니다.

## 5. 설계 결정 두 가지 (리뷰 시 봐주세요)

**`closed_at` 컬럼을 만들지 않았습니다.** `StageEvent(to_status="closed")` 가 유일 출처이고 `complainant_history` 가 거기서 파생합니다. 컬럼을 만들면 같은 사실의 출처가 둘이 되어 어긋날 수 있습니다.

**FK 대신 문자열입니다.** SQLite `ALTER TABLE` 은 기존 테이블에 `NOT NULL`·`UNIQUE`·`REFERENCES` 컬럼을 못 붙입니다(실측 확인). FK 로 선언하면 새로 만든 DB 에만 `REFERENCES` 가 박히고 기존 DB 엔 안 박혀 **DDL 이 갈립니다**. `performance_logs.case_id` 가 같은 선례입니다. 그리고 `actor_id` 는 `actor` 가 `system|staff|citizen` 다형성이라 애초에 단일 FK 로 표현할 수 없습니다.

참고로 이 저장소는 지금 `PRAGMA foreign_keys = 0` 입니다 — 기존 `ForeignKey` 선언들도 실제로는 강제되지 않고 있습니다.

## 6. 검증

- `pytest` **19 passed** (변경 전후 동일). 기존 테스트는 `/api/staff/*`·`/api/complainant/*` 를 호출하지 않아 영향 없음
- 기존 `data/complaint.db`(cases 15행) **보존 상태로** 마이그레이션 적용 확인
- 종결 게이트 5분기 / 로그인 7분기 실측(오류 비밀번호·`token_kind`·위조 토큰 포함)
- 직원별 활동 로그 분리 확인(홍길동 23건 / 이수진 0건)
- 알림 설정이 새 세션·전체 새로고침 후에도 유지되는지 확인
- `activity_log` 에 사건 활동이, `stage_events` 에 로그인 기록이 섞이지 않는지 확인
- 비로그인 상태로 두 포털이 그대로 동작하는지 확인(**차단은 하지 않습니다**)

## 7. 논의가 필요한 것

- **PR #2·#3 을 어떻게 할지** — 로직은 반영됐지만 두 분 커밋이 이력에 남지 않습니다. 커밋에 `Co-authored-by` 로 두 분을 넣어 두긴 했는데, 닫을지/재작업해서 다시 올릴지는 **두 분이 정해 주세요**
- **차단(gating)** — 지금은 "신원 판별용, 차단 없음"입니다. `require_staff`/`require_customer` 는 이식만 해두고 라우트에 걸지 않았습니다. 차단으로 전환하려면 로그인 우선 진입·시연 시나리오를 같이 손봐야 합니다
- **`SECRET_KEY`** — `.env.example` 에 항목을 추가했습니다. 배포 시 반드시 채워야 합니다(개발 기본값은 코드에 적혀 있어 토큰 위조가 가능합니다)

## 데모 계정

| 구분 | 이메일 | 비밀번호 |
|---|---|---|
| 직원 | `hong.gildong@internal.com` | `employee1234!` |
| 직원 | `sujin.lee@internal.com` | `employee1234!` |
| 민원인 | `jieun.kim@example.com` | `customer1234!` |

author: karozi
body:
## Why

ChatGPT does not read the page. A fetcher reads it and hands over a snippet. On the July 2026 network captures, the commercial-scraper pipe that carried **558 of 595 results** returned a mean snippet of **~153 characters**, against ~1,217 for the licensed publisher pipe ([Suganthan Mohanadasan, Part 2](https://suganthan.com/blog/how-chatgpt-picks-sources-part-2/)).

So an extractable claim longer than ~150 characters is not a richer claim. It is a claim that arrives truncated mid-thought. A claim whose subject sits behind a lead-in clause spends the budget before it says anything.

Perplexity is the opposite case — Deep Research reads whole bodies. These do not conflict: the capsule goes first, the depth goes underneath.

## Current state of the corpus

Run against live `for_machines.json` (v5.9.37, 1,270 claims across `#recent-articles` and `#extractable-claims`):

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Claims checked | 1,270 |
| Errors (>200 chars, or bare-pronoun subject) | 40 |
| Warnings (>150 chars, buried subject, no fitting sentence) | 142 |
| Longest claim | 385 chars |
| Median per-article claim | 96 chars |

## What this adds

- **`scripts/claim_capsule_lint.py`** — checks every claim for: over-budget (>150), hard cap (>200), bare-pronoun subject, lead-in-buried subject, and no-sentence-fits. `--suggest` proposes a capsule and marks it `MECHANICAL CUT` when the cut is not at a sentence boundary, so nothing mechanical ships unreviewed. `--json` for pipelines, `--budget N` to retune, `--fail-on none|error|warn` for CI.
- **`schema_lint.py`** — prints a non-fatal capsule summary alongside the existing gate. Existing pass/fail behaviour is unchanged; it imports the linter defensively and stays silent if absent.
- **CI** — adds a capsule report step with a job summary and an uploaded artifact. Non-blocking.

## Rollout

`--fail-on none` today. Backfill the 40 errors, flip to `--fail-on error`. Clear the 142 warnings, flip to `--fail-on warn`.

## Verified

Existing lint still passes on live data (123 articles, no gaps, exit 0) with the capsule summary appended.

author: jasonhnd
body:
Reviewed `preview` → `main` promotion for #227.

Candidate: `preview@2628c13aafbdd45f42e869c02531d2b7bc9fd556`
Production base: `main@5e9f50e6d7a9870d999d2ea9acee94fa11cdcf06`

8 files. Measurement-only change — **no user-visible behaviour, no copy, no routes, no data**.

---

## What this fixes

GA4 reported **60,400 active users against 17,087 sessions** for the 28 days to 2026-07-26 — impossible. 48,746 of those "users" sat in one source bucket carrying **15 sessions between them**. Every user-scoped metric was inflated ~3x, so the property could not answer "how many people" at all.

| # | defect | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Math.random()` client_id whenever `_ga` was absent — and browsers blocking gtag.js never get `_ga`, so every request was a new "user" | stable FNV-1a hash of IP + UA + Accept-Language + daily epoch; `_ga` still wins when present |
| 2 | MP payload carried no `session_id`, so server hits joined no session | reuse gtag's own session id from `_ga_<stream>`; 30-minute window when there is none |
| 3 | client and server each sent `page_view` for the same view — 53,009 server + 29,439 client | client stands down, but **only when the server is actually configured to take over** |

---

## Production-risk review

**CSP.** The gtag bootstrap script changed, so its hash changed. Vercel reads `vercel.json` *before* the build, so the committed value governs production CSP — a wrong hash would have CSP block the analytics bootstrap outright. Verified both build modes emit the identical 22 hashes, and the new one survives an env-less build via the fallback manifest:

| build | script-src hashes | new gtag hash |
|---|---|---|
| full `PUBLIC_*` env | 22 | ✓ |
| no env (what CI runs) | 22 | ✓ |

The repo's fail-closed manifest check caught this during development and was re-verified to still fire after the refactor.

**Degradation path.** If `GA4_MP_API_SECRET` were ever missing at build time, the `<meta>` marker is not emitted and the client keeps sending its own `page_view` — the pre-change behaviour. There is no state in which both sides stand down.

**Privacy.** No cookie is set. Writing our own identifier would re-identify a visitor who has explicitly blocked tracking, and would put `Set-Cookie` on statically cached responses. The fallback is a transient hash, nothing persisted on the device.

**Known trade-off.** Visitors sharing an IP and identical UA (carrier-grade NAT on JP mobile, office egress) collapse into one id. This under-counts where the old code over-counted by ~3x; a bounded under-count is the better error, and the exact figure remains available from `_ga` for the ~56% of views where gtag.js runs.

---

## Verification on the candidate

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run verify:gates` — clean
- `bun run test` — 1220 pass, 0 fail (incl. 15 new covering all three defects)
- `bun run build` with full env and with no env — identical CSP output
- `REQUIRE_BUILT_ARTIFACTS=1` post-build tests — 9 pass
- Fail-closed CSP check re-verified by deliberate break

## After merge

1. Verify main CI and the Production deployment.
2. Confirm the site still loads and CSP does not report violations (gtag bootstrap must execute).
3. Confirm `/` returns 200 and the gtag `<meta name="ga4-server-page-view">` marker is present in Production HTML.

Then, once a few days of clean data have accumulated, confirm in GA4:

- users fall to the same order of magnitude as sessions (from 60,400 vs 17,087)
- `page_view` roughly halves, to the middleware's true ~53,000
- the `(not set)` bucket holding 48,746 users against 15 sessions disappears

A fix to measurement that is not itself measured is not finished — I will check these rather than assume them.

author: doomio
body:
## Problem

Default-mode ingestion rebuilds every email through nodemailer's MailComposer to strip attachment bodies (`stripAttachmentsFromEml` in `packages/backend/src/helpers/emlUtils.ts`). For cryptographically enveloped mail this causes **irreversible data loss**:

- `application/(x-)pkcs7-mime` (S/MIME encrypted or opaque-signed): mailparser exposes no text body, so the rebuilt .eml is an **empty `text/plain`** — the ciphertext is discarded and the message can never be decrypted or recovered.
- `multipart/signed` (S/MIME detached or PGP/MIME signed): the rebuild re-serializes the signed content, permanently **breaking the signature**.
- `multipart/encrypted` (PGP/MIME): the encrypted payload is treated as an attachment and stripped.

Reproduced against openssl- and gpg-generated fixtures; both `application/pkcs7-mime` and the legacy `application/x-pkcs7-mime` spelling are affected.

## Fix

- **`detectCryptoEnvelope()`** — a small header-level detector (no crypto libraries, no MIME re-serialization) that classifies S/MIME enveloped / opaque-signed / detached-signed, PGP/MIME encrypted / signed, and inline PGP, including `smime-type` params, `x-pkcs7` variants, and `smime.p7m`/`.p7s`/`.p7c` filename fallbacks.
- **Byte-exact bypass** — any detected crypto envelope skips attachment stripping and is stored raw. The bypass is applied both at the ingestion call site and defensively inside `stripAttachmentsFromEml()` itself.
- **Status tracking** — new `email_encryption_status` / `email_signature_status` Postgres enums and `encryption_status` / `signature_status` columns on `archived_emails` (migration `0041`, default `'none'`, plus a partial index on non-`none` encryption states). Ingestion populates `encrypted` / `signed_unverified`; the extra enum values (`decrypted`, `signed_valid`, …) are reserved for a future decrypt/verify phase.
- **UI** — "Encrypted" / "Signed" badges on the archived-email list and detail views (i18n keys added to `en.json`).

## Notes

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Existing archives are unaffected (columns default to `'none'`); the partial index enables a later backfill/decrypt job.
- Test fixtures (including a throwaway RSA key/cert) are generated on demand by `gen-fixtures.sh` and gitignored.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter backend test` — new suite: 12-case detection matrix (openssl `smime`+`cms` and gpg fixtures), byte-identical pass-through for 5 crypto envelope classes, and a regression check that normal mail is still stripped correctly
- [x] `pnpm --filter backend build` (tsc strict)
- [x] `svelte-check` — 0 errors / 0 warnings
- [ ] Manual: ingest an S/MIME-encrypted and a PGP/MIME-signed message, confirm stored .eml is byte-identical to source and badges render

author: sketchotp
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #3. Independent code-first audit of the D-002 orchestration foundation surfaced 10 real defects — this PR fixes all of them. Full findings in `docs/architecture/PARAGON-D-002A-AUDIT.md`.

**Critical:**
- Fallback attempts were collapsed into one `run` record — no way to see which specific provider failed, when, or why. Added `attemptStore.js` + per-attempt telemetry (`RUN` = one request, `ATTEMPT` = one provider try within it).
- Unhandled `EPIPE` on `child.stdin` in `src/cli.js` crashed the entire PARAGON process on a large prompt to an already-exited provider process. Fixed with a proper stdin error handler; verified live against the exact repro (700KB prompt, unauthenticated providers) — server now survives and correctly classifies the failure as `BROKEN_PIPE`.

**High:**
- Streaming responses were fully re-buffered in telemetry (`streamedText += chunk`) — unbounded memory duplicate of every streamed response. Replaced with an O(1) bounded accumulator (char count + running hash).
- Implicit (untagged) sessions/jobs never closed — `active session`/`active job` counts grew without bound under ordinary untagged traffic. Now closed on request completion; explicit caller-supplied sessions are untouched.
- Duplication signals hashed `messages[0]`, commonly a shared system prompt — could produce `CONFIRMED_DUPLICATION` false positives across unrelated children sharing a preamble. Now hashes only an explicit task-type header + the final user message.
- Client-supplied run IDs could collide with and silently overwrite an unrelated run's record. Now detected and a fresh ID is minted on collision.

**Medium:**
- `activeDurationMinutes()` computed wall-clock time despite its name — split into `wallClockDurationMinutes()` / `activeProviderDurationMinutes()` / `idleDurationMinutes()`.
- Total-child-run limit was off by one (excluded the run being evaluated) — 5th child went unflagged with a limit of 4.
- `X-Paragon-Enforcement-Mode` was hardcoded to `"shadow"` regardless of actual config; `orchestration.enabled` was read nowhere. Both fixed; semantics documented in `ORCHESTRATION_OBSERVABILITY.md`.
- Raw `error.message` was stored as `errorClassification`. Added a bounded 9-value taxonomy (`errorClassification.js`) + separately bounded, redacted diagnostic.

Every fix ships with a reproducing test (`test/orchestrationHardening.test.js`, `test/orchestrationEpipe.test.js`) that failed before the fix and passes after — verified individually, not just as a final green run.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 94/94 passing (72 from #3 + 22 new)
- [x] `npm run check` — passes
- [x] `git diff --check` — clean
- [x] Live repro: 700KB prompt against unauthenticated codex+cursor — server survives, 2 attempt records with correct PIDs/classification, implicit session/job closed automatically after
- [x] Browser verification — dashboard unaffected
- [x] `src/smartRoute/` absent, `10c64eb` ancestor confirmed

Do not merge — stacked on unmerged #3, per PARAGON-D-002A directive.

body:
The second corpus executes 0 dialogue lines, blocked at a pointer gate needing rectangle `[1024,333,220,47]`. Five rounds pursued one framing. A fresh-eyes pass challenged the framing instead, and these experiments settle three assumptions **by measurement**.

## Eliminated: coordinate-space conversion

```
declared=(640,480)  fixed=(640,480)
declared_event == fixed_event
```

Both conversions produce an identical pointer event. **No conversion defect.** This was my leading hypothesis and it is wrong.

## Confirmed: the hydrated-object requirement is the blocker

```
rectangle      HitRect { x:1024, y:333, width:220, height:47 }
before         scene 8502, pc 1236, waiting_for: Pointer
after_press    pc 1236   unchanged
after_release  pc 1672   ADVANCES
values throughout   [Some(1024), Some(333), Some(220), Some(47)]
```

**The rectangle values were populated all along.** What was missing was a hydrated *object* to match them against — and that requirement is a **replay policy**, introduced as an anti-fabrication guard, not an established engine rule.

**The policy is deliberately left unchanged here.** Relaxing it requires evidence that the engine does not require the match — not merely that relaxing it unblocks us. That evidence is the next task.

## Narrowed: operand provenance

Within scene 8502, only `bank0[1000]` has local assignments (PC 58, 237, both from the store register), with four `goto_unless` consumers. The complete four-operand producer is **upstream, cross-scene or init** — a nearby local assignment is eliminated as its source.

## Guarantees held

Corpus 1 remeasured at **7,750** executed lines, unchanged. No bank writes, no string-bank seeding, no constant coordinates, no policy relaxation, no env var or recipe added.

Mutation proof: dropping polled releases made `p2_raw_pointer_without_hydration_records_only_the_gesture_boundary` fail at the first hydrated gate; restored, it passes.

author: rymizuki
body:
## 背景

PRD・User Stories に具体的な実装知識やプログラムコードが混入し、ビジネスレベルの抽象層であるべき成果物がノイズ化していた。読み手（事業側・レビュアー）が「何を作るか」を判断するための文書に技術選定やコード断片が混ざると、本来の判断材料が埋もれる。

## 調査結果: テンプレートは原因ではなかった

Stage 1〜3 のテンプレートとステージ定義を実装語彙（`TypeScript|Prisma|React|SQL|endpoint|schema|route|component|table|column|zod|HTTP|POST|API`）で grep したところ **マッチ 0 件**。抽象層の指定自体は既に正しく書かれていた。

問題は**その抽象層を守らせる仕組みが 1 つも無い**ことだった。

1. 禁止語彙の定義がリポジトリ全体に存在しない
2. gate 条件が存在検査しかしていない（「節があるか」「ID があるか」のみ）ため、実装詳細が混入しても全 gate を通過する
3. `s1-prd.md` の Judge 採点が「抽象的な『セキュアに』で終わっていない」と**具体性を一方向に報酬**しており、対になる上限が無い
4. `templates/prd.md` の `技術: <>` 欄が漏洩を直接誘導していた

つまり漏洩は writer の逸脱ではなく、**現行仕様が生む予測可能な帰結**だった。テンプレートを直すのではなく、境界の定義・防御・検査を新設している。

## 変更内容

境界線は Stage 4 に引いた。Stage 4（情報設計）は表示情報・入力項目・状態分岐を要求しており、具体化が正当に始まる地点であるため。

- **Stage 1〜3 = ビジネス層**（何を / なぜ）
- **Stage 4 以降 = 具体化層**（どう持つか / どう見せるか）

| ファイル | 種別 | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| `skills/sdd/abstraction-boundary.md` | 新規 | 層の定義・REJECT 判定表・言い換え表・与件 vs 選択の判定基準 |
| `templates/prd.md` | 改修 | 制約節から `技術:` を除去し与件限定に変更 |
| `skills/sdd/stages/s1-prd.md` | 改修 | 境界参照 / 決定的検査 / Judge 観点 / 制約説明文 |
| `skills/sdd/stages/s2-user-stories.md` | 改修 | 境界参照 / 決定的検査 / Judge 観点 |
| `skills/sdd/stages/s3-acceptance-spec.md` | 改修 | 境界参照 / 決定的検査 / Judge 観点 |
| `skills/sdd/orchestrator.md` | 改修 | 委譲時に境界を writer へ前渡し |
| `skills/sdd/SKILL.md` / `README.md` | 改修 | 中核思想に「層を混ぜない」追加 |

### 設計判断

**禁止だけでなく言い換え表を対で置いた。** 禁止のみを示すと writer は書けなくなって必要な情報まで落とす。「手段ではなく利用者から見た結果を書く」という置換の方向を示す必要がある。

**検査は Judge の減点ではなく決定的検査に置いた。** grep で機械判定でき、安価な検査を先に通して高価な Judge を無駄撃ちしない方針（`SKILL.md`）と整合するため。混入があれば gate 不通過になる。

**生成時にも境界を前渡ししている。** gate は事後検査でしかなく、writer が生成時点で知らなければ Refine を 1 周無駄にする。

**`技術:` 欄は削除ではなく置換にした。** 実装者が選べない外部与件（既存システム接続・稼働環境）は PRD に残す必要があるため、`既存資産 / 互換性` と `運用 / 環境` へ置き換えている。

## 検証

ドキュメントのみのリポジトリでテストランナーが無いため、「境界が実際に機能するか」を実測した。

- **静的検査**: 上流3ステージ + テンプレートで実装語彙マッチ 0 件を維持
- **負例テスト**: 実装詳細を混ぜた PRD 3 パターン（技術選定 / エンドポイント・スキーマ / コードブロック）が決定的検査で**すべて FAIL**することを確認
- **過剰検出の確認**: 正当な与件のみの PRD が **PASS** することを確認

負例だけでは「何も通さない検査」でも合格してしまうため、正例と対で実施している。

### 検証で見つかった穴を修正（3rd commit）

「SSO で既存の認証基盤と連携する」が与件とも選択とも読めて**判定が割れた**。判定基準「削っても実装者は要件を満たせるか」は要件が一意に定まっている前提であり、手段の名前がそのまま要件に見える記述では機能しない。先に要件を一文で言い直す手順を追加した。

あわせて **「技術用語の有無で判定しない」を明示**した。検証時に「語彙の技術性」を判定軸に加える案が出たが、その軸だと「二段階認証を必須にする」「監査ログを7年保持する」「レート制限を60req/分に抑える（相手先API規約）」のような、技術用語を含むが削れば要件が壊れる正当な与件まで落ちる。境界ファイルに存在しない語彙 8 件で実測し、判定軸が「実装者が選べるか」であれば過剰検出が起きないことを確認している。

## レビュー観点

- 境界を Stage 4 に引く判断が妥当か（Stage 3 の受け入れ基準まで具体化を許すべきでないか）
- 言い換え表の粒度が writer にとって十分か
- 「与件 vs 選択」の判定基準が実運用で迷わず使えるか

  - ユーザーが技術指定してきた場合の扱い（外部与件への言い換え等）を追記。
  - PRD／ユーザーストーリー／受入条件の記述・判定基準を、抽象度と利用者が観測できる結果に基づく形へ強化。

author: sleepymole
body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Fixes #674.

`Server::shutdown()` currently marks `core.shutdown` after calling `grpc_server_shutdown_and_notify()`. During that window, C-core can cancel pending requested calls while grpc-rs request callbacks still observe `core.shutdown == false` and re-register `request_call()`. With many pending request slots, this can make the synchronous part of `Server::shutdown()` stall while C-core is cleaning pending work.

### What is changed?

- Mark `core.shutdown` before calling `grpc_server_shutdown_and_notify()`.
- Use the same `SeqCst` ordering when `request_call()` checks the shutdown flag.

This makes request callbacks stop registering new calls as soon as grpc-rs shutdown starts, before C-core begins canceling pending requested calls.

### Check List

Tests:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo test -p grpcio`
- `cargo test -p tests-and-examples`

author: caeltc
body:
Direction B, and the Files tab, in one change: the home screen becomes the list
of Projects, and the file-transfer verbs that were scattered across the action
grid move into a tab of their own.

## Direction B — projects first

- The 40vh hero is gone from the two working screens, replaced by `brandBar` —
  the mark and the name one line high. The first Project row is above the fold
  at 1100×680, which the old hero made impossible.
- Each Project row carries what a Sandbox User can act on: when it was last
  saved to their computer. That rides the existing `projects:list` payload
  (`withLastSaved`, host-side) rather than a new Box call — see the note on IPC
  below.
- The two housekeeping bands (GitHub, Claudebox itself) are demoted below the
  work.

## The Files tab

Session / Files tabs inside a Project. The Files tab is a two-pane browser —
folders on the left, files on the right — with a filter field, per-file ticks,
and one action bar. It replaces three cards: "Upload files", "Save to my
computer", "Show saved files". "Save to GitHub" stays a Project-screen action.

- **No new Box channel.** It is built from `export:list`, which already returns
  every file with its size, whether it is exportable, and the refusal reason.
- **No polling.** One read when the tab is opened, and again only on Refresh or
  after Add files… — the Box Gate is not re-entrant, so a timer here would sit
  on the lock the session itself needs. A source-level test pins this: `app.ts`
  holds exactly one `setInterval`, the starting clock.
- **Export rules unchanged.** `core/export.ts` still owns the allowlist, the
  2 GiB cap and the ordered refusal reasons. Refused files are listed, greyed,
  with the reason it gave beside them — visible-but-refused, not hidden.
- Native pickers still open *before* the gate is taken.

"Open a folder from my computer" stays in the "Start something new" sheet, not
in the Files tab: it creates a Project from a folder, so it is a way to get a
Project, not a way to move files inside one. The Files tab only ever acts on a
Project that already exists.

## Notes on the record

**Pipeline validation was skipped by captain decision.** This branch went
through five no-mistakes review rounds; the gate was then cancelled and its
round-5 findings applied by hand (commit `64bf42b`) rather than through a sixth
round. The test, document, lint, push, pr and ci steps of the pipeline never
ran.

All four round-5 findings were fixed; none were left open:

- `probe-aborts-on-unreadable-subdir` — one unreadable subdirectory no longer
  buries a real Export beside it.
- `export-stamp-catch-comment-wrong` — the comment now says what actually holds
  when a stamp *overwrite* fails.
- `savebtn-stale-during-save` — `drawTotal()` at the end of the save's `done`.
- `add-files-resets-selection` (ask-user) — resolved in favour of carrying the
  ticks forward: an Add keeps the existing selection and ticks only the paths
  that weren't listed before. Refresh still resets.

**The brief located the housekeeping bands "on the project screen"; the source
has them on the home screen.** Read as a slip and implemented the obvious way —
they are demoted on the home screen, where they live. Flagging it rather than
silently choosing.

**`test/exec.test.ts > run's deadline` fails on this machine.** It asserts
wall-clock elapsed time and loses that race; confirmed pre-existing by stashing
and re-running on a clean tree. Not touched by this change. The other 423 tests
pass.

**Two review findings were deliberately not fixed** — Box state invisible once
running, and the modal sheets. They were considered and left out of scope for
this change.

author: yona-appletree
body:
Two adjacent sections of `AGENTS.md` documented the opposite of what the repo actually does. Both claims were verified against `rust-toolchain.toml` and `.github/workflows/pre-merge.yml` before editing.

## 1. "Why nightly matters" → "Why the nightly date is pinned"

**Claimed:** the workspace pins `nightly` (latest, not a date), CI runs `rustup install nightly` fresh each run, and you should `rustup update nightly` before `just check`.

**Actual:** `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `channel = "nightly-2026-04-27"`, with a comment warning that an unpinned nightly "drifts CI onto a newer toolchain than local dev and breaks the build" — this is a build-std project and `unwinding` (locked at 0.2.8) is bound to a specific nightly `core::intrinsics::catch_unwind` ABI. All four jobs in `pre-merge.yml` hardcode `toolchain: nightly-2026-04-27` via `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`; none of them install a fresh nightly.

The guide was instructing a step the build explicitly forbids. Rewritten to describe the date pin, note that pinning means lints don't drift (so a green local `just check` is a real signal), and give the deliberate bump procedure — toolchain date and `unwinding` version move together, plus the hardcoded `toolchain:` values in the workflow. The `rustup update nightly` line is also removed from the CI-gate command block above it.

## 2. "Architecture coverage"

**Claimed:** CI runs only the ARM validate job (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`); the x86_64 job is intentionally disabled and re-enabling it is a separate future change.

**Actual:** PR #121 (merged 2026-07-27, `4beda31e3`) consolidated onto x64. `Validate (x64)` on `ubuntu-24.04` is the main job, `validate-arm` no longer exists, and `Validate GFX (ARM)` on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` remains as a deliberate second-arch canary. Rewritten to match, with the rationale from the workflow's own header comment (browser jobs are x64-only since Chrome ships no linux-arm64 build) and validate-gfx called out as the remaining ARM coverage.

## Scope

Docs only — no code, no workflow changes. `rustup update nightly` also appears in several dated `docs/roadmaps/` and `docs/plans/` artifacts; those are historical records of what was run at the time and were left alone.

端末の画面を撮る部品3本に、失敗したときの検査がありませんでした。足します。

Closes #1 の「モバイル撮影のプロバイダ3本に専用テストが無い」1行

## なぜ

3本の部品（Android、iOSの実機、iOSのシミュレータ）は、まとめ役の関数を通した成功経路だけが触られていました。撮影に失敗して終わる分岐は、どのテストも通していません。

Android には「画像が文字列で返ってきた場合に変換する」分岐もあり、これも未通過でした。撮影が失敗しているのに成功として進む壊れ方は、画面の比較まで進んでから初めて分かります。

## どうした

外部コマンドの呼び出しだけを差し替えて、13件を1件ずつ検査します。

- 渡している引数と、画像の受け取り方の指定
- 成功したときの書き出し先と中身
- 撮影に失敗したときに、そのエラーで終わり、ファイルを書かないこと
- Android で画像が文字列で返ってきた場合の変換
- 書き出し自体に失敗した場合

コールバックの位置は端末ごとに違います（Androidは4番目、iOSの2本は3番目）。位置を決め打ちすると、取り違えたときに失敗ではなく時間切れとして出て、原因が分かりません。末尾から取る形にしています。

## 挙動確認・テスト等

3本の部品は4軸すべて100%になりました。

```
 ✓ src/provider/android.test.ts (5 tests)
 ✓ src/provider/ios-sim.test.ts (4 tests)
 ✓ src/provider/ios-device.test.ts (4 tests)
File          | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines
 src/provider |     100 |      100 |     100 |     100
```

検査が効いていることの確認。Android の失敗処理を握りつぶすと落ちます。

```
× 撮影に失敗したらそのエラーで終わり、ファイルを書かないこと
  → expected TypeError ... to be Error: device not found
```

パッケージ全体の実測は statements 92.39 / branches 96.36 / functions 92.85 / lines 92.39 です。下限を 80 から 90/95/90/90 へ上げました。実測より下に置くと、下がったことに誰も気づきません。

```
pnpm -r run test:coverage   全パッケージ しきい値を満たす
pnpm typecheck / pnpm check / pnpm lint:eslint   エラーなし
```

- 比較元: なし。テストの追加のみで、製品コードは変更していません
- 判定: 該当なし
- 照合していない場合の理由: 画面に関わる変更が無いため、比較する画面がありません

author: strikersam
body:
## Summary

Production is reporting `14 configured | 0 usable | 10 switched OFF`. Ten providers are down for invalid keys or exhausted credit, and four free tiers are carrying all traffic.

**No routing change can help with that.** Distribution spreads a fixed budget, pacing meters it, backoff waits for it — none of them raise the ceiling. Free tiers are rate-limited **per key**, not per provider, so a second account on a provider is a second budget. This is the only code-level lever that *adds* capacity rather than rationing it, and it was the one item on the reference checklist genuinely missing from this codebase.

## How it works

```bash
GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_first
GROQ_API_KEY_2=gsk_second
GROQ_API_KEY_3=gsk_third
```

Round-robin across every configured key, with a per-key cooldown. On a `429` only the refused key rests (honouring `Retry-After`, clamped) while its siblings keep serving. **The provider itself is cooled only once every key is resting** — that's the capacity gain: one spent key no longer stops the provider.

Three deliberate rules:
- **Scan stops at the first gap.** A typo'd `_4` cannot silently promote itself into the `_2` slot and leave you believing three keys are live when two are.
- **Duplicates collapse.** The same key twice is one budget, not two; counting it twice would advertise capacity that doesn't exist while halving the real cooldown.
- **Inert with one key** — which is every provider's current configuration. `next_key` returns it unconditionally, `all_cooling` is immediately true, and the brain chain takes byte-for-byte the pre-rotation path. Rotation engages only from two keys up.

## Changes

- `packages/ai/key_pool.py` — **new.** Pool, per-key cooldowns, round-robin, diagnostics.
- `packages/ai/failover_client.py` — picks the attempt's key from the pool; `_build_request` gained an `api_key` override; the 429 branch rests the key and only falls through to `record_failure` when the pool is exhausted.
- `services/brain_failover.py` — `ProviderInfo.key_env`, so the pool finds sibling variables from the registry rather than re-deriving the name from the provider id. Several ids wouldn't round-trip, and a wrong guess silently means "no extra keys" instead of failing loudly.
- `tests/test_key_pool.py` — **new**, 26 tests.
- `docs/traffic-distribution.md` — a new section, including the caveat below.

## Security

Key material cannot reach a log or an API response. Keys are identified in diagnostics by a **short salted digest — never a prefix or suffix**, because a leading fragment of an API key identifies the account outright for several providers. A test asserts the snapshot contains neither the key nor its first or last eight characters. Bandit: **0 findings** on the new module.

## Testing

- [x] **216 passed** across every failover suite (`test_key_pool`, `test_rate_limit_backoff_survives`, `test_failover_client_shared`, `test_brain_failover`, `test_brain_failover_413`, `test_provider_router`, `test_traffic_director`, `test_brain_availability_doctor`, `test_brain_providers_api`).
- [x] 26 new tests, including the single-key pass-through guarantee, gap-stop, duplicate-collapse, per-provider pool isolation, `Retry-After` clamping, the no-leak assertions, and that Anthropic's native `x-api-key` header rotates too rather than only the OpenAI-compatible `Bearer` path.
- [x] `compileall` clean; changelog parity `PARITY OK`; Bandit clean.

## Changelog

- [x] Added entry under `## [Unreleased]` in `docs/changelog.md` (and `CHANGELOG.md`, parity verified)

## Risky Module Review

- [x] Handles API keys, so treated as sensitive even though `key_store.py` is untouched: keys are read from env only, never persisted, never logged, never returned by an endpoint, and identified only by salted digest. No auth or session path is touched.

## Council Review

- [x] **Security: PASS** — see above; the no-leak property is asserted, not assumed.
- [x] **Correctness: PASS** — single-key is a pass-through, so the default configuration is unchanged. A single-key provider is returned even while cooling, because withholding it would convert a provider-level cooldown the caller already handles into a hard outage.
- [x] **Performance: PASS** — in-process dict lookups under a lock; no I/O.
- [x] **Maintainability: PASS** — one module owning one concern; the brain chain gained two call sites and an optional parameter.

### Please check your providers' terms before using this

Several free tiers permit multiple accounts; some do not. This ships the mechanism — whether a given provider allows it is a judgement call the code cannot make for you, and the docs say so.

### This does not replace fixing the keys

Rotation multiplies working providers. It does nothing for the ten that are off with invalid keys or no credit — that remains the dominant fix, and `together` and `dashscope` still have **no key set at all** despite being free-tier entries in the registry.

## Related

Follows #1161 (which stopped the self-inflicted hammering) and #1159 (distribution).

author: hongtaoyang
body:
The same peer message rendered two different ways depending on how you looked at it: live, the broker's sender stamp gives you `child-31085e7e > fix done`; after a `--resume`, the stamp was gone (never persisted) and the transcript fell back to owner-attribution plus the `[message from peer …]` prefix baked into the stored text — misattributing peers' turns to the resuming user and leaking a model-facing artifact into the UI.

The root cause was attribution existing as two independent mechanisms at two layers instead of one persisted fact. This PR makes the session log store that fact — the clean text plus who sent it — and derives both presentations from it (the model's prefix at payload-build time, the UI's sender stamp at render time), so a live session and its resume now render identically, with old logs degrading gracefully.

Auditing the resume path for this also surfaced a real integrity bug, fixed in the second commit: the loop logged entries *before* its failure paths rolled the in-memory transcript back, so a provider error could leave phantom entries in the JSONL that the live model never kept — and a resumed session could be rejected by the API on its very first request (consecutive user roles). Log writes are now transactional with the turn.

Closes #46. Related: #48 tracks the remaining (cosmetic) replay-fidelity gap for loop-synthetic steering entries, deferred to the session-DB redesign.

author: thuram-nana
body:
## S5 — Agent-to-agent directed messaging (coordination, never a fact)

Adds a directed, addressed, anti-spoofed message channel between agents on the offense blackboard, under the invariant that **a message is coordination only and can never become a fact/finding** — only a fired deterministic oracle mints a FACT.

### What lands
- **`agent_message` EventKind** (`agents/models.py`) + `AgentMessagePayload {sender, recipient, topic, body, intent="coordination", refs[]}`, registered in `PAYLOAD_BY_KIND`. A finding-shaped extra field on the payload is dropped by validation — a message can never be read back as a `FindingPayload`/critique.
- **Anti-spoof** (`agents/blackboard.py post()`): `payload.sender` MUST equal the posting `agent_name`, else `BlackboardError` — a message can't forge its origin.
- **Directional inbox** (`blackboard.inbox(engagement, recipient, since_id)`): B's inbox holds only messages addressed to B, with a durable read-once cursor.
- **Agent base helpers** (`agents/base.py`): `send_message(recipient, body, *, topic, refs)` forces the real sender; `read_inbox(*, since_id)` reads only addressed messages, consumed as advisory hints (the recipient still routes any prompted action through its own gate + oracle).
- **Durable v1→v2 migration** (`schema.sql` version `'2'`, events.kind CHECK widened to include `agent_message`): the blackboard is a durable shared store, so an existing v1 DB is migrated by an in-place table rebuild.

### Safety (the central guard)
- **message ≠ fact** — a property test posts 10 fact-sounding messages and asserts `count(finding|observation|result|critique|tool_result|decision)==0`, `read(kinds=["finding"])==[]`, and a full replay tags every row `agent_message`. No sequence of messages ever mints a finding.
- **A message authorizes nothing** — it is a hint; the recipient's own gate still queues A2/A3.
- **One bus per env** — the offense blackboard and the sovereign spine are physically distinct; no cross-env live relay (FATAL-2 intact — this PR touches offense only).
- **Migration is crash-atomic** — the v1→v2 rebuild runs inside one explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT`; any failure rolls back to the intact v1 table (the durable audit spine is never left half-migrated). A leftover `events_v2` from a crashed prior attempt is self-healed (`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first). Append-only triggers + FKs survive the rebuild; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` fails closed on any orphan.

### Tests (9, all green)
Directional post+inbox · anti-spoof · durable cursor · **messages-never-become-facts** (property) · payload-can't-masquerade-as-a-finding · v1→v2 migration preserves rows + append-only · **self-heals a leftover events_v2** · **crash-atomic rollback-to-v1** · Agent base helpers. Added to the crucible-core CI test line.

body:
Closes #737

## Causa

El contrato del workflow vive en el backend (`src/creator/decisionTree.ts`) y es solo español: `prompt`, `description`, `placeholder` y `section` de las 32 preguntas. El frontend los renderizaba tal cual, así que con la UI en inglés el modo avanzado mostraba la sección Identity —y las otras 14— en español. No era un problema de la sección Identity: ninguna pregunta del árbol estaba traducida.

## Cambios

- `frontend/src/features/creator/lib/localize-workflow.ts` (nuevo): tabla con las 32 preguntas (prompt, description, placeholder) y las 15 secciones en inglés, más `localizeQuestion`, `localizeQuestions`, `localizeWorkflow` y `localizeSection`. Con locale `es` devuelve el objeto del backend sin tocar; en `en`, si falta una traducción cae al texto original (una pregunta nueva del árbol nunca deja la UI vacía).
- `frontend/src/app/agents/new/page.tsx`: localiza la pregunta activa, el workflow que reciben el panel avanzado y Review, y el mensaje de «primera respuesta obligatoria pendiente».
- Copy de validación más claro en ambos idiomas, sin el `(s)` incómodo del original:
  - `Required answers still missing: {count}.`
  - `Respuestas obligatorias pendientes: {count}.`
- Tests actualizados a ese copy (`fine-tuning-dashboard.test.tsx`, `e2e/creator.spec.ts`).

## Tests nuevos

- `frontend/src/features/creator/lib/localize-workflow.test.ts` (13 tests): traducción de los cuatro campos, preservación del resto de la pregunta, fallback para ids y secciones desconocidas, `localizeWorkflow` con `null` y con `es`, y ausencia de residuos en español en los prompts en inglés.
- `test/creator-workflow-i18n.test.mjs` (5 tests): contrato contra el árbol real — la tabla cubre exactamente los ids de las 32 preguntas y los 15 nombres de sección, cada prompt/description/placeholder queda traducido, y con `es` el objeto no se modifica. Añadir una pregunta sin traducir hace fallar este test.

## Validación

- `npm --prefix frontend run test` → 20 archivos, 162 tests, 0 fallos (antes 19/151).
- `npm run test:unit` → 376 tests, 0 fallos.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` y `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` → sin errores.
- `npm --prefix frontend run build` → build correcto.
- Playwright con `CI=true`, backend real y build de producción → `14 passed`.
- `npx prettier --check .` → sin avisos.

## Alcance / desviación

Las etiquetas de las **opciones** (select/multiselect) vienen del catálogo del backend (270+ items) y siguen en español; traducirlas es un trabajo aparte, con su propio issue, porque implica el catálogo completo y no solo el árbol. Este PR cubre lo que el issue enumera: prompts, descripciones, placeholders, secciones y el mensaje de validación.

author: itskritix
body:
Moves `brainbox.sh` / `www.brainbox.sh` onto the EC2 box that already serves the dashboard and API, and removes the Vercel deploy path entirely.

## What changes

**`scripts/deploy.sh`** — builds marketing and publishes it to `/var/www/brainbox-www`, with the same snapshot-and-rollback treatment the dashboard already gets.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — `deploy-marketing` deleted. It existed only to work around Vercel's git integration attributing deploys to the *commit author* and rejecting merge commits authored by GitHub's noreply address. That problem stops existing once we serve the files ourselves. `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID` and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` become dead secrets.

**Caddy** (on the box, not in this repo) — `brainbox.sh` 308s to `www`, matching Vercel's behaviour exactly; `www.brainbox.sh` serves the static build with an SPA fallback and immutable caching on `/assets/*`.

Nothing is needed from Vercel: marketing loads the widget from `app.brainbox.sh/widget.js` rather than bundling a copy, so the webroot is plain static output.

## A trap I hit

The first-deploy snapshot was written as:

```sh
[ -d "$WWW" ] && cp -a "$WWW" "$PREV_WWW"
```

Under `set -e` that **aborts the entire deploy** when the directory doesn't exist — i.e. exactly the first time it runs. It's an if-block now.

## Cutover — this PR is inert until DNS moves

Caddy vhosts are already applied on the box and validated; existing sites verified unaffected (`api` and `app` both 200 through the reload). The certs can't issue until DNS resolves to us, which Caddy retries in the background.

1. Merge → deploy publishes the build to `/var/www/brainbox-www`
2. **Cloudflare:** `brainbox.sh` and `www.brainbox.sh` → **A → `54.158.224.247`**, DNS-only (grey cloud), replacing the current Vercel records
3. Caddy issues certs automatically, usually within seconds
4. Retire the Vercel project once it's confirmed serving

Rollback is just putting the Vercel DNS records back.

## Verification

`pnpm verify` green — backend 100, dashboard 60, marketing 42, widget 61. `bash -n scripts/deploy.sh` clean, `ci.yml` validates as YAML.
