author: jagpat
body:
## What

Closes the autonomous loop's one **silent transition**: the clean-merge success path.

Today the gate's clear branch runs in this order: set the required `codex-current-head` status to `success` → merge (or arm auto-merge) → update the `autonomous-review-state` sticky comment to `clear`. That final comment update happens **after the PR is closed**. Sessions watching a PR receive comment updates reliably only while it is open, and success statuses are never forwarded to them — so every *failure* state wakes the watching session (findings, retries, timeouts, draft returns all arrive as events), but a *clean merge* does not. The loop's continue-to-next-task signal was the only one that required polling.

## Change

One additional sticky-comment update in the clear branch, **before** the success status is set (and therefore before GitHub auto-merge can close the PR):

- `state: 'review_clean'` — same `statusBody` format, same sticky comment, carrying the clean detail and attempt count, with `next: 'GitHub sets the required status and completes this exact reviewed head.'`

Since the PR is still open at that instant, the comment-update webhook is delivered to subscribed sessions — the success path becomes an event: the watcher is woken with the clean verdict, verifies the merge, and continues the loop. The post-merge `clear` update, the status publication, thread resolution, and merge completion are all unchanged.

## Tests

- New source-order test pins `review_clean` update **<** success status **<** merge completion **<** post-merge `clear` update, alongside the existing `evidence < success < completion` pin.
- `pnpm test:automation` **52/52**.

No application code, no schema, no migration — orchestrator script + its test only.

Adds a **Coaching** tab to race analysis — the pit-wall **delta-time** instrument the site was missing. Pick any two drivers and see exactly *where* one gains or loses time over a single lap, built from each driver's fastest clean lap.

author: vkehfdl1
body:
## Summary

Fixes #31 — `minsync init && minsync sync` on a pre-populated directory exited 0 with `already_up_to_date: true` while never writing `cursor.json`, leaving every query failing as `never synced` and the suggested recovery command looping forever.

## Root cause

`init()` scans existing files into `manifest.json`. `sync(full=false)` then diffed that baseline against the unchanged filesystem and hit the `changes.is_empty() && !full` early return before any cursor was written.

## Fix

- `sync` now detects a missing `cursor.json` and upgrades itself to a full sync — a cursor-less workspace has no meaningful incremental baseline. This makes the `already_up_to_date` early return structurally unreachable while no cursor exists.
- `SyncResult` gains a machine-readable `initial_sync: bool` flag (JSON output), and text mode prints `Initial sync: no cursor found — performed full sync.`
- `NeverSynced` now names `minsync sync --full`, the command that always resolves the state.

## Test plan (TDD)

- RED first: `test_init_then_plain_sync_is_queryable` failed on unchanged code at "sync must never report already_up_to_date when no cursor exists"; GREEN after the fix.
- New regression tests: `test_init_then_plain_sync_is_queryable` (init→plain sync→cursor created→immediately queryable) and `test_sync_after_initial_sync_is_incremental_not_initial` (second sync is `already_up_to_date` + `initial_sync: false`); `test_query_never_synced` now asserts the error names the resolving command.
- Full suite: `cargo test` green (27 integration + all unit tests), `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Manual QA with the real binary against a local TEI-compatible stub: `init` → `sync --format json` reported `files_processed: 1, already_up_to_date: false, initial_sync: true`, `cursor.json` created, `query -k 3` returned the document with exit 0.

## Note

`src/sync/mod.rs` was already 382 pure LOC before this change (over the 250 ceiling); this PR adds ~10 lines for the minimal bugfix. Splitting the module is deferred to a dedicated refactor PR to keep this diff reviewable.

body:
A completed **Acquire Fluorescence Image** task rendered as *no row at all* — it looked like the task never ran. FIB-324 made those runs record their z-stack; this displays it.

Closes FIB-169.

## What it does

The panel's loader was `FibsemImage.load` plus a greyscale resize, and an FM acquisition is a multi-channel z-stack. It now dispatches on `.ome.tif*`, max-projects each channel over z, tints each by its channel colour and blends additively — the same composite the FM canvas shows, so a stack looks the same in review as it did live.

## The composite comes from PR #111

`fibsem/fm/composite.py` is #111's `fm_composite.py`, lifted **verbatim** (only the docstring differs). It's Qt-free, and its home under `fibsem/ui/` meant CI could never import it — so it had no unit tests. It has 15 now, including that `gray` ramps to white and that `green` uses napari's `(0,1,0)` rather than matplotlib's `(0,0.5,0)`.

> **When #111 lands**, its copy should become a one-line re-export of `fibsem.fm.composite` rather than a second implementation. Main has no `canvas/` package so #111 merges cleanly — which means the duplicate is silent unless someone acts. Its four importers need no change.

## Cost

Measured on a real METEOR stack, `(3, 21, 2048, 2048)` uint16, 348 MB on disk:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `FluorescenceImage.load` | 0.76 s, 528 MB array |
| per-channel MIP | 0.03 s → 25 MB |

The volume is released before compositing — a 21× reduction — since the panel may load several in a row.

## Discovery

`fluorescence_images()` mirrors the reference-image path but has **no filename fallback**: FM output never followed a discoverable convention (lamella name + time-of-day stamp, no task name), so an experiment written before FIB-324 has none to find, and guessing a pattern would attribute files to the wrong run. It shares the dedupe and existence guards, which matter here because `MillCoincidentTask` records under this role too.

## Two problems found testing in the application

Neither came from tests — both from running the real app.

**Tiles were scaled to fill the tile width.** Beam images are 3:2 and so were width-limited, but a stack is square: it rendered 512×512 against a 384-tall placeholder — half again the height of its neighbours — and the row jumped 128 px when the image finished loading.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEM/FIB (3:2) | 512 × 341 | 512 × 341 — unchanged |
| FM (1:1) | 512 × 512 | **384 × 384** |

**Rows laid tiles out on one line** at fixed width, and the panel scrolls vertically only, so a third tile was unreachable. Rows now wrap at 2 per line. To be clear about scope: **no task in use produces three images** — only `MillCoincidentTask` could, and it isn't in use — so this is defensive layout, not a fix for something users hit.

Also, a task that produced nothing now says so rather than being omitted: an absent row is indistinguishable from a task that never ran, which is the confusion this whole feature exists to remove.

## Every run of a task, not just the last

The panel collapsed history by name and kept the last entry, so re-running an acquisition *replaced* the previous one in the display. For fluorescence — where each run writes its own timestamped file — that silently hid every earlier acquisition.

Discovery now takes any number of runs and returns the **union** of what they produced. One rule, no branching on task or file type:

| | filenames | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reference images | same every run (overwritten) | repeated runs contribute identical paths → collapses to one set |
| fluorescence | uniquely timestamped | each run contributes its own → all kept |

Measured on the local experiments: **37 rows before, 37 rows after** — every repeated task there (`Setup Lamella Position`, `Spot Burn Fiducial`) records byte-identical file sets, so nothing about existing experiments changes.

The row stays *the task* rather than *a run*, so labels need no timestamp to disambiguate. Only the fluorescence count is unbounded; reference images are still capped to the highest-magnification pair.

**The collapse is an assumption about naming, not intent**, so a test pins it. If reference filenames ever become unique per run, that test fails — and the panel showing every run's beam images becomes an explicit decision rather than a silent consequence of a change elsewhere.

## Testing

29 new tests. Projection, compositing and discovery live outside `fibsem/ui/` so **CI runs them**; only the Qt layout tests are skipped there.

Mutation-verified **11/11**, including the over-corrections — beam images also shrinking, every tile getting its own line, the existence filter dropping live files.

Verified visually against two real stacks: the METEOR file (3 channels, hex colours, OME-fallback metadata) and a fibsemOS-acquired one (2 channels, named colours). Both composite correctly, and the second's near-white appearance is the simulator's test pattern, not a blend fault.

Full suite: **1042 passed, 7 skipped**.

## Known, not addressed

- **FIB-279.** Where `FluorescenceImage.load` transposes C and Z, this panel will project over *channels* and show something wrong-but-plausible. That's the serialiser's defect; fixing it here would be fixing it under cover of a display change. The tests deliberately bypass `save()` with a comment saying why. I added a sharper repro to FIB-279 — a synthetic, warning-free reproduction exists, which that issue currently says it doesn't.
- **Expanding an FM tile re-reads the full stack**, because the expanded view is 2× the cached tile's width. Correct, but the slowest interaction here; caching the projection would avoid it.

author: vikrammali14
body:
## Summary
This PR adds support for shops to apply custom numbering patterns to paint shade codes and optionally hide manufacturer names. When a shop has a custom pattern, all UI surfaces now consistently display the shop's encoded codes instead of manufacturer codes, and respect the shop's preference for showing or hiding shade names.

## Key Changes

- **New hook `useShadeCodeScheme()`**: Fetches and caches the shop's shade code scheme from the API. The in-flight promise is shared across components to avoid duplicate requests, and fails gracefully to `null` for signed-out visitors.

- **New hook `useShadeLabels()`**: Provides a consistent interface for all components to format shade codes and names according to the shop's pattern. Exports `patterned`, `showNames`, `codeOf()`, and `nameOf()` helpers.

- **Search function `matchesQuery()`**: Extracted and enhanced to match only what's visible on screen. When a shop has a pattern, only the encoded code is searchable (not the manufacturer's). When names are hidden, they're excluded from search results.

- **Updated all catalogue and studio components** to use `useShadeLabels()`:
  - `CatalogueToolbar`: Displays and copies shop codes; filters search results accordingly
  - `ShadeGrid`: Uses encoded codes in search and UI labels
  - `MatchList`: Shows shop codes and respects name visibility
  - `ShopCombos`: Displays shop codes in combo previews and search
  - `FabricPalette`, `FanDeck`, `WhitesFinder`, `CompetitorTranslator`, `FullscreenSwatch`, `Harmonies`, `CompareTray`, `CompareOverlay`, `BoardsPanel`, `HeartButton`: All updated to use `nameOf()` and `codeOf()` for consistent labeling

- **Test coverage**: Added comprehensive tests for `matchesQuery()` covering pattern matching, name hiding, and code replacement scenarios.

## Implementation Details

- The scheme is fetched once per session and cached in a module-level variable, with a `resetShadeCodeSchemeCache()` function for testing and sign-out scenarios.
- All components that display shade information now call hooks at the top level (before early returns where necessary) to ensure consistent behavior.
- The `encodeShadeCode()` and `decodeShadeCode()` functions from the shade-codes library are used to transform codes according to the shop's pattern.
- Search logic respects visibility: if a shop hides names, searching for a name returns no results; if a shop replaces codes, the manufacturer's code becomes unsearchable.

author: abcde-rgb
body:
## Qué hace

Dos cosas, en tres commits: **(1)** arregla la verificación automática del frontend —ESLint no analizaba ni un fichero y CI no lo ejecutaba— y con ella salieron a la luz una calculadora caída y once tarjetas rotas del panel admin; **(2)** rediseña el sistema visual para que deje de parecer una plantilla cripto y pase a leerse como un producto financiero.

Se puede revisar por commits: `00d01b2` (fallos), `b012090` (documentos de auditoría), `9b1772d` (rediseño).

## Cambios

**Verificación (`00d01b2`)**
- `frontend/eslint.config.mjs` — la config cargaba `@babel/eslint-parser`, pero CRA no deja un `babel.config.js` en el repo, así que el parser abortaba con *"No Babel config file detected"* en **283 de 283** ficheros. Se pasa a espree (entiende JSX sin Babel ni `NODE_ENV`). Con `react/jsx-uses-vars` activado, los 1987 falsos positivos de `no-unused-vars` se quedan en 111 reales.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — paso `Lint (ESLint)` nuevo, y `py_compile *.py` en vez de una lista a mano que omitía 6 módulos (`price_action`, `timeframes`, `market_data`, `nowpayments`, `revolut`, `affiliate_program`).

**Fallos que encontró el linter al funcionar**
- `FibonacciCalculator.jsx` — usaba `idx` en dos `.map((item) => …)` que nunca lo declaraban → `ReferenceError` **al pintar los niveles**, o sea en cuanto alguien pulsa calcular. Está enlazada desde `DashboardPage`.
- `AdminPage.jsx` — **11 tarjetas** repetían `useEffect(…, [])`. Tras un F5 el token vive sólo en memoria y arranca a `null`: la petición sale con `Bearer null`, el backend responde 401, el `catch` se lo traga y no se reintenta nunca. El proyecto ya había parcheado este fallo dos veces por separado; en vez de un parche número 12 se añade el hook compartido `useAuthedLoad`.
- `backend/server.py` — la búsqueda de usuarios del admin pasaba `q` crudo a los operadores `~`/`~*` de PostgreSQL: un paréntesis devolvía 500. Nuevo `_literal_regex()` + `tests/test_admin_search_regex_unit.py` (5 tests).

**Dependencias**
- `agent-browser` fuera de `dependencies`: 73 MB, cero imports, cero menciones en el repo. `node_modules` 624 → 551 MB.
- `axios ^1.8.4 → ^1.18.1` — la única vulnerabilidad alta que de verdad viaja al navegador.

**Rediseño (`9b1772d`)**
- `src/index.css` — base con temperatura (gris puro → oscuro ligeramente frío), verde de marca desaturado de 80% a 58%, y sistema de superficie nuevo (elevación, filo de luz de 1px, cifras tabulares, CTA pastilla, `prefers-reduced-motion` global).
- `src/App.css` — `.font-unbounded` gobierna **217 titulares** de toda la app: cambiarla a Space Grotesk con tracking apretado reviste la web entera sin tocar componentes.
- `public/index.html` — se descargaban 4 familias de fuentes y sólo se usaban 2 (Inter: **0 usos**). Quedan 2, y fuera de la ruta crítica de render.
- `LandingPage.jsx` — CTA pastilla, cifras honestas, rejilla de funciones a tratamiento único (antes: 8 colores distintos para 8 tarjetas).
- `AnimatedHeroChart.jsx` — las velas al 25% con máscara radial: son ambiente, no contenido.
- `Header.jsx` — el botón de registro usa la misma pastilla que la portada.

**Documentación**
- `docs/AUDITORIA_2026-07-27.md` y `docs/BACKLOG_AUDITORIA_2026-07-27.md`.
- `docs/ESTADO_PROYECTO.md` §1/§2/§6 y `CLAUDE.md`: seguían mandando dar de alta **OxaPay**, retirada del código hace tiempo (hoy es **NOWPayments**). Sólo se actualizaba §7, así que la corrección vivía 1200 líneas más abajo mientras la cabecera mentía.

## Verificación

- [x] `python -m py_compile *.py` — los 16 módulos
- [x] `node frontend/scripts/i18n-check.js` → **5328 claves × 8 idiomas, faltan 0 | sobran 0**
- [x] `pytest tests/ -q` → **264 passed, 74 skipped** (+5)
- [x] `npm run build` compila (exit 0, 744 URLs de sitemap)
- [x] `npx eslint src scripts` → **0 errores** (128 avisos de limpieza heredados)
- [x] `node frontend/scripts/check-fetch-credentials.js` limpio
- [x] Probado manualmente: el fallo del buscador se reprodujo y se corrigió **contra PostgreSQL 16 real** (antes: `InvalidRegularExpressionError`; después: busca literal y sigue siendo insensible a mayúsculas). El `ReferenceError` de Fibonacci se reprodujo en Node.
- [x] Smoke de navegador: los **6 temas** (oscuro, claro, oro, cripto, forex, nasdaq) renderizan con **0 pageerrors** y contraste de texto entre **15,5:1 y 18,2:1**.

## i18n

- [x] Claves añadidas en los 8 locales (`en, es, de, fr, ar, ru, ja, zh`) — una: `statsCalculators`
- [ ] Sin claves nuevas

## Notas / riesgos

**Toca `frontend/**` y `backend/**`, así que al mergear disparará los dos despliegues.**

Tres decisiones que conviene mirar con calma porque van a contracorriente:

1. **`react-router-dom` se deja como está, a propósito.** `npm audit` lo marca *high*, pero el aviso es *"RSC Mode CSRF Bypass"* y esto es una SPA de CRA: no hay React Server Components (verificado). El "arreglo" que propone npm es **bajar a 7.11.0**, un salto mayor hacia atrás. Cambiar una versión que funciona por un aviso que no aplica es empeorar el proyecto.

2. **`no-unused-vars` queda en `warn`, no `error`.** Los 128 avisos son deuda heredada real, pero ninguno rompe nada en ejecución y no deben bloquear el PR de otra persona. Lo que sí bloquea es lo que revienta en el navegador (`no-undef`, `rules-of-hooks`). Cuando el contador llegue a 0, súbelo a `error`.

3. **El CSP del HTML NO se activa en este PR**, aunque es el mayor hueco de seguridad abierto (GitHub Pages no permite cabeceras, así que la web va sin CSP mientras la API sí lo tiene). La variante `<meta>` **no admite report-only**: o la política es correcta a la primera, o rompe TradingView, GA4, OAuth, Stripe y PayPal de golpe en producción. Queda la política concreta y el procedimiento de verificación en §9.1–9.2 de la auditoría, para hacerlo con un navegador delante.

**Regresión que introduje y corregí antes de cerrar:** la pastilla blanca del CTA *desaparecía* en el tema claro, dejando el botón principal menos visible que el secundario. El par de color va ahora en variables y cada tema lo invierte (en claro, pastilla casi negra). Está verificado en el smoke de los 6 temas.

**Sobre el rediseño:** sube el listón y sobre todo lo hace coherente, pero una identidad genuinamente incopiable no sale de tokens — sale de una tipografía propia o con licencia (Aeonik es de pago) y de motion hecho a medida. Eso es dirección de arte con presupuesto.

Introduces a new `extraction/` bounded context (`ExtractionResult`, audit logger), one narrow domain-agnostic `on_tool_output` hook on `run_loop` (kernel stays domain-free), an LLM tool wrapper `fetch_instagram_post` in `sources/instagram/tools.py`, and ADR 0005 — Multi-agent shape as Accepted. Recommender-side `dispatch_extraction` is a companion ticket (#18); this PR is what #18 will consume. Also rolls in three tightly-related fixes: post-M9 stale paths at `monitor/cli.py:51` and `monitor/logging.py:18`, and the pre-existing `save_event` docstring pointer at `catalog/tools.py` (closes #9).

`branch-code-reviewer` returned **APPROVE — no findings** on the three-commit stack. Every critic-MAJOR fix from the Revision 1 plan is present at the file:line the plan named:

- MAJOR 1 (no `search_events(source_url=…)` `TypeError`) — happy path parses `Event` from `save_event`'s `saved` sub-dict; test patches `search_events` and asserts `call_count == 0`.
- MAJOR 2 (heading-rank verbatim-parser fragility) — HTML comment anchors bracket the byte-verbatim block; `#### Terminal calls` is level 4 nested correctly under `### Delegation brief — Extractor`; anchor-uniqueness test asserts each anchor appears exactly once.

body:
## What changed

- Mark `cmm` as provided by the curated templates instead of reinstalling the full `cmm` catalog group.
- Verify the provided component exists in the generated project and preserve every existing template file.
- Install only `bbs`/`login` with the recipe's explicitly validated dependency set.
- Turn the former collision-only integration check into both a successful `board-login` assembly test and an `after-components` rollback test.

## Root cause and impact

`board-login` requested the `cmm` group even though `simple-backend` already ships a template-specific `cmm` baseline. The installer therefore tried to copy roughly 705 `cmm` files and stopped on 38 divergent existing files.

The fix does not overwrite or claim ownership of those files. A successful run now installs `bbs` 88 files, `login` 41 files, and 4 SQL scripts (133 files total), and `validateProject` reports `ok=true`.

- `npm run prepublishOnly`

author: kristenoneill
body:
## What it does

Automates Surescripts eligibility and medication history requests for upcoming appointments, then surfaces the results in the chart so a provider can reconcile them against the patient's active medications in one place.

- **Daily crons** — eligibility (08:00 UTC) and medication history (11:00 UTC) for patients with appointments at configurable pre-appointment day offsets (default T+1 and T+7). Providers without an `spi_number` are skipped, one warning each per run.
- **Rx History action button** on the chart medications section opens a modal splitting returned history into **New / Unresolved**, **Matched**, and **Dismissed**. Matching runs on RxNorm, NDC, description, and an NDC→RxNorm cross-reference through FDB. Unresolved rows can be added to the note as a `MedicationStatement` or dismissed; dismissals auto-clear once a medication matches or a newer fill arrives.
- **Surescripts Requests** provider menu item does the same in bulk for a date range and set of providers.
- **Non-prescriber support** — a user without an SPI can pick an SPI-registered provider to request on behalf of, since Surescripts rejects requests from unregistered staff.

## Why

Surescripts history is one of the few reliable signals about what a patient is actually filling, including prescriptions written elsewhere, but without tooling it sits outside the charting workflow — staff skip it or retype medications by hand. This requests the data before the visit and reduces reconciliation to a click per medication.

## Configuration

Four secrets, one required:

| Secret | Required | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `namespace_read_write_access_key` | Yes | `medication__history` custom-data namespace for dismissals |
| `pre_appointment_days` | No | Cron day offsets, default `"1,7"` |
| `commit_medication_statements` | No | Commit added statements vs. leave staged (default staged) |
| `mock_history_data` | No | Demo only — inject five labeled fake rows for instances with no real data (default off) |

Full details in the plugin README.

## Notes for reviewers

- Every `MedicationStatement` the plugin originates carries command metadata `data_source=surescripts`. The `command_uuid` is set plugin-side so originate, metadata, and commit can be chained in one response.
- Eligibility fires alongside med history on manual requests — history depends on the ISA-13 interchange control number the 271 returns, so requesting history alone can silently return nothing.
- Staff-initiated requests log the initiator alongside the provider whose SPI was used, under a greppable `Surescripts request:` prefix. There is no durable audit record beyond the log.
- The FDB NDC→RxNorm lookup is memoized per payload build and skipped entirely when the patient has no active RxNorm codes; appointment queries use `.iterator()` + `.only()`.
- MIT licensed, matching the convention in `extensions/`.

## Testing

`uv run pytest` — 178 tests, 94% coverage.

Not yet exercised against a live Surescripts-enabled instance; verification is by unit test.

author: iasakura
body:
Closes #101.

`src/proof/` was a flat directory that encoded its structure in a
`yjs_<area>_<part>` file-name prefix. As the store and text proofs were split
for build parallelism the prefix grew long and the grouping stayed visible only
in the name.

This keys the layout on the Go type, and inside a type makes the proofs **four
layers**, each depending only on the ones below it:

| layer | file | holds | may mention |
|---|---|---|---|
| model | `model.v` | the pure model and its theory | rocq-yjs only |
| value | `value.v` | Go-level values and what they denote | + `yjs.*`, `loc`, `w64` |
| heap | `heap.v` | representation predicates, invariants, ghost state | + Iris |
| wp | `<Method>.v` / `wp_private.v` | the WP proofs | + the code |

A layer never depends upward, and `<type>.v` is a `Require Export` facade so
downstream files still Require one name. A layer a type does not need is
absent: `id` has no pure model of its own (its model side is rocq-yjs's
`YjsId`), and `Text` is a handle over a store type, so the sequence it exposes
is the `yType` model and `text/` starts at `heap.v`. Things that are global
rather than per type stay at the top level, where everything reaches them.

```
src/proof/
  core.v            # rocq-yjs re-export (pure) + YjsItem_countable
  prelude.v         # the goose package-init instances (no definitions)
  algebra.v         # generic Iris RA laws, about none of our definitions
  network_model.v   # pure model of the op history / network
  history.v         # the Iris ghost op history
  ws_prelude.v      # staged for perennial's new/proof/

  id/     value.v  heap.v  wp_private.v                   id.v
  item/   model.v  run_theory.v  value.v  heap.v  wp_private.v  item.v
  ytype/  model.v  value.v  heap.v  newYType.v  findPos.v  ytype.v
  store/  model.v  value.v  heap.v  wp_private.v
          Integrate.v GetNode.v splitNode.v repair.v applyUpdate.v  store.v
  text/   heap.v  Insert.v  Delete.v  Len.v                 text.v
  doc/    model.v  heap.v  ApplySyncUpdate.v                doc.v
  demo/   pingpong.v  ws_echo.v
```

`model.v`, `value.v` and `heap.v` have one fixed shape: **all section
boilerplate first, then every definition, then every lemma**, under two
banners, and **every definition of a type lives in one of the three**, never in
a WP file. Each opens with **its API**: the definitions it introduces and the
laws a caller is expected to know, so a reviewer who wants the representation
and the state transitions reads those headers and stops.

Which theorems earn a place in a layer is the one judgment call. It is decided
by asking whether the statement is part of the layer's **interface** or a
**step inside one proof**: would you spend a line on it in the header, does it
survive a change of proof strategy, does it read on its own. Laws of a
predicate, relations between predicates (coherence, projection, observation)
and state-transition laws belong to the layer owning the stronger predicate;
everything else belongs in the WP file that needs it. "The WP proof uses it" is
not a reason. Facts mentioning no cert-yjs definition at all (generic Iris RA
laws) move to `algebra.v`.

This is why `store/heap.v` no longer declares a `Context` in the middle of its
section. That idiom kept new assumptions away from the proofs above, but under
`Set Default Proof Using "Type*"` it also decides which section variables each
lemma is generalized over, so it silently couples a lemma's statement to its
position in the file. Hoisting them means the store's method files now all
carry the same `Context` set (`ftypes_inG` joins the two they already had),
which is uniform boilerplate rather than a per-file accident.

Comments annotating a `Require` line with what it is for are gone.

## What moved, and why

The layers were interleaved before:

| file | Iris decls | Iris-free decls |
|---|---|---|
| old `item/repr.v` | 5 (93 lines) | 27 (212 lines) |
| old `commons/common.v` | 8 (93 lines) | 38 (425 lines) |
| old `store/repr.v` | 67 (1268 lines) | 71 (797 lines) |

`common.v` dissolves: most of it was the item cell model, not anything shared.
What is genuinely shared is `prelude.v`, 31 lines with no definitions at all.

The store's WP files keep their local helper lemmas: those are scaffolding for
one proof, and hoisting them would both hide them from their use site and
serialize the build behind one file. Their **definitions** do move up
(`integrate_loop_inv`, `own_linked_item`, `pool_invs`, `WireReplay`, the
`wire_*` drain model, ...), so no method file declares one.

Placement notes:

- `toYjsId` is the `Id`'s abstraction function, so it moves out of the shared
  base into `id/runtime.v`; `is_origin_id` is an `Id`-cell predicate, so it
  goes to `id/heap.v` rather than travelling with the item helpers.
- The document-sequence validity theory that had been sitting in
  `store/Integrate.v` moves to `ytype/model.v`, where the sequence lives,
  together with the Text-level repackagings that had no home of their own.
- `doc/model.v` keeps its three topical sections: it is a mathematical
  development, so definitions come first within each section rather than
  across the file.
- `ws_prelude.v` stays at the top level: `New.proof.ws_prelude` is the logical
  path goose emits for `wsnet`, and the one the file keeps when it is
  upstreamed into perennial's `new/proof/`.

## Toolchain

No `_RocqProject` or `Makefile` change is needed. `-Q src New` binds the subtree
recursively, so `src/proof/store/Integrate.v` is `New.proof.store.Integrate`,
and the Makefile discovers `src/**/*.v` with `find` and lets `rocq dep` compute
the DAG.

## Acceptance

No functional change: no statement, spec, proof or Go behavior is altered. The
tree holds the same **783 top-level declarations as `main`, byte for byte**,
plus three additions, each a `#[local]` instance re-declared where a file lost
sight of it (`cell_has_id_dec` in `store/Integrate`, `rwmutex_inhabited` and
`tie_body_timeless` in `store/wp_store`), the same idiom the store files
already use for `cell_le`'s merge_sort instances. Every `model.v` mentions no
goose value and no Iris; every `runtime.v` mentions no Iris; both are checked by
the build, since those files open no `heapGS` section.

`./build.sh` (go build -> goose -> vos + vok) is green, as is `go test ./yjs/`.

`rocq_mcp_cache_2916387_.v` at the repo root is dropped in passing: a rocq-mcp
scratch buffer accidentally committed in 571d8f2, whose single line
`From New.proof Require Import yjs_common.` this rename would have left
dangling. The `rocq_mcp_cache_*.v` pattern is gitignored so it cannot come back.

Docs move with the code: CLAUDE.md's architecture section, WORKFLOW.md,
`docs/proof-engineering.md`, the `/quiz` skill's source map, the `src/proof/...`
citations in Go comments, and the cross-file references inside the proof file
headers.

author: roshne
body:
Closes #148

Part of #143 — Phase A. Finally puts a feature on `src/vendor/wow-static-data/static-data.json`, which has been fetched by `fetch-static-data.mjs` and CI-checked by `check:static-data` since #137 **with no importer in app code**.

## The bridge the issue didn't anticipate

As flagged [on the issue](https://github.com/roshne/wow-companion/issues/148#issuecomment-5100524204): the addon saves currencies under **its own field names** and never writes an id, while the bundle is keyed by **numeric currency id**. The ids exist only in the addon's `data/currency.lua`.

`CURRENCY_IDS` carries them across — in TS beside the lookup it feeds, not in the parser. **All ten keys the addon currently writes resolve against the bundle**, and a test pins that: the two halves are maintained independently (addon Lua vs a vendored release feed), so their continued agreement is exactly the thing that will break quietly.

## Unknown keys are a live case, not a hypothetical

The database already holds **`AdventurerCrest` and `Manaflux` on 3 characters** — written by older addon versions and since dropped from its field list. They render by humanised key ("Adventurer Crest"), sort after the known currencies, and the header states how many are unresolved.

That's the same path a new season's currency takes on **12.1 day**, before the bridge and the bundle catch up — so it's the degradation that matters most, and it's exercised by real data today.

## Other decisions

- **Columns are the union of what the data contains**, not a fixed list — which is what lets a bundle refresh introduce a currency with no code change. That's the point of reading the bundle at all.
- **Caps prefer the addon's figures over the bundle's `maxQty`.** The addon separates a weekly *earn* cap from a hard *hold* cap; the bundle's single value can't, so it's a fallback. A bundle `maxQty` of `0` means uncapped and is normalised to no cap rather than a cap of zero.
- **Icons** come from Blizzard's render CDN, whose host the app's `img-src` CSP **already permits** — no config change. They're decorative: slugs can disagree with CDN filenames (and at least one contains a space), so the URL is encoded and a failed load hides the image, leaving the name.

## Test plan

**Automated** (23 new; 663 passing overall):

*Logic — `currencies.test.ts` (15):* every key in the bridge resolves against the bundle with a name and icon; unknown key degrades to a humanised name with no id or icon; a zero `maxQty` normalises to no cap; icon slugs with spaces encode correctly; columns built from data; unknown currencies sort last; **cap precedence** (weekly → addon hold → bundle) across three cases; uncapped stays uncapped; characters with no currencies omitted; stale marked and sorted last.

*Rendering — `WarbandCurrencies.test.tsx` (8):* known currency named from the bundle with its amount and cap; unknown key rendered with the "shown by addon key" note; icon present for known and absent for unknown; **a failed icon load hides the image and keeps the name**; capped amount marked; a currency a character doesn't hold renders as a dash; stale marker; empty state.

**Manual:**
- **Verified against live data:** all 10 current addon keys are present on all 58 characters and resolve; `AdventurerCrest` and `Manaflux` appear on 3 and take the unknown path.
- **Icon URLs verified against the live CDN**, rather than assumed: six of the resolved slugs return **200**, and the space-containing slug (`jewelcrafting_uncut epic gem_color1`, Untainted Mana-Crystals) returns **403** — the exact case the `onError` fallback exists for. So icons genuinely render, and the one that can't fails into the name-only path by design.
- **Not done:** visual check in the running Tauri window.

author: altogennn
body:
**Stacked on #191** — contains it. Merge #191 first; this PR's own diff is the last two commits.

## 1. The knowledge-base row was fake. Now it is real or absent.

`home_tab.dart` had `_tickerLines`: three hardcoded strings rotating on a 5-second timer with **nothing behind them** — no paper count, no ingest state. It implied live indexing that was not happening.

New migration `20260728050000_knowledge_base_stats_rpc.sql` adds `get_knowledge_base_stats()`:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `studiesIndexed` | **DISTINCT** `citations[].paperId` across all claims |
| `edgesVerified` | rows in `verified_edges` |
| `lastIndexedAt` | `max(loaded_at)`, null when nothing was ever loaded |

- **Distinct papers, not claim rows.** One paper commonly supports several edges; counting claims would inflate the study count.
- **`security invoker`** — `relationship_claims` already has an authenticated read policy, so this adds no readable surface. Definer would grant strictly more than the read needs.
- **Tolerates malformed input** — `jsonb_typeof` guard means a non-array `citations` contributes nothing instead of erroring the whole query.

Verified locally against a disposable insert (rolled back): two claims sharing `10.1/aaa` plus one `10.1/bbb`, one empty `paperId`, one citation with no `paperId`, and one non-array `citations` → `studiesIndexed = 2`. Correct on every case.

**The row now renders only when a real read returned real content.** A failed read returns `null` rather than empty, so an outage hides one row instead of asserting an empty corpus it never read. `1 study indexed` stays singular — the Run 4 corpus really is one paper, and rounding up would overstate the evidence base.

## 2. Home aligned to the design file

From `Biotope Biomech Botanical.dc.html`:

- real date eyebrow + `Afternoon, <name>` greeting line;
- gold hairline fading to nothing, on the hero and on section eyebrows;
- `SIGNALS TODAY` with the design's gradient rule;
- **7-day delta pill**, rendered only when the day's coverage *and* the 7-day average both exist and differ. No baseline means no pill — never `▲ 0`;
- the hero `breathe`, gated on `MediaQuery.disableAnimations` so a continuous ambient loop is not forced on users who turned motion off;
- hero artwork pushed clear of the status text with a later, harder feather, since the asset is an opaque rectangle rather than a cutout.

### Two deliberate divergences from the design

1. **Kept `/100 coverage`, not the design's `/100 index`.** That number is `log_completeness`. Calling it an "index" would imply a composite health score the app does not compute.
2. **No invented status sentence.** The design shows "Your biome held steady through the weekend." There is no real derivation for that phrasing, so it was left out rather than fabricated.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `flutter analyze` | `No issues found!` |
| `flutter test` | **276 pass, 26 skipped** (was 256) |
| RPC correctness | verified against a rolled-back fixture, see above |
| Physical Samsung SM-A165F | Home re-rendered and re-checked after each change |

Landing delta 57 paths / 7,670 added lines — inside 115 / 8,500, but only ~830 lines of headroom left. **The next unit will need the gate base advanced again after #191 merges.**

## Left for the next session

- #200 — Archive: trend data alongside past insights.
- #201 — Scan: scanning-motion restyle.

author: ludoal
body:
Clicking a fitted module to pick it back up frequently did nothing at all. Picking a module up happens only inside the branch guarded by `input.LeftMouseReleased && input.LeftMouseHoldDuration < ClickThresholdSeconds`, and that threshold is 0.10s — shorter than a normal, slightly deliberate click. Past it no branch handles the press, so the module is simply never loaded onto the cursor.

`InputState.LeftMouseHeld` defaults to 0.15s for what counts as a held button, and `ShipYardArcMove` calls it with no argument, so this screen was also disagreeing with the rest of the input layer about where a click ends. Aligning on 0.15 fixes both: an ordinary click is a click again, and the two thresholds no longer leave a window that is neither.

author: shalom-karr
body:
Upstream feature drop from Shalom-Karr/SK-Music `main` — everything that landed since the fork point, offered here so the iOS fork can pick what it wants.

## Player

- **Gapless playback (double-buffer prime)** — a second hidden YT player pre-cues the next queue track and primes it immediately (muted buffer, parked at 0), then fires ~0.5s before the end **or on the ended event** (YouTube over-reports durations by whole seconds, so a pre-end window alone gets skipped). Players swap roles on the standby's PLAYING; measured ~200ms fire-to-advance with no intro skip. Embed-dead videos are blacklisted from cueing. **iOS note:** the whole mechanism is gated to `PB.mode === "yt"` — your HTML5 `/stream` path is untouched, and your dual-`<audio>` equivalent could reuse the same warm/prime/fire state machine.
- **Empty-queue Play** — resumes the last listen at position if it ticked within 20 minutes (`zw_lastPlay`), otherwise starts the endless trending mix.
- Both embed players use the **`youtube-nocookie.com` host** — kills the doubleclick/ad-beacon console spam that dies against content filters.

## Zemer Radio (server-backed autoplay)

- Worker `GET /radio` pass-through to `search.zemer.io/radio` (deliberately uncached — stations are per-session).
- Queue-end **Autoplay continuation** (kind=song seeded by the last track, opaque continuation paging), **prefetched when the last queued track starts** so the advance is instant; Up Next toggle (`zw_radioAutoplay`, default on).
- **Radio buttons**: artist + album detail (kind=artist/album), playlist + curated playlist detail (kind=playlist), Home "Radio mode" (kind=shuffle). All suppressed in Acapella-only mode; server applies allowFemale/kidZone/blocked-ids in-engine, client re-gates its local-only filters.

## Discovery / content

- **`/zemer-new` Worker proxy** (KV+edge cached, fetched unfiltered, client-side gate) — Home "Latest Releases"/"New Songs" and For You "New for you" now order by REAL release dates from the upstream releases feed, corpus fallback when empty.
- **For You cold start** — no recents/likes → "Popular right now" seeded from the telemetry top-50 (acapella variant during mourning periods).
- **Artists page**: A–Z fast-scroll strip (tap/drag, letters reflect the filtered view) and `sizedArt()` — googleusercontent/ggpht covers are rewritten to square center-crops (`=s320-c`, 640 hero, 128 rows): ~25 KB instead of the raw ~290 KB `=w2880` banners.

## Navigation / UX

- **Back behavior**: artist pages go "up" to the Artists tab; album/playlist detail returns where you came from, with tab fallbacks for deep links (history entries carry an in-app depth marker).
- Deep links, share timestamps, Now Playing artist links etc. from the earlier commits since your fork point.

## Desktop shell (Tauri — skip if iOS-only)

- Bridge contract: `now_playing` carries `videoId`/`queueBase`/`queue`; `__skMediaControl` gains `like`/`radio`/`playindex:<n>`/`resumecheck` (post-sleep wedge self-heal). Redesigned collapsible mini player, tray Up Next/Like/Radio, autostart, update dialog + daily checks.

## Merge notes

- Expect conflicts in `assets/ui.html` (your HTML5-audio/iOS changes overlap the player region) and `engine/index.mjs`/`wrangler.jsonc` (your `/stream` + R2 work). The gapless + radio blocks are self-contained sections that should transplant cleanly even if you cherry-pick rather than merge.
- Heads-up on your `/stream` route: as shipped it accepts any videoId — worth gating against the whitelist before it gets discovered as an open extractor.

## Formål
Retter systemårsaken bak fragmenterte og stikkordspregede `desc`-tekster.

## Forskningsgrunnlag
Policyen bygger på redaksjonelle prinsipper om å prioritere ett hovedpoeng i ingressen, utsette detaljer til brødteksten og skape kohesjon gjennom kjent–ny informasjonsflyt.

## Ny ingressmodell
- `desc` er en leksikalsk ingress, ikke en komprimert innholdsfortegnelse
- én styrende idé før teksten skrives
- normalt én til tre sammenhengende setninger
- ingen hard ord- eller faktagrense
- navn, årstall og epoker tas bare med når de tjener hovedideen
- kronologiske inventarlister og «fra A via B til C»-konstruksjoner avvises redaksjonelt
- detaljer utsettes til `popupDesc`

## Leveranser
- oppdatert canonical-regel
- maskinlesbar ingresskontrakt

author: mechkhc05
body:
## Summary
Second project in the workspace: a PEMFC (25 cm²) performance prediction model, building on the lab's own [JIEC 2025 paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jiec.2025.10.027) that compared RF/GB/SVM/ANN/XGBoost surrogates trained on CFD data.

**Plan:**
1. ~~Baseline~~ — reproduce the paper's surrogate comparison on the provided CFD dataset (done, see below)
2. PINN — physics-informed model using a 0D/1D polarization-curve equation (V = E_Nernst − activation − ohmic − concentration losses) as a physics constraint, trained on sparse CFD data. Chosen over a full 3D field-based PINN since only scalar CFD outputs (not spatial fields) are available.
3. DeepONet — trained on data generated cheaply from the validated PINN, for real-time inference
4. Unity — Python backend serving the trained model, Unity client for visualization
5. Publication

## What's in this PR
- `README.md` — full project scope and phased roadmap
- `data/raw/dataset_formodel_paper2-3.xlsx` — the CFD dataset (306 rows: 51 operating conditions × 6 voltage points; inputs: pressure, anode/cathode temperature & humidity & stoichiometry, voltage; outputs: power density, system efficiency, O2 distribution uniformity)
- `src/baseline_reproduce.py` — reproduces the paper's model comparison (without Optuna tuning) to validate the data pipeline before building PINN/DeepONet on top of it

**Baseline results** (this repro vs. paper's Table 7):

| Model | PD R² | SE R² | ODU R² |
|---|---|---|---|
| XGBoost | 0.988 (0.989) | 0.999 (0.999) | 0.921 (0.935) |
| Gradient Boosting | 0.986 (0.985) | 0.999 (0.999) | 0.914 (0.926) |
| Random Forest | 0.981 (0.970) | 0.996 (0.997) | 0.855 (0.851) |

Close enough to confirm the data pipeline is correct.

## Test plan
- Ran `python src/baseline_reproduce.py` locally, confirmed R²/RMSE land close to the paper's published Table 7 for all 5 models

PR5 of the #22 arc (see #121-#125). `profiles.yml` gains `extensions: [httpfs]` plus a `settings:` block (`s3_region`/`access_key`/`secret_key`/`endpoint`/`use_ssl`/`url_style`), driven by the same env vars `app/core/storage.py`'s `configure_duckdb_s3()` reads on the Python side. author: panghy
body:
## Problem

Clicking menu bar items that route through renderer IPC did nothing: Intent > Settings..., File > New Workspace, Open Recent items, New Agent/Note/Terminal/Browser, Close Tab, Reopen Closed Tab, Window > Select Previous/Next Tab, and the browser-panel zoom variants. Keyboard shortcuts (cmd+, / cmd+N / ...) still worked because the renderer's KeyboardShortcutManager handles them directly — only the native-menu-click → IPC path was dead.

## Root cause

The renderer listeners for the `navigate` and `menu:*` channels lived in `app-layout-saga.ts`, deleted with the saga runtime in 95d908a2 without re-homing (same class of breakage as the notification channels fixed by `notification-ipc-service.ts`).

## Fix

`createMenuIpcMiddleware()` (`src/store/renderer/middlewares/menu-ipc-service.ts`), following the notification-ipc-service pattern: registers `window.electronAPI.on` listeners for `navigate` + all 11 `menu:*` channels on middleware creation and ports the deleted saga semantics verbatim:

- `navigate`: `/workspace/new` and `/?create=true` → `setShowCreateModal(true)`; anything else → `goto(path)` (covers Settings, New Workspace, Open Recent)
- `menu:new-agent`: terminal-focused → `workspace:new-terminal` window event; else `createAgentRequested`
- `menu:new-note` / `new-terminal` / `new-browser`, `close-tab` / `reopen-closed-tab`, `select-previous-tab` / `select-next-tab`: workspace-scoped dispatches; no-op without an active workspace
- `menu:zoom-in/out/reset`: `browserTabZoomRequested` only when the focused panel's active tab is a browser tab

Registered in `middleware.ts`. Dependency-light per AGENTS.md middleware guidance (no module-scope selector imports; state read directly off the store).

## Testing

- 31-test suite (`menu-ipc-service.test.ts`): per-channel dispatch/goto assertions, navigate routing incl. invalid payloads and swallowed nav failures, new-agent focus branches, no-active-workspace no-ops, zoom gating, exact 12-listener registration, non-Electron no-op
- `pnpm run check` 0 errors; `pnpm tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; eslint clean
- Independently re-verified by a second review agent against the pre-removal saga at 95d908a2^

## Related

- Remaining non-menu orphaned channels tracked in intent-hq/monorepo#1002

author: macbot26-boop
body:
Macht aus `zu_wenig_daten` zum ersten Mal ein echtes Urteil.

## Der Kern in einer Zeile

Bis jetzt bekam die Vorprüfung immer genau **eine** Messung gereicht:

```
vorpruefung(tarif, [{ mbps: gemessenMbps, tag: "einzelmessung" }])
```

Damit konnte sie nur `zu_wenig_daten` antworten — eine einzelne Messung erfüllt keines der drei Kriterien des § 57 Abs. 4 TKG. Die Rechnung selbst konnte Messreihen **schon immer**; sie bekam nur nie eine. Dieser PR baut keine neue Rechnung, er füttert eine vorhandene.

## Wo der Verlauf liegt

**Auf dem Gerät**, nicht auf unserem Server. Kein Konto, keine Kennung, die uns erreicht — und damit keine Abhängigkeit von der Datenschutzerklärung aus Phase 8.

Kennung, Zeitstempel und Formatversion sind trotzdem von Anfang an dabei. Das sind genau die drei Felder, die eine spätere Zusammenführung mit einem Server-Verlauf braucht, und genau die lassen sich **nicht nachrüsten** — die Messungen wären dann schon da, ohne sie.

## Welche Messungen ins Urteil gehen

Drei Filter, alle aus der offiziellen Kampagne der Bundesnetzagentur übernommen:

| Filter | Warum |
|---|---|
| Nur der gewählte Tarif | Ein anderer Vertrag heißt ein anderes Produktinformationsblatt — also die falsche Messlatte. |
| ≥ 5 Minuten Abstand | Zehn Messungen in zehn Minuten beschreiben eine Viertelstunde, keine Leitung. |
| Letzte 3 Messtage, innerhalb von 14 Tagen | Die Regel lautet „an **2 von 3** Messtagen". Über einen unbegrenzten Verlauf wären das irgendwann 2 schlechte Tage von 40 — ein Daueralarm statt eines Urteils. Ohne die 14-Tage-Klammer verschmölzen der 1. Januar und der 15. März zu „drei Messtagen". |

Messungen, die wegen des 5-Minuten-Abstands nicht zählen, werden auf dem Schirm **ausdrücklich genannt**. Wer gerade gemessen hat und den Zähler nicht steigen sieht, hält die App sonst für kaputt.

## Ein Speicher darf nie ein Urteil verhindern

Blockiertes Schreiben (privater Modus), gesperrtes Lesen und beschädigte Daten führen alle zu „kein Verlauf" — nie zu einem Absturz. Die gerade gemessene Zahl steht in **jedem** dieser Fälle trotzdem im Urteil; das Verhalten fällt dann exakt auf das von vorher zurück. Ein einzelner beschädigter Eintrag nimmt keine gesunden mit.

## Belege

**297 Tests grün** (276 + 21 neue). Der Kern-Beleg ist einer davon:

> `aus „zu wenig Daten" wird nach 3 Messtagen ein echtes Urteil`
>
> Dieselbe schlechte Leitung liefert bei **einer** Messung `zu_wenig_daten` und bei **drei Messtagen** `auffaellig` — während eine gute Leitung an drei Tagen `unauffaellig` bleibt.

Dazu Tests für jeden Filter einzeln, die 14-Tage-Grenze (Tag 14 drin, Tag 15 draußen), die Reihenfolge bei gleichen Zeitstempeln, alle vier kaputten Speicher-Fälle, die Obergrenze und den lokalen Kalendertag (eine Messung um 00:30 gehört zu dem Tag, den der Nutzer auf seiner Uhr sieht — über UTC gerechnet spränge der Messtag nachts zurück).

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` und `npm run build` sauber — der Build schließt das Server-Rendern von `/messung` ein, also genau die Stelle, an der ein Zugriff auf den Gerätespeicher zur falschen Zeit auffliegen würde.

### Am laufenden Schirm geprüft (lokal gegen den Docker-Peer)

Eine echte Messung durchgeklickt, Tarif „MagentaZuhause XL" (bis zu 250) gewählt, gemessen 144 Mbit/s:

> **DEINE MESSREIHE · MESSTAG 1 VON 3 · 1 VON 10 MESSUNGEN**
> Für ein Urteil fehlen noch 2 Messtage — miss an einem anderen Tag erneut. Deine Reihe bleibt auf diesem Gerät gespeichert.

Und im Gerätespeicher lag danach genau das, was dort liegen soll:

```json
{"id":"2f5302df-…","mbps":143.7,"tag":"2026-07-28","zeit":1785221103513,
 "tarifSlug":"magentazuhause-xl-svdsl-250","verbindung":"unknown"}
```

**Was ich NICHT am Schirm sehen konnte:** den Urteils-Sprung bei 3 Messtagen und den 5-Minuten-Hinweis. Beide brauchen eine zweite Messung, und die kommt lokal nicht zustande — siehe unten. Beide sind durch Tests abgedeckt.

## Ein vorbestehender Fehler, den ich dabei gefunden habe (NICHT von diesem PR)

**„Nochmal messen" führt zu keiner zweiten Messung.** Die Oberfläche bleibt bei „Laufzeit wird gemessen (Ping) …" stehen, während im Protokoll `rtt: measurement finished` steht (10 Anfragen, 10 Antworten, 0 Fehler) — das Messwerk ist also fertig, nur die Anzeige geht nicht weiter. Auffällig: Jede Protokollzeile erscheint **doppelt**, was auf zwei laufende Messwerke nach dem Neustart hindeutet.

**Auf `main` gegengeprüft und dort identisch reproduziert** — ohne eine einzige Zeile aus diesem PR. Gehört in einen eigenen Fix.

## Eine offene Design-Frage — bewusst nicht entschieden

Der neue Kasten hängt an der Handlungsleiter, und die erscheint nur, wenn das Urteil **nicht** „gut" ist. Das heißt: Wer heute gut misst, sieht seine Messreihe nicht — auch dann nicht, wenn sie aus den beiden Vortagen bereits `auffaellig` ist.

Das ist kein Fehler in diesem PR, sondern eine Frage an das Produkt: Soll ein „passt alles"-Schirm auf eine auffällige Vorgeschichte hinweisen? Ich halte es für den ehrlicheren Weg, aber es ändert einen Schirm, der abgenommen ist — deshalb entscheide ich das nicht allein.

author: antonireus
body:
CI wall-clock roughly doubled on 2026-07-27 with no change to `ci.yml` (last touched 07-23). One commit poisoned the shared Cargo cache in a way that **cannot self-heal**, so every job recompiles the full 387-crate DataFusion/Arrow/Iceberg tree, four times per run. Run [30284577915](https://github.com/exasol-labs/lakehouse-engine-rs/actions/runs/30284577915) took 63 min.

This restores cache reuse and cuts the critical path: **~55 min → ~26 min, ~81 → ~46 billed job-minutes.**

## Root cause

`b7fc59e` added `[profile.dev] debug = 1` to the root `Cargo.toml`. Profile settings are part of every crate's fingerprint, but they never entered the cache key — so every job restored the 07-24 cache as an **exact** hit, cargo rejected all 387 artifacts, and because the hit was exact rust-cache logged `Cache up-to-date.` and **skipped saving**. GitHub cache keys are immutable, so it could never repair itself.

Why the key missed it: Swatinem/rust-cache hashes each workspace *member* manifest in full, profiles included — but this workspace's root is **virtual**, so `cargo metadata --no-deps` doesn't list it and the root `Cargo.toml` is never read. `[profile.*]` is only legal there. That is upstream [Swatinem/rust-cache#268](https://github.com/Swatinem/rust-cache/issues/268), open since 2025-10-05, with no fix on master.

**Fix:** move the dev profile into a checked-in `.cargo/config.toml`. rust-cache raw-hashes that file into the *strippable* part of the key, and Cargo honours `[profile.*]` there (stable since 1.43), overriding the manifest. A profile edit now rotates only the exact key — the fallback still restores, the save fires, the poisoning heals. This replaces the manual "bump the `-rlib` suffix" workaround, which never covered profile edits, which is why it recurred.

An intermediate approach (hashing the root manifest via `env-vars`) is in the branch history and was reverted: rust-cache builds `restoreKey = prefix+envHash`, so an env hash lands in the **prefix** and any byte change to the root manifest — a routine pin bump, or a comment — would forfeit the fallback restore entirely.

## Also in this PR

- **Deleted the `build` job.** It warmed a cache `unit-tests` restores under an identical key — 11 min of pure serialization for nothing. `unit-tests` is now the writer (`cargo test` emits `.rlib`, the superset clippy and E2E need), with `save-if` gated to `main` so PR branches stop minting duplicate caches.
- **Both E2E jobs → `needs: [build-so]`.** They only consume its `.so` artifact but waited ~18 min on gates they don't read. `release` now lists `lint`/`unit-tests`/`licenses` explicitly, since it used to inherit them through `e2e` — without that, a main push with failing tests could mint a tag and Release. `e2e-lakekeeper` is also in `release`'s `needs` now (it never was, even pre-PR — a lakekeeper regression could ship).
- **Dependencies build with `debug = 0`.** `cargo test` links 29 separate test binaries against the full dep tree and debug-info volume dominates link time. Workspace crates keep line tables; backtraces keep dependency function names.
- **Cache quota back under 10 GB** (was 10.45, causing LRU eviction of caches that matter): dropped the `licenses` registry cache, split `build-so`'s into restore/save so only `main` writes.
- Removed dead `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG`, merged the two `cargo deny` steps.
- **Review fixups:** `.cargo/config.toml` added to the `docker-cargo` key so a future `[profile.release]` edit rotates it instead of poisoning it. (`cache-on-failure` on the writer was tried and reverted: it would pin a partial dep-compile under the immutable exact key if a dependency itself failed to build on `main` — worse than the red-main cold window it fixed. So a red `main` skips the save until green.)

## Verification

Local: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `make cross-musl-udf-build` (163 MB `.so`, max `GLIBC_2.35` ≤ the SLC's 2.36, both UDF entry points exported). Profile confirmed from its new location: workspace crates `-C debuginfo=1`, dependencies `-C strip=debuginfo`.

**This PR's own CI runs cold and saveless by design** — the key rotated and `save-if` gates saves to `main`, so every push recompiles the full tree in four jobs. Expected, not a failure signal.

After merge, in order:
1. First `main` run compiles once and **saves** — the `Unit Tests` rust-cache `Post` step should take minutes, not 1s. A 1s `Cache up-to-date.` means the key still isn't rotating.
2. Second `main` run is the real check: `Unit Tests` and both E2E logs show `Compiling=2`, `Check & Lint` shows `Compiling=20`.
3. One-time `gh cache delete` of the `Linux-cargo-registry-*` and stale branch-scoped `docker-cargo-*` entries — deleting the cache *steps* doesn't evict existing entries.

## Known gaps

- A `features`/`default-features` edit in root `[workspace.dependencies]` moves neither the lockfile nor any hashed file, so it still poisons the cache silently — same #268 blind spot, narrower blast radius. Documented in `Cargo.toml`; declare features on the member crate, whose manifest is hashed.
- Dropping the E2E gates removes fail-fast: a PR with a clippy error burns a full E2E run. `main` has no branch protection or rulesets, so gating was already convention-only. Reversible in one line.
- `paths-ignore: ["specs/**"]` remains a latent blocker if required status checks are ever enabled — pre-existing, neither worsened nor fixed here.

author: steipete
body:
Closes #111999.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw treated a service-qualified iMessage/SMS handle as if it were an existing Messages chat GUID. For ordinary local media it passed synthetic `iMessage;-;<handle>` / `SMS;-;<handle>` strings directly to one-shot `send-attachment`; the newer remote-host path repeated the same synthesis for `send.attachment`. When the real existing conversation was stored under another GUID such as `any;-;<handle>`, attachment delivery could silently fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both local and remote ordinary non-voice handle media with a concrete SMS/iMessage service now fall through to the existing canonical `imsg rpc` `send` path. That path already carries `to`, effective service, file, caption, region, transport, remote staging, and formatting; upstream `imsg` resolves real direct-chat candidates and returns authoritative `chat_guid` and service facts, which OpenClaw already records in the result and reply cache.

Explicit `sendTransport: "bridge"` remains on the one-shot attachment path so a new service-qualified conversation can still be materialized. Native voice remains there because AppleScript/generic media semantics cannot preserve the voice flag. Explicit chat IDs/GUIDs, automatic-service handles, national-format handles, chat identifiers, threaded media, and custody/partial-delivery behavior remain covered.

This is iMessage transport-owned target resolution; no core target parser, config, storage, default, or Plugin SDK surface changes.

Production LOC: +10/-0. Tests: +159/-47.

## User Impact

Generated images and other ordinary attachments sent to explicitly selected iMessage or SMS direct conversations are delivered through the real existing chat, locally or through a remote Messages host. Captions travel with the same media send, and the provider-resolved chat GUID/service are retained for subsequent message actions.

## Evidence

- Before the production change: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` failed exactly 4 new routing assertions while 80 sibling tests passed. Local SMS/configured-iMessage/caption paths invoked the synthetic one-shot attachment route; the remote path invoked `send.attachment` with `chat_identifier: iMessage;-;<handle>`.
- After the production change and two fixture corrections for existing cache/custody semantics: the identical command passed 1 file / 84 tests.
- Initial exact-head CI exposed two higher-level durable-delivery tests that still used service-qualified targets to exercise the old two-send custody path. Moving those fixtures to the unchanged auto-handle path preserved every custody/partial-delivery assertion; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/test-plugin.test.ts` then passed 2 files / 105 tests.
- The regression coverage asserts local SMS and iMessage routing, remote file staging, combined caption delivery, provider-returned `chat_guid`/service, reply-cache persistence, explicit-bridge preservation, and unchanged auto-handle custody failures.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed after the implementation on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kzk6aec757jc2wrgx6fdpnb8` (Actions `31312191891`) and again after the CI test correction on `tbx_01kzk78zj0zbxeyp9qpqvgrb6j` (Actions `31312894889`).
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted` completed clean after the implementation and again after the test-only CI correction; neither round reported accepted/actionable findings.

Dependency contracts were inspected directly at `imsg` commit `e22dfad8e54ef5ae9ef8b64a3db05f0ce25cd52c`:

- `BridgeAttachmentCommand.swift` documents `--chat` as a chat GUID and forwards it unchanged; it performs no handle-to-chat resolution.
- `RPCServer+Handlers.swift` accepts direct `to + service + file`, resolves existing chat candidates, and returns real `chat_guid`/service.
- `ChatTargetResolver.swift` tries service-aware candidates including the `any;-;` form for iMessage handles.
- `RPCServer+BridgeMessageHandlers.swift` confirms `send.attachment` expects an existing chat identifier/GUID; it is not the canonical direct-handle resolver.

Behavior-validator contract: ordinary local and remote service-qualified media must use RPC `send` with the original handle/service/file, preserve captions, expose provider chat/service facts, and keep explicit bridge/voice controls. All contract clauses pass through the real OpenClaw sender boundary with deterministic provider responses.

Native proof gap: no real Messages recipient/account destination was approved for this session, so I did not send a private message, touch a live Messages database, or claim the focused boundary suite as native readback proof. The prior ClawSweeper review explicitly treats real behavior proof as not required for this maintainer-authored PR; this gap is recorded rather than silently bypassed.

The distinct announce-path media loss in #112309 is not fixed or closed by this PR.

AI-assisted: yes; current-main local/remote paths, upstream Swift contracts, provider-fact/cache behavior, red/green proof, and sibling controls were independently inspected.

body:
## What

A **requirements correctness rubric** — the sixth rubric, covering the most foundational phase. Everything downstream traces to requirements, so a weak set silently caps the whole design.

## The finding it exposes

Live inspection: the substantive requirements *decision* is generic prose ("the following requirements ensure functionality ... they address power, size, mounting, and environmental considerations") with **no numbers** — the quantified constraints live only in the auto-generated phase summary — and nothing states **how each requirement is verified**.

## Checks (6)

1. `requirements_decision_present`
2. `functional_reqs_stated`
3. `quantified_constraints` — mass / size / power with units
4. `interfaces_specified`
5. `operating_environment` — temperature / supply voltage
6. **`verification_criteria`** — acceptance / verification method (ISO-15288 verifiability)

## Honest live baseline (L1)

**requirements = 0.833** — functional, quantified, interfaces, and environment all present; the single gap is **`verification_criteria`**: the constraints are quantified but never tied to an acceptance criterion, so they aren't testable.

**Next target it surfaces:** a requirements pass that attaches an acceptance / verification method to each quantified constraint (e.g. "mass ≤ 10 g, verified by scale").

## Test

- `tests/unit/test_requirements_rubric.py` — quantified-but-unverifiable misses exactly one check (0.833), verifiable requirements score 1.0, generic prose scores low (3 tests).
- Verified live (0.833).

Eval-only tooling → `test(...)` title, no binary release.

author: brofalo
body:
`load_cell_fusion.c` divided the sample sum by a variable `sensor_count`.
Targets with no divide instruction resolve that through libgcc, linking
`__divmodsi4` on AVR and `__divsi3` on Cortex-M0, and
`scripts/check-software-div.sh` fails the image on either.

That is why `atmega644p` failed the check with the load-cell drivers switched
off entirely: the fusion module still came in through

```
config NEED_LOAD_CELL_FUSION
    depends on WANT_HX71X || WANT_ADS1220
```

## The change

`sensor_count` is 1 to `MAX_FUSION_SENSORS` at that point. `add_sensor` shuts
down above the cap, `query` shuts down on zero, and `process_group` returns
early unless the group is active, so a switch covers every reachable value and
lets the compiler fold each divisor to a constant.

gcc folds 1, 2 and 4 inline but still calls libgcc for 3, so that case takes
the high half of `sum * 0x55555556` and adds the sign bit, turning the floor
the multiply produces back into C's truncate-toward-zero.

## Verification

Checked against `sum / 3` for every one of the 4294967296 int32 inputs:

```
naive floor form : 2147483648 mismatches over 2^32
corrected form   : 0 mismatches over all 4294967296 int32 values
```

The naive form without the sign correction is wrong for every negative input,
which is why the constant carries that note in the comment. Cases 1, 2 and 4
are literal `sum / N`, so they are identical by construction.

Cost on AVR is `__mulsidi3` and `__ashrdi3`, neither a divide, and only on the
three-sensor path.

## Matrix

Built from a clean checkout in the pinned toolchain from
`scripts/Dockerfile-build`, all 39 targets:

- `atmega644p` moves from SOFTDIV to clean
- no link failures
- every target still failing `check-software-div.sh` has
  `CONFIG_WANT_HX711S=y`

So this removes one of the two causes outright. The float and integer divides
in `sensor_hx711s.c` are the only remaining one.

body:
## 概要

認可根治戦役 Wave7。スコープ認可の敷設が漏れていた 2 ドメイン（`service` のカスタムフィールド定義・機能設定、`proxyvote` の議案投票制御）を是正し、API 契約テストを新設した。

いずれも「認可を呼び出し元まかせにしたまま未回収だった」同型の敷設漏れで、同一ドメインの兄弟クラスが既に採用している作法をそのまま踏襲して塞いだ。独自の認可方式は導入していない。

## 変更内容

### service ドメイン

`ServiceRecordFieldService` に `AccessControlService` を注入し、兄弟の `ServiceRecordService` / `ServiceRecordExportService` と同じ作法（`AccessControlService` + `SCOPE_TEAM` 定数）で認可を敷設した。

権限粒度は兄弟 `ServiceRecordService` の「参照 = `checkMembership` ／ 変更 = `checkAdminOrAbove`」に揃えた。

- 参照系: `listFields` / `getSettings`
- 変更系: `createField` / `updateField` / `deactivateField` / `updateSortOrder` / `updateSettings`

`ServiceRecordFieldController` は各 EP で `SecurityUtils.getCurrentUserId()` を Service へ渡すよう配線した。

### proxyvote ドメイン

`ProxyVoteMotionService` に `AccessControlService` を注入し、`startVote` / `endVote` に操作ユーザーを渡すようシグネチャを変更したうえで、同一ドメインの兄弟（`addMotion` / `updateMotion` / `deleteMotion`）が一貫して採用している `checkOwnerOrAdmin`（セッション作成者またはスコープ ADMIN/DEPUTY_ADMIN）を敷いた。

併せて `startAllVotes` も同粒度へ引き上げた。従来は末尾の `getSession()` が副次的に `checkMembership` を行うのみで、粒度が兄弟と揃っていなかったため。

### BOLA（Broken Object Level Authorization）対策

認可スコープは path 変数を鵜呑みにせず、必ず fetch 済みエンティティ由来のスコープで判定している。

- `service`: 単一フィールド対象の操作は `findByIdAndTeamId` で path の `teamId` に束縛して fetch し、認可は `entity.getTeamId()` で行う。束縛に失敗した場合は既存の `FIELD_NOT_FOUND` で存在秘匿する。
- `proxyvote`: 対象 EP の URL は path 上にスコープを持たないため、`motionId` → 議案 → 所属セッションと辿り、セッション entity 由来の `resolveScopeId()` / `scopeTypeName()` で判定する。

### バッチ巻き添えの回避

投票タイマー満了による自動終了（`ProxyVoteScheduledService`）は実行ユーザーを持たないシステム起点の処理である。認可ゲートは利用者が到達する public 入口 `endVote(motionId, currentUserId)` にのみ敷き、認可を伴わない中核処理を `endVoteBySystem(motionId)` として明示的に切り出した（共有メソッドに認可を埋めるとバッチが巻き添えで落ちるため）。

### 存在秘匿の看板倒れ防止

`SERVICE_RECORD_002` / `PROXY_VOTE_001` / `PROXY_VOTE_002` は `GlobalExceptionHandler` の `ERROR_CODE_STATUS_MAP` に未登録で、`Severity.WARN` 既定の 400 を返していた。「404 で秘匿したつもり」の看板倒れになるため `NOT_FOUND` を登録した。

## テスト

### 新設した契約テスト

- `ServiceRecordFieldScopeContractIT` — 7 EP / 27 ケース
- `ProxyVoteMotionScopeContractIT` — 3 EP / 18 ケース

象限は「非メンバー / 別スコープ ADMIN（BOLA）/ 非 ADMIN メンバー / 正当な権限保持者」。認可を敷いた結果として機能を壊していないことの証明として、各 EP に正常系（200 / 201 / 204）を必ず含めている。`proxyvote` では `checkOwnerOrAdmin` の owner 経路（ADMIN ではないがセッション作成者本人）が通ることも検証した。

金型は `EquipmentScopeContractIT`。`@Transactional` 付きで共有 Testcontainer を汚染せず、ADMIN は `memberships` と `user_roles` の両方に seed している。

### 既存テストの追随

Service のシグネチャ変更に伴い、呼び出し側を grep で機械的に洗い出して追随させた。

- `ServiceRecordFieldServiceTest`
- `ProxyVoteMotionServiceTest`

（`ProxyVoteScheduledServiceTest` は `motionService` を `@Mock` 宣言するのみで対象メソッドを stub しておらず追随不要）

### 認可番人 凍結ストア

`AuthzControllerGuardArchTest` は Controller から 2 ホップまでの委譲を辿って認可シグナルを判定する。Service 側に `AccessControlService` 呼び出しを敷いたことで Controller → Service の 1 ホップで判定に到達するようになり、凍結済みだった 9 エンドポイントの違反が解消した。

解消分をストアから除去し（795 → 786 行）、`ArchUnitFreezeStoreIntegrityTest` の期待値定数を同一コミットで更新した（同テストが要求する運用手順どおり）。`--tests` 絞り込み実行による誤削除ではなく、正当な根治に伴う縮小である。

author: koala73
body:
Closes #5696.

Our most differentiated analysis ran client-side only — an MCP agent asking "is anything converging on Hormuz?" got nothing. This extracts those engines into shared client/server cores and exposes **nine** new MCP tools (42 → 51).

## Shared cores (one implementation, no fork)

Six client services became thin shims over dependency-free `shared/` modules that the Vite client, Vercel Edge bundle, and tsx tests all import:

| Core | Extracted from | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `analysis-geo-convergence` | `geo-convergence.ts` | grid engine is now a class; `generateSignalId` injected, dropping the i18n-contaminated import |
| `analysis-focal-points` (+ `analysis-entity-index`, `entities-data`) | `focal-point-detector.ts` | stateless core; `lastSummary` stays in the client shim |
| `analysis-infrastructure-cascade` (+ `pipelines-data`, `ports-data`) | `infrastructure-cascade.ts` | datasets are parameters; splits `PIPELINES` from a mid-file `getCSSColor` DOM import |
| `analysis-military-surge` (+ `military-bases-data`) | `military-surge.ts` | engine class with injected clock and cross-service callbacks |
| `analysis-hotspot-escalation` (+ `geo-data`) | `hotspot-escalation.ts` | moves the 29 curated hotspots / 13 waterways / 10 conflict zones server-side |
| `analysis-population-exposure`, `analysis-temporal-severity` | client **and** server twins | de-duplicates two pre-existing copy-paste pairs |

Dashboard behavior is unchanged — each extraction was proven by a differential harness running the pre-change module beside the new shim (33,408 cases for escalation; full-surface parity for focal points, cascade, geo convergence, surge).

## New MCP tools

`get_signal_convergence` · `get_focal_points` · `simulate_infrastructure_cascade` · `get_military_surge` · `get_temporal_anomalies` · `get_test_site_seismicity` · `get_population_exposure` · `get_alert_digest` · `get_hotspot_escalation`

Design notes worth review:

- **`get_military_surge` never merges the two surge algorithms.** The seeder's `military:surges:v1` uses different baselines than the snapshot engine, so it is reported in a separate labeled `seeded_surges` block rather than silently blended.
- **`get_alert_digest` trips each domain on its own producer's severity vocabulary** — no thresholds invented here. Domains with data but no trips are `quiet`; domains whose cache is unavailable are listed separately, so silence is never read as calm.
- **`get_hotspot_escalation` publishes the documented 1–5 composite**, not 0–100 (the issue's phrasing was wrong — components are 0–100, the composite is a 30/70 blend with the curated baseline).
- **`get_test_site_seismicity`** reads enrichment the earthquake seeder already writes, so it adds no new fetch.
- Seven now-redundant `EXCLUDED_FROM_MCP` entries and the population-exposure REST parity exclusion were removed, since these tools genuinely cover those keys.

## Fixes found while building

- Error paths on four tools returned a bare `{error}` while their `outputSchema` marked `cached_at`/`stale`/`data` required — a strict client would reject a legitimate error response. The output-contract test structurally cannot catch this (it monkey-patches `_execute`), so the envelope is now guaranteed on every path and pinned by a new test.
- `generate-public-product-facts.mjs` rewrote the tool count in only 2 of 25 pro-test locales, and never in the translation baseline — so a count bump left 23 locales stale and demanded an LLM translation pass for a numeral. Now covers every locale, the baseline, and the quickstart phrasing.
- `docs-stats.mjs` counted the population table at its pre-extraction path and **failed open to 0**; repointed and made to throw, matching the counter beside it.
- `vite.config.ts` pinned the 48KB military-bases chunk by old path — verified post-fix that the chunk still emits at 44KB rather than duplicating into panel chunks.

## Verification

17,957 tests pass (≈190 new, written red-first), both typechecks, biome, boundaries, sebuf contract, docs-stats (91 claims), product-facts, and a full `vite build`.

**Review note:** the multi-agent code review could not run — the account hit its weekly limit mid-session — so the review was done inline against the same briefs. The adapter fixtures are hand-written from producer source, so a fixture wrong in the same way as its adapter would pass; that residual is called out rather than papered over.

author: copilot
body:
Queued SYNC traffic from a peer that is no longer the active sync session was already being rejected correctly, but the rejection path emitted one warning per discarded block. On stale queued streams, that turned harmless rejects into a DataThread/log I/O flood.

- **Preserve the stale-SYNC guard**
  - Keep the existing rejection condition unchanged:
    ```cpp
    if(nCurrentSession != TAO::Ledger::nSyncSession.load() || fSynchronized.load())
    ```
  - Only the diagnostic behavior changes; stale or post-sync SYNC blocks are still ignored.

- **Replace per-block warning spam with per-session throttling**
  - Add a small bounded stale-SYNC diagnostic helper keyed by peer session ID.
  - Track:
    - last warning time
    - suppressed rejected-block count
    - whether the session has emitted its first warning
  - Emit immediately on the first rejected block for a stale session, then at most once per interval with the accumulated suppressed count.

- **Keep the hot path cheap**
  - Avoid formatting/log construction unless the limiter decides to emit.
  - Capture sync-session / synchronized state once for the warning path and use the rate limiter before calling `debug::warning(...)`.

- **Bound memory and clean up on disconnect**
  - Use a small fixed-capacity map with the same low-risk clear-on-cap pattern already used elsewhere in `src/LLP/tritium.cpp`.
  - Clear limiter state for the disconnected session so a recycled/new connection does not inherit stale counters.

- **Add focused regression coverage**
  - Add unit tests for:
    - first event logs immediately
    - repeated events in-window are suppressed and counted
    - next event after the interval reports the accumulated count
    - different sessions are isolated
    - bounded-cap/reset behavior

Example of the new warning shape:

```cpp
debug::warning(FUNCTION,
    "ignoring unsolicited sync block from session ", std::hex,
    nCurrentSession, " sync_session=", nSyncSession,
    std::dec, " synchronized=", fAlreadySynchronized,
    " suppressed=", decision.nSuppressedBlocks);
```

body:
## What changed

Docs only, no code. Records the `curl -sI` half of OW1's Verify block, which is now **done**.

All six headers and both CSPs are live on `https://liberatingscripture.org/` and match `docs/security-headers.md`, including the 2026-07-22 `form-action` move to Report-Only and the same-day `*.sibforms.com` correction:

| Header | Live value |
|---|---|
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains`, no `preload` |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` |
| `Permissions-Policy` | `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()` |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` |
| Enforced CSP | `frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'` — correctly without `form-action` |
| Report-Only CSP | present, corrected values |

OW1 had recorded this step as impossible from a Claude session, because outbound requests to the domain were blocked at the time. That turned out to be environment-specific rather than permanent: a later session reached the domain fine, so the check just ran.

## Why the second change

The origin inventory's two `cloudflareinsights` rows now carry a warning not to prune them as unused. The Web Analytics beacon is **edge-injected by Cloudflare**, so it appears in no source file in this repo, and injection is **skipped for non-browser user agents** — meaning a plain `curl` shows no beacon and makes those rows look dead. A browser-UA fetch confirms `static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4513226…` is served on every page.

This came out of the sibling litbible repo hitting the inverse problem twice: two of its audits concluded its beacon was missing, and it had to add the two origins its curl-based inventory had never seen. This repo got it right only because F2 inventoried origins by loading pages in a real browser. The note exists so a future cleanup doesn't undo that.

## What still remains in OW1

The console pass over `/support/` and `/contact/`, watching for Report-Only violations — especially on a real Give Lively payment step, whose deepest Stripe/PayPal origins were never inventoried. That needs a human driving a real payment flow with devtools open, so OW1 stays open.
