author: zkwizard
body:
## The gap

The `v1.1.0` tag exists (`610ef2a`, 2026-07-10) and shipped to the live site the same day — but there is **no GitHub release for it**:

```
$ gh release list
v1.0.1 - HD tiles in the right place   Latest   2026-07-09
v1.0.0 — the open Earth-observation globe        2026-07-08
```

So the Releases page has told every visitor "Latest: v1.0.1 (2026-07-09)" for 17 days, and `docs/launch/` holds release-notes files for `v0.2.0` and `v1.0.0` with **nothing for v1.1.0**. Anyone evaluating the project sees a repo whose newest published release predates its best work — the trend detection, the published accuracy validation, the citation chain.

This is the one awareness surface that is **not** an external venue: it lives on our own repo, so it is not blocked behind anyone's posting rules.

## What this adds

`docs/launch/release-notes-v1.1.0.md` — a pure release body, same shape as its two siblings so `--notes-file` takes it directly. Narrative rather than a changelog paste, leading with the two things that distinguish this project for a research audience:

1. **Seasonal Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope** — a real trend test with the seasonal correction, surfaced in the panel, the CSV, and on the chart.
2. **We published our own bad accuracy numbers** — the full `docs/validation.md` RMSE table (aerosol 0.13, SST 5.1 °C, soil 8.2 kg/m², air temp 19.0 K, precip 20.4 mm/day, LST no-data) with the honest "relative use, not absolute" reading and #170 named as the fix.

Then units/uncertainty/legends, the DOI + BibTeX/RIS + METHODS.md citation chain, the geolocation pin, and a contributor call-out.

**Every figure re-verified today** against `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/validation.md`, `METHODS.md`, and the tag range (`git log v1.0.1..v1.1.0` = 18 commits). The "314 → ~375 unit tests" and "22 → 44 contract assertions" spans are the two rounds combined, taken from the changelog's own round footers.

## ⛔ Not published — and gated for a sharper reason than the outbox drafts

The notes link the canonical `https://roamingeye.org/`, which still fails TLS today (re-measured: curl now reaches the host but gets `SEC_E_WRONG_PRINCIPAL` — GitHub's default `*.github.io` cert, so the hostname mismatches; `https_enforced: false`, Pages' own `html_url` is `http://`).

On top of that, **the release's own "You are here" feature cannot work while the site is plain-HTTP** — geolocation requires a secure context. Publishing now would announce a headline feature that is dead for every reader who tries it.

Publish after **Enforce HTTPS**, with:

```bash
gh release create v1.1.0 --title "v1.1.0 — measure the trend, and how much to trust it" --notes-file <(tail -n +8 docs/launch/release-notes-v1.1.0.md)
```

(`+8` strips the DRAFT comment and the H1, which becomes the title — verified against the formatted file.)

## Scope

Deliberately minimal: **one new file plus the log**. It does *not* edit `TARGETS.md` (not a venue) or `outbox/README.md` — the standing by-file check found **five** open comms PRs (#571, #573, #580, #593, #606) already queued on those two paths, and a sixth editor would only add conflicts. #606 is adding a `docs/launch/README.md` index and will pick this file up. Verified first that none of the 176 open PRs covers release notes.

Also measured, not acted on: there is **no Zenodo integration in the repo** (no `.zenodo.json`, no mention anywhere), so a GitHub release does not currently mint a DOI — worth knowing before anyone counts on it for the citation track.

Docs-only. No `src/`, no CI, no other specialist's domain.

author: aaronprobha18
body:
Fixes: #281 

## Changes
* Migrated all `datetime` usage in `fenn/logging.py`, `fenn/reproducibility.py`, `fenn/cli/pull.py`, `fenn/dashboard/app.py` and `fenn/dashboard/scanner.py` to the `whenever` library.
* Added `whenever>=0.10.3` to the project dependencies in `pyproject.toml`.
* Replaced `datetime.now()` and `datetime.now().replace(microsecond=0)` with `whenever` equivalents using `Instant`/`PlainDateTime` (`Instant.now().to_system_tz().to_plain()`).
* Replaced `datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc)` with `Instant.from_timestamp(ts)` for UTC log-entry timestamps.
* Replaced `datetime.strptime(...)` parsing (used for the session `started` field and the `/api/sessions` `started_after`/`started_before` query parameters) with `PlainDateTime.parse(..., format=...)`.
* Replaced the duration calculation (`(ended_at - started_at).total_seconds()`) with `PlainDateTime.difference(..., naive_arithmetic_ok=True).total("seconds")`.
* Replaced `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` in `fenn/cli/pull.py`'s template registry with a small `_isoformat_utc_now()` helper in `cli/utils.py`.

## Notes
* All formatting and parsing calls now use explicit `whenever` pattern strings (such as `"YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss"` and `"YYYYMMDD_hhmm"`) instead of relying on the library’s default string or ISO formatting. This is important because the default output includes a `T` separator and nanosecond precision with a `Z` UTC suffix, which would change the existing on-disk formats. By using explicit patterns, we ensure that all stored strings in `.fn` XML files, `.log` files, the template registry, and session IDs remain exactly byte-for-byte identical to what was produced by the previous standard library implementation.
* The `PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME` setting was intentionally left using the standard library `timedelta` because it is a Flask/Werkzeug configuration value. Flask internally expects a standard `datetime.timedelta` when calculating session expiration. Specifically, `SessionInterface.get_expiration_time` adds `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` to this value, and mixing it with `whenever.TimeDelta` would cause a type error since the two types are incompatible. For this reason, it must remain a standard library `timedelta` and is excluded from the migration.
* The `test_reproducibility.py` test for timestamp behavior was also updated because it previously mocked `fenn.reproducibility.datetime`, which no longer exists after switching to `whenever`. Timestamps are now generated using `Instant`, which is an immutable Rust-backed type and cannot be monkeypatched directly. As a result, the test was adjusted to mock the module-level `Instant` reference instead.

author: ploenk42
body:
Fixes the reported "3D sim doesn't place any robots".

## Reproduced

Chromium against a freshly started server, before anyone presses start: the arena, trees and nursery draw, the HUD reads `alive 0/0`, no robot and no boulder appear, and the net dropdown offers only `net: none`.

## Cause

The `world` message describes the arena, the trees and the sun. Where the bodies stand — and where pushed matter has ended up — is **frame** state. Frames came only from `_sim_loop`, which runs while `running` is set, and `running` is `False` on every boot. So a viewer arriving after a restart saw a world with nobody in it.

Because `running` is a module global, one viewer pressing start repaired the view for everyone — which is what made this look intermittent rather than broken.

`reset`, `arm` and `next_episode` all already push a frame after changing state. Connecting was the one path that did not.

## Change

- `SimulationRunner.frame()` reports current state **without advancing anything**, so connecting cannot cost a tick; `tick()` returns it instead of duplicating the call.
- `last_temps` starts at the ambient temperature where each body stands rather than 0 °C, since that value is now read off the opening frame before the first tick.
- `server.py` sends one frame after `world`/`auth`/`state`.
- `SCHEMA.md` documents the opening frame as part of the handshake rather than an implementation detail.

## Verification

Regression test asserts what the eye checks: a paused server places every robot, carries the matter, and does not step. Existing handshake tests updated for the new message.

Before / after, same fresh paused server: `alive 0/0` with an empty arena → `alive 3/3` with three bodies on the nursery and the net dropdown populated.

`166 passed`.

**Note on deployment:** the server only pulls a new image on boot, so this needs a `redeploy` run to go live. The currently-running image is also older than main — the two builds after `33c85cd5` failed on the stale lock, so nothing newer was published until today.

author: chordsnstrings
body:
## The problem

The crawler already visits up to four pages of each prospect's website to find an address — and threw the rest away. So the writer received six thin fields (name, URL, emirate, the search term we happened to use, a size guess, a mandate wave) and produced mail that could have gone to any company.

Worse: when the model call failed or returned unparseable JSON, it silently fell back to a hardcoded template **and sent it**. The generic email wasn't the writer's best attempt — it was the writer having failed with nobody noticing.

## What changed

**Keep the crawl data.** `crawlSite()` now returns page facts alongside contacts — title, meta description, headings, body text. Same pages, same budget, one extra pass over HTML already in memory.

**Extract facts in the call that already runs.** The Prospector's scoring pass now also pulls from the site: what they actually do (in their own terms), sectors served, locations, ERP/accounting systems named, and anything concrete and checkable. No extra model call. Stored on `prospects.siteDigest` and `prospects.profile` (migration 0009).

**Use the contact's name.** `prospect_contacts.name` was being stored and never used. Now passed through as a first name, with titles (`Dr`, `Eng`) and shared-mailbox words (`Sales`, `info`) rejected rather than used as a person's name.

**Rewritten personalisation rules** in the prompt: open with a specific verifiable detail, connect it to why a provider matters *for them*, never write "Dear Sir/Madam", write shorter rather than padding when facts are thin.

## Two guards against silent regression

`personalisationEvidence()` requires a draft to cite a detail **beyond the company name** — a fact from their site, their emirate, or the contact's name — and rejects template tells ("Dear Sir/Madam", "I hope this email finds you well", "As a leading…").

A term already present in the company's own name doesn't count. *Gulf Freight Systems* trivially contains "freight"; without that rule the check passes on its own input. **This was caught by a test failing, not by inspection.**

- A draft that fails the check never auto-sends regardless of approval mode — it waits for a human.
- A **first touch** that can't be personalised isn't sent at all: the thread is torn down and retried in 6 hours, by which time enrichment may have filled the gap.
- **Follow-ups** may still use the plain template — that recipient already got the personalised first email.

## Security

Website text is untrusted input reaching a prompt. It is fenced with explicit data-only framing, length-capped (3.5k), and stripped of scripts, styles and comments before use.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run` — **89 passed**; `next build` succeeds.
- 13 new tests across the evidence check, name parser and digest builder, including the self-matching case and a 50k-word hostile page.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

On team.openclaw.ai (~800 sessions, 3 agents), session switching pays 210-310ms warm for `chat.history`/`chat.startup` and ~93ms for `sessions.messages.subscribe`. A read-only cost map traced the slices: subscribe loads the whole session store to extract one config-derivable canonical key; `chat.history` structuredClones every store entry (O(800)) for a single-entry lookup, which also defeats the identity-keyed child-session index; `chat.startup` rebuilds pure config projections (agents list with per-agent git-checkout `existsSync` walks, startup metadata) per call; the model-catalog join uses the 750ms default budget instead of chat.startup's 25ms discipline; and an omission log serializes the full normalized payload per call even when nothing was omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each switch re-derived facts that are stable across calls (canonical keys, config projections) or paid store-wide costs for single-row needs. Fixing at the owning layers removes the cost for every caller rather than special-casing the chat path.

## User Impact

Session switching gets materially faster server-side: subscribe drops to config-only derivation (~0 store cost), chat.history stops cloning the store per call, chat.startup serves memoized projections, and history responses no longer block up to 750ms on a slow model catalog.

## Evidence

- B4: five diagnostics spans (`session_entry`, `model_catalog`, `history_page`, `startup_projections`, `session_info`) make remaining latency attributable.
- B1: subscribe/unsubscribe derive canonicalKey via `resolveSessionStoreKey` config-only; regression test proves no store load (spy), alias keys included.
- B2: single-entry reads use `loadExactSqliteSessionEntryReadOnly`-backed exact access, clone only the selected entry, preserve alias-linked children, and make the child-session candidate index actually hit (it previously always missed on fresh store identities). Consumer audit: borrowed entries feed read-only row builders only; default callers keep cloned entries; explicit `clone:false` callers keep their borrowed contract.
- B3: agents list + startup metadata memoized on runtime-config identity (client caps in key, reload-race protection).
- B5: chat.history joins the catalog with the same early-start + 25ms budget as chat.startup; degraded fields follow the existing contract.
- B6: omission-log bytes computed only when an omission occurred.
- Validation: 1,664 tests across the 40-file sweep, 228/228 in final affected suites, core typechecks, oxlint/oxfmt clean. Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30335162730. Autoreview: six findings fixed, one rejected with proof.

body:
## What is Tavily Hub?

Tavily Hub 是面向国内 AI 创作者的自建 Tavily 聚合网关 — 把多把 Tavily Key 合成一个动态号池，对外一个端点（thb- 开头），绕开官方免费档 1000 次/月的硬上限。

- 仓库：https://github.com/sharyuke/tavily-hub
- 官网：https://tavily.sharyuke.com

## 三大核心能力

1. **Credit 池 + 定时回充** — 池容量 + 每分钟回充，避开月度配额硬切
2. **多账号号池 + 自动负载均衡** — round_robin / weighted / least_used 在线热切换
3. **MCP streamableHTTP + SSE 双协议** — 一行配置接 Claude / Cursor / Cherry Studio 等 9 个客户端

## Connect

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tavily-hub": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://tavily.sharyuke.com/api/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "thb-<your-hub-key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

老版本客户端（pre-MCP-2025-03-26）把 URL 末尾加 `/sse` 即可。

## Entry

- Transport: streamable-http + sse
- Auth: API key (Hub key, thb- prefix) in Authorization header
- Category: Search
- Tools: `tavily_search`, `tavily_extract`, `tavily_crawl`

body:
## What changed

- adds a Test Suite-owned native Android runtime companion, bounded Android Debug Bridge controller, and row-specific evidence projector
- adds the general source-derived repair adapter and implementation prompt for any Candidate App and selected profile
- distinguishes install-artifact packaging, publication generation, remote acquisition, bounded caching, and catalog discovery
- adds a generic, content-format-agnostic RESPECT Publication Pack workflow
- derives a normalized manifest from explicitly confirmed repair-adapter lesson candidates and owner-supplied identity facts
- refuses candidates without truthful source-derived titles and refuses unconfirmed candidate inventories
- emits a complete static discovery and acquisition surface: CanApp descriptor, OPDS catalog, Readium manifests, acquisition pages, exact lesson bytes, covers, integrity declarations, and Android Digital Asset Links association
- emits deployment metadata, a JSON Schema, content-bound receipt, standalone cache-aware reference server, and container recipe
- extracts the package identifier and signing-certificate fingerprint directly from a supplied Android Package Kit and rejects package mismatch
- records provisional versus production status and rejects local production origins, debug production signers, and omitted production signer classification
- verifies every local artifact and relationship, then optionally verifies every deployed HTTPS byte, media type, content length, cache validator, and conditional `304 Not Modified` response
- keeps proprietary parsing and runtime integration in Candidate App-owned production code

## Publication Pack workflow

`publication-manifest` turns a confirmed source-derived inventory into a normalized, schema-backed manifest without learning the proprietary lesson format.

`publication-pack` emits the complete static publication plus deployment machinery and receipt. It accepts either a real signer fingerprint or an Android Package Kit from which the signer and package are inspected.

`publication-serve` provides the portable reference server with exact media types, content lengths, `Last-Modified`, content-derived entity tags, and conditional requests. Certificate and key inputs enable provisional local HTTPS; production may terminate HTTPS at an owner-controlled ingress.

`publication-verify` validates the pack locally. With a deployed origin it fetches every declared resource over HTTPS, compares every byte with the pack, validates headers, and requires a successful conditional request. A local certificate authority may be supplied only as an explicit provisional trust input.

## Mobile_KB proof

The generic analyzer found exactly the three real JiMSongs through Mobile_KB's source references. After explicit inventory confirmation, the generic Kit—not Mobile_KB's own generator—emitted the descriptor, catalog, three acquisition pages, three Readium manifests, three exact JiMSongs, three covers, association file, deployment contract, server, container recipe, schema, and receipt.

The Kit inspected the real debug Android Package Kit to obtain `org.jims.mobilekb` and its signer fingerprint. The deployed-origin verifier then fetched every emitted resource from the generic reference server over local HTTPS, confirmed every byte and required header, and received `304 Not Modified` for every conditional request.

The resulting repair adapter classifies Mobile_KB as `external_on_demand`: embedded false, on-demand acquisition true, bounded cache true, and catalog discovery true.

## Validation

- focused Publication Pack, command-line, repair-adapter, and schema tests: passed
- full pytest suite: 125 passed
- generic Mobile_KB Publication Pack: 3 real lessons, valid receipt
- deployed local HTTPS verification: every resource returned matching bytes and a valid conditional `304`
- Android Package Kit signer and package extraction: passed against the real Mobile_KB debug artifact
- source distribution and wheel builds: successful
- wheel distribution inspection: valid
- migration manifest validator: valid
- REUSE licensing check: 177/177 files compliant
- git diff --check: clean

author: willgriffin
body:
## Summary

Finishes the PostgreSQL backend collapse that #1149 started, and repairs the documentation and dead code it left behind.

- collapse `postgres-tests.yml`'s two structurally identical jobs into a single `postgres` job and remove the `backend` input from both `workflow_call` and `workflow_dispatch`
- rewrite the `.github/CI.md` PostgreSQL section so it describes the ephemeral-container model that actually exists
- delete `scripts/cleanup-ci-postgres.mjs` and its test
- remove the wrapper's runner-mounted-file fallback, the last shared-backend remnant in code, and add tests so the resulting two-source contract is enforced rather than asserted
- correct two false statements: the wrapper's "the janitor will remove it after six hours" drop-failure message, and the `required-ci` comment claiming the reusable workflow "scopes its suites internally"

### Why this is a re-land

#1157 was filed during review of #1149, and its premises did not hold on `main` at the time — `main`'s `shared` job had no service container, took its credential from the runner-mounted `/var/run/ci-services/postgres/url`, and **did** invoke the cleanup script. Landing the fix then would have deleted live, workflow-invoked code.

The fix was therefore prepared on top of #1149 and merged as #1161. But #1149 was squash-merged to `main` as 9ff8e4f at its pre-#1161 head, so #1161 landed on `codex/1148-runner-pool` after that branch had already served its purpose, and its content never reached `main`.

As of 9ff8e4f the issue's premises are all true on `main`, so this re-lands the same reviewed change directly:

- `postgres-tests.yml` has two jobs, `shared` and `service-container`, both on `arc-happyvertical` with the same digest-pinned `pgvector/pgvector:pg17@sha256:d2ef61f4…` container and the same `postgres`/`postgres` credentials
- `.github/CI.md` still describes a least-privilege shared credential (line 98), a nightly cleanup of databases older than six hours (line 96), a shared-backend manual run (line 103), and a service-container fallback (line 153)
- no workflow on `main` invokes `scripts/cleanup-ci-postgres.mjs`

The diff is identical to the one reviewed on #1161; `main`'s tree was byte-identical to #1149's head, so it cherry-picked without conflict.

## The collapse

Both jobs are the same mechanism under two names: same `runs-on`, same image digest, same credentials, same steps. The gate simplifies from `inputs.backend != 'service-container' && (dispatch || enabled)` to `dispatch || enabled`, equivalent for every trigger — `workflow_call` never passed `backend`, and on `workflow_dispatch` both branches ran a byte-identical job. Caller-visible results are unchanged: with `CI_POSTGRES_ENABLED` unset the reusable workflow still reports `skipped`, which `required-ci` still forgives.

## Documentation

The old section described a least-privilege shared credential, a nightly cleanup of abandoned CI databases older than six hours, and a shared→service-container fallback. None of those exist. The rewrite states only what the code does, and deliberately makes no claim it cannot support:

- the container is created and destroyed with the job, and that is the whole retention model
- the credentials are public constants granting superuser inside one throwaway container, worth nothing *as a secret* — **not** "confer nothing beyond that job", which would have been an unverifiable confinement claim given `ports: ['5432:5432']` and broker capacity that CI.md intentionally leaves unspecified
- the per-suite unique database is namespacing, not privilege separation (all suites connect as the same superuser), and a failed drop only writes to stderr — no Actions annotation, suite still passes — so a leak appears in the raw log and nowhere else
- every trigger runs the complete registry; this lane has no affected-closure mode, so `postgres-scope` only decides whether a skipped result is forgiven
- `CI_POSTGRES_ENABLED` gates the reusable call **and** the nightly schedule, so while unset the lane never runs *automatically* — `workflow_dispatch` still runs it, as does the dispatch-only smoke test
- broker-selected capacity must support service containers — a requirement that became load-bearing once a container was the only backend, and which #1149 had dropped

## The orphaned script, and one more remnant

`cleanup-ci-postgres.mjs` is invoked by nothing and referenced only by its own test, which keeps passing and implies coverage that is not there. Both files are gone.

Removing it exposes a second problem worth fixing in the same pass. `run-with-ci-postgres.mjs` fell back to `/var/run/ci-services/postgres/url` whenever `CI_POSTGRES_BASE_URL` was empty, and returned a **managed** connection — so a job that forgot the variable would silently create and drop databases on a shared server. With no janitor, any interrupted run on that path would leak `sdk_ci_*` databases that nothing reclaims, which is precisely the retention story the rewritten docs declare impossible. Both workflows set the variable explicitly and no test covered the branch, so it is now `CI_POSTGRES_BASE_URL` (managed) or `DATABASE_URL` (unmanaged), else throw. `CI_POSTGRES_BASE_URL_FILE` is dropped from `turbo.json` accordingly.

Because that invariant is security-relevant, it is now tested rather than merely documented: `resolveBaseUrl` is exported and pinned by three cases (managed only from `CI_POSTGRES_BASE_URL`; `DATABASE_URL` unmanaged and never outranking it; fail-closed when neither is set). Verified by mutation rather than assumed — reintroducing the `readFileSync` branch fails two of the three whenever the credential file is present, and is correctly inert when it is absent. Net script coverage is up despite the two deleted tests: 21 cases versus 20 before.

## Validation

- `pnpm test:ci-scripts` — 28/28 pass after the rebase (21 here plus the 7 `select-pnpm-store` cases #1159 added)
- `pnpm agent:check` — exit 0
- `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0
- `pnpm lint` — exit 0
- `pnpm build` — exit 0
- `yamllint -c .github/.yamllint.yml` and `actionlint` on both changed workflows
- `node --check scripts/run-with-ci-postgres.mjs`
- lefthook pre-commit (`validate-workflows`, incl. `act --list`) and commit-msg hooks
- two-reviewer review cycle on the full diff (on #1161, same diff); all material findings accepted and fixed, both reviewers ending clean

### Rebase onto `main` (49a6e86)

Both failures on the previous head were external to this diff, and both are now
fixed on `main`:

- `Validate Changes / Run Tests` failed on `@happyvertical/weather#test`, whose
  `environment-canada.spec.ts` called the live Environment Canada API. This PR
  touches no weather code. Fixed by #1168 (a798aa15).
- `Validate Workflow Files` failed on `error: externally-managed-environment`
  and then a missing `/root/.local/bin/yamllint`, breaking every
  workflow-touching PR repo-wide. Fixed by #1159 (49a6e865).

The test job checks out the PR head in isolation rather than a merge with
`main`, so a re-run alone could not pick either fix up; the branch had to
contain them. Rebased onto 49a6e865 with no conflicts — #1159 edits
`on-pull-request.yml` around line 367 and the runner/pnpm-store part of
`CI.md`, while this PR edits line ~689 and the PostgreSQL section. Verified the
patch body is byte-identical before and after the rebase, and that #1159's
`command -v yamllint` guard and its pnpm-store documentation both survive
intact.

The `@happyvertical/geo` `TS2322` line in `pnpm build` output is pre-existing and appears identically on an untouched base; no TypeScript is changed here.

No runner backend activation, capacity change, or production cutover was performed. `CI_POSTGRES_ENABLED` remains unset, so this lane stays skipped-and-forgiven until someone enables it deliberately.

Resolves #1157

author: pixexid
body:
Related #310. Documentation only.

Three acceptance items from #310 had no artifact: the enrolled-repository inventory with owners, the per-repo 0–3 incident-rule audit, and the usefulness/noise re-check after representative PRs. `projects.json` is a project→repo map with no ownership and no enrollment semantics, so it does not discharge any of them.

## Lane contract

Written late — this branch predates contract v5 — and recorded here so the exact-head review verifies the diff against it rather than discovering it.

**Lane.** #310 acceptance items 1–3: record which repositories are enrolled in path-scoped review, who owns each enrollment, and what the first noise re-check found.

**Authority boundary.** Each repository's own `AGENTS.md` is the sole authority for its incident-derived rules. This table is an index, never a second copy — it records *where* rules live and *how many*, and holds no rule text. `projects.json` is the authority for repository identity and release-gate ownership.

**Commit point.** The merge of this PR to `llm-collab` `main`. Nothing else reads or caches the table.

**Retry behavior.** None — the change is a static document with no runtime path.

**Non-goals.** Does not create, change, or restate any repository's review rules. Does not discharge item 1 of #310 on its own: that needs the companion `amiga` change to land. Does not make the table self-updating; the re-check is explicitly dated and scheduled by prose.

## What this adds to `AGENTS.md`

**`### Enrolled repositories`** — a four-row table: repository, owner, rule count with names, and where the rules live.

| Repository | Owner | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `llm-collab` | codex | 3 (`## Code Review Rules` below) |
| `amiga` | codex | 2 — paid/provider idempotency + replace-lock authority; public Supabase RPC role execution — **not on `main` yet** |
| `amiga_house_cleaning_company_docs` | codex | 0 — content repository, no executable surface |
| `nuvyr_app` | kimi | 0 — no adjudicated incident yet |

It points at repo-local authority rather than restating any rule. A restated rule is a cached copy that goes stale silently — the failure `## This file is the source of truth` exists to prevent, and the one that let eight memory files teach a `deliver.py` invocation that dropped 27 packets.

**`### Rule usefulness and noise re-check`** — recorded against the first representative run under manual-only review: PRs #340, #342, #345, #348, sixteen connector findings across nine requested exact-head reviews. Every independently reproduced finding was real; none was rule noise, so no rule is removed. Two observations recorded without acting on them: findings clustered in Tier A families the rules already name, and several rounds found test artefacts masking production behaviour — #306's "test-only is not intrinsically low risk", holding up a second time.

## Changes since the previous requested head (`9db059d`)

Rebased onto contract v5 (`b1c55c9`) — clean, no conflict; the section's anchors (`## This file is the source of truth`, `#306`) are unchanged under v5. Then two table facts corrected after checking them against the repositories:

- The `amiga` row pointed at `### Code Review Rules` in that repo's `AGENTS.md`. That heading exists only on the unmerged branch `claude/gh310-manual-review-policy`; `origin/main` there has none. A pointer to a section nobody can open is the failure this table was written to avoid, so the row now names the branch and says it is not on main.
- The `nuvyr_app` row named codex as owner. `projects.json` gives nuvyr a `release_gate_agent` of `kimi`, the only ownership signal the workspace records.

## Verification at `f9a038bee234e1af75c898c9c363d334e1ee7acb`

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — **1856 tests, 1 failure**: `test_inbox.InboxMarkAllReadTest::test_exact_session_requires_runtime_identity`.
- **Measured against baseline.** `origin/main` at `b1c55c9` was run in a separate detached worktree with the same interpreter: identical 1856 tests, same single failure. This diff introduces nothing.
- That failure is host-dependent and pre-existing, from #351: the test asserts the `exact_session_runtime_missing` branch, but on any host where `activation_reader_runtime_id()` resolves a real runtime session it falls through to `exact_session_runtime_mismatch` instead. It passes only on a machine with no live Claude/Codex session — i.e. not on a worker's. Follow-up issue filed; not fixed here (documentation-only lane).
- Environment note: the workspace had no interpreter with `jsonschema`/`watchdog` installed, which silently degraded the suite to 1700 tests with 131 failures and 31 errors. Repaired locally with a 3.11 venv from `requirements-runtime.txt` + `requirements-dev.txt`; both numbers above are from the repaired environment.
- `git diff --check` clean; the diff is `AGENTS.md` only.

## Not in this PR

The companion `amiga` change (rewriting the two "rely on automatic review" instructions and adding that repo's Tier A/B/C rule and two incident rules) is a separate repository and a separate PR, on branch `claude/gh310-manual-review-policy` at `539d51b`.

Issue #310 stays open: item 1 is only discharged once the amiga change lands.

author: mathr81
body:
Follow-up fixes to make the standalone page more faithful to the extension.

## 🔍 Letter "doublure" on Blink (Chrome/Vivaldi/Android), not WebKit
Root cause found: `background-clip: text` clips an element's gradient to the union of **all descendant glyphs**. The *container* elements — the syllable `.line` (text lives in child `.word`/`.letterGroup`/`.dot`), the `.letterGroup` (text lives in child `.letter`s), and the musical `.line` (interlude dots live in a `.dotGroup`) — each paint that clipped copy at the **container's** transform, while every child word/letter/dot also paints itself at its **own** independently-animated transform. Blink's compositor lands these in separate layers → a static ghost behind the moving glyphs. WebKit composites them together (hence fine on Orion/iPad).

Previous attempts (de-promoting via `will-change`/`backface-visibility`) couldn't work because the animator forces `translate3d` inline every frame.

**Fix:** blank the container's own gradient fill (`background-image: none`) so only leaf text paints. Line-mode and Static lines hold their text directly (no `.word` child) and are left untouched. Verified in headless: active line renders with the karaoke sweep, non-active lines stay visible (they render via their 0-blur text-shadow).

## 📜 iOS scroll lag-then-jump
The engine locks `scroll-behavior: smooth` with a 3-class selector that out-specified the previous `.iOS` override, so smooth scrolling (which iOS defers inside momentum containers) stayed on. Mirror that selector shape (+ `.iOS`) so instant scrolling actually wins.

## 📱 iOS bottom playback controls invisible
Only the top ViewControls + timeline showed on the cover. The bottom row (shuffle/prev/play/next/loop) sizes through a nested container-query chain (`container-type: size` inside `container-type: size`) that iOS resolves unreliably, zeroing the buttons' height. Pin concrete heights straight off `.MediaBox` and drop the intermediate size container, scoped to `.iOS`.

## 🔘 Cover round buttons
Add the extension's ViewControls for **swapping the cover/lyrics sides** (`NowBarSideToggle`) and **toggling compact mode** (`CompactModeToggle`), wired to the reused engine layout (a manual compact toggle overrides the automatic narrow-viewport heuristic).

## 🖥️ Desktop Document PiP
Now opens the extension's **compact PiP composition** (small cover + metadata above full-width lyrics, inside `.spicy-pip-wrapper` + `ForcedCompactMode`) instead of the wide cover-on-the-side layout, restoring the prior state on close.

## Verification
- `bun run web:build` green; lint clean (only pre-existing warnings).
- Headless Chromium screenshots confirm: lyrics render correctly (no visibility regression), all six cover buttons present in the DOM, compact/portrait layout fills the width.
- ⚠️ Needs on-device confirmation (headless can't reproduce): real-GPU Chrome doubling removal, iOS scroll, iOS bottom-controls visibility.

## What changed

- Added a native C++/WinRT GATT server binding for Windows.
- Added radio-state tracking, advertising lifecycle handling, dynamic services, characteristics and descriptors, read/write requests, notifications, indications, subscriptions, MTU updates, and connection lifecycle events.
- Made the WinRT binding the default on `win32`; the raw HCI backend remains available with `withBindings('hci')`.
- Added Windows build targets, binding resolution, TypeScript declarations, documentation, and service-setup error regression coverage.
- Documented manual `withBindings('win')` selection, handle-specific disconnects, platform requirements, supported features, and native API limitations.
- Hardened the shared thread-safe callback lifecycle used by native bindings.

## Why

Windows previously defaulted to raw HCI access, which requires a dedicated adapter and WinUSB driver. The native binding uses the normal Windows Bluetooth stack and exposes bleno's peripheral APIs through WinRT.

## Impact

Windows users with an adapter that supports the Bluetooth LE peripheral role can use the system Bluetooth driver. Raw EIR and iBeacon advertising, application-controlled local names, and peer RSSI reads are not available through this binding; these limitations are documented.

- GitHub Build matrix passed, including native Windows x86 and x64 compilation, prebuild generation, and artifact upload.
- GitHub Test / Lint matrix passed on Node 18 and 20 across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

author: luismutec
body:
Monta la base para recibir usuarios autenticados: proyecto de Supabase, login con Google restringido a cuentas `@utec.edu.pe` y la sesión en cookies siguiendo la convención `proxy.ts` de Next 16. No hay UI ni cambios en `page.tsx`: el login es opcional y la app funciona exactamente igual sin sesión. Rutas: `GET /auth/login`, `GET /auth/callback`, `POST /auth/signout` y una página mínima de error.

Es infra, no una feature con comportamiento visible, así que no lleva spec. Las decisiones y su porqué quedan en [`docs/auth.md`](docs/auth.md).

## Decisiones de implementación

- **El dominio se valida en tres capas** porque ninguna alcanza sola: `hd=utec.edu.pe` en la URL de Google (comodidad, es quitable desde el navegador), el hook `Before User Created` en Postgres (la barrera real del alta, corre solo al crear el usuario) y una revalidación en el callback (cubre a alguien que ya existiera con otro correo).
- **El SQL del hook no sale de la doc oficial de Supabase**: su ejemplo compara `lower(domain) = lower($1)`, donde `$1` es el `event jsonb` completo y no el dominio, y falla abierto si no encuentra match. La versión de acá es una allowlist estricta de un dominio que falla cerrado.
- **La allowlist es exacta, no un sufijo.** `endsWith('utec.edu.pe')` dejaría pasar `@notutec.edu.pe`. `@alumno.utec.edu.pe` queda fuera a propósito.
- **`getClaims()` en vez de `getSession()`/`getUser()`**, que valida la firma del JWT en lugar de confiar en la cookie.
- **Ningún cliente de Supabase en scope de módulo**: con Fluid compute las instancias se reúsan entre requests y filtrarían la sesión de un usuario a otro.
- **Sin variables de entorno la app compila y corre igual**, porque el job `build` del CI no tiene secretos. `updateSession` sale temprano si faltan.
- **El `matcher` del proxy se amplía de `/api` a todas las rutas menos estáticos**, porque el refresco del token tiene que correr también en las páginas. El rate limit sigue aplicando solo a `/api`; se extrajo a `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` para poder testearlo.

## Coverage

El trinquete sube a `lines 29.47 / statements 29.34 / functions 25.69 / branches 21.4`. Los tests nuevos cubren la allowlist de dominio, el rate limit (que estaba en 0% y ya existía), el origen del request y el matcher del proxy.

## Verificación

Las cuatro compuertas del CI pasan en local, incluido `pnpm build` con `.env.local` fuera para replicar el runner sin secretos.

El flujo se probó end-to-end en local contra el proyecto real, partiendo de `auth.users` vacío. Los logs de auth de Supabase encadenan `/authorize` → hook (`success: true`) → `user_signedup` → `POST /token` con `grant_type: pkce`. Quedó una fila con `email_verified: true` y el `sub` de Google en `auth.identities.provider_id`. El `code` no sobrevive al redirect: `GET /auth/callback?code=… 307` → `GET / 200` sin el parámetro. Y `getClaims()` valida de verdad — en los logs aparece la descarga de `/.well-known/jwks.json`, o sea que verifica la firma en vez de confiar en la cookie.

`POST /auth/signout` responde 303, el navegador sigue con `GET /`, y las sesiones y refresh tokens quedan en 0 sin borrar el usuario.

El rechazo de una cuenta fuera del dominio también se probó por el navegador. El hook corta el alta y su mensaje viaja entero hasta la UI: `GET /auth/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=Solo+se+permiten+cuentas+%40utec.edu.pe.` → `GET /auth/error 200`. No se creó fila en `auth.users`. Aparte, el hook está validado por SQL contra 8 casos borde (mayúsculas, subdominios, `@utec.edu.pe.evil.com`, sin `@`, vacío).

Un detalle que salió de la prueba: el claim `hd` llega correctamente, pero Supabase lo anida en `raw_user_meta_data.custom_claims.hd`. No afecta a nada acá porque la autorización va por el correo, no por `hd`.

## Fuera de alcance

Tabla `profiles`, RLS, persistencia de horarios en la base, y cualquier UI de sesión (botón de login, avatar). Cuando llegue la tabla de perfiles, la llave es el UUID de `auth.users` y nunca el correo — Google avisa que el correo puede cambiar y no es único.

author: rekkaindio
body:
The definer-RPC lint baseline drifted from ~31 to 87 as new functions landed without grant hygiene (Postgres auto-grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function). Auditing the function bodies rather than the counts surfaced three real gaps hiding in a warning list we had already agreed to ignore.

Authorisation fixes:

- vault_has_access performed no authorisation at all. Any signed-in user could ask it about any other user; verified live that a non-admin, non-cohort caller got `true` for Vault cohort members. Gated internally rather than by revoking, because the admin UserProfile page calls it as authenticated. The `auth.uid() is not null` term is load-bearing: five internal/cron callers and a service_role edge function run with no JWT.

- close_gym_visit applied its ownership scope to the UPDATE only. The follow-up INSERT used the caller-supplied p_visit_id unguarded, so an authenticated user could forge an 'exit' event onto another user's visit, where it rendered in the victim's timeline on the admin UserProfile page. Guarded with an ownership predicate rather than `if not found`, so repeat closes of the caller's own visit still log and existing telemetry behaviour is unchanged.

- get_taken_grid_cells gated its non-admin branch on a global feature flag with no brand-membership check. Not currently exploitable (the flag reads false), but flipping it on would have exposed every brand's occupied ad-inventory map to any authenticated user. Tightened rather than revoked, since it is the sole data source for the shared PlacementGridMap.

Grant hygiene:

- Revoked the dead API grants on six trigger functions. They cannot be invoked over the API at all (plpgsql rejects them at compile time, PostgREST excludes trigger-returning functions from its schema cache), and EXECUTE on a trigger function is only checked at CREATE TRIGGER time, so the triggers are unaffected. This restores the convention already applied to the other ten.

- Removed anon EXECUTE from eleven user-scoped RPCs that already reject a null auth.uid(), so the internal check is no longer the only thing standing there.

- Dropped the redundant anon/authenticated table grants on four service-role-only tables. RLS with no policy was already denying correctly, but it was the sole barrier in front of reward_brand_shopify's live access and refresh tokens.

Applied to production as 20260727153603; filename matches that version. Lints 91 -> 68, anon-executable definer functions 18 -> 1. The remaining one is is_admin(), a deliberate keeper: RLS policies on partners/rewards/waitlist/ profiles evaluate it as the querying role for anonymous landing-page reads.

Verified post-apply: all six triggers still attached and enabled; vault_has_access still works for self, admins, service_role and the JWT-less cron path while raising cross-user; get_my_vault_access unaffected on app load.

author: rerankerguo
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes #236 by making the embedding batch size configurable per provider.

## Changes
- Added `maxBatchSize` to `OpenAIEmbeddingConfig` so users can set provider-specific batch limits
- Lowered default from 256 to 64 to avoid exceeding Tencent API limit of 10 items per request
- Updated both `OpenAIEmbeddingService` and `ZeroEntropyEmbeddingService` to use the configurable batch size
- Documented known provider limits (Tencent: 10, OpenAI: 2048, DashScope: 10)

## Problem
The hardcoded `MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 256` exceeded the Tencent Embedding API limit of 10 items per request, causing silent failures for users of Tencent's embedding service.

## Solution
- Replaced the hardcoded constant with a configurable `maxBatchSize` in the embedding config
- Set a safe default of 64 that works across most providers
- Users with known provider limits (e.g., Tencent) can now configure `maxBatchSize: 10` explicitly

## BREAKING CHANGE
Default batch size changed from 256 to 64. Users with high-throughput providers (e.g., OpenAI) who relied on the larger batch size should set `maxBatchSize: 256` (or higher) explicitly if they need the previous throughput.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] The fix is minimal and focused on the issue
- [x] Both embedding services updated (OpenAI and ZeroEntropy)
- [x] Backward compatible: existing configs without maxBatchSize will use the new safe default

author: ionfwsrijan
body:
## Summary

Prevents permanent CSRF token null when the `<meta name="csrf-token">` tag exists but lacks a `content` attribute, allowing the fetch-based token retrieval to execute.

## Problem

In `src/lib/apiClient.js`, when the meta tag exists without a `content` attribute, `getAttribute('content')` returns `null`. This null is cached permanently. On every subsequent call, the code finds the meta tag, caches null, and returns — the fetch path that would retrieve a valid CSRF token is never reached. All state-changing requests proceed without a CSRF token, causing 403 errors.

## Fix

- Added a truthy check on the `content` value before caching and returning
- When the meta tag exists but has no content, execution falls through to the fetch-based token retrieval

## Testing

- Verified that a meta tag without `content` no longer blocks CSRF token fetch
- No change when meta tag has a valid content attribute

Closes #3991

author: zakkaus
body:
## 一、`reap` 会删错文件

`reap` 用 `rglob(f)` 按文件名找路径，而 `rglob` 把参数当模式。用旧实现实测：

```
孤儿 'pkg-?.tar.gz'     报告删掉 ['pkg-?.tar.gz']，磁盘上它还在
                        被删的是无辜的 pkg-1.tar.gz
孤儿 'a-[1.0].tar.gz'   报告删掉 []，文件永远清不掉
```

线上目前没有带 `[ ] ? *` 的文件名，所以它一直没暴露。改成用调用方已经列好的路径删。

这是仓库里唯一会删 distfiles 的代码，而 distfiles 是上游撤了就取不回来的原件，此前它没有任何测试。新增 `build/test-audit-distfiles.py`，九个用例进 CI。

## 二、告警越需要发的时候越发不出去

Telegram 拒收超过 4096 字的消息，`curl -f` 因此非零退出，而整个发送被 `|| true` 吞掉。告警正文随失败包数增长，所以一轮里坏的包越多，消息越长，越发不出去。

超过 3500 字截断并标明，发送失败改成写进构建日志而不是静默返回。

## 三、`status.sh` 看不见 distfiles

五项检查没有一项碰 distfiles。每小时的同步整个停掉——cron 被删、机器卡住——两台机器都查不出来。

`distfiles-status.json` 是每轮同步结束时写的，用它的年龄回答同步还在不在跑。阈值六小时：同步每小时一轮，六小时够区分「一轮慢了」和「不跑了」。

author: nabilaldhamari
body:
Three defects found while chasing "prayer times are unstable and inaccurate", plus the reference tests that would have caught them. Rebuilt on top of #8/#9/#10 — the masjid-matching work there is untouched and this does not overlap it.

## Settings reverted on their own, and the city came back as Makkah

`onChangeSettings` handed the store a whole `Settings` value captured when the screen composed, so a write applied whatever that snapshot held rather than a change to what was stored. A second tap undid the first, and a tap made before the stored settings had been read carried `city = null`, which removes all eight city keys and falls back to the compiled-in Makkah.

Reading positions make this constant rather than occasional — `onRemember` writes on every rest of the scroll. Actions now carry an edit, `(Settings) -> Settings`, so the bug is no longer representable. `onChangeCity` already did this correctly, which is why the picker mostly worked and everything else drifted.

Nothing is drawn until the stored settings load, so the default city's times are never shown under another city's name.

## Fajr and ʿIshāʾ were an hour or more out above ~48°

`HighLatitudeRule.recommended()` took no coordinates and always answered `MIDDLE_OF_NIGHT`. adhan applies that rule as a floor at *every* latitude, so it drove Fajr and ʿIshāʾ together wherever the sun stops reaching the twilight angles. Against the London Unified timetable on 27 July 2026 it put Fajr 81 minutes early and ʿIshāʾ 97 late; the last seventh of the night puts ʿIshāʾ within 4.

`inferProfile` now takes the city, and the rule follows `abs(latitude)` so the southern hemisphere gets it too. Only the *inferred* profile changes — a matched masjid profile keeps whatever rule the solve recovered.

`timingProfileFor` also stopped defaulting an unchosen madhhab to Shāfiʿī after `inferProfile` had just put Ḥanafī there for PK/IN/BD, which moved ʿAṣr by up to 78 minutes for anyone who never opened Settings.

## Tests that check something we did not generate

Every prayer fixture was adhan's own output at two low-latitude cities, so the suite proved we drive the library the way its authors do and nothing about correctness. It was green throughout.

- **Method angles** pinned to the table praytimes.org publishes.
- **London** checked against the London Unified Prayer Timetable as East London Mosque prints it for 2026 — eight days across midwinter, midsummer and both sides of the BST boundary. With the margins that timetable states openly (sunrise −3, Ẓuhr +5 from transit, Maghrib +3) the astronomy matches within a minute on seven of eight days, two on 31 October. Both madhāhib land: Mithl 1 and Mithl 2 are printed separately.

Fajr and ʿIshāʾ are deliberately **not** asserted against a method — that timetable takes them from Hizbul Ulama, not a sun angle, so nothing we compute reproduces them and a test claiming otherwise would be bending the reference to fit us. The measured gap is pinned instead: ʿIshāʾ inside 20 minutes all year, Fajr −22 in midwinter to +55 in early July.

author: lacker
body:
`complete_graph_zero_forcing_number_lt`: given two distinct vertices, the zero forcing number of the
complete graph is strictly below the vertex count. All but one vertex is a zero forcing set — the
single white vertex is adjacent to every blue one, so each of them sees it as its only white
neighbour, and one round finishes.

Also adds two general finite-set lemmas that were missing. `src/finite_set/` defines `fs_remove`
through the underlying set but states the membership rule only at the `Set` level, so
`fs_remove_contains_eq` lifts it — the same service `fs_insert_contains_eq` already performs for
insertion — and `fs_remove_subset` follows.

**On what is and is not proved.** This is the upper bound only. The matching lower bound — that no
smaller set works, giving equality with `fs_card(s) - 1` — is a separate statement and I have
recorded it as its own item rather than claiming the exact value. The argument is that two white
vertices leave every blue vertex with two white neighbours and nothing can force, but stating it
requires producing a second white vertex from a cardinality gap, which is a different kind of step
from anything here. The hypothesis of two distinct vertices is likewise real rather than
convenient: with fewer there is no blue vertex to do the forcing.

`acorn check --strict` passes.

## Summary

Completes the testing plan (Phase 4). Builds on the unit suite already in `main` with a recognition/decoding regression gate, fuzzing, and CI — turning the review work into something that stays fixed.

### Regression corpus (`make corpus`)

`tests/corpus/` holds **11 committed PNG images** — numeric/alpha/byte modes, all four ECC levels, versions 1–10, mild 10°/25°/45° rotations, and a small-module/large-quiet-zone case — plus a manifest of expected payloads. `check_corpus.c` reuses the `dbgutil` PNG loader to run the full identify+decode pipeline over each image and verify the **exact decoded payload**. `gen_corpus.py` regenerates the images from an independent encoder, but the images are committed so the check needs no Python. All 11 decode correctly.

### Fuzzing (`make fuzz CC=clang`)

Two libFuzzer harnesses in `tests/fuzz/`:
- `fuzz_decode` — fuzzed `quirc_code` → `quirc_decode` + `quirc_flip` (RS/format/payload paths)
- `fuzz_identify` — fuzzed grayscale image → full `quirc_begin/end/extract/decode` pipeline

## Summary

- Fixed the `RelationSelector` component to use `onChange(null)` instead of `onChange(undefined)` when clearing a single-select relation

When clearing a single-select relation field in the Dashboard, the component was calling `onChange(undefined)`. Since `undefined` values don't serialize in JSON, the GraphQL API would ignore the clearing request, causing previously selected values to persist on the server.

Changed `onChange(undefined)` to `onChange(null)` which properly serializes to JSON and allows the GraphQL API to receive and process the null value, effectively clearing the relation field.

author: deathgun44
body:
## What this PR does

Migrates the **group and center integration tests** from the old REST-assured HTTP client to the typed Feign SDK client

## Why

The old tests call the server with hand-written REST-assured requests and read untyped JSON. Moving them onto the generated Feign client gives typed requests and responses, so the tests are safer to change and consistent with the rest of the migrated suite.

## What changed

**Test classes migrated**
- `CenterIntegrationTest` 
- `GroupTest` 
- `GroupLoanIntegrationTest` 

**New typed helpers**:
- `FeignGroupHelper`, `FeignCenterHelper`, `FeignStaffHelper`, `FeignGlimHelper`

**Removed the old stopgap:**
- Deleted `FeignGroupCenterHelper` (a raw-HTTP helper from an earlier PR) and repointed its two users `LoanReschedulingWithinCenterTest` and `ExternalIdSupportIntegrationTest` - at the new typed helpers.

**Production change (minimal, additive):**
- Added the missing fields to `PostGroupsRequest` and `PostCentersRequest` in the Swagger DTOs so groups and centers can be created through the typed model. These are additive only - the API wire format is unchanged.

**Production change (minimal, additive):**
- Added the missing fields to the Swagger DTOs so groups, centers, clients and loans can be driven through the typed model: the creation fields, the `?command=...` request fields, the `changes` objects those commands return, the retrieval fields the tests assert on, and the group / GLIM fields on the loan application and approve bodies. Touches `GroupsApiResourceSwagger`, `CentersApiResourceSwagger`, `ClientsApiResourceSwagger` and `LoansApiResourceSwagger`.
- These are additive only - no field removed, no type or `required` changed, and the API wire format is unchanged. The backward-compatibility check against develop reports no breaking changes.

## Raw HTTP is gone

No `FeignRawHttpHelper` and no REST-assured remain in the migrated code - every request and response goes through the generated Feign models, including the `?command=...` endpoints and the GLIM application / approve / retrieval flow. Retrieval no longer needs the REST-assured-era `CenterDomain` POJO either.

One case is still bound by hand, but stays typed: `GET /centers` and `GET /groups` return a plain JSON array unless `paged=true`, and an operation can only declare one response schema (the paged one), so the generated `retrieveAllCenters` / `retrieveAllGroups` can't decode the array. Rather than document the endpoint incorrectly, those requests are bound to the generated page-item models through a small Feign interface, `NonPagedListingApi` - the same pattern as the existing `InternalExternalEventsApi`.

`paged=true` is not an equivalent substitute there: `retrievePagedAll` ignores `orphansOnly`, so the paged variant returns every group of the office. That is documented on the interface.

No assertion was weakened and no REST-assured was introduced.

## Checklist

- [ ] Write the commit message as per [our guidelines](https://github.com/apache/fineract/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests)
- [ ] Acknowledge that we will not review PRs that are not passing the build _("green")_ - it is your responsibility to get a proposed PR to pass the build, not primarily the project's maintainers.
- [ ] Create/update [unit or integration tests](https://fineract.apache.org/docs/current/#_testing) for verifying the changes made.
- [ ] Follow our [coding conventions](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/FINERACT/Coding+Conventions).

- [ ] [This PR must not be a "code dump"](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/FINERACT/Pull+Request+Size+Limit). Large changes can be made in a branch, with assistance. Ask for help on the [developer mailing list](https://fineract.apache.org/#contribute).

author: fabioneves
body:
Two changes: the transcription-error fix your engine session just hit, and the README refresh.

## No model transcribes a SHA again

Your session invented the eighth character of a head OID in a review prompt; the reviewer refused to attach a closing verdict to a revision it couldn't match (correct — and worth noting the review contract caught it), costing ~10 minutes of reviewer time. That is a transcription no model should be asked to perform, so it no longer has to.

`dispatch.mjs` now appends an `autoloop-dispatch-context-v1` stamp it derives **itself** from the checkout it is about to launch in:

```
<!-- autoloop-dispatch-context-v1
role: code-review
revision: 37d4ff0e45d87e41ea265960cbeafb02a5959727
checkout: clean
This stamp is written by dispatch.mjs from the checkout it launched in.
It is the authority for the revision under review; a revision named
anywhere else in this prompt that disagrees with it is a transcription
error, and this stamp wins.
-->
```

So a review prompt never needs to state a head, and if one is stated and disagrees, the machine-supplied value wins rather than the round dying. Fail-open by design: an unreadable checkout stamps nothing rather than failing a dispatch that would otherwise run. The skill gains the matching rule — a 40-hex OID is copied from the tool result that produced it or supplied by the machine, never read off an earlier line.

Self-test pins the stamp reaching the engine's stdin with the real head, the dirty-tree case, and the fail-open case (43 → 46).

## README describes the v0.49 loop

Steps 2 and 6 were still documented as orchestrator work. Now: the pipeline table names the fresh planner and fresh simplifier, the invariant-first planning rule and same-predicate escalation are stated, the per-step model/effort division is a table with its reasoning, the `plan` role and `--model`/`--effort` flags are in the dispatch surface, and the live-watchable dispatch pane is described.

v0.49.9 literals + CHANGELOG; full verify green.

author: mremond
body:
A pull request now pays only for the CI jobs its diff can break: a docs-only PR runs nothing, a Rust-only PR skips the Node and Playwright jobs, and a TypeScript-only PR skips the two Rust jobs.

`scripts/ci-changed-scopes.sh` maps a list of changed paths to two booleans, `js` and `rust`. A new `changes` job fetches the PR's file list from the GitHub API — the diff GitHub itself computes, so it is immune to force-pushes, rebases and shallow clones — pipes it through the classifier, and publishes the result as job outputs. The four existing jobs gain `needs` and an `if` guard; none of their steps change.

Two properties the classifier must keep, both covered by `scripts/ci-changed-scopes.test.sh`:

- **Fail-safe.** A path matching no explicit rule enables both scopes, so forgetting a pattern can only waste minutes (free on a public repo), never silence a job.
- **Rule order is load-bearing.** `apps/fluux/src-tauri/*` is matched before `apps/fluux/*`, otherwise every Tauri change would classify as `js`.

Jobs are suppressed with `if:` rather than a workflow-level `paths:` filter: a skipped job reports a conclusion, a workflow that never ran does not, so required status checks stay satisfiable if any are added to `main` later.

### Measured effect

Over the last 50 merged PRs: 2 classify as Rust-only (15 min → 2.5 min), 38 as TypeScript-only, 10 as both, 0 as docs-only. The TypeScript-only case drops two checks without moving wall-clock, since the Rust jobs were never on the critical path.

Narrowing `e2e-scroll` — the only job on the critical path at 9–15 min — would reach that majority, but is deliberately out of scope: this project's scroll regressions have repeatedly come from indirect changes to stores and read pointers, so a path gate there would trade real safety for time.

## Bugs found and fixed
1. **Audio paths ignored the Vite base path.** `scenario03Dialogues.js` built voice-line `src` as root-absolute (`/scenario03/audio/...`). Every other scenario's static asset paths go through `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` for exactly this reason (see `RegionAgencyResolver.js`, scenario01/02's video/photo consts) — without it, this would 404 forever once deployed at `ericingptt.github.io/CIBAR/`, even after real recordings are dropped into place. author: nickkolay
body:
## Why

`127.0.0.1` keeps the server off the network, but localhost is machine-local, not user-local:

- any process on the host could read transcripts or post messages impersonating any participant;
- websites could send blind cross-origin "simple" POSTs through the visitor's browser (no CORS preflight for `text/plain` bodies, and the server JSON-parsed the body regardless of content-type) — a prompt-injection path into room-joined agents;
- DNS rebinding could have allowed cross-origin reads.

## What

- Random per-installation token generated at `~/.agent-room/token` (mode `0600`; data dir created `0700`)
- All `/api` routes except `GET /api/health` require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; blind POSTs are rejected before body parsing
- Room viewer page requires `?token=…`; the page embeds the token for its same-origin fetches; `viewer_url` / `open` include it automatically
- Non-localhost `Host` headers rejected when bound to `127.0.0.1` (DNS-rebinding defense)
- Agent-facing invitation stays token-free — the CLI reads the token file automatically, so agents never handle or leak it
- Timing-safe token comparison; clear CLI error on token mismatch
- `scripts/smoke.sh`: 17-check end-to-end test (auth matrix + full meeting flow) against an isolated `AGENT_ROOM_HOME`/port
- README security section; SKILL.md notes auth is automatic and room codes exclude the `?token` query
- Version bump to 0.6.0 so a running pre-auth server is auto-replaced on first use

## Verification

`scripts/smoke.sh` — all 17 checks pass (401 without/with wrong token, 401 on simulated drive-by POST, 403 on foreign Host, viewer gated, CLI create/join/send/listen/transcript/close intact).

body:
## Why

This is a follow-up to #4188. Roleplay typing became substantially smoother, but holding Backspace in Firefox on macOS could still hitch in a repeating delete–pause cadence. Illustrator could also lose a selected Comic Page or manga format when Image Style guidance and generic illustration composition tags were applied independently.

## Root cause

- Held deletion still allowed debounced draft persistence and forced textarea autosizing to wake while the physical delete key remained down.
- Illustrator prompt-mode instructions and Image Style instructions were assembled at different stages. Generic profile subject tags such as “single scene” or “visual novel CG,” plus blanket `text` negative tags, could contradict a selected multi-panel prompt.
- Manual Gallery illustration prompt writing did not include the selected Illustrator prompt template, so a Comic Page selection could fall back to one coherent scene.

## What changed

- Defer Roleplay draft persistence and textarea autosizing until Backspace/Delete is released, while retaining the latest draft and resizing once afterward.
- Avoid ordinary-input slash-completion state work and full-string whitespace allocation on the hot path.
- Send the selected Illustrator prompt template and resolved Image Style instruction in the same prompt-writer request.
- Make prompt mode authoritative for format, layout, framing, subjects, and text behavior; Image Style controls visual treatment only.
- Withhold generic per-kind composition tags when a dedicated Illustrator prompt owns composition.
- Remove generated blanket text bans when the selected prompt explicitly requests comic/manga lettering, while preserving authored negatives such as “unreadable text.”
- Apply the same compatibility contract to automatic runs, manual Gallery illustration/background generation, retry flows, and selfie prompt-writer paths.

## Validation

- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm regression:prompt`
- `pnpm exec playwright test e2e/core-flows.e2e.ts --project=desktop-chromium --grep "held Roleplay deletion"`

The full lint gate retains one pre-existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning in `NoodleHome.tsx`; there are no lint errors.

## Manual verification

- [ ] On Firefox desktop/macOS, hold Backspace in a long Roleplay draft and verify deletion remains continuous without periodic stalls.
- [ ] Release Backspace, reload or switch chats, and verify the final shortened draft persisted.
- [ ] Select Illustrator → Comic Page with Image Style → Auto, run Illustrator automatically in chat, and verify the provider prompt remains explicitly multi-panel.
- [ ] Use Gallery → Illustrate with Comic Page selected and verify it generates a comic page without asking whether to generate.
- [ ] Spot-check another explicit style profile (for example Anime or Photorealistic) and verify it changes rendering without collapsing the selected prompt format.

author: oarriaga
body:
Steers the GEAR-WBC MuJoCo demo from a PlayStation pad instead of the
keyboard, and fixes two problems found while testing it.

## Controller

The keyboard `key_callback` is gone. MuJoCo's passive viewer keeps its own
key bindings live, so every steering key also toggled viewer state. The pad
is read outside the viewer, so nothing leaks into it.

Every input self-centers, which makes the command a pure function of pad
state: no accumulated globals, no drift, and releasing the pad returns the
robot to standing at 0.74 m with a level torso.

| Input | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Left stick | forward / lateral velocity, 0.5 and 0.4 m/s |
| Right stick left / right | yaw rate, 1.0 rad/s |
| Right stick up / down | base height, 0.74 m ± 0.15 m |
| L2 / R2 | torso roll, ±20° |
| D-pad up / down, left / right | torso pitch, torso yaw |

Only axes and the hat are used, so no button indices are involved. Lateral
speed is capped below forward speed because upstream recommends staying near
0.4 m/s when strafing.

The full-deflection caps are a judgement call: upstream has no clip ranges
for GEAR-WBC, so 0.4 m/s comes from its strafing note and the rest from
reading `cmd_scale: [2.0, 2.0, 0.5]` as 1/range. They are single constants
in `controller.py` if you want them louder.

## jit, and CPU by default

`compute_action` called the Keras actor eagerly every control step:

| | eager | jitted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU | 7.74 ms/call | 0.27 ms/call |
| GPU | 18.52 ms/call | 1.15 ms/call |

Against a 20 ms control period, eager GPU inference alone ran the loop at
0.96x real time before the viewer drew anything. `compile_actors` now jits
both experts and warms them up, so neither stalls the loop when a command
first selects it. The loop went from 0.96x to 9.61x real time. The demo
defaults to CPU because one 15-joint actor at batch one is bound by launch
latency, not throughput; `JAX_PLATFORMS` overrides it.

## Two demo fixes

`mujoco.viewer.launch_passive` keeps SIGINT for itself, so Ctrl-C never
became a `KeyboardInterrupt` and neither MuJoCo demo could be stopped
without `kill`. Reproduced with a viewer-only script containing no pygame and
no JAX, so this is pre-existing. Both demos now restore
`signal.default_int_handler` after `launch_passive`.

The gear_wbc camera also tracks the pelvis. Fixed at the origin it lost the
robot after about 2.5 m of walking, which reads as a frozen scene.

## Verification

- `pytest examples/gear_wbc` — 18 passed (9 new, covering the pad mapping and
  every sign convention)
- `pytest examples/sonic` — 11 passed
- `python3 mujoco_demo.py --headless --steps 1000` — ends upright at 0.747 m
- SIGINT to both running demos — exits cleanly; both hung before
- Scripted drive through every full-deflection command — never falls, stays
  upright, tracks the height command exactly
- pyflakes clean, nothing over 79 columns

Adds `pygame` to the `gear_wbc` extra.

author: devben5
body:
> **PR empilée sur CC-21.** Base : `feat/CC-21-tags-a-la-capture`. Dernière du lot.

## Le point que le ticket demandait de vérifier — et il avait tort

> ⚠️ **Un tag retiré peut revenir à la collecte suivante** sur un item Immich ou YouTube — les collecteurs réappliquent les leurs à chaque passe. **À vérifier avant de promettre le contraire.**

Vérifié :

| | |
|---|---|
| `tags` dans les collecteurs | **uniquement à l'insertion**, jamais dans un `update` |
| `insertNewItems` | `ON CONFLICT (dedup_key) DO NOTHING` — un item existant est **intouché** |
| les seuls `.update()` du module | `unavailable_at` et `deleted_at` |

**Un tag retiré ne revient pas.** Les collecteurs ne réappliquent rien : ils n'écrivent qu'à l'insertion.

## Ce qui change

La barre de sélection ne proposait qu'un geste : **supprimer**. Tout le reste se faisait item par item, et les tags ne se modifiaient **nulle part** — l'écran laissait filtrer par tag, affichait une barre de tags alimentée depuis toute la table, et ne permettait d'en poser aucun.

Quatre gestes — tags, lu / non lu, à lire plus tard — offerts **des deux côtés** : sur les cases cochées (`POST /items/bulk`) et sur tout ce que le filtre désigne (`POST /items/filtered/bulk`, CC-108). Ce qui change entre les deux est la façon de désigner l'ensemble, jamais ce qu'on lui fait : **un seul service applique**.

⚠️ **Aucune ne sort de Command Center**, et c'est ce qui les sépare de la suppression. Pas d'ordre à tenir entre deux systèmes, pas de partiel à assumer, **pas de confirmation** — exiger un « êtes-vous sûr » pour marquer lu banaliserait le seul dialogue du module qui compte. Pas de plafond d'identifiants non plus : les 200 de `itemIdsValidator` bornaient ce qui part dans un seul `DELETE /api/assets`.

## Les deux gardes, et pourquoi chacune porte

**Un seul `UPDATE` par action**, `array_append` / `array_remove` en SQL paramétré. Lire trente lignes, les modifier en JS et les réécrire une par une serait trente allers-retours **et** une fenêtre de concurrence à chaque ligne.

⚠️ **`array_append` ne déduplique pas, et `text[]` n'a aucune contrainte.** Sans `NOT (? = ANY(tags))`, un second clic écrit `{ia,ia}` : deux pastilles identiques sur la ligne, et un **double comptage dans la barre de tags**, qui agrège par `unnest` — donc un filtre qui existe deux fois.

⚠️ **La même garde rend le compte honnête.** Sans elle, `rowCount` vaudrait la taille de la sélection quoi qu'il arrive, et le retour annoncerait « 30 marqués comme lus » sur trente items déjà lus. C'est ce compte qui décide du ton `info`.

⚠️ **`read_at IS NULL` pour la même famille de raison.** C'est un timestamp, pas un booléen : sans elle, un geste groupé sur une page à moitié lue **réécrirait** la date de tout ce qui l'était déjà — invisible à l'écran, qui n'affiche qu'une pastille.

⚠️ **Les quatre écritures filtrent `deleted_at IS NULL`.** Ce sont des **écritures** : un oubli ne fait pas ressortir un supprimé, il le **modifie**, ce qui ne se voit sur aucun écran.

## Gates

`lint`, `typecheck`, **800 Japa + 71 Vitest** (17 tests neufs), `npm run build`.

## Vérification par mutation — et ce qu'elle a corrigé

| ce qui a été cassé | ce qui a rougi |
|---|---|
| la garde `NOT (? = ANY(tags))` | `expected [ 'rust', 'ia', 'ia' ] to deeply equal [ 'rust', 'ia' ]` |
| `deleted_at IS NULL` sur `queue.add` | **rien, d'abord** — puis `queue.add a touché un supprimé` |

⚠️ **La seconde a démasqué un faux-positif dans mon propre test.** Le cas `deleted_at` utilisait **un seul fixture** pour les six actions — tagué, lu, en file. Or `queue.add` porte aussi la garde `reading_queue = false` : l'item étant déjà dans la file, il était exclu **de toute façon**, et retirer `deleted_at IS NULL` ne faisait pas rougir le test.

C'est exactement le faux-positif que le `CLAUDE.md` décrit pour les six tests `deleted_at` de CC-63 — dans le fichier même qui cite l'avertissement. Chaque cas part maintenant de **l'état que son action changerait**, et une assertion de longueur rougit si une action est ajoutée sans son cas.

## Ce qui reste non vérifié

⚠️ La passe navigateur. Les deux barres gagnent six boutons chacune : qu'elles restent lisibles, qu'elles restent **distinctes** l'une de l'autre (l'invariant de CC-108, mis à l'épreuve par six boutons identiques des deux côtés), que le `prompt` de saisie de tag soit acceptable à l'usage, et qu'un tag posé devienne filtrable depuis la barre latérale.

author: chielvantongeren
body:
## Waarom

`api/mice.js` deed geen enkele authenticatiecontrole en zette er `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` bovenop. Wie het adres kende, kon `/api/mice?path=/events` opvragen en kreeg de complete eventlijst uit MICE terug — klantnamen, contactpersonen, aantallen, prijzen. Zonder inlog, vanaf elke site.

Gevonden bij het doorlezen van deze repo voor een andere klus. Ik heb het niet live kunnen bevestigen (de bouwomgeving blokkeert `vercel.app`), maar in de code zat geen enkel slot.

## Wat er verandert

- **`middleware.js`** (nieuw): Basic Auth over het hele project, via `PLANNER_USER` en `PLANNER_PASS`. Zelfde patroon als `stoom-dashboard`, met één bewust verschil: deze sluit **fail closed**. Staan de env-vars niet ingevuld, dan gaat er niets naar buiten en krijg je een 503 die uitlegt wat je moet doen. In `stoom-dashboard` zet een ontbrekende configuratie het slot juist *open* — dat leek me hier de verkeerde kant om te falen.
- **`api/mice.js`**: wildcard-CORS eruit, alleen GET, het `path` wordt gecontroleerd zodat de proxy geen doorgeefluik naar willekeurige adressen is, en geen caching.
- **`index.html`**: de testknop in Instellingen verwees naar `settings.apiKey`, een veld dat niet meer bestaat — hij stuurde `Basic undefined` mee en werkte dus niet. Loopt nu ook via de proxy.

Bewust **niet** aangepast: het API-adres (`app.miceoperations.com`) en de `X-Authorization`-header. Die werken hier al. Dat `stoom-dashboard` `api.miceoperations.com` en de `Authorization`-header gebruikt is een opruimklus, geen beveiligingskwestie — en ik wil in een security-fix niets veranderen wat werkt.

## Wat jij moet doen

1. Zet in Vercel twee environment variables: `PLANNER_USER` en `PLANNER_PASS`. Kies een fatsoenlijk wachtwoord.
2. Deploy opnieuw.

**Tot je dat doet, is de planner dicht.** Dat is de bedoeling — beter dicht dan open. Het kost je twee minuten.

## Nog te overwegen

Als die lijst inderdaad open heeft gestaan, is de MICE-sleutel zelf niet gelekt (die stond altijd al server-side), maar de eventgegevens mogelijk wel. Of dat merkbaar is hangt ervan af of iemand het adres kende. Je kunt de sleutel voor de zekerheid vervangen in MICE.

Los hiervan: controleer bij `stoom-dashboard` of `DASHBOARD_USER` en `DASHBOARD_PASS` daar écht ingevuld staan in Vercel. Zo niet, dan staat dat dashboard om dezelfde reden open.

Nog blijven staan (buiten scope): de melding "API key vereist — ga naar Instellingen om je MICE API key in te vullen" klopt niet meer, dat instellingenveld bestaat niet.

body: ## Summary Replaces the generic grey silhouette on `/reviews` — a real Google profile photo where one exists, a branded initials tile where it doesn't. ## What I found Pulled `reviewer.profilePhotoUrl` from the GBP API (the same OAuth the `review_stats_sync` cron already uses). Google **always** returns a URL — for users with no photo it generates a coloured letter tile on the fly, so "has a URL" ≠ "has a photo". Of the four reviewers still showing the placeholder: | Reviewer | Google has | Now shows | |---|---|---| | Christina Phang | ✅ real photo | self-hosted photo | | Sze Yoong | ⬜ generated tile | `SY` on pastel blue | | Sook Yeen Lee | ⬜ generated tile | `SL` on sky blue | | Tan Bee Wah | ⬜ generated tile | `TW` on tint blue | Across all 91 reviews it's 43 real photos / 48 generated tiles, but only 11 reviews appear on the site. ## Why self-host rather than hotlink `lh3.googleusercontent.com` URLs rotate when the user changes their photo, with no cache guarantee. `wee_min_lee.png` is a live example — his Google account no longer has the photo we captured, but the site still shows it because it was copied. ## Accessibility Initials use charcoal on the three lighter brand tints: **6.6:1, 10.5:1, 13.2:1** — all clear WCAG AA. White text was the obvious choice but fails at 1.5–2.4:1 on these tints. Tint is picked deterministically from the name, so an avatar never changes between renders. Initials are first + last (`Sook Yeen Lee` → `SL`), otherwise it would collide with `Sze Yoong` at `SY` in the adjacent card. ## Notes - Added `.webp`/`.avif` variants for the new photo to match the existing convention (the `` doesn't use `` yet, so they're unused for now — same as the other reviewer images). - `patient.svg` is now unreferenced; left in place rather than deleted. ## Privacy These photos are published by the reviewer alongside a public review of the clinic and are shown in the same context. Worth pairing with a takedown-on-request line in the privacy policy — flagged separately, not in this PR. ## Verification - `npm run build` ✅ - Confirmed in the running app: all 11 avatars resolve to the intended photo or initials, with the expected tints and charcoal text. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: wannysim
body:
곡마다 손으로 하던 가사 제작 과정을 스크립트와 문서로 남기고, 앱에 About 시트를 붙였다.

## 가사 워크플로

```bash
python3 scripts/fetch-lyrics.py <slug> --write   # lrclib에서 싱크 가사 받아 뼈대 생성
python3 scripts/check-lyrics.py                  # 전체 검증
```

- `docs/LYRICS.md` — 두 경로(lrclib / 앱의 싱크 편집 모드)와 새 곡 추가 절차
- `check-lyrics.py`는 특히 **time이 순증가하는지** 본다. `currentLineIndex`의
  `findLastIndex`가 정렬을 전제하므로, 시간이 뒤로 가면 엉뚱한 줄이 하이라이트된다.
  손으로 만든 JSON에서 나기 쉬운 실수다

### 문서에 남긴 함정 두 가지

**제목 표기가 갈린다.** lrclib은 등록자가 붙인 이름을 쓴다. 「タイムパラドックス」는
로마자 `Time Paradox`로만 올라와 있어서, 원제로만 검색했을 때 "싱크 가사 없음"으로
잘못 결론 냈었다. 스크립트가 원제 · 아티스트 조합 · 자유 검색을 모두 시도하는 이유다.

**길이로 판별해야 싱크가 맞는다.** 같은 곡도 MV · 앨범 · 리레코딩이 섞여 있고 각각
타임스탬프가 다르다. 재생할 `videoId`의 길이를 YouTube에서 읽어 가장 가까운 후보를
고르고, 2초 넘게 차이 나면 경고한다.

이 스크립트로 **타임 패러독스 가사를 만들었다** (227s 정확 일치, 30줄). 이제 9곡 전부
가사가 있다. 가사 파일 자체는 저작물이라 여전히 커밋하지 않는다.

## About 시트

곡 목록 하단의 "이 앱에 대해 · 곡 추가 요청"으로 연다. 왜 만들었는지, 어떻게 쓰는지,
곡 추가 요청 연락처(`wannysim@gmail.com`, 제목이 미리 채워진 mailto), 음원과 가사 출처를
담았다.

라우터를 들이는 대신 드로어로 했고, 목록을 닫고 나서 열어 드로어 중첩을 피한다.

## E2E flake 제거

모바일 센터링 테스트가 간헐적으로 실패했다. 원인은 **재생이 시작되면 활성 줄이 계속
넘어가면서 자동 스크롤이 따라가**, "탭한 줄이 가운데" 단언이 깨지는 것이었다. 즉 그동안
"재생이 안 된다"는 우연에 기대고 있었다. 모바일 스펙에서 YouTube 요청을 막아 결정적으로
만들었고, 덤으로 CI의 네트워크 의존도 사라졌다.

3회 연속 53/53 통과로 확인했다.

## 검증

- 유닛 79개, 커버리지 94.9%
- E2E 53개 — chromium · firefox · webkit + mobile-chrome
- `check-lyrics.py` 9곡 전부 통과
