10에이전트 전수 검증(v150~v154 주장 검증 + 적대적 반박)이 잡아낸 잠복 결함 4건. 전부 **주입 0의 실플레이**로 재현·수정 확인.

## ① v152 잡몹 동사 2/3이 데드코드였다
구울 「도약 물기」·도깨비불 「점화 쇄도」의 발동 조건이 `this._pounceCd <= 0`인데 초기값이 undefined → `undefined <= 0 === false` → **영원히 안 열린다.**
- 실플레이 관측: 구울 1,673틱 중 도약 **0회**, 위습 3,341틱 중 쇄도 **0회** (정예 강타만 정상, 링 143개)
- ★ **v152 검증 스크립트가 테스트에서 이 필드를 0으로 주입해 버그를 가렸다**
- 수정: def에서 상태 필드 초기화 → 재검(자연 진행) 도약 6회 · 쇄도 29회 발동

## ② 열기 스텔스 조절의 잔존 경로
`input.js` mousemove가 캔버스에만 붙어 있고 mouseleave/blur 리셋이 없어, 레터박스 여백(16:9가 아닌 창)으로 포인터가 나가면 좌표가 **마지막 위치에 얼어붙는다**. 로드아웃 줄 위에서 마우스를 뺀 뒤 키보드만 써도 현상금이 계속 조절됐다 (실측 1200×760: 3→6→4).
→ mouseleave/blur에서 좌표를 화면 밖으로. 호버를 쓰는 **모든 UI의 공통 뿌리** 수정. 재검: 캔버스 밖 ArrowRight×3 → 값 불변

## ③ 「중갑 서약」 무한 중첩
v151 희귀 14종 중 유일하게 `flag`도 `max`도 없어 무제한 픽 가능 (실측 런당 평균 2장, **최대 8장** = HP+24·이속 ×0.43) → `max: 2`

## ④ 등급이 계열 행세를 했다
태그 공명(`1+0.7×tagCount`)이 '희귀' 태그에도 걸려, 희귀를 집을수록 희귀 전체 가중이 오르는 되먹임 → 등장률 사양 10%의 **1.7배(16.7%)**.
→ 등급 태그 공명 계수 0. 재측정 **7.3~8.2%**

## 부수 (v154 미관 지적 해소)
현상금 8단계 문구가 버튼을 파고들던 것(버튼 8px 외곽), 하한·상한 딤 표시, 죽은 `heatButtonRects` 제거, 호버 시 '←→ 조절' 안내 복원(v154에서 사라져 보이지 않는 기능이 됐었다).

## 검증
- 주입 0 자연 진행 4분 관측(구울·도깨비불·정예), 희귀 등장률 200런×20레벨 ×2 정책, 스텔스 경로 1200×760 재현 테스트
- 5분 봇 소크: 에러 0, 스프라이트 가드 클린, 1막 완주

> 검증 스크립트가 **초기 상태를 주입하면 초기화 버그를 가린다.** 상태 관련 검증은 반드시 '주입 0'의 자연 진행으로 한 번 더 잰다.

author: kevinansfield
body:
no issue

The root AGENTS.md is loaded into context for every agent session, so every line in it is paid for on every task regardless of relevance. The i18n, ESLint config and CSS architecture sections only matter when working on those specific things, so they now live where they load on demand:

- i18n and ESLint config become skills, loaded when a task calls for them
- CSS architecture moves to apps/AGENTS.md, loaded when working under apps/

Short pointers stay behind in the root file, keeping the two rules that bite when you aren't already thinking about the topic: never split a sentence across `t()` calls, and never use `'warn'` for a lint rule.

Trims the always-loaded file from 18.5k to 12.8k characters.

author: esubaalew
body:
## Summary
- Harden `PermissionEngine._command_allowed` so a bare allowlisted `find` no longer auto-approves helper execution (`-exec` / `-execdir` / `-ok` / `-okdir`), including the `{} +` form that bypasses shell-operator rejection.
- Users who intentionally want that authority can still opt in with a prefix that names the flag (e.g. `find . -exec`).
- Align `docs/config.example.toml` with empty defaults and warn against bare interpreters / unsafe binaries.

## Context
Defaults were already emptied because of `find -exec` (see `coworker/config.py`), but:
1. Operator rejection only catches `… -exec … ;` (`;` is a shell operator), not `… -exec … {} +`.
2. The example config still recommended `find` / `python3` / `node`, which recreated the footgun for anyone copying it.

Verified before fix: `allowed_commands=["find"]` → `find . -exec touch /tmp/pwned {} +` returned `allowed=True`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_permissions_risk.py tests/test_tools_permissions.py` (50 passed)
- [ ] Confirm allowlisted `find . -name '*.py'` still auto-runs
- [ ] Confirm allowlisted `find` + `find . -exec … {} +` now asks for approval
- [ ] Confirm `allowed_commands = ["find . -exec"]` still auto-allows matching `-exec` commands

author: mohanedsayed
body:
Closes #68.

Adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the first PR check that runs the test suite.

| job | runs |
| --- | --- |
| `typecheck` | `next typegen` → `tsc --noEmit` |
| `test` | `db:migrate:test` → `db:check:test` → `npm run test`, against a `postgres:16` service |

Two jobs rather than one so a red X names the failure, and so each can be
required independently when branch protection goes on.

## The CI role

This is the part the ticket flagged and it is the reason for
`scripts/ci-db-bootstrap.sql`. Tenant isolation here is RLS; a superuser
bypasses RLS; the service container's default `postgres` user is a superuser.
Run the suite as it and every isolation test passes without evaluating a single
policy — green CI, untested guarantee, no symptom. The bootstrap creates a
`NOSUPERUSER`/`NOBYPASSRLS` role and `RAISE EXCEPTION`s if that role ever holds
either attribute, so a mis-provisioned role fails the job instead of quietly
hollowing out the suite.

Verified the tests are not vacuous by pointing them at a connection that *does*
bypass RLS. All six isolation tests fail, with the assertions you would want:

```
× only sees rows belonging to the active tenant
    expected [ …, … ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
× blocks writing a row for a different tenant
    promise resolved "Result{ command: 'INSERT' }" instead of rejecting
× sees no rows outside any tenant context (fails closed)
    expected [ … ] to have a length of +0 but got 1
× order_payments / pos_adjustment_events / pos_held_tickets: …
```

## Two blockers found on the way

CI has to install dependencies and build the schema from nothing. Neither
worked on `main`, and both are fixed here in their own commits.

**1. `db:migrate` cannot build the schema from empty.** drizzle's migrator wraps
every pending migration in *one* transaction, and `0017` adds
`invoice_status.pending_verification` then creates a partial index naming it:

```
ERROR:  unsafe use of new value "pending_verification" of enum type invoice_status
HINT:   New enum values must be committed before they can be used.
```

The run rolls back and the database stays empty — 0 tables. Every environment
got past 0017 by hand with `db:repair`, which already lifts `ALTER TYPE … ADD
VALUE` out of the transaction; the fix existed, it just was not in the runner.
`applyMigrations` now commits per migration and applies enum additions first,
outside the transaction, skipping values already present. Selection logic is
unchanged — same watermark rule, same ledger format — so unreachable migrations
stay `db:repair`'s job. No migration file is edited; changing one would change
its hash and show it as pending everywhere it has already been applied.

**2. `npm ci` fails.** Nine entries are missing from `package-lock.json`
(the `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` fallback chain, its hoisted `@emnapi`
packages, vitest's esbuild). `npm install` papers over this silently; `npm ci`
refuses. Regenerated with `--package-lock-only`: nine added, none removed. The
one substantive change is `apps/pos`, where `better-sqlite3` moves to
`optionalDependencies` to match its manifest.

## Acceptance criteria

Each verified locally against Postgres 16 with the CI role, reverting after.

- [x] **A PR that breaks a test gets a red check** — `vitest` exit `1`
- [x] **A PR that breaks types gets a red check** — `tsc` exit `2`, `TS2322`
- [x] **Migrations out of sync with the journal get a red check** — `db:check` exit `1`, both directions:
  - a `.sql` the journal never lists → `1 migration file(s) are not listed in drizzle/meta/_journal.json`
  - a journal entry with no file → `ENOENT`
- [x] **RLS tests genuinely fail if RLS is disabled** — six failures, above

The first of those needed a new guard. `db:check` reads `_journal.json`, so a
`.sql` file the journal does not list is not *pending*, it is invisible — never
applied, absent from the counts, unreportable by a report whose input is the
journal. `findUnjournaledMigrations` compares folder against journal and
`db:check` exits 1 on the difference. That case is realistic here: hand-written
migrations like `0002_fix_tenant_settings_policy_nullif.sql` are added to the
folder and the journal in two separate steps.

Full sequence, run end-to-end against a database created empty:

```
### npm run db:migrate:test → applied: 20/20 migrations
### npm run db:check:test   → every migration on disk has been applied.
### npm run test            → Test Files 87 passed  Tests 484 passed  (43.45s)
```

## Decisions worth a second opinion

- **Lint is not included.** The ticket flagged 8 pre-existing errors on `main`;
  adding it now turns every PR red for reasons no PR introduced. Fixing them is
  small (an eslint ignore for `dist-electron/` and the vendored brand asset, one
  unescaped entity) but it is a separate change.
- **`db:check:test`, not `db:check`.** Same script; `db:check` defaults to
  `.env.local`, which CI does not write.
- **`postgres:16`** matches the Postgres this project's tests already run against
  locally (16.14). Worth revisiting if production is on a different major.
- **`next typegen` is not load-bearing today** — nothing under `src/` uses
  `PageProps`/`LayoutProps`, and `tsc` passes without it. It is in because it is
  the recipe the Next 16 docs give for CI, and `tsconfig.json` already includes
  the generated types. Comment in the workflow says so, so nobody strips it as
  dead weight.
- **`fileParallelism: false` is untouched**, with a comment on the test step
  saying why, since sharding is the obvious "optimisation" to reach for.

## Not verified

The workflow itself has never executed on GitHub — this PR is its first run.
Everything above was verified by running the same commands locally against a
`NOSUPERUSER`/`NOBYPASSRLS` role on Postgres 16. What local runs cannot prove:
`psql` on the runner image, service-container networking, and `npm ci` on Linux
(the lockfile gaps involve platform-flavoured optional deps, so Linux may
resolve them differently). Watch the first run.

## Follow-ups

- Branch protection on `main` requiring these checks, once they have proven
  themselves — deliberately not in this PR, per the ticket.
- Lint, after the 8 pre-existing errors are cleared.

author: andreaserradev-gbj
body:
## Summary

- `dev-workflow-core` decided whether a PRD line or table row was a step by whitelisting the status glyph in its marker slot (`⬜ ✅ ⏭️ ⛔ ⏹️`). Any other glyph made the row invisible rather than unknown, so it dropped out of both the numerator and the denominator: a 10-step sub-PRD carrying one `⚠️` reported `9/9` and a status of `complete`, silently.
- On the write path the same whitelist made `status-update` reject a row it had already matched by step number, then report `Phase N not found`. That names the wrong layer and sends debugging toward phase resolution instead of glyph classification.
- Step recognition is now structural and separate from status classification, in one module (`glyphs.ts`) that the parser and the writer both route through. A line is a step when an emoji token leads its marker slot; a table row is a step when its shape says so, whatever the status cell holds. An unrecognized marker counts toward `total`, never toward `done`, and raises a warning naming the file, step, and glyph.
- `status-update` now refuses an unrecognized marker with a message that says so, and exits 1. It does not flip the glyph: the writer replaces the whole status cell, so overwriting `⚠️ Written, unverifiable` would destroy the annotation along with the marker.
- The same defect existed in the master-plan inline form, which the original report did not cover. Both forms are fixed. A latent writer bug is fixed as a side effect: `⛔` and `⏹️` inline steps were countable by the parser but unwritable by the writer.

New `warnings?: string[]` on `Feature` and `FeatureDetail`, plus `unrecognizedMarker?: string` on `SubPrdStep`. Both keys are omitted when empty, so payloads for healthy features keep their shape. `progress-summary` and `feature-show` carry warnings in `--json` and print them to stderr in human mode, leaving piped stdout parseable.

### Note on existing PRDs

Correcting the denominator moves real numbers. A feature that previously read `complete` because a step was invisible will now correctly read `in-progress`. That is the bug surfacing, not a regression, and anything archived on the strength of a 100% reading is worth re-checking. Measured against every feature in this repo (24 in `.dev/` and `.dev-archive/`), no count changed.

## Test plan

- [x] core 319, CLI 133, dashboard 141, TUI 36 (all four suites)
- [x] `bash tests/test-scripts.sh`: 46 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `sh scripts/code-hygiene.sh`: knip `total: 14 (baseline 14)`, jscpd under threshold
- [x] Pre-commit dashboard-bundle gate observed failing on a core-only stage before being trusted, then passing after rebundle
- [x] Frozen fixtures unchanged: no assertion moved in `full-feature`, `subprd-mixed-steps`, `master-range-subprds`, or `master-hybrid-redundant`
- [x] End-to-end against the shipped bundle: `progress-summary --json` reports `{done:1,total:2,percent:50}` with warnings; `status-update` exits 1 naming `⚠️` and leaves the refused row byte-identical

New fixtures: `subprd-unknown-glyph` (the original repro), `subprd-empty-status-cell`, `master-unknown-glyph` (with prose decoys, guarding against denominator inflation), `master-blocked-deferred-steps`, `master-hybrid-unknown-glyph`.

author: gfazioli
body:
## The problem

Unlike `lens-select`, this component **already had** `aria-activedescendant` wired up. But it pointed at ids derived from the item value alone — `ds-item-${value}` — which are global, not per-instance. Two DepthSelects sharing item values collide.

Measured on the **published docs page**, not hypothesised:

| | |
|---|---|
| option elements | 49 |
| distinct ids | **31** |
| `ds-item-snap-1` | appears **6 times** |
| listboxes pointing at a duplicated id | **6 of 13** |

A screen reader resolves a duplicated reference to the **first match in the document** — an option belonging to a *different* component. So it doesn't fail visibly: it announces the wrong card. Duplicate ids are also invalid HTML.

## The fix

Ids are now `${useId()}-option-${index}`: unique per instance, and index-based rather than value-based so they stay valid when a value contains spaces or other id-unsafe characters.

## Test plan

Three regression tests, each **verified to fail without the fix** (2 of them fail immediately if the old id scheme is restored — checked before committing):

- `aria-activedescendant` resolves to a real option with `aria-selected="true"`
- two instances sharing the same item values produce **unique** ids
- each listbox resolves its `aria-activedescendant` to an option **inside itself**, and exactly one element in the document carries that id

- [x] yarn test — 38/38 (35 existing + 3 new)
- [x] yarn build + docgen + docs:build
- [x] oxlint clean

## Two notes

**The linter warning is silenced inline, with its reason.** `jsx-a11y/interactive-supports-focus` asks for `tabIndex` on the cards; that would make every card in the stack its own tab stop, including the ones rotated out of view behind the front card.

**Docs gain a Keyboard navigation section — and it corrects an easy assumption.** `ArrowUp` moves to the *next* card and `ArrowDown` to the *previous* one, which is the inverse of what one would guess. I had written it the wrong way round first; the existing keyboard tests are what set it straight.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Accessibility**
  * Improved keyboard navigation documentation, including supported keys and focus behavior.
  * Enhanced screen reader support with listbox and option semantics.
  * Prevented accessibility ID conflicts when multiple selectors display similar options.
  * Ensured the active option is correctly announced and associated with its selector.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: liorshk
body:
## Summary

A retryable transport failure could occur after an assistant stream had already persisted reasoning or tool input. Retrying the same step then appended a second model attempt to the same assistant message, producing an invalid Anthropic history that could brick every later turn.

This change makes the retry boundary explicit:

- derive whether the attempt produced output from its newly persisted message parts
- retry only when every new part is the structural `step-start`
- remove those structural parts before starting the retry
- halt normally after a mid-stream failure so cleanup records the failed assistant turn; existing replay behavior excludes that errored turn from future model requests

This keeps the V1 patch local to the processor and makes persisted message state the source of truth. Both the guard and its regression test are marked for removal when the V2 event-sourced runner replaces this processor path.

## User impact

Transient failures before output remain transparent. Failures after partial output are surfaced once, and the session remains usable on the next turn instead of replaying a merged assistant response that Anthropic rejects.

## Notion task

https://www.notion.so/bespo/3abec4e58f15811384e8ff61e20db7ff

author: ayushdeolasee
body:
Fixes the flaky red on `main` after #79.

## Root cause

`ScratchpadStore.pruneOrphanedAttachments` snapshots the note's referenced attachment ids and hands the sweep to a detached background task:

```swift
let referenced = ScratchpadAttachmentStore.referencedIds(in: text)
Task.detached(priority: .utility) {
    ScratchpadAttachmentStore.collectGarbage(in: dir, referencedIds: referenced)
}
```

The sweep therefore runs at an unpredictable moment *after* the snapshot was taken, and any attachment written in that gap is — correctly — absent from `referenced`. It was deleted as garbage even though it belongs to an edit the snapshot simply predates.

**This is a product bug, not a test artifact.** Opening a document whose note is empty dispatches a sweep with an *empty* reference set. Saving an image immediately afterwards — a drop, a paste, or a region snapshot on a freshly opened note — races that sweep. Losing the race deletes the bytes just written and leaves a broken `vellum-scratchpad://` reference in the note.

## Why it looked like cross-suite pollution

`clearText()` fails closed when a referenced image is unreadable, returning nil. Under full-suite load the detached `.utility` task is scheduled late enough to land between `ScratchpadAttachmentStore.save(...)` and `clearText()`, so the attachment vanishes mid-test and the `XCTUnwrap` fails:

- `SafeClearTests.testScratchpadClearFollowsSameSessionStampForUndoRedoAndAttachments` (line 162)
- `SafeClearTests.testScratchpadUndoRestoresAttachmentBytesAndRedoPreservesNewWork` (line 73)

Both pass in isolation because the sweep lands *early*, before the save — which is exactly why the failures varied between runs and read as ordering-dependent state leakage. The shared state is real (these seams are process-global, #102) but it was not the cause; the two tests were poisoning themselves through a genuine race in product code.

## The fix

`collectGarbage` now takes the moment the reference set was captured and skips any file created or modified at or after it:

```swift
static func collectGarbage(
    in directory: URL, referencedIds: Set<String>, referencedAsOf: Date? = nil
)
```

A file spared this way is not leaked — if it really is an orphan, the next sweep sees it as older than that snapshot and collects it. Timestamps that cannot be read keep the file, since a missed collection is recoverable and deleting a live attachment is not.

The synchronous save path is deliberately left alone: it computes its reference set from the *current* text microseconds earlier, so it does not have this defect, and passing a cutoff there would change GC semantics on the main persistence path for no proven gain.

## Verification

Causality was established by widening the window rather than by inference. A 400 microsecond sleep before the sweep:

- **before** this change: fails `testScratchpadUndoRestoresAttachmentBytesAndRedoPreservesNewWork` deterministically, in isolation, with the identical `XCTUnwrap` signature — one timing knob reproduces both observed failures;
- **after** this change: 31/31 green with that same sleep still in place.

Then, with the probe removed:

- **6 consecutive full-suite runs, all green**: 442 XCTest + 147 Swift Testing, 0 failures (441 + 1 new test). Before the change, the first full run on a pristine `origin/main` worktree reproduced the failure.
- `SafeClearTests` and `ScratchpadMarkdownExporterTests` green in isolation.
- Regression test `testGCSparesAttachmentsWrittenAfterTheReferenceSnapshot` mutation-checked: disabling the cutoff fails that test and nothing else.

Also resets `ScratchpadAttachmentStore.activeDirectory` on the way *into* `SafeClearTests`, not only on the way out, so the suite cannot inherit that process-global from whatever ran before it.

author: juninho1976
body:
## Summary

Closes #51
Closes #52
Closes #53
Closes #54
Closes #55

- adds central Better Auth username/password accounts with permanent UUID user IDs, D1 sessions, secure cookies, database-backed login rate limiting, logout and temporary-password changes
- adds protected browser administration for player creation, one-time generated passwords, name changes, password resets and account enable/disable, including final-admin protection
- gates game routes through branded central login while preserving the selected game destination
- removes Zavi Dash's name prompt and localStorage identity; score requests now contain only score data and the server derives ownership from the authenticated session
- rebuilds leaderboard ownership around stable user IDs while showing current, non-unique public display names
- upgrades Next.js to 16.2.12 and Wrangler to 4.114.0 after the dependency audit identified patched security releases

## Identity architecture

Better Auth's `user.id` is the permanent owner key. Username, public display name, password credential, role and disabled state can change without moving scores. Better Auth's separate `account` records can later link Google, Apple or another provider to the same user ID, so games do not need an identity migration.

Better Auth currently requires an email-shaped core field. Zavi Arcade generates an opaque, non-routable `@players.invalid` value internally; it is never collected, displayed in the UI or used for login/recovery. The administrator remains the recovery route.

Future games call the shared server-side `requirePlayer()` contract and their APIs derive the owner from the server session.

## Administrator workflow

1. Configure `AUTH_SECRET`, temporary `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`, and `BETTER_AUTH_URL`.
2. Apply migration `0006_add_player_accounts.sql`.
3. Call the one-time bootstrap endpoint documented in the README.
4. Remove `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`.
5. Manage all later players at `/admin/players`.

No secret or real credential is committed.

## Schema and legacy data

A read-only production check on 2026-07-28 confirmed exactly one legacy leaderboard row: `scores.id = 1`, Zavi Dash score `80`, display name `RAK`.

Migration `0006`:

- adds Better Auth user, session, provider-account, verification and shared rate-limit tables
- deletes only legacy `scores` and `players` rows
- rebuilds `scores.user_id` as a foreign key to the permanent account
- preserves games and all unrelated data

Changing a display name updates historical leaderboard presentation because leaderboard reads join the current account name. Duplicate display names remain separate owners.

## Security and child privacy

- no public sign-up, email recovery, security questions, tracking or advertising
- maintained Better Auth password hashing/session cryptography; no custom credential cryptography
- HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies, Secure in production
- generic login errors and five-attempt-per-minute D1-backed login limiting
- every admin mutation repeats server-side role checks
- password reset and disablement revoke sessions
- score APIs reject anonymous/disabled sessions and ignore browser-supplied identity
- usernames/admin data stay out of public leaderboards; nickname guidance is built into admin copy
- Next.js patched from 16.2.10 to 16.2.12 for current framework advisories

## Validation

- `npm run test` — 75 unit and isolated D1 integration tests passed
- `npm run test:browser` — 18 desktop/mobile login, admin and gameplay journeys passed
- `npm run lint` — passed (two warnings only in generated Cloudflare declarations)
- `npm run build` — passed
- `npm run build:worker` — passed
- local D1 migration — passed
- production D1 inspection — read-only; no production migration or deployment performed

## Screenshots

- [Central login](https://github.com/Juninho1976/zaviarcade/blob/agent/central-player-accounts/docs/screenshots/account-login.png)
- [Administrator player creation](https://github.com/Juninho1976/zaviarcade/blob/agent/central-player-accounts/docs/screenshots/admin-player-created.png)
- [Authenticated Zavi Dash](https://github.com/Juninho1976/zaviarcade/blob/agent/central-player-accounts/docs/screenshots/authenticated-zavi-dash.png)

## Remaining limitations / release notes

- Client-generated scores retain the existing proportionate validation and idempotency but are not server-authoritative anti-cheat proofs.
- Production requires the documented secret configuration, coordinated migration, one-time bootstrap and smoke test after approval/merge.
- The npm audit still reports inherited OpenNext build-chain advisories for which npm suggests an unsafe major downgrade; no Better Auth advisory is reported. Next.js and Wrangler were upgraded to their patched versions.
- This PR does not deploy or mutate production.

author: cuecrux-myles
body:
Follow-up to #545. Two defects, found by running the post-deploy verifier against **pre-deploy** prod before touching the host — a check that can't tell old from new is worthless, so I ran it to watch it fail, and it failed in a way I did not expect.

## 1. The eight tools were DENIED, not just unadvertised

```
RCX capability denied: denied:capability_not_permitted
```

`rcx_local_capabilities` builds the permitted capability set by filtering the catalogue through `vaultcrux_local::tool_surface::is_local_tool`. A tool with no `TOOL_SURFACE` entry never contributes `crux-mcp.<name>`, so the RCX router refuses **every call**. Deploying #545 as-is would have shipped eight dead tools.

**Nothing caught it because nothing could.** The daemon's test suite runs with no RCX router, so `enforce_rcx_tool_capability` returns early and every tool appears to work. #545's own integration test — which asserts MCP↔HTTP parity across all eight — passes for precisely that reason. The gap only appears when something calls through a real capability token.

All eight are `Local` tier: each executes against the project graph, workspace scan and fact store of whichever daemon the client is connected to, with no hosted control plane. Same reason they already declare `x-crux-min-tier: free`.

## 2. They could never have surfaced either

`tools/list` on host `crux` returns 16 tools, not 129 — `CORECRUXD_TOOL_SURFACE=dynamic` serves a core floor plus up to `DYNAMIC_TOP_N` ranked by declared intent. Ranking reads `tool_affinity`, which had no entry for any of the eight, so each scored 0 and would never rank in under any intent.

Mapped to `session`, beside `create_handoff` / `accept_handoff` / `get_workspace_storyline` — a dossier **is** the cross-session handoff of what an agent concluded, and the storybook is the project state a resuming session reads first. That puts them under `session_review`'s 30-point bias, where an agent picking work back up actually lands.

## The guard matters more than either fix

`every_catalogued_tool_carries_a_tier` fails any new tool that lacks a tier. Its `KNOWN_UNTIERED` list enumerates the **85 tools already in that state** — including `coord_status`, `coord_announce`, `list_work`, `create_work`, the entity/edge CRUD, the feature-registry tools, github, punchcards and orchestrators. **Every one is unreachable over MCP on an RCX-gated daemon today.**

That list is a **defect list, not an exemption**. Which tools are free-local and which are hosted-gated is an entitlement decision, not mine to make for 85 tools, so they are recorded to be triaged deliberately rather than silently tiered by whoever noticed. A second assertion keeps it from rotting: a name that gets tiered, or leaves the catalogue, must come off — which immediately caught `alice` and `openai`, neither of which is in `list_tools()`.

Worth a maintainer's eye: that 85 is a real production gap with its own scope, and it explains prior confusion about `feature_suggest_next` being unreachable over MCP.

## Verification

777 crux-mcp tests · `clippy -D warnings` + `fmt --check` clean. Both fixes are advertisement/entitlement only — no handler or response-shape change.

author: turbobobbytraykov
body:
## Description
With the `--recurse-containers false` flag, the step applies **only the NuGet author signature** to the package itself (`.signature.p7s`) and leaves the container contents untouched. Nothing of value is lost:

- **DLLs are still Authenticode-signed** — the dedicated "Sign DLLs" step (+ "Validate DLL signatures" gate) runs *before* `dotnet pack`, so the package embeds already-signed assemblies. The container pass was merely re-signing them redundantly.
- **The package is still author-signed and timestamped** — `dotnet nuget verify` continues to pass.
- **JS static web assets enter the package pristine**, matching the manifest hashes.

This also generalizes: any of our ASP.NET Core / Blazor packages that ship static web assets (JS/CSS with SRI hashes in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props`) has the same hazard, and `--recurse-containers false` is the same one-line fix, provided assemblies are signed pre-pack.


## Motivation / Context
Fixes [#267](https://github.com/IgniteUI/igniteui-blazor/issues/267) — `Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource '...IgniteUI.Blazor.Lite.*.lib.module.js' ... The resource has been blocked.` when consuming the published package in a .NET 10 Blazor WebAssembly app.

Referencing `IgniteUI.Blazor.Lite` 0.1.0 from a stock .NET 10 Blazor WebAssembly Standalone app and running `dotnet run` leaves the app stuck at **"Loading"**. The browser console shows:

```
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource
'http://localhost:xxxx/_content/IgniteUI.Blazor/IgniteUI.Blazor.Lite.5g0qjy678t.lib.module.js'
with computed SHA-256 integrity 'Ezw3dvPXa+ZVVStf5TpfIu2ZK0+nZw8g14iZW05IeWE='.
The resource has been blocked.
```

Because the blocked file is a Blazor JS initializer (`*.lib.module.js`), the WASM runtime fails to start entirely (`MONO_WASM: Failed to import library initializer`).
By default the `sign` tool treats the nupkg as a **container** and recursively Authenticode-signs every supported file *inside* it — including all 8 `.js` static web assets (`.js` is a signable WSH-script type for the tool, signed by appending a `// SIG // ... // SIG // End signature block` comment trailer).

The failure chain:
1. `dotnet pack` computes SHA-256 hashes of every static web asset and freezes them as `<Integrity>` values in `build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props` inside the package.
2. The post-pack signing step then **mutates the `.js` files inside the nupkg** by appending the `// SIG //` signature block — invalidating the frozen hashes. Audit of the shipped 0.1.0 package: **27 of 81** manifest entries mismatched (every `.js` asset).
3. In a consuming .NET 10 app the SDK emits those stale hashes as SRI `integrity` attributes (via the importmap generated by `OverrideHtmlAssetPlaceholders`), the browser's subresource-integrity check fails, and the file is blocked.

It only manifests in `dotnet run` / development because `dotnet publish` re-fingerprints and recomputes asset integrity, masking the corruption.

Note: Authenticode signing of `.js` files exists for **Windows Script Host** scripts (AppLocker/WDAC script enforcement). It is meaningless for browser-delivered JavaScript — browsers don't verify Authenticode, and Microsoft does not Authenticode-sign `dotnet.js`/`blazor.webassembly.js` either. For static web assets the signature block is pure corruption.

author: radumarias
body:
## Summary

Two fixes, both already running on https://echo-read.fly.dev/ — this PR brings `main` in line with what is deployed.

1. A request no longer dies when one Gemini model is overloaded.
2. Seeking into the text works on touch devices, not just desktop.

---

## 1. Model fallback on overload (`2893c14`)

`/api/fetch-article` was returning 503 with no recovery. The client refetched the article and hit the same busy model again:

```
08:28:27  Article retrieved … retrievedBy:"jina"
08:28:27  Request failed  status:503  "This model is currently experiencing high demand"
08:28:38  Article retrieved …            ← refetch, same busy model
08:28:45  Request failed  status:503
```

`callWithModelFallback` gives each model a few attempts with exponential backoff, then moves to the next model in a list. Three failure classes are handled differently:

| Failure | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| 429 / 503 | retry the same model (3 attempts, 1s → 2s), then fall back |
| 404 | skip to the next model immediately, no retries |
| anything else | fail at once — a bad prompt or missing key fails identically everywhere |

The 404 case is not hypothetical. **`gemini-2.5-flash-lite` is still advertised by `models.list` but `generateContent` answers 404** (*"no longer available to new users"*). An earlier version of this change treated 404 as permanent and would have failed the whole request on a rotten chain entry.

Every model in both chains was checked against `generateContent` rather than taken from the listing:

- **Text:** `gemini-2.5-flash` → `gemini-3-flash-preview` → `gemini-flash-lite-latest`
- **Speech:** `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` → `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` → `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts`

`gemini-2.0-flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro` and the `2.0-flash-lite` variants were dropped — all answer 429 quota-exceeded, so they would be dead weight in the chain.

The provider's own `retry in Ns` hint is honoured but capped, so a long hint cannot leave a request hanging. Both chains are overridable without a code change, since chains rot:

```
GEMINI_TEXT_MODELS=gemini-2.5-flash,gemini-3-flash-preview
GEMINI_TTS_MODELS=gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts
```

**Trade-off:** if every model is overloaded a request now spends ~9s on backoff before failing, where it used to fail instantly.

---

## 2. Tap a word to play from there (`d758af0`)

Double-click had no touch equivalent: on mobile a double-tap is claimed by zoom, and the handler depended on the browser having word-selected the text under the cursor, which selection handles do not reproduce. The feature was effectively desktop-only.

A single tap behaves the same under a mouse and a finger, so one `onPointerDown`/`onPointerUp` pair now covers both. Three gestures are filtered out so tapping does not hijack normal reading:

| Gesture | Threshold | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| travel > 10px | scroll or drag-select | scrolling on mobile starts as a touch on the text |
| press > 700ms | long press | that is the touch selection gesture |
| live selection | reader is selecting | do not seek while they are copying |

Coordinates map through `caretPositionFromPoint`, falling back to `caretRangeFromPoint` for Safari, then snap to the start of the word so narration never resumes mid-word. Whitespace snaps forward, so tapping a gap plays the following word rather than repeating the one before it.

The instruction moved out of the `title` attribute onto the page — hover tooltips never appear on touch, so the feature was undiscoverable on mobile.

**Behaviour change:** on desktop a single click now seeks, where before it did nothing. That is inherent to having one shared gesture.

---

## Verification

Model fallback — 7 logic scenarios (fallback, fail-fast, exhaustion, same-model recovery, capped retry hint, empty list, 404-skip), plus an end-to-end run through the real adapter with two dead models at the head of the chain: both were skipped and a real answer came back. TTS returned 113 KB of audio.

Tap-to-seek — driven against the real component in Chromium, 10 assertions, all passing:

```
desktop (mouse)
  ok  click mid-"lazy"  -> 35      ok  click mid-"river" -> 58
  ok  click mid-"quick" -> 4       ok  click mid-"rests."-> 84
  ok  click the highlighted word "jumps" -> 20
  ok  drag-to-select does not seek
mobile (touch, Pixel 7)
  ok  tap mid-"brown" -> 10        ok  tap mid-"wide" -> 53
  ok  scroll gesture does not seek
  ok  long press does not seek
```

The highlighted-word case matters: the active word sits in a `<span>` that splits the text nodes, and offsets stay correct through it. Plus 18 unit assertions on word-snapping covering multi-space runs, punctuation, newlines and bounds.

`npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both pass.

In production, the previously failing request now returns `HTTP 200` with the article text in 14.1s.

author: jhyoo1203
body:
## 개요

찜한 스팟 목록 화면(SCR-024c)이 요구하는 상단 만개 배너와 카드 정보를 `GET /api/spots/favorites` 응답에 결합한다. 신규 엔드포인트·테이블·마이그레이션은 없고 기존 응답에 필드만 더한다.

## 배너는 카드마다가 아니라 목록 상단 1건

화면 실물의 배너는 목록 맨 위에 하나뿐이라, 찜한 스팟 전체에서 가장 먼저 알릴 1건을 서버가 고른다.

1. 오늘이 만개 구간 안인 스팟 — 종료가 임박한 순
2. 없으면 만개가 임박한 스팟(D-1 ~ D-`banner-lead-days`) — 남은 일수가 적은 순
3. 둘 다 없으면 `banner = null`

동률은 `spotId` 로 갈라 정렬이 매번 같은 결과를 내도록 했다.

## 절정 판정은 추정 상태가 아니라 날짜로

`status == PEAK` 로 거르지 않고 오늘이 `peak_start ~ peak_end` 안인지로 판정한다. 개화 추정은 산출일 기준 스냅샷이라, 산출 후 하루라도 지나면 상태가 아직 `PREPARING` 인데 오늘 이미 절정일 수 있다. 상태로만 거르면 **만개가 오늘 시작하는 스팟이 배너에서 통째로 빠진다** — 1순위는 상태 불일치로, 2순위는 남은 일수가 0이라 범위 밖으로 걸러진다. 날짜 기준 판정은 시기 필터에 쓰는 산식과도 같다.

**날짜 표시 문자열은 서버가 만들지 않는다.** `3.28(토) ~ 4.5(일)` 같은 카피는 화면마다 형식이 달라, 문구 본문과 원본 날짜만 내리고 포맷은 클라이언트가 한다. 문구의 조사(`이`/`가`)는 스팟명 종성으로 고른다.

## 카드에 붙는 것

| 항목 | 값 |
| --- | --- |
| 대표 개화 | 상태·만개 시작/종료일·만개 지속일·임박 여부. 상태 우선순위 → 신뢰도로 1건 |
| 꽃 카테고리 칩 | 종료된 추정을 뺀 카테고리 목록 |
| 방문 기록 수 | 게시된 기록 수 |
| 사진 | 최근 게시 기록 사진 최대 4장 |

개화 추정은 명소에만 있으므로 동네형 스팟은 개화 정보와 칩을 비운다. 기록 사진이 없는 명소형만 대표 이미지 1장으로 대체하고(빈 사진 영역 방지), 대체가 필요 없으면 명소를 조회하지 않는다.

찜 추가·알림 토글 응답도 같은 조립 경로를 타게 했다. 새 필드를 빈 값으로 내리면 "데이터 없음"으로 오해되기 때문이다.

## 조회

조립을 `SpotFavoriteListAssembler` 로 분리하고, 개화 추정·기록 수·사진을 각각 배치 1회씩만 조회한다. 스팟 수와 무관하게 쿼리 수가 고정이고 루프 안 반복 조회가 없다. 사진은 `spot_records` ⋈ `spot_record_photos` 윈도우 함수로 스팟당 상위 N장만 뽑으며, 도메인을 가로지르는 조인은 만들지 않았다(개화 추정은 따로 조회해 명소 id 로 맞춘다).

native 프로젝션에는 카멜 별칭을 붙이지 않았다. PostgreSQL 이 따옴표 없는 별칭을 소문자로 접어 `spotId` 가 `spotid` 라벨이 되면 인터페이스 프로젝션이 값을 찾지 못한다. 윈도우 함수·상한·정렬은 JPQL 로 검증할 수 없어 Testcontainers 통합 테스트로 확인했다.

## 범위

찜 목록은 기존대로 전량 조회다. 이번에 사진·기록 수 조회가 붙으면서 찜이 아주 많은 사용자는 `IN` 절이 커지지만, 페이징 도입은 응답 계약이 바뀌어 별도로 다루는 게 맞다고 보고 넣지 않았다.

author: abishekk92
body:
Closes #363.

Half of this issue was already fixed on the branch by 9922f2e, which the
issue predates. Measured against the current binary, all four user-written
reference sites now report as errors:

| site | status |
|---|---|
| `requires … else X` | ✅ Error (9922f2e) |
| `match` arm `abort X` | ✅ Error (desugars to a synthetic `requires`) |
| effect `else X` | ✅ Error (9922f2e) |
| `checked_{over,under}flow_error` pragma | ✅ Error (9922f2e) |

So the lint gap is closed. This PR does the structural half the issue also
asked for, which is what stops the class recurring.

## One resolver

`emit_errors` built the declared set from `error_codes` plus three synthesis
predicates that lived inside it as locals, so no other emitter could ask what
the enum would contain. Each one guessed, and they guessed in opposite
directions:

- checked arithmetic named `MathOverflow` whether or not the spec declared
  it, and the enum did not carry it: non-compiling program, `check` silent;
- `integration_test::authorization_error` went the other way and deliberately
  UNDER-approximated, refusing to name `InvalidLifecycle` because it could
  not tell whether the enum would have it.

New `codegen_shared::error_variants` owns the answer.
`emit_errors` and `authorization_error` both read it.

## What that fixes, concretely

The bundled multisig spec declares neither `Unauthorized` nor
`InvalidLifecycle`, but has non-init pre-statuses, so `codegen_mir`
synthesizes `InvalidLifecycle` into its enum (`InvalidLifecycle = 7`, in the
committed `errors.rs`). `authorization_error` could not see that and degraded
every forged-signer test to a weak assertion:

```rust
-    // AGENT: the spec declares no authorization error, so this only
-    // asserts that SOME error fired — it also passes on a deserialization
-    // or missing-account failure.
-    assert!(outcome.is_err(), "propose should reject wrong creator");
+    // propose must reject a forged creator with the spec's authorization error.
+    outcome.check(Outcome::error(
+        program::errors::MultisigError::InvalidLifecycle,
+    ));
```

Five assertions across multisig's integration tests were passing for the
wrong reason. `None` is still reachable and still degrades — it just no
longer fires spuriously, and there is now a test for each direction.

## The gate

`tests/error_variant_closure.rs`: for each bundled example at each target,
run codegen and assert every `<Prog>Error::<Variant>` token under `src/`
resolves to a variant the generated `errors.rs` declares. 10 example/target
pairs across Anchor, Quasar, and Pinocchio.

This closes the class rather than the instances — a reference site added
tomorrow is covered without anyone remembering to extend a list. Fast
(codegen only, no cargo), so it runs in the normal suite.

Deliberately NOT written against `emitted_error_variants`, which would be
circular: if the resolver were wrong, emitter and check would agree and the
test would pass while the crate failed to build. It reads the generated
`errors.rs`, which is what `cargo build` sees.

It also carries `the_scan_detects_an_undeclared_reference`, which generates
the live #363 shape and asserts the scan finds it. A gate that cannot fail
reads as coverage and provides none.

## One thing from the issue I did not do

The issue's step 2 says to make the `unknown_error_variant` lint consume the
resolver too, and step 3 recommends switching policy to "synthesize
user-written names + informational lint". Both are superseded by 9922f2e,
which chose the opposite and better policy: report user-written names, and
synthesize only codegen's own defaults.

Feeding the resolver to that lint would actively break it — a misspelled
`else Unathorized` would become a synthesized variant no guard ever raises,
which is a silent behavior change instead of a compile error. The module doc
records this so the next reader does not "finish" the issue by wiring it up.

## Tests

- `error_variant_closure`: 10 example/target pairs + the scan self-test.
- `authorization_error_tracks_the_emitted_enum`, which also asserts the
  emitter really carries what the scaffold names, so the two cannot drift.
- `authorization_error_degrades_when_the_enum_carries_neither`, keeping the
  weak-form path covered.
- Multisig example regenerated; `check --regen-drift` clean.

Full suite green (40 suites, 1649 tests). clippy and rustfmt clean.

## Notes

Stacked on #379 → #378 → #377 → #373. Merge in that order.

author: samatstariongroup
body:
`design.md` said nothing about primary keys or a PostgreSQL version — grepping for `uuid|Guid|primary key|identity column` returned no hits, and §8 names only natural keys.

That gap is load-bearing: DD-18 generates both the DAOs and the DDL from the Enterprise Architect model, so the key strategy is a property of one set of uml4net templates. It applies uniformly to every entity, and changing it after A-01 has run is a migration across every table and every foreign key. Cheap to decide before F-10 writes a template; expensive afterwards.

The two halves are one decision because `uuidv7()` is built into PostgreSQL 18 and no earlier release.

### The decision

1. Every entity carries a **UUIDv7 surrogate primary key**, generated in .NET with `Guid.CreateVersion7()`, with `DEFAULT uuidv7()` on the column for migrations and DD-18's hand-written tables. Natural keys keep their unique constraints — they are what enforce §8.1's invariants.
2. **PostgreSQL 18 is the minimum supported version**, in every topology of §5.1.

### What decides it

- **UUID over `bigint` identity** — §5.1.6 replicates a metadata index upstream-to-downstream, so rows minted in one database must land in another without collision or renumbering. The sequence fixes (offset ranges, per-installation blocks) are exactly the cross-installation coordination §5.1 exists to avoid.
- **v7 over v4** — random keys insert at random B-tree points: a dirtied page per insert, WAL inflated by full-page images, no right-edge locality. DD-15's download events, DD-17's job rows and A-06's audit trail are that write pattern, and they are the tables that grow.
- **18 over a plpgsql shim** — the shim is a dozen lines, but DD-18 hand-writes every migration, so it becomes a hand-maintained RFC 9562 implementation that gets the sub-millisecond monotonicity edge subtly wrong. The floor also buys skip scan (§12.1 facet counting), asynchronous I/O, and `RETURNING old.*`/`new.*` for A-06.

The DD also records what is **not** a reason — opacity, since §8.2 and DD-11 keep surrogate keys out of every URL — so the decision rests on replication rather than on a benefit Forge does not collect.

### Affordability of the floor

DD-21's shape, and a smaller ask than object storage was. PostgreSQL 18 released September 2025, GA on Amazon RDS November 2025 and on Azure Flexible Server December 2025, supported upstream until November 2030. PostgreSQL 13 is already out of support and 14 leaves in November 2026.

### Two things recorded to stop them going wrong later

- **A UUIDv7 is never a secret.** At most 74 random bits and an embedded creation time. F1-02's API keys stay random material hashed at rest — the shortest path to a token guessable from a timestamp is the assumption that an identifier already exists.
- **One contract test.** .NET `Guid` and PostgreSQL `uuid` do not share a byte layout across the first three fields, so the ordering property the whole decision rests on depends on Npgsql's conversion being canonical. §17 asserts it.

### Also in this PR

- §8, §12, §15 and §17 cross-references, including a runtime-prerequisites bullet that the document previously lacked.
- Plan rows F-07, F-10 and A-01 gain the corresponding scope; the §1 boundary table's stale `DD-01…DD-17` becomes `DD-01…DD-23`.

Documentation only — no source, project or DDL file is touched.

There was no plan row or open issue for this one (DD-21 and DD-22 came in via F-02 and F-11), so the branch is named for the decision rather than `GH##`. Happy to raise an issue for traceability if you want one.

author: apnex-greg
body:
**Fixes bug-428.** The highest-value shippable item in the arc, and sequencing-critical: deploying `ois` from current `main` would break re-seed on every seat.

## The defect, measured

```
registry versions:  0.1.3 0.1.4 0.1.11 0.1.12 0.1.13 0.1.14 0.1.19 0.1.20
dist-tag latest:    0.1.20
ois/bin/ois:49:     0.1.16   <-- DOES NOT EXIST
```

Pinned for nine days. **A fresh seat could not be seeded at all.** Existing seats survived only via the `:291` short-circuit — *"installed copy already matches, skip the install."*

⚠️ **And it compounds with bug-429:** a seat whose installed copy is destroyed cannot be re-seeded, because the short-circuit has nothing left to short-circuit on. Neither bug is critical alone; together, a destroyed seat is unrecoverable by the sanctioned path.

## The fix

Moved to **`0.1.20`** — current `latest`, the version the repo itself is on, verified not deprecated. **Not `0.1.19`**, which resolves but is deprecated for failing post-publication qualification.

## The guard is the durable half

**A pin is a claim about the registry, and no in-repo assertion can check it — only the registry can.** `scripts/test/ois-plugin-pin-resolves.test.sh` reads the pin out of `ois/bin/ois` and asserts that it (1) resolves and (2) isn't deprecated. Wired into the existing `ois shell tests` job.

### Why this needs a network check rather than a literal sweep

Miss one of the 21 in-repo version literals and the **build fails loudly** (`wrong package version`). Miss this one and **the publish succeeds** while every seat keeps installing the old version, with nothing reporting it.

**Loud versus silent is the whole difference** — and it's why this is the 22nd site rather than one of the 21.

## Falsified, both arms, with a control

| # | pin | result |
|---|---|---|
| **M0** | `0.1.20` (as shipped) | EXIT 0 — guard not saturated |
| **M1** | `0.1.16` (the live defect) | EXIT 1 — *does not resolve on the registry* |
| **M2** | `0.1.19` (deprecated) | EXIT 1 — *is DEPRECATED: Failed post-publication qualification* |

**M2 matters separately:** `0.1.19` *resolves*, so a resolve-only guard would pass it and seed every new seat with a version withdrawn for failing qualification.

`bash -n ois/bin/ois` clean.

author: nategeier
body:
## What

The most common stranger wallet — ETH, no stables — answered the flagship "Buy $12 of AAPL" with **"no USDC on Base, Ethereum, or Arbitrum"**: real money, invisible. This PR makes native ETH a first-class funding source for the Robinhood Chain plan, end to end.

**Routes probed live 2026-07-28 before building** (all three origins): native ETH → USDG and ETH → gas ETH onto chain 4663 quote through the **same canonical LiFi diamond** (`0x1231…4EaE`) we already pin, via across/relaydepository, `transactionRequest.value == fromAmount` exactly, 1–2s execution.

- **Scan** (`readFundingShortfall`): ETH origin rows — movable = balance minus a per-chain keep-back (mainnet 0.002, L2s 0.0002; the leg's own signature stays payable), priced off the venue quoter, fail-soft when unpriceable. Sub-keep-back ETH ≥ $1 becomes a **named-only** row (`spendable: false`): refusals must say it, chips never spend it, and the gas-stranded rescue never claims it (it IS the missing gas). Stables sort first.
- **Chips** (`planRobinhoodFundingChips`): best = the **first covering origin** (was `origins[0]`), so dust USDC can't force a combine past an ETH balance that covers the plan alone. Labels/segments were already token-generic (`Base ETH`, `using eth`).
- **Builder** (`buildLifiBridgeLeg`): native sell side — sized at build time off Yeetful's own ETH/USD read, sold as `msg.value` on a **single** bridge step (no approval exists), balance-checked against `sellAtoms + keep-back`. The echo + guard flip their value invariant: ERC-20 legs must carry zero, native legs must carry **exactly** the sold atoms, and any approval step in a native leg refuses. ETH→USDG price sanity reuses the priced-leg tolerance vs our own read.
- **Contract**: `parseRobinhoodFunding` + compile grow `using eth` (valid from every origin); the refresh route's token allowlist too. Both refusal copies now read "top up **USDC or ETH** on Base, Ethereum, or Arbitrum".

## Also in this PR (own commit): the unsigned-turn fence counts loopback

`next start` stamps `x-forwarded-for` with the socket address, so loopback arrived as a header **value** — `::1` had quietly become a 169-count fence bucket in Neon, and two same-hour harness runs walled their own tails (dummy-wallet keys accumulated across runs too). `clientIpFrom` now reads loopback as "no platform IP", and a null IP skips the fence **entirely** — exactly what the module contract already documented. No prod change (the proxy always stamps real client IPs); the wall drill still exercises both tiers via its forged `x-real-ip`.

## Verification

- `tsc` + `build` green; `test:api` vs a prod server: **1060 passed / 1 failed** — the standing router-select known-red only. 15 new checks: native-mode echo/guard units (value = atoms, approval-in-native-leg refused), `using eth` parse/compile, ETH-only chips whose resumes compile with the token in both legs, first-covering-origin ordering, named-only sub-keep-back ETH (never rescued), empty-wallet copy, and the fence loopback pin.
- **Live drill (burner, nothing signed)**: real scan returned spendable Base/Arbitrum ETH rows + a named-only sub-keep-back mainnet row; a real $1 Base-ETH→USDG leg built with **all six guard checks green** — single value-carrying step to the pinned diamond.
- **Live HTTP drills** through the chat route: "Buy $12 of AAPL on robinhood" → chips outcome naming the ETH holdings, USDC leading (stables first). "Buy $14…" → downsized counter-offer whose resume is a **mixed-token combine**: `Fund robinhood chain with $12 from base, then Fund robinhood chain with $2 from arbitrum using eth, then buy $13.75 of AAPL`.

No DDL, no env changes. Follow-up PR incoming: ask-failure snapshot grows a USDT read so `/dashboard/failures?funded=1` can measure USDT-only demand before we build USDT legs.

author: gtanczyk
body: ## Summary When `GAMES_SNAPSHOT_BUCKET` is set, published catalog / play / media are served **only** from the Cloud Storage snapshot. GitHub is no longer consulted on that request path for misses or Storage errors. Unset `GAMES_SNAPSHOT_BUCKET` remains the local/dev / fixtures / `local-games-repo` opt-out — not a fallback from a configured bucket. GitHub is still used for the bake job, draft/PR previews, `forceFresh` / `refreshOnMiss` catalog reads during the publishing→published transition, submissions, issues, and contract checks. ## New published-serve failure modes (bucket configured) | Situation | Response | |---|---| | Snapshot hit | Unchanged | | No `current.json` / empty pointer | **503** — no `getCatalog` / `getGameSources` / `getGameMedia` | | Storage / transport error | **503** — no GitHub fallback | | Slug published in snapshot catalog but game object missing | **502** (bake inconsistency) | | Media allowlisted but object missing | **404** | | Slug not in catalog | **404** (unchanged; catalog still decides publication) | In-process caches (catalog TTL, game TTL, last-known catalog on refresh failure) still cache snapshot results only. ## Bake: no pointer on partial failure `publishSnapshot` no longer calls `putPointer` when `failures.length > 0`. Immutable objects under the new snapshot id may still be written for debugging, but `current.json` stays on the previous good snapshot. The job still exits non-zero. Do **not** drop failed games from a newly published catalog while flipping the pointer — that would unpublish them. Prefer “pointer stays put”. ## Docs Updated `docs/games-snapshot.md` and the open-question resolution in `docs/games-repo.md`: GitHub remains SoT for content and previews; it is no longer the published-serve fallback. ## CI note Rebased onto `master` after #291 (`save` GameKit module). The earlier Games-repo contract failure was lockstep drift against games-repo `main`, unrelated to this change.

author: echoofdawn
body:
## ELI16 — main breaks its own rule, and that refusal lands on whoever tries to update an old pull request

A repo rule (Rule 3.1) says: if code reads state from an outside system, it must ship a short
paragraph justifying that, plus a row in the state-detector registry. A pre-commit check enforces it —
but only over **staged** files. So a file that reached `main` without ever tripping the check is never
looked at again.

`src/commands/devClaimCheck.ts` is one of those. It runs `gh` and parses the JSON it returns — textbook
state detection — and arrived in June (#813, `144ff6122`) with neither half of Rule 3.

**Why it stopped being cosmetic.** A merge stages *everything*. Merge `main` into an older branch and
git treats you as the author of all of `main`, so the check inspects the whole tree, finds this file,
and refuses your commit — for a violation that is not in your diff and that you cannot see. That is a
hard blocker on locally refreshing older open PRs, and it is how this was found: it blocked exactly
that work on 2026-07-28.

## What this adds

Both halves Rule 3 asks for: the in-file rationale, and the registry row.

## The part worth reviewing

The registry row is **🟡 Partial, not 🔵 Exempt** — deliberately, and unlike its neighbours. The
adjacent `gh --json` reads are exempt on "versioned structured contract" reasoning, which applies here
too. What does not apply is the fallback claim.

| path | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `gh` throws (missing, auth, network, bad JSON) | degrades **loudly** — caller sets `ghDegraded`, reports spec-scan-only |
| `gh` returns **empty stdout** | `JSON.parse(stdout \|\| 'null')` → `null` → caller's `?? []` → **"zero PRs claim these files"**, no flag |

A check that could not run renders identically to one that ran clean. Narrow — `gh pr list --json`
emits `[]` on success, not empty — and advisory-only, so the blast radius is a false all-clear on a
pre-build hint, never a wrong gate verdict.

**Not fixed here, deliberately.** Fixing it changes behaviour and deserves its own tests; bundling it
into a comment-only commit would hide a behaviour change inside a documentation change. Filed
separately. The row flips to Exempt when that path degrades as loudly as the throw path.

I could have written a tidier rationale that omitted this. The rule exists to surface the part
somebody should worry about, so it is in the comment, the registry row, and the release note.

## Verification — observed, not predicted

- Violation confirmed on `main` itself: `grep -c "RULE 3"` on `origin/main`'s copy returns **0**, and
  the file is absent from the diff of the branch that hit the refusal.
- The refusal reproduces and the fix resolves it, in three observed steps: **blocked** before the
  rationale → **blocked again** for the missing registry row → **passed** with both present.
- Comment + registry row only. No statement, signature, export, or type changes; `tsc` emits identical
  JS.
- Full instar-dev gate chain green (Tier 1: ELI16 + side-effects + trace). Pre-push gate green,
  including `tests/unit/dev-claim-check.test.ts` (10/10).

## Risk

Low. Reverting restores the pre-existing violation and with it the merge blocker.

---

## Correction after opening — this was TWO files, not one

The version I opened this PR with covered only `devClaimCheck.ts` and claimed that unblocked merging
`main` into an older branch. **That claim was false.**

An A/B test caught it. Branching from a pre-#813 `main` commit and staging a merge of current `main`
flags **two** files:

```
  src/commands/devCiFailures.ts
  src/commands/devClaimCheck.ts
```

Fixing one of two blockers unblocks nothing. `devCiFailures.ts` now carries its own rationale and
registry row in this PR.

It is marked **🔵 Exempt** rather than Partial, and the asymmetry with its sibling is the interesting
part: `devCiFailures.ts` has **no `|| 'null'` default** on its `JSON.parse(stdout)`, so empty output
throws and rejects as "gh returned non-JSON" instead of degrading into a successful-looking empty
result. Every caller catches, prints, and returns exit 1. Same command family, same API, opposite
failure behaviour — which is why one row is Exempt and the other is Partial.

### The check nearly fooled me the same way the code does

My first A/B run reported the fixed side **PASSING**. It had not passed — the merge failed on a ref I
had not fetched, so nothing was staged and the checker exited 0 over an empty file list.

That is precisely the defect this PR documents, reproduced in my own verification: **a check that
could not run is indistinguishable from one that ran clean.** The re-run asserts the check had input
before believing it — 7,499 staged files / 905 `src/*.ts` on the failing side, and it refuses to read
0 staged files as a pass.


### The A/B, re-run correctly

```
A: base 22542d636 (2026-06-01) + current main       staged src/*.ts = 905   REFUSED
     flagged: src/commands/devCiFailures.ts
     flagged: src/commands/devClaimCheck.ts

B: base 22542d636              + main WITH this PR  staged src/*.ts = 905   PASS
```

**Both sides stage 905 `src/*.ts`** — equal input volume is what makes B meaningful: the pass reflects
a check that actually ran, not one handed an empty list.

Scope note, so this is not read as broader than it is: the blocker set is
`(latent violators on main) ∩ (files changed since that branch's base)`. A read-only sweep finds **26**
files on main matching a state-detection pattern with no in-file marker; this PR fixes the **2** that
bite a 2026-06-01 base. The other 24 are unchanged since that base, so they are never staged and never
evaluated — but they will surface for branches with different bases.

Fixing those one at a time is whack-a-mole. The generalisable fix — judge the author's contribution
rather than everything a merge stages — is filed separately and deliberately not attempted here.

## What changed

- Replace cross-node browser `Range` selection in annotation mode with a geometry-based PDF text selection engine.
- Reconstruct visual lines and runs from screen coordinates, including fragmented right-side text.

author: tdakkota
body:
## Bug

`SignalsSpec` declares four toggles, but only `Profiles` was ever read
(`profilesEnabled`). `renderConfig` emitted `metrics_backend`, `traces_backend`,
`logs_backend` and the `prometheus`/`tempo`/`loki` bind blocks unconditionally,
and `apiPorts()` did not look at the spec at all.

## Impact

`signals: {metrics: false}` was accepted by the API server, stored in the CR, and
did nothing — the backend, the Prometheus API bind, the remote-write port and the
Service port all stayed wired, with no indication anywhere that the field was
ignored.

## Fix

- `internal/controller/signals.go` (new): `metricsEnabled`/`logsEnabled`/`tracesEnabled`/
  `profilesEnabled` share one `signalEnabled(*bool)` helper (nil = enabled, unchanged
  default), plus `validateSignals`.
- `renderConfig` gates each `*_backend` key together with its API bind block on the
  matching toggle, exactly as `profiles` already did. `health_check` stays unconditional.
- `apiPorts` now takes the CR and drops `prom-rw`/`prom-http`, `tempo-http`, `loki-http`
  and `pyroscope` for disabled signals, so both the container port list and the client
  Service lose them. OTLP ingest, self-metrics, health check and the peer port are
  always exposed. Port names moved to constants in `naming.go`.
- Disabling every signal is rejected. Validation lives in `renderConfig`, matching the
  existing `storage.s3.bucket is required` check, so it propagates through
  `buildConfigMap` → `reconcile` → the `Degraded` condition the controller already sets.
  No CEL/webhook was added: the repo has no `XValidation` markers and no webhook package,
  so this follows existing practice.
- Field godoc added for the four toggles (the `+kubebuilder:default=true` markers were
  already correct); README's "`profiles` is the meaningful toggle" note updated.

Tests in `internal/controller/signals_test.go` cover each signal individually disabled
(backend key, bind block, container ports, Service ports all gone, other signals intact),
nil toggles keeping everything, each signal working as the only enabled one, and
all-disabled being rejected at `validateSignals`, `renderConfig` and `buildConfigMap`.

`make test` and `make lint` (custom golangci-lint build) both pass.

Closes #2

author: tan3li
body:
## Summary

Run #98 failed: "Fetch ticket data" succeeded, "Commit and push data changes" failed with rebase conflicts in all five data files. Two runs 17 seconds apart (the external trigger's on-time job, and GitHub's own cron firing ~30min late — the exact delay the external trigger exists to compensate for), correctly serialized by the existing `concurrency` group, but not by the checkout.

## Part 1 — the checkout race

`actions/checkout` with no `ref` checks out `github.sha`, fixed at *run-creation* time, not the branch tip when the job actually *starts*. A run queued before the other one pushed does its work on a now-stale base, then can't rebase its own data commit onto files the other run already rewrote line-for-line with a different `fetchedAt`. Nothing can resolve that — it's not a merge conflict in the normal sense, it's two "regenerate everything" snapshots disagreeing about ground truth.

Fix: `ref: ${{ github.ref_name }}` on both `actions/checkout` steps (`fetch.yml`, `fetch-intensive.yml`). Verified against GitHub's own docs, not assumed, that `ref_name` resolves correctly for every trigger this repo uses:
- `schedule` → the default branch
- `repository_dispatch` → the default branch
- `workflow_dispatch` → whichever branch/tag was actually dispatched to

That last one matters: this repo relies on `workflow_dispatch` against a feature branch for pre-merge verification (see below), so hardcoding `"main"` would have silently made those runs operate on the wrong branch instead of failing loudly.

Combined with the existing concurrency group, the window is closed: a queued run can't start until the previous one has pushed, and its checkout now includes that push.

**`git pull --rebase` stays exactly as failure-prone as before, on purpose.** I'd earlier suggested these files could resolve automatically since every run regenerates them wholesale — that reasoning was wrong, and it's now recorded in a comment next to the `git pull --rebase` line in both workflows so nobody rediscovers it the hard way: a conflict means the *other* run's push contains a sample this run's own checkout never had, and resolving in either direction drops it silently. A red "Commit and push data changes" step that costs one sample is strictly better than a green one that quietly loses a data point.

**A failed push now looks like:** "Fetch ticket data" green, "Commit and push data changes" red. The inverse (fetch red, commit green skipped) means a different fault entirely — worth knowing when triaging a future failure.

## Part 2 — the Node warnings (two separate things)

**Not (fully) ours:** the annotation says `actions/checkout@v4`/`actions/setup-node@v4` declare Node 20 and are being forced onto Node 24 by the runner. Bumped both to **v7** — checked their `action.yml` directly, both now declare `node24` natively, closing the gap at the source instead of waiting for GitHub to update v4's bundled runtime. Checked for breaking changes across the version jump before committing to it:
- setup-node v5 added automatic caching triggered by a `packageManager` field in `package.json` — this repo has none, so it never fires.
- setup-node v6 narrowed that caching to npm only — more conservative, not a new risk.
- checkout v6 changed how credentials are persisted when `persist-credentials: true` — irrelevant, this repo already sets it to `false`.

**Ours:** `setup-node`'s own `node-version` was pinned to `"20"`, which reached end of security support 2026-04-30. Bumped to `"24"` — checked which version is current Active LTS rather than picking a number (22 is already past its own active-support window and only in maintenance; 24 has security support through 2028-04-30, and happens to match the runtime the runner already forces every action onto regardless). Matching bump to `package.json`'s `engines.node` and the note in `CLAUDE.md`.

The real Node 20 removal deadline (2026-09-16, when GitHub drops it from runners entirely) isn't urgent by itself — this is about not running our own scraper on an already-EOL runtime in the meantime.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` on actual Node 24.18.0 (installed via Homebrew specifically to verify this, not inferred from what's on the machine by default) — 343/343 passing

author: tachyon-beep
body:
Release branch for 1.5.0 (workspace is already at `1.5.0`; latest published tag is `v1.4.0`). Cut from `main`, which was 5 commits ahead of `origin/main` — those are now published here.

## CI was red on every branch for 16 days

Last green: 2026-07-10. First red: 2026-07-12. Every branch since — `main` pushes, PRs, dependabot — failed identically, so the floor CLAUDE.md requires was unclearable and real regressions were indistinguishable from the standing red.

**Three breakages, each masked by the one before it** (a job stops at its first failing step, so only the outermost is ever visible):

1. **Rust** — `doctor --fix` exited 1 on any machine with no language plugin, i.e. every CI runner and every fresh install. Classifier evidence comes from plugins, so `analyze` can only record `skipped_no_plugins` — which doctor reported as a repairable `problem` that `--fix` could never clear. Now degrades to the warning `plugin.availability` already raises, scoped to the two states a missing plugin explains; a `failed` run or malformed coverage still fails closed. `doctor_fix_registers_mcp_then_reports_healthy` also asserted *full* health while inheriting the developer's global plugin install — green locally, red on CI — so it now ships its own fixture plugin.
2. **Python** — the B.4* scale-gate artifact aged past its 30-day bound around 2026-07-18. Re-run on the reference workstation: GREEN, `mini_wall_seconds` 11.363 against a 30s guard.
3. **Python, revealed by fixing 2** — `test_pyright_session_queries_builtin_named_type_parameter` builds a module with PEP 695 syntax (`def identity[str](...)`), a syntax error before 3.12. CI runs 3.11. Guarded with the idiom already used for the sibling case in `test_extractor.py`.

## Also on the branch

- **`fix(cli)`: retire syntax findings for files that now parse cleanly** — clarion-3f0430d777. A stale `LMWV-<PLUGIN>-SYNTAX-ERROR` row survived its file being fixed and pinned classifier coverage to `failed` on every later run, forcing `classification.complete: false` across all eight tag read surfaces. Found on a 64k-entity index degraded since 2026-07-17.
- **10 week-review follow-ups** — analyze diagnostics + `doctor --fix` repair locking, memoized nested-class rebinding, conditionally-shadowed exports kept as reachability roots, federation seam goldens gated against producer drift, ruff extended to `scripts/`, plus the worktree-index design docs.
- **3 security fixes** — #86 ENOTDIR treated as stale (was blocking `analyze`/`doctor --fix`), #87 project `weft.toml` no longer redirects authenticated Filigree traffic (bearer-token exfil), #88 doctor's git calls go through the hardening wrapper.
- **6 dependency bumps** — #89 quinn-proto (lock-only), #67 checkout, #66 action-gh-release, #68/#65/#69 the Pages trio.

## Verification

Every gate run locally, and the whole workspace suite run **twice** — normally, and under the plugin-less `PATH` that was actually failing:

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt` / `clippy -D warnings` | pass |
| `cargo nextest --workspace --all-features` (plugins present) | 2135 passed |
| `cargo nextest --workspace --all-features` (plugin-less PATH) | 2135 passed |
| `cargo doc -D warnings` / `cargo deny check` | pass |
| ruff / ruff-format / mypy --strict | pass |
| pytest on 3.12 / on 3.11 (CI's version) | 314 passed / 312 passed + 2 skipped |
| `check-b4-gate-result.py --run-b5-smoke` | pass |

## Two things to know

- **A semantic conflict that clean textual merges hide**: #88 correctly drops the `std::process::Command` import when it moves the git call sites to `hardened_git_command`, but `repair_classifier_analysis` still spawns our *own* binary with it. Fixed in 0e7b30e.
- **The B.4* gate recurs.** It is a manually-run benchmark behind a 30-day CI bound, so CI goes red on a timer unless someone remembers. Refreshing the artifact clears today's red, not the pattern — clarion-40132c951e. `deploy-site.yml` is also not exercised by CI, so the three Pages bumps are validated only by an actual deploy.

## Bugfix pass (added after the first green run)

Three Filigree items, each verified against the code before being picked up rather than taken on the ticket's word.

- **`fix(doctor)`: probe a route the read API actually serves** — clarion-7ad374bac4. The liveness probe aimed at `/health`, which the read API **never registered**, so every operator with HTTP enabled got "stale port metadata … not reachable" against a live server. Now probes `/api/v1/_capabilities` — the one deliberately unauthenticated route, and so the only sound target (any other may legitimately 401/403 on a healthy server). The test fake answered *any* path with 200, which is why this shipped; it now mirrors the real route contract and reports the path actually probed. *Ticket stays open for the SIGTERM half.*
- **`fix(core)`: clear the environment before spawning hardened git** — clarion-9202f4acec. Git's repository selectors (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_CONFIG_*`, …) **override** the `-C <repo_root>` the wrapper passes, so a hostile or merely stale environment repointed every probe — for every caller. Demonstrated and now regression-tested: doctor read a hijacked repo's index and called this project's untracked db "tracked", and `--fix` would have run `git rm --cached` against that unrelated repository. Now `env_clear()` + a minimal allowlist (PATH, SYSTEMROOT on Windows, pinned `LC_ALL`/`LANG=C`), which fails closed on selectors nobody has enumerated yet. *Ticket stays open for the bounded-subprocess-I/O half.*
- **`docs(operator)`: stop steering operators away from Rust dead-code** — clarion-01e0bf5f6e, closed. `README.md` advertised "dead-code is Python-only today" against `language-support.md` and ADR-054 in the same tree. The sibling claim had already been fixed by the ADR-054 work — verified, not assumed.

The two partial tickets carry comments recording exactly what shipped and what did not, so the remaining halves are not lost.

Supersedes #90. Closes #86, #87, #88, #89, #65, #66, #67, #68, #69 on merge.

Часть пользовательских фраз была написана техножаргоном («API НБ РБ», «места встраивания», «Изменения не будут применены»), а ошибки не объясняли **где** произошёл сбой, **что** случилось и **что делать дальше**.

Прошёлся по всем видимым фразам (`i18n/locales/ru.json` + `en.json` и RU-литералы в `app/pages/index.vue`) по трём принципам:

**1. Проще и понятнее** — убрал техножаргон:
- «API НБ РБ» → «сайт НБ РБ»;
- «места встраивания» → «элементы приложения» / «виджет в чате»;

**2. Ошибки: где / что / что делать дальше:**

**3. Про нажатие** — действия-подсказки (retry-кнопка, «Обновить курсы», hold-to-reveal QR «удерживайте») уже сформулированы как явные действия — оставлены как есть.

author: kimoamer
body:
## What changed
- Added a storage router that keeps only `Repost Item Valuation.reposting_data_file` on the local private filesystem.
- All other files, including Prepared Reports, continue through the existing S3 implementation.
- Added a deduplication guard so repost files cannot inherit an existing S3 `file_url`/`s3_key` before the write hook runs.

## Why
ERPNext v15 creates the repost `.json.gz` file through the `File` doctype, then rewrites the same file in place using `open(file_doc.get_full_path(), "wb")`. S3-backed files return an API download URL rather than a filesystem path, causing `FileNotFoundError`.

The provided failing File record confirms the exact routing fields:

- `attached_to_doctype = Repost Item Valuation`
- `attached_to_field = reposting_data_file`

## Impact
- Repost working files are stored under the site's local `private/files` directory.
- Normal attachments, Prepared Reports, thumbnails, backups, and deletion behavior remain on S3 and are unaffected.
- No ERPNext monkeypatch is required.

## Existing failed records
Existing repost attachments already stored on S3 must be cleared by restarting the failed Repost Item Valuation document after deploying this change. The recreated attachment will be local.

## Validation
- Compared against `version-15`.
- Changes are limited to the storage router, one hook target, and the File deduplication guard.
- Full bench runtime testing still needs to be performed on an ERPNext v15 site.

author: lfarrand
body:
The v1.3.10 release failed on both Linux legs:

```
chmod: cannot access '.../publish/qrshard': No such file or directory
```

The Native-AOT output is named after the **assembly** — `QrShard` — not the tool command name `qrshard`. Windows and macOS have case-insensitive filesystems so the lowercase path resolved there; Linux is case-sensitive and it didn't. That's why the step shipped green on two of four platforms.

Verified locally: `dotnet publish` produces `QrShard`.

## Fix
Uses the correct name, and now fails with a directory listing rather than a bare `chmod` error if the publish layout changes again — this took a log dig to identify when it should have been self-describing.

## What held
The **`needs: binaries` gate** added a day earlier skipped the `nuget` job, so **nothing reached nuget.org**. The release stopped with two binaries attached and no packages published — recoverable rather than permanent. That gate went in on the argument that publication is the one irreversible step; this is the first time it mattered, and it paid for itself.

## Release state
`v1.3.10` currently has 2 of 4 binaries and no packages. Once this merges, the tag needs to be re-pointed at the fix (or a 1.3.11 cut) — I'll confirm which before touching a public tag.

author: sorenwacker
body:
Every test builds its schema with `Base.metadata.create_all`, so the suite is green whether or not the Alembic migrations work at all.

That is not hypothetical. `260728_spec_unpub` shipped with `op.inline_literal`, which rendered the partial-index predicate as the string literal `'deleted_at IS NULL'` and made `alembic upgrade head` fail outright — while the full suite passed. It was caught only by running the migration against a real database by hand.

Two tests, both against a scratch database recreated from empty so the run is meaningful:

- `alembic upgrade head` succeeds, driven as a subprocess exactly as a deploy does.
- Alembic's own `compare_metadata` finds no difference between the migrated schema and the models.

Sabotage-verified both ways: restoring the `inline_literal` bug fails the first test with the original error, and adding a model column no migration creates fails the second, naming the column.

This is the gate CLAUDE.md asks for — "drift between two things that must agree is caught by a test, not a periodic sweep". Needs the same local Postgres the rest of the suite already needs, and adds about a second.

body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @kalagarahari0-cpu :ghost:
