author: kookyleo
body:
Closes the code half of #138.

## The problem

Commit `74cf20ab` ("chore: point repo URLs at Actrium org") rewrote repository URLs to the Actrium organisation — but the six subtree upstreams were never actually moved there. `Actrium/{dagre-rs,d2-little,mermaid-little,plantuml-little,vison,graphviz-anywhere}` do not exist; all six lived under `kookyleo/` until being archived today. Every one of those URLs 404s.

This is not cosmetic: the same URLs go out in crates.io metadata, and an outside user filed [kookyleo/d2-little#5](https://github.com/kookyleo/d2-little/issues/5) about exactly this (migrated here as #138).

## What changes

**Cargo manifests → `Actrium/supramark`** (16 lines across 9 manifests, `repository` and `homepage`). The source genuinely lives here, and this matches the crates that were already correct — `font-metrics`, `supramark-diagram`, and the `*/packages/native` wrappers.

| Manifest | Was |
|---|---|
| `crates/dagre/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/dagre-rs` |
| `crates/d2-little/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/d2-little` |
| `crates/d2-little/packages/web/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/d2-little` |
| `crates/mermaid-little/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/mermaid-little` |
| `crates/mermaid-little/packages/web/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/mermaid-little` |
| `crates/mermaid-little/packages/native/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/mermaid-little` |
| `crates/plantuml-little/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/plantuml-little` |
| `crates/plantuml-little/packages/web/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/plantuml-little` |
| `crates/vison/vison-core/Cargo.toml` | `Actrium/vison` |

**UPSTREAM.md → `kookyleo/<name>`** (6 files). These record provenance rather than a current home, so they should point at the repository the code actually came from, annotated as no longer developed there. The pinned commits in each file were verified to match those repositories' HEADs before they were archived, so nothing was left behind by the merges.

## Safety

No build impact. `[patch]` is `crates-io` only and no git dependency uses any of these URLs — the `[patch."…/Actrium/dagre-rs.git"]` mentioned in `crates/mermaid-little/UPSTREAM.md` no longer exists. These are metadata fields only.

- `cargo metadata --no-deps` — OK
- `bun run license:check` — 66 manifests, all allow-listed

## Not covered here

crates.io metadata is immutable per published version, so the listing in #138 keeps showing the dead URL until the affected crates are republished. The same dead URLs also remain in `package.json` files, several READMEs, and some Rust/TS source comments — including a reference to `Actrium/mmdflux`, which exists under neither owner and needs its provenance re-checked. All tracked as checkboxes on #138.

author: mgttt
body:
跟进 Windows agent 的代码审查。Linux 部分的 10 条我逐条核实，本 PR 修掉其中 5 条（4 高 + 1 中）+ fmt，**两个提交分开**（安全修复 / 纯格式）。

## 高：seccomp 拒绝项超过 255 会静默 fail-open

BPF 的跳转偏移是 `u8`，旧实现让「命中就跳到末尾那一个 ERRNO」，偏移随拒绝项数量线性增长。第 256 项时 `n - i` 算出 256，转成 `u8` **溢出成 0** —— 「跳 0 条」就是继续往下走，一路落到 `ret ALLOW`。**过滤器静默放行，且不报任何错。**

没有加「上限检查然后祈祷没人超」，而是换成每条拒绝项后面紧跟一个 `ret ERRNO` 的形状 —— 跳转偏移恒为 0/1，**结构上不可能溢出**。代价是每条多一条指令（BPF 上限 4096，够 2000 个 syscall）。

配 300 项的回归用例，断言没有任何一条命中路径能走到 ALLOW。

## 高：卷目标允许 `..` 穿越

`-v /tmp/x:/../../etc` 只被检查了前导 `/`，落地时 join 成 `<rootfs>/../../etc` 指向宿主目录，且 `create_dir_all` 会真的在宿主上建出来、bind mount 照挂。

改成拒绝含 `..` 的容器路径 —— `-v` 的目标是用户显式写的，带 `..` 一定是笔误或攻击，静默规范化成别的路径只会让人更迷惑。

## 高：overlay 不可用时默认写共享镜像缓存

探测失败后打一句 stderr 警告然后**照常启动**，容器对 `/` 的写入直接落进共享镜像缓存，跨容器污染。

这不只是隔离缺口 —— 它**直接违反 PRD §2.2 自己的核心约束**：「限制无法生效时必须明确报错，不允许静默裸跑」。一句警告不算明确报错，它不改变退出码，脚本里根本看不见。

改成**失败关闭**。确实接受共享写入语义的用 `WBOX_NO_OVERLAY=1` 显式声明 —— 逃生口要用户自己按，不能由程序替他按。build 的 RUN 那条路（`direct_rootfs_writes`）不受影响。

## 高：OCI 层处理的内存放大

HTTP 响应上限 8 GiB 与解压上限 8 GiB 叠加，最坏同时持有约 16 GiB；未压缩层还多做一次整份 `to_vec()`。

响应上限收到 2 GiB（真实层压缩后极少超过几百 MB），未压缩层改成 `Cow::Borrowed` 不拷贝。最坏占用 16 GiB → 10 GiB。

**这仍不是流式下载** —— 整层还是要先进内存才能算 digest。真正的解法是边下载边 digest/解压/解包，那是一次单独的改造，我另立了条目而不是在这里做一半。

## 中：arm64 宿主硬编码拉 amd64

新增 `oci::default_arch()`，规则**按宿主与执行方式分开**：

- **Windows 恒 amd64** —— `wbox-linux` 是 x86-64 模拟器，拉 arm64 进去一条指令都跑不了，即便 wbox 自身编成 arm64 Windows 也不变
- **Linux 跟随本机架构** —— 原生后端用真 CPU 执行，架构不符是 `Exec format error`，报错发生在容器内部很难联想到根因

## fmt（单独提交）

直接跑 `cargo fmt` 会产生 10,635 行改动，其中大部分在 `crates/wbox-tls/src/roots.rs` —— 那是**生成的证书数据**，rustfmt 把字节串按行宽拆开重排，git blame 与 diff 全废、可读性更差。

给那张表加了 `#[rustfmt::skip]`，总改动降到 **1,987 行**，剩下的都是真代码。

## 验证

- `cargo test --workspace` → **771 passed / 0 failed**
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` → 干净
- `cargo fmt --all --check` → 通过
- `scripts/test-linux-backend.sh` → **232 PASS / 0 FAIL / 2 SKIP**
- 端到端 `pull` / `run` 照常，manifest digest 不变

## 本 PR **没有**做的（审查其余各条）

| 条目 | 为什么留到后面 |
|---|---|
| **#1 rootfs symlink 逃逸**（高）| 已确认成立，代码里甚至自己注释着「已知缺口」。修法是 `openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT)`，要动 guest VFS 的整条路径解析，且需要内核 5.6+ 的回退分支 —— 单独一个 PR |
| **#5 流式下载** | 上面只收紧了上限，真正的流式化是 pull 路径的重构 |
| **#6 Ubuntu 只是部分可运行** | 属引擎 ABI 覆盖，需要补动态加载器与符号版本 |
| **#7 guest 套件 16 个 known failures** | 同上，逐组收紧是长期工作 |
| **#8 卷 `:ro` 嵌套 mount、文件型源** | 已确认，下一批 |
| **#10 Wine job 可全 SKIP、门禁依赖公网 BusyBox** | 属 CI 编排 |

按严重程度，**#1 是剩下最该先做的**，我可以接着做。

author: fabiomadge
body:
Part of #6491, JavaScript variant — the sibling of #6497 (Go).

The runtime's universal equality `_dafny.areEqual` sends objects that are not Dafny-generated classes (no `_tname` marker) to `a.equals(b)`. Extern class instances carry no `_tname`, so:

- an ordinary extern class with **no** `equals` method **crashed** any generic comparison — `var s := {a, b}` died with `TypeError: a.equals is not a function`;
- an extern **with** a structural `equals` silently subverted verified reference equalities, as on the other backends.

**Fix.** A 3-line arm in the dispatch: objects without an `equals` method compare by identity — the equality Dafny gives reference types. Defining an `equals` method remains the structural opt-in for extern value types, the same contract as Go's `EqualsGeneric` (#6497). Because JS collections are linear scans through this same dispatch, set/map/seq operations over method-less externs become sound too — no hashing discontinuity exists on this backend.

**The behavioral delta is confined to programs that previously crashed.** Probed inhabitants of the changed arm: extern classes without `equals`, plain object literals, host objects (`Date`), and typed arrays all previously threw and now compare by identity; every `equals`-bearing object (including all runtime value types) is dispatched exactly as before. Survey of in-repo JS externs (5 files): all define classes with no `equals` — each was one generic comparison away from the crash; none relies on structural equality.

One nuance for review: the check is per-object capability (`typeof a.equals !== "function"`), not per-type — an extern inheriting `equals` through its prototype chain counts as opted in. That is the only type boundary JS offers, and it matches the pre-existing structural dispatch.

The regression test uses a method-less extern class and exercises set construction and membership (previously the crash site).

## Scope: the crash was reachable without externs

The new arm is not reached only by extern references. Two native reference kinds are plain JavaScript objects with no `equals` method — a multi-dimensional array (`_dafny.newArray` returns a bare `{dims, elmts}` literal, with no `_tname` either) and an iterator. Comparing either generically fails on master with `TypeError: a.equals is not a function`:

```dafny
var a := new int[2, 2];
var b := new int[2, 2];
var s: set<array2<int>> := {a};   // crashes on master
print a in s, " ", b in s, "\n";  // this branch: true false
```

Verified against a master build: it crashes; this branch prints `true false` and verifies. `git-issue-6491-js-native.dfy` covers both kinds, with no extern code and no `--input` shim, and the news fragment has been widened accordingly — it previously described the fix as extern-only.

author: ran-git-hub
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes `hermes status` print a yellow warning plus the exact `launchctl bootstrap` command needed when the macOS gateway LaunchAgent has been unloaded from launchd but the plist file is still on disk. Without this, the gateway stops polling Telegram/Discord/WeChat silently and the user only notices when their bot stops responding — observed up to **24 days** of silent outage on at least one user's machine.

The root cause is that `hermes_cli/status.py`'s Gateway section relies on `get_gateway_runtime_snapshot().gateway_pids`, but the `serve` (dashboard API on port 9120) process is always alive, so PIDs look healthy even when no messaging polling is happening. The macOS-specific `_probe_launchd_service_running()` helper (defined at `hermes_cli/gateway.py:1277`) was never called from `hermes status`.

`launchd_start()` and `launchd_restart()` already self-heal (see existing tests `test_launchd_start_reloads_unloaded_job_and_retries` and `test_launchd_restart_boots_out_stale_registration_before_bootstrap`). This PR only closes the *visibility* gap, not the auto-recovery path on macOS.

## Related Issue

Fixes #73368

Related (sibling bugs in the same family): #55441, #28632, #42675 (CLOSED — Docker side).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update (the misleading "container_boot auto-starts on the next boot" log message in `gateway/run.py` is replaced with a platform-aware note)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding test coverage — 6 new tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_status_launchd_unload.py`)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/status.py` (+18, −1) — Add macOS-specific branch to the Gateway section. When `snapshot.service_installed and not snapshot.service_running` on `sys.platform == 'darwin'`, additionally probe via `_probe_launchd_service_running()` and `get_launchd_plist_path()`. If plist exists and probe returns False, print a yellow ⚠ warning plus the exact `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID <plist>` command to repair.

- `gateway/run.py` (+9, −2) — Replace the misleading `"gateway_state=running so container_boot auto-starts on the next boot (issue #42675)"` log message with a platform-aware note that explains the actual macOS behavior (launchd has no equivalent to container_boot; manual bootstrap required when the service is unloaded) and points the user at `hermes status` for the fix command.

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_status_launchd_unload.py` (new, +254) — 6 unit tests covering:
  1. Warning fires on macOS when plist exists + launchd probe returns False
  2. Warning suppressed when launchd is actively supervising
  3. Warning suppressed when plist file is absent
  4. Warning suppressed when snapshot reports service running
  5. Warning suppressed on Linux/Windows regardless of probe state
  6. Import smoke test for the new symbols

## How to Test

**Unit tests** (the standard pipeline):

```bash
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_status_launchd_unload.py -v
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_status.py tests/hermes_cli/test_status_provider_label.py -v
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py -v
```

Expected: 6 + 22 + 189 passing.

**Manual reproduction (macOS)**:

1. Fresh install: `hermes setup`, confirm gateway polling via `tail -f ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`.
2. Trigger unload: `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist`
3. `launchctl list | grep ai.hermes.gateway` → empty
4. `hermes status` → should now show:
   ```
   ⚠ launchd:      plist found but service is not loaded into launchd
     Fix:          launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) /Users/<you>/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist
   ```
5. Run the suggested fix command → service reloaded, polling resumes, no restart of `serve` needed.

**Linux/Windows**: no behavior change. Verify `hermes status` output is byte-identical before/after.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) contribution rubric.
- [x] My change preserves prompt caching (no system-prompt mutations, no mid-conversation context edits).
- [x] My change is additive on macOS, a strict no-op on Linux/Windows/Docker.
- [x] I have added tests that exercise the new path and at least four regression-guard cases.
- [x] I have not grown the model-tool surface area — no new tool definitions, no new environment variables.
- [x] The behavior contract is "users see a warning when their gateway is silently broken" — not a specific number of log lines or a specific output format, so the implementation has room to evolve without breaking the contract.

author: diegofrata
body:
Builds on #79 by @Bl4Cc4t, whose commit is included here — thanks for spotting the false positive and for the kind words about the package.

## The problem

The analyzer flags every collection member of an `[Equatable]` type with GE001, even when the collection type provides its own equality. That is a genuine false positive.

## Why #79's fix needed narrowing

#79 suppressed GE001 whenever the member type satisfies `HasProperEquality()`, which falls back to "implements `IEquatable<T>`" for types from referenced assemblies. Implementing that interface says nothing about the semantics of the implementation.

`ImmutableArray<T>` is the case that matters: it implements `IEquatable<ImmutableArray<T>>` by comparing the underlying array **by reference**. Under #79 alone this compiles clean and silently compares unequal:

```csharp
[Equatable]
public partial class Sample
{
    public ImmutableArray<int> Items { get; set; }   // no GE001
}

var a = new Sample { Items = ImmutableArray.Create(1, 2, 3) };
var b = new Sample { Items = ImmutableArray.Create(1, 2, 3) };
a.Equals(b);   // false
```

That is precisely the bug GE001 exists to catch, on one of the most common collection types in modern C#. Verified against the branch before this commit.

The metadata-only fallback also meant #79 did not fix the scenario in its own description: a hand-rolled `IEquatable<T>` collection **in the same assembly** was still flagged. Its added test passes because the collection is `[Equatable]`, which is a different (and safe) condition.

## What this changes

**Signal.** GE001 is now suppressed when the collection type has *generated* equality: a visible `[Equatable]` attribute, or the generated nested `EqualityComparer` class. The latter only exists on types Generator.Equals processed, and unlike the `[Conditional]` attribute it survives to metadata, so cross-assembly detection keeps working. `EqualityTypeModelTransformer` already had this check privately; it moves to `TypeSymbolExtensions` and both callers now share it.

**Escape hatch.** `[DefaultEquality]` now suppresses GE001, matching the opt-out it already provided for GE002/GE003. Collections that genuinely implement their own value equality opt out explicitly rather than by inference.

## Reviewer notes

- `[DefaultEquality]` suppresses GE001 only in implicit mode. In `[Equatable(Explicit = true)]` the attribute is what opts a member into the comparison at all, so treating it as an opt-out would make GE001 unreachable for explicit-mode types entirely. Two existing tests encoded that behaviour and caught the first attempt. The consequence: an explicit-mode user with a hand-rolled `IEquatable<T>` collection still needs `[SuppressMessage]`.
- `AddDefaultEqualityCodeFix` is deliberately left alone. Offering "Add `[DefaultEquality]`" as a lightbulb on GE001 would suggest exactly the wrong thing for a plain `List<int>`; `SuppressWithAttributeCodeFix` already covers deliberate silencing.
- `HasProperEquality()` is unchanged and still used by GE002/GE003, where leniency about cross-assembly types is the intended behaviour.

## Tests

1374 pass. Two updated to the new `[DefaultEquality]` semantics, four added:

- same-assembly hand-written `IEquatable<T>` collection still reports GE001
- `ImmutableArray<int>` still reports GE001 (the regression this pins)
- cross-assembly collection with a generated comparer reports nothing
- cross-assembly collection with reference-based `IEquatable<T>` reports GE001

The last two compile a real referenced assembly, so they exercise the metadata path #79 relied on.

author: hayke102
body:
## What

Every transcript walk used a `bufio.Scanner` capped at 1MB per line. A Scanner reports an over-long line by returning `false` from `Scan()` and setting `ErrTooLong` — **indistinguishable from a clean EOF unless `Err()` is checked, and none of the four callers checked it.** Each therefore answered from whatever it had read *before* the long line, and answered confidently.

An entry carrying a pasted image or a large tool result is a single JSON line, so this is ordinary transcript content, not corruption. **4 of 554 local transcripts hold a line over 1MB**, the worst 2% of the way into the file.

## How it surfaced

A `D` snapshot showed a session as `finished` while every other signal said running: pane showing `✢ Topsy-turvying… (3m 59s · ↓ 12.5k tokens)`, transcript growing every 1–3s, Claude's own status file `busy`.

That transcript is 12,826 lines with its first oversized entry at line 4,341:

```
lastLeadTranscriptTimestamp() → 2026-07-12 14:26:47   ← 16 days stale
true last lead entry          → 2026-07-28 12:31:53
```

Both `conversationActivePastHook` conditions fail on that stale value, so the tiebreaker for the between-bursts frame — where a working agent's activity line is momentarily absent and the persistent `❯` box reads as a finished idle prompt — silently answered `false`. One such frame flipped a mid-turn session to finished:

```
15:32:04.867  ✻ Topsy-turvying… (3m 42s · … · thought for 8s)   ← thinking block ends
15:32:05.417  matched prompt ❯ linesFromBottom=3                 ← one frame, no activity line
15:32:05.510  hook says waiting but pane shows idle prompt, overriding to finished
```

Recovery was slow for a second reason: `fastPassSessions` carries only Running/Waiting/Starting, so on flipping to Finished the session dropped from the 500ms pass to the 2s round-robin — 14s of silence in the log before the capture.

## Blast radius

The same scanners back `sessionRotationVerdict`, where truncation biases every signal the same direction — a timestamp that looks un-advanced, a parent link that looks absent, a uuid that looks missing, all reading as *"not a rotation"*.

## The fix

One `forEachTranscriptLine` helper on `bufio.Reader`, which has no line limit, replacing all four scanner sites. Lines past an explicit 8MB cap are **skipped and the walk continues** — losing one entry is recoverable (its neighbours are usually seconds away), whereas abandoning the walk turns the entire rest of the file into "doesn't exist". Read errors are returned **and logged**: a missing transcript stays quiet (routine — a session may not have written one yet), while permission errors and mid-read I/O failures log at Warn with the path, so a partial walk is visible instead of returning a stale answer that reads as authoritative.

## Tests

Two cases that place the interesting entries **after** an oversized line and assert each reader still finds them — timestamps and `transcriptContainsUUID` (the rotation path) — plus the over-cap skip and an unterminated final line.

Run against a reverted implementation they fail, reproducing the real-world symptom exactly:

```
lastLeadTranscriptTimestamp = 2026-07-12 14:26:47, want 2026-07-28 12:31:53
transcriptContainsUUID missed a uuid located after the oversized line
```

Full suite green with `-race`; `vet`, `gofmt`, build clean.

## Deliberately not included

- **The fast-pass change.** Keeping a session on the 500ms pass briefly after a Running→Finished flip would cut the recovery lag, but that's an amplifier rather than the cause, and it has its own CPU cost — worth deciding on its own.
- **Any claim this closes the parked-job rotation bug.** Those transcripts have no line over 93KB, so that diagnosis stands independently and remains open.

  * Improved reliability when transcripts contain very large lines, including proper handling of the final entry even without a trailing newline.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage ensuring transcript scanning continues after oversized lines.
  * Added coverage for missing transcript and error reporting when the final JSONL line is unterminated.

author: brandonrobare
body:
Found during the 2.0.0 release verification walkthrough (Phase 5), running a real 73-frame reconstruction against COLMAP 4.1.0.dev0.

## Impact

**Every COLMAP reconstruction fails.** The run reaches 40% ("model conversion") and aborts:

```
COLMAP model conversion failed: rigs, cameras, frames, images, points3D
files do not exist at "...\data\colmap\1\sparse"
```

The queue retries once (`max_attempts=2`) and fails identically — so the user waits ~9 minutes to be told it failed. Nothing downstream can run: no TXT model → no registered-image count, no geo-transform, no splat training, no point cloud, no exports.

## Cause

COLMAP's mapper writes into a **numbered sub-model directory** (`sparse/0`, plus `sparse/1`… when the reconstruction fragments), never into `sparse/` itself. The `model_converter` step passed `colmap_dir / "sparse"` for both `--input_path` and `--output_path`.

Reproduced in isolation against the real workspace:

```
--input_path .../sparse    → rigs, cameras, frames, images, points3D files do not exist
--input_path .../sparse/0  → writes cameras.txt frames.txt images.txt points3D.txt rigs.txt
```

#319 introduced `_pick_best_submodel` and applied it at the two *read* sites (~`:886`, ~`:1808`) but missed this call site — which is where the sub-model directory is first consumed. Same shape as the CLI bug in #540: the fix landed on some callers and missed one.

The command is now built lazily, because `steps` is constructed before the mapper runs and the sub-model directory does not exist at that point.

## Second defect

The new fragmented-reconstruction test caught a separate bug in `_pick_best_submodel`:

```python
return candidates[[int(s[0]) for s in sizes].index(int(sizes[0][0]))]
```

`candidates` is ordered by directory name; `sizes` is ordered by image count. Indexing one with a position from the other returns the largest sub-model **only when it is also the lowest-numbered**. With `sparse/0` (2 images) and `sparse/1` (5), it returned `sparse/0`. Now it names the directory directly.

Latent today (needs a fragmented reconstruction), but it silently discards the better model when it fires.

## Why CI missed it

No test asserted the `model_converter` command. `test_reconstruction_service.py` mocks `subprocess.Popen` and checks the *return value* of `_run_colmap`, never the commands issued — so a step that fails 100% of the time against real COLMAP passed the suite. The two new tests assert the command itself.

## Verification

`ruff check .` clean; **961 passed / 1 skipped**. Both new tests fail without the fix.

## Summary

- give Research a bounded interactive source-navigation tool group while keeping high-authority browser controls closed
- activate reviewed optional-capability tool groups correctly in manifest v3
- add cross-profile tool and skill parity coverage for every built-in profile

## Why

A Research workspace created through onboarding could lack practical source-navigation tools, and explicit-catalog workspaces silently discarded the tool groups contributed by active optional capabilities. This left computational research, visualization, programming-lab, technical-documentation, and frontend tasks with selected skills but missing tools.

## Changes

- add a Research-specific browser group for observation, navigation, controlled interaction, pagination, and agent-owned tab cleanup

- accept task-time groups only when they come from an enabled, profile-compatible, non-disabled capability
- verify folder discovery, artifacts, planning, profile-plugin skills, and exact default groups across all six built-in profiles
- document the user-visible profile contract correction in the 0.4.17 changelog

body:
## Summary

- `DripStream::initialize` now emits a `created` event, mirroring every other state-mutating entry point in `events.rs`, so a stream is observable at its own contract address the moment it's created.
- `force_cancel` now emits a distinct `force_cancelled` event instead of reusing `cancel()`'s `cancelled` event, so recipient-initiated force cancellations are distinguishable on-chain from sender-initiated ones.
- `DripFactory` gains a batch `stream_addresses(ids)` resolver pairing with `streams_by_sender`/`streams_by_recipient`, resolving a page of stream IDs to addresses in one call instead of one `stream_address` round-trip per ID. Capped at `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, mirroring `create_batch_streams`.
- `DripGovernor` gains role-gated `pause_factory`/`unpause_factory` passthroughs that cross-contract-call `DripFactory::pause`/`unpause` by function name (via `env.try_invoke_contract`, avoiding a circular crate dependency), giving a `Role::Admin` holder an actual entry point to the factory's emergency halt when `GovernorAddress` is wired to the `DripGovernor` contract.

Closes #196

author: byk
body:
## Problem

A user on macOS arm64 hit this on `lore run opencode` shutdown:

```
[lore] Shutting down…
[lore] Shutdown timed out after 4000ms — forcing exit.
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error:

💣 Program crashed: Signal 6: Backtracing from 0x18c40a5e8...
zsh: abort      lore run opencode
```

Intermittent/timing-dependent — happened once on the latest nightly.

## Root cause

The shipped binary is now **Node SEA + fossilize** (replaced legacy `bun build --compile`, `packages/gateway/script/build-binary-sea.ts:6-8`). Under Node, `safeExit()` (`packages/gateway/src/cli/exit.ts:21-47` in the old version) couldn't use the `bun:ffi` `_exit` bypass and fell through to `process.exit()`.

When the 4000ms `SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS` fired while the embedding worker was mid-inference in the native onnxruntime-node addon — an uninterruptible single-threaded native call that `worker.terminate()` couldn't break (`packages/core/src/embedding.ts:1610-1632`, hard cap at 1500ms but a native batch is uninterruptible) — `process.exit()` walked the atexit/NAPI env-destructor chain with the addon's native code still in flight. The addon threw an uncatchable `Napi::Error` → `libc++abi: terminating` → SIGABRT.

A clean shutdown is unaffected: the worker self-exits via `setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 0)` (`packages/core/src/embedding-worker.ts:808`) before `safeExit` is called, so no native code is running on the way out.

Bun-mode was previously protected by `e2ebf9bc` ("avoid Bun NAPI teardown crash on gateway exit"); Node SEA was never given the equivalent treatment.

## Fix

Add `forcedExit()` (`packages/gateway/src/cli/exit.ts:89-106`) — always skips teardown:

- **Bun**: libc `_exit` via FFI (existing approach)
- **Node**: `process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGKILL')` — the only portable Node mechanism that matches `_exit()` semantics (`process.reallyExit` still runs C++/libuv teardown and would crash the same way)

Route the **6 forced-exit call sites** to `forcedExit`:

| File | Site | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `shutdown.ts:108` | direct-owns-teardown, 2nd signal | never started graceful |
| `shutdown.ts:137` | child-forward, 2nd signal | never started graceful |
| `shutdown.ts:113` | post-`runShutdownWithDeadline` | deadline may have fired |
| `run.ts:251` | child exit with signal | timed-out shutdown possible |
| `run.ts:254` | child exit (code) | same |
| `run.ts:263` | child error | same |

`runShutdownWithDeadline` now returns `{ timedOut: boolean }` so callers can pick the right exit path. Clean exits (`start.ts`, `main.ts`, `logs.ts`, `run.ts` pre-launch / no-agent / no-remote branches) keep `safeExit`.

## Trade-off

Forced exits show **137** ("Killed") instead of the signal-correct `signalExitCode`. Acceptable — a clean exit code was never going to happen on the forced path, and crash-report noise is worse than 137.

## Tests

- **New** `packages/gateway/test/exit.test.ts` (7 cases) covers both helpers under Bun/Node, including FFI success ordering, FFI failure, SIGKILL self-kill, and the unreachable-in-prod `process.exit` fallback. Uses `Module._load` interception (the CJS hook) since `vi.mock` doesn't intercept bare `require("bun:ffi")` calls.
- **Updated** `packages/gateway/test/shutdown.test.ts`: mocks `forcedExit`; asserts 2nd-signal and timed-out paths use `forcedExit`, never `safeExit`; asserts the `timedOut` flag on `runShutdownWithDeadline`.

## Verification

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/gateway/test
  → 178 files | 3104 passed | 220 skipped
pnpm run typecheck
  → clean across all 4 typed packages
pnpm run lint
  → clean on all touched files (pre-existing unbound-method warnings only)
```

Manual verification path on a MacBook once this lands: `pnpm --filter @loreai/gateway run build:binary:sea -- --platforms darwin-arm64`, run the binary, send SIGINT during a distillation that triggers embed-drain, confirm no SIGABRT (137 acceptable).

## Out of scope

- Bumping onnxruntime-node to 1.27.0 (PR #1444, merged into 0.38.0). The latest nightly already has it. This fix is independent and stacks cleanly.
- Refactoring the embedding worker to a child process. Bigger architectural change; this is the minimum change that ends the crash.
- Changing the 4000ms deadline. Even at 40s the same race exists — the fix is to make the exit itself safe, not to outrun the race.

author: davidpit1565
body:
## Summary
Continuing this session's bug-hunt into UI files with zero test coverage (alertChannels, toastNotifications, loadingStates, liveTicker, coinLogo, backtestView, portfolioView, gridView). Found and fixed 6 concrete, reproducible defects — each verified by hand before fixing:

- **coinLogo.ts**: `initialsFor`'s own doc comment claims it distinguishes PEPE/PENGU/PENDLE, but capped anything over 4 characters at 3 — so PENGU and PENDLE both collapsed to "PEN". Now takes up to 4 characters.
- **loadingStates.ts**: `showLoadingOverlay`'s returned cleanup called the shared `hideLoadingOverlay()`, removing *every* `.loading-overlay` in the document — so two overlapping callers would have one finishing first and ripping down the other's still-in-flight overlay. Each caller's cleanup now removes only its own element.
- **gridView.ts**: a market/timeframe combo can resolve `ok: true` with zero candles. Without a length check, `Math.min(...[])`/`Math.max(...[])` silently produced Infinity/-Infinity grid bounds instead of a clear message.
- **portfolioView.ts**: Buy/Sell stayed enabled while `trade()` awaited a price fetch, so a rapid double-click (or Buy then Sell before the first resolved) fired two concurrent trades from one intended click. Both buttons now disable for the duration.
- **backtestView.ts + gridView.ts**: Win rate and max drawdown are plain 0–100% magnitudes, not signed deltas, but were rendered through the signed-delta formatter — producing a spurious "+" on win rate and, for a near-zero drawdown, a confusing "-0.00%" (verified: `(-0.004).toFixed(2)` is literally `"-0.00"` in JS). Both now format as plain unsigned percentages, matching the pattern already used elsewhere (monitoringView, validationView).

`alertChannels.ts`, `toastNotifications.ts` and `liveTicker.ts` were reviewed and found to have no concrete defects.

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 633/633 passed (11 new tests locking in the fixes)
- [x] `npx vite build` — succeeds

author: nosen-nvt
body:
`next-session-container-backend-followups.md` の残 follow-up **#1 (唯一の本体実害) と #2 (テスト診断性)** を片付ける。どちらも `internal/dispatcher` の同じ 2 ファイル。

## #1 — `ResizeRuntimeID` に deadline の床が無い

PR #862 が `CanAttach` に対して直したのと**完全に同型の欠陥が、隣の関数に残っていた**。`CanAttach:1690` は `context.WithTimeout(ctx, sessionControlCallTimeout.Get())` を挟むようになったが、`ResizeRuntimeID` は呼び出し元 ctx を素通ししていた。

実害の経路 (実地で辿った):

- 唯一の呼び出し元 `internal/server/job_runtime_routes.go:55` が `req.Context()` を渡す
- daemon の `http.Server` に `ReadTimeout` / `WriteTimeout` が一切設定されていない (`internal/server/server.go` の 3 箇所とも `&http.Server{Handler: ...}` だけ)
- よって `POST /api/jobs/{id}/resize` のクライアントが接続を保ったまま engine が固まると、`ResizeRuntimeID` が **in-flight adopt のオーナーとして無期限に居座る**
- `container_backend.go` の joiner は `<-attempt.done` と `<-ctx.Done()` を select するのでハングはしないが、**bounded な joiner (`StopJobRuntime` / `SignalJobRuntime`) は全員 30s を使い切って失敗し続ける** = engine が wedge している間ずっと `boid task stop` が成功できない

修正は `CanAttach` と同じ 1 行 + `defer cancel()`。呼び出し元 ctx から**派生**させているので、より短い caller deadline と caller cancel はそのまま効く。`SandboxSession.Resize` は ctx を取らない (`containerSession.Resize` が `context.Background()` から自前で作る) ので、ctx を shadow しても Resize 呼び出しは切られない。

### ついでの原因分離

`ResizeRuntimeID` は client 切断時に `engine did not respond in time: context canceled` を返していた — ctx が呼び出し元由来である以上 `Canceled` は `DeadlineExceeded` と同じくらい起きるのに、**engine が無関係な事象まで engine のせいにしていた**。#862 が `CanAttach` でやった分離を適用:

| 原因 | ログ | エラー文言 |
|---|---|---|
| `DeadlineExceeded` (床 or caller deadline) | Warn (engine が wedge = actionable) | `engine did not respond in time` |
| `Canceled` (HTTP client 切断) | Debug (日常的・非 actionable) | `the caller went away before the engine answered` |

ログを足しているのは、この error が `job_runtime_routes.go` で **HTTP 400 の body になるだけで boid.log に一切残らない**ため。operator が daemon ログを grep しても resize 失敗の痕跡が無い状態だった。

## #2 — hang しやすいテスト 6 箇所

`*_HangingAdoptHitsDeadline` 4 本 + `Stop`/`SignalJobRuntime` の `*_AdoptTimeoutWarnsLoudly` 2 本が、`hangingAdoptBackend` を inline で呼んだ上で「返ってきてから elapsed を見る」形だった。PR #862 は自分が触った 8 箇所を goroutine+select に変換したが、この 6 箇所はスコープ外にしていた。

**両形式とも今日は pass する。違うのは落ち方**: 床が退行したとき inline 形式は自分の elapsed assertion に到達せず、`go test` の `-timeout` (既定 10 分) までパッケージごとハングして goroutine dump になる。

## 検証 (mutation × テストの対応を実測)

| mutation | 落ちるテスト | 落ち方 |
|---|---|---|
| `ResizeRuntimeID` の床 2 行を削除 | `_UnboundedCallerContextHitsDeadline` / `_TimeoutWarnsLoudly` | 5s で clean fail |
| 原因分離を 1 分岐に潰す | `_CallerCancelIsNotReportedAsEngineTimeout` (3 assertion とも) | 即 fail |
| `context.Background()` 由来の床を**全部**削除 | 変換した 6 本 + #862 が変換済みの 4 本 | **全部 5s で clean fail**、パッケージは 50s で完走 (変換前ならここで 10 分ハング) |

- `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` clean
- `go test -race ./internal/dispatcher/ -count=1` ok (46s)

## 残 follow-up

`next-session-container-backend-followups.md` の #3 (`container_backend.go` の nil ガード直前の `slog.Warn`) と #4 (init 側の engine 障害分岐の非対称) は実害小・別ファイルなので別 PR にする。

author: koppor
body:
KeePass-compatible password manager based on Flutter.

Fixes https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/208272

This was my password manager on Debian; and I wanted to run it on nixOS, too.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Claude Fable 5, model claude-fable-5)

Because I am new to nixOS packaging and I trust Fable somehow...

Built from a main-branch snapshot: the latest tagged release v1.9.11 (2024-02) no longer builds with any Flutter version in Nixpkgs. Uses the F-Droid entrypoint since upstream's production entrypoint is GPG-encrypted; OAuth credentials for the proprietary cloud storage integrations can be supplied via override arguments (documented in the Nixpkgs manual).


---

Notes for reviewers:
 
 - Why a main-branch snapshot (1.9.12-unstable-2026-07-27): the latest tagged release v1.9.11 (2024-02) pins a lockfile no Flutter version remaining in Nixpkgs can build. Upstream main is active and pins Flutter 3.44.7, matching flutter344.
- Why the F-Droid entrypoint: upstream's production entrypoint is GPG-encrypted (contains their service credentials), so the F-Droid flavor is the supported third-party build. Analytics disabled; local files, WebDAV and AuthPass Cloud work out of the box.
- Proprietary cloud storage (Dropbox/Google Drive/OneDrive) needs OAuth app credentials upstream cannot redistribute. Following the chromium API-key precedent, they can be supplied via override arguments — documented in a new manual section (doc/packages/authpass.section.md), including the Dropbox permission-scope pitfall.
- License is GPL-3.0-only per upstream LICENSE/README ("version 3", no or-later grant); the issue's gpl2+ was incorrect.
- The desktop file is installed as authpass.desktop (not upstream's Flatpak-oriented app.authpass.AuthPass  name) so GNOME/KDE can match the window's WM_CLASS/app-id to the launcher.

---

author: saket3395
body:
## What

Adds a **Pattern Analysis** tab that analyses one symbol top-down across **Monthly → Weekly → Daily → 4H** and produces a rule-based structural report: Overall Assessment, per-timeframe analysis, Stage Analysis, Pattern Summary, Key Support/Resistance and a final conclusion.

Purely additive — no existing tab, route or engine is modified.

## Data (real OHLC only)

| Market | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NSE | Upstox historical-candle | `day`/`week`/`month` native. 4H is aggregated from 30-minute candles anchored to the 09:15 session — how TradingView buckets 4H on NSE. Today's bars are merged from `/intraday`, since the historical endpoint only serves completed sessions. |
| US | Alpaca market data v2 | `4Hour`/`1Day`/`1Week`/`1Month` native, `feed=iex` by default. |

Bare symbols route India-vs-US by lookup in the Upstox NSE master. A timeframe with no data is reported as **missing**, never guessed — consistent with the existing "we do not fabricate data" stance in `lib/backtest.mjs`.

## Analysis

Swing pivots (5-bar fractals) feed least-squares boundary fits; every tolerance is **ATR-scaled** so the same rules port across timeframes.

**Stage Analysis (Weinstein)** uses the 30-period MA: its slope decides advancing vs declining, and the *prior* slope separates a flat MA that is basing (Stage 1) from one that is topping (Stage 3).

**Patterns detected:** rectangle · ascending/descending/symmetrical triangle · rising/falling wedge · ascending/descending channel · bull/bear flag · pennant · cup & handle · VCP · double top/bottom · head & shoulders + inverse · breakout · breakdown · breakout/breakdown retest · trend continuation/reversal.

Each carries **Status** (Developing / Confirmed / Failed), **Confidence %** (a weighted sum of that detector's own evidence — line-fit R², touch count, symmetry, depth, volume dry-up, break distance in ATR) and **Technical Score /10**.

Score is adjusted for **higher-timeframe alignment**: a Daily bull flag inside a Weekly Stage 4 scores below the same flag inside a Weekly Stage 2. Detections under 55% confidence are dropped, so an empty table is an honest "no high-confidence structure".

Support/resistance are **confluence clusters** across all four timeframes (swing pivots, 30/50/200 MAs, pattern boundaries), weighted by timeframe (Monthly 4× … 4H 1×) and merged within 0.6 daily ATR.

## UI

Symbol **autocomplete** backed by TradingView's own symbol search, filtered server-side to NSE/NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX so the dropdown cannot offer a symbol we have no history for. Keyboard-driven combobox (↑/↓/Enter/Esc), 180 ms debounce, stale-response guarding. Prefills and auto-runs once from the active TradingView chart symbol.

Two relevance fixes on the raw search results: rows must be explained by the query (ticker prefix or a word in the company name), since TradingView pads the tail of every list with unrelated names; and US warrant/structured-note tickers (`AAPLWXX`, `INFYPBX`) are dropped because they swamped the real listings.

## Test evidence

No test script exists in this repo, so verification is `node --check` on every module plus live endpoint smoke tests against a running server.

```
== node --check (all modules) ==
  ok  lib/analytics.mjs   ok  lib/backtest.mjs   ok  lib/history.mjs
  ok  lib/journal.mjs     ok  lib/patterns.mjs   ok  lib/signals.mjs
  ok  lib/tpo.mjs         ok  lib/tv.mjs         ok  lib/upstox.mjs
  ok  server/server.mjs   ok  public/app.js

== live endpoint smoke tests ==
  PASS GET /api/symbols — ['NSE:RELTD', 'NSE:RELAXO', 'NSE:RELIANCE']
  PASS   empty query handled
  PASS GET /api/patterns india — Bearish        (4/4 timeframes)
  PASS GET /api/patterns usa — Strong Bearish   (4/4 timeframes)
  PASS   bad symbol degrades
  PASS   missing param guarded
  PASS GET /api/status
  PASS GET /api/config
  PASS GET /api/tpo/scan — 2963 names
  PASS GET /api/test/summary
  PASS GET /api/analytics
  PASS GET /api/snapshot
  static / -> 200   /app.js -> 200   /style.css -> 200

RESULT: ALL PASS
```

The last six checks confirm the pre-existing tabs are unaffected.

Spot-checked output — AAPL: Monthly/Weekly/Daily all Stage 2, composite +0.86 aligned, Daily Ascending Triangle Confirmed 86% 10/10. RELIANCE: Weekly Stage 4, Weekly Descending Triangle Developing 90% 8.94/10.

**Not verified by screenshot:** browser automation is blocked on this origin, so the rendered tab was checked statically (all 15 DOM ids the renderer touches and all 6 new CSS classes resolve) rather than visually. Worth an eyeball before merge.

## Secrets

Audited before committing: no key material in the working tree, the staged diff, or anywhere in git history. Alpaca credentials are **market-data only**, live in the gitignored `.env`, and no trading endpoint is ever called. `.env.example` documents the variable names with empty values. `.gitignore` now also excludes `data/journal.backup-*.json` (local trading data that was otherwise uncommitted-but-not-ignored).

author: merathilis
body:
This pull request implements several performance optimizations in the ElvUI_MerathilisUI addon based on user feedback. The changes focus on reducing global lookups and improving string concatenation efficiency.

Key changes include:

- **Core/Functions/Strings.lua**
  - Localized frequently used string, math, and table functions to avoid global lookups.
  - Replaced repeated string concatenation with `table.concat` for better performance.
  - Optimized `F.String.Abbreviate` to minimize repeated function calls by accumulating results.

- **Modules/Nameplates/Nameplates.lua**
  - Localized `string.find` for efficiency.
  - Cached database access for nameplate settings to reduce nested queries.

- **Modules/Unitframes/UnitFrames.lua**
  - Localized `string.find`.
  - Cached `frame.db.name` and `ElvUF.objects` to minimize repeated accesses during loops.

These changes do not alter the functionality of the addon but aim to enhance performance, particularly in string processing and UI update paths. Further optimizations can be explored in other areas if desired.

author: damianmarti
body:
https://github.com/austintgriffith/ethskills/blob/master/concepts/SKILL.md

Tasks for `skills/concepts`, per #1. Two quizzes and one goal.

`concepts` is mostly a mental-model skill rather than a facts skill, so the pick was about which of its claims can actually be graded off an artifact. What came out testable: onchain randomness, whether an incentive is *big enough*, and three of the four CROPS habits (admin key as a censorship vector, what a public ledger exposes, and contracts-are-verified standing in for a forkable stack).

### What each task targets

**`concepts-quiz-001` — "Randomness Is Hard" (5 expects).** A 5 ETH meetup raffle, entries close Friday 20:00, prize handed over that same evening. The prompt never says *random*, *VRF* or *commit-reveal* — it asks for the exact sequence from entries-close to payout, who sends each transaction and the window it has to land in. That can't be answered without picking a source. The same-evening constraint is load-bearing: it's what makes the 256-block blockhash window (~51 min at 12s blocks) and VRF callback latency bite instead of staying abstract. Expects 2 and 3 are per-path (commit-reveal vs external service) and each passes trivially when the run took the other one, so every design still faces the same three shared lines.

**`concepts-quiz-002` — "is the incentive sufficient?" (4 expects).** This is the third question SKILL.md attaches to every state transition, and the one I couldn't find covered anywhere else. The design handed to the executor already passes the first two questions — `harvest()` is permissionless and it pays its caller — so the only thing left to get wrong is the arithmetic: 1% of ~$0.88/day against 250k gas of mainnet cost.

Deliberately distinct from `ship-quiz-003`, which grades whether a design names a caller and a reason **at all**. This grades whether the reason is big enough to move a caller who's paying gas.

Worth flagging how the numbers landed: my first draft was a $250k vault with a 1% cut, and checking live gas killed it — at ~0.09 gwei and ETH ~$1,945, a daily harvest is comfortably profitable and there's no derivation left to test. Re-sized to launch scale ($8k of deposits), where the caller's fee is ~$0.009/day against ~$0.05 of gas: break-even ~5-6 days now, ~50 days at 0.9 gwei, months if gas returns to multi-gwei. A stale-prior model that reads gas as expensive reaches the same verdict, harder. The expect grades the break-even the run derives *from the prices it states*, not a fixed interval — the spread inside sub-1-gwei alone is a factor of ten, which is too much to freeze into a rubric.

**`concepts-goal-001` — the same claim, unprompted (7 expects).** Onchain billing for a small API service: pre-funded USDC balances, monthly plans, cancel any time, and the backend needs a per-request "is this address subscribed" check. The prompt never says automatic, keeper, cron, incentive, admin, privacy, open source or decentralization. "Charged monthly for as long as they keep the subscription" is the trap — there is nothing to run it. The per-request check is deliberate too: it leaves the read-time accrual design (no periodic transaction exists to pay for) available as the strongest answer without hinting at it.

Expects 2-4 grade *nothing is automatic* plus the hyperstructure test (can a customer still get their funds out with nobody operating the thing). Expects 5-7 grade the CROPS habits the skill says to surface rather than scaffold silently: censorship (5), privacy (6), and open source (7) — the last one leans on the fact that the subscription buys access to a weather API the provider runs, so public contracts are visibly not the whole stack. Bare workspace, no template, stack left to the executor — so we also record what it reaches for.

Read together: quiz-002 measures knows-when-asked, goal-001 measures applies-unprompted. The issue's "keep as skill" row is only reachable from that split.

### What these tasks don't cover

So the coverage claim is legible rather than implied:

- **CROPS "Security" — "audited" treated as proof of security.** Untested here. A derivation-shaped test of it lands on `skills/security` / `skills/audit` turf rather than this one, and this build has no natural hook for it. Flagging that #39's audit tasks don't cover it either, so it's currently a hole in the suite as a whole.
- **The "Teaching Your Human" section.** The pedagogy framing isn't gradable off an artifact. Its two hard technical claims already are, elsewhere: the approve pattern / infinite approvals in `security-quiz-004`, and never reading prices from a DEX pool in `security-quiz-002`.
- **The SpeedRun learning path.** Not gradable this way.
- **`onchain` vs `on-chain`.** See below.

### Notes on the `notes:` blocks

Following the point raised on #3 — the `notes:` reader is a fresh orchestrator that never saw this PR. So they carry only what's needed to run and grade: the claim and its SKILL.md section, which input clauses are load-bearing and must not be softened, the ground truth to re-check on run day, what to record per run, and the workspace shape. Scenario history, review back-and-forth and the reasoning above live here in the PR body instead.

Where a carve-out has to reach the **judge**, it's written into the expect line itself rather than the notes — the judge never sees notes.

### Three things for reviewers

**1. Vendored `skills/concepts` has drifted from live, and CROPS is being spun out into its own skill.** Live `ethskills.com/concepts/SKILL.md` now expands CROPS' O to "Open Source **and Free (as in Freedom)**", rewrites that bullet around licensing (a verified contract with no real license isn't open), reworks the second catch-yourself question, and adds a pointer to a new `crops/SKILL.md` — which exists (`https://ethskills.com/crops/SKILL.md` returns a full skill covering custody, admin keys, hosted infra, privacy, user exit and restrictive licenses). It isn't vendored here and isn't on #1's checklist. The vendored copy at `191dcc1` predates all of it.

Tasks are written against the vendored copy, since that's what actually gets installed into the workspace. Diffed the two: nothing outside the CROPS section changed, and expects 5-7 grade the censorship, privacy and whole-stack points, which survive both wordings. Two things a re-vendor would bring: a licensing claim nothing here tests, and a `with_skill` run that may fetch `crops/SKILL.md` over the network — which would make the delta about the bundle rather than this skill, the same problem `ship`'s notes flag. Worth deciding whether `crops` becomes a 20th vendored skill with its own tasks, in which case expects 5-7 arguably belong there.

**2. `onchain` vs `on-chain` is graded nowhere.** The skill makes the call explicitly, and a run's prose is the obvious place to check it. I left it out of the expects on purpose: a run passes only when *every* line passes, so a single hyphen would sink an otherwise-correct build and make the delta unreadable. All three tasks record it per run in `notes:` instead. Happy to promote it to an expect if you'd rather grade it.

**3. Two things in the tasks that exist for evidence-plumbing reasons, not eval reasons.**

- `goal-001`'s input carries the generated-dirs guardrail line that `ship-goal-001` already has. `scripts/verify.ts:21` drops `lib/ dist/ build/ out/` from the snapshot, and `:221` grades any workspace containing `.git` from `run.diff` — which `git add -N` + `git diff` leaves **empty** if the run committed its own work. Without the guardrail a Foundry or `create-eth` run could show the judge nothing and fail expect_1 for code sitting right there. The `notes:` tell the orchestrator to check the evidence before grading rather than grading the gap.
- `goal-001` expect_2 is scoped to the provider withdrawing revenue that accrued **without** that transaction. An earlier wording allowed "revenue it has already earned", which is itself an operator-only transactio

author: kusui26
body:
## 概要

散布図で、k-means のクラスタ番号に**欠番**（例 `{0, 2, 3}`）が生じると、最大番号のクラスタの点が**警告なしに描画されない** silent data loss がありました。PR #33（配色変更）の検証中に発見し対象外としていた事象です。

診断・設計・検証の全記録は [`docs/260728_fix_scatter_chart_sparse_cluster_labels.md`](../blob/fix/scatter-sparse-cluster-labels/docs/260728_fix_scatter_chart_sparse_cluster_labels.md)。

## 根本原因

生産側と消費側の前提がズレていました。

| 層 | 前提 |
|---|---|
| `presenter.ts:70` | `clusterCount = new Set(clusters).size`（＝**種類数**） |
| `protocol.ts` | 両者の関係を**規定していなかった**（`z.number()` のみ） |
| `ScatterChart.tsx:39-42` | `0..clusterCount-1` が**すべての**ラベルだと仮定 |

k-means の Lloyd 反復は空クラスタを作りうるため、生の割当は欠番を含みえます。空が**末尾**なら連番のままで無害ですが、**中間**が空だと `{0,2,3}` のような欠番になり、UI は `c = 0,1,2` の dataset しか作らないため `cluster === 3` の点がどこにも入りません。

## 再現（実測）

| 項目 | 実測 |
|---|---|
| 入力 | `x = [2,2,8,7,1,0,12]`（`y` は全点 0）＝ 7 点 |
| ラベル | `[0,0,2,2,0,3,2]` → 種類 `{0,2,3}`（**1 が欠番**） |
| `clusterCount` | 3 ／ `max+1` = 4 |
| dataset 点数 | `[3, 0, 3]` |
| **描画** | **6 / 7 点**（`x=0` の駅が消失） |

`buildGrowth` → `scatterPanel` の **domain 実経路でも同一**でした。

**発生頻度**：小標本かつ離散値のときに限り 0.005–0.01%（n=7–15）。n≥20 では 20,000 試行中 0 件。20 万試行の探索では空クラスタ 14,851 件に対し欠番 15 件で、この偏りは「k-means++ が候補枯渇時に重複重心を**末尾に追加**する」性質で説明できます。

**実データ**：`/api/growth` を 576 組合せ（6 指標ペア × 48 エリア × 除外 2）走査して **0 件**。ただし **n=5〜11 の小標本が実在 8 件**（地価増減率 × 人口増減率＋低分母除外の地方県）＝リスク域は日常的に作られています。

## 修正内容（6 ファイル・+171 / −6 行）

- **`src/domain/growth/kmeans.ts`（案 A）**：戻り値のラベルを **昇順で 0..m-1 に詰める**（`compactLabels` / 純関数）。JSDoc の契約を「0..m-1 の連番（m ≤ k・欠番なし）」に更新。**昇順**なので欠番のない通常ケースは**恒等変換**。
- **`src/components/panels/scatterDatasets.ts`（新規・案 C）**：`groupPointsByCluster()` — 点を実在するクラスタ番号ごとに 1 パスで束ね昇順で返す純関数。描画から分離してテスト可能に。
- **`src/components/panels/ScatterChart.tsx`**：dataset 構築を上記に置換し **`clusterCount` への依存を解消**（O(clusterCount × n) → **O(n)**）。配色・点サイズ・凡例・クリック挙動は不変。
- **`src/shared/protocol.ts`**：`cluster` に「`0..clusterCount-1` の連番」という不変条件をコメントで明文化（コード変更なし）。
- **テスト +10**：最小再現の回帰／ランダム 4,000 試行の連番不変条件／境界値（空・1 点・`n<=k`・全点同値）／`buildGrowth` の `clusterCount === max+1`／`groupPointsByCluster`（昇順・入力順保持・**欠番でも全点保持**・総点数保存）。

`src/shared/api.ts` / `src/app/api/**` / `src/db` / `src/ai` / `pipeline` / `supabase` は **diff 0**。

## Description

This PR fixes a thread-safety race condition described in #1320. The issue occurred when `BaseDB.db_execute()` released the lock before the `Result` was consumed, causing `Row._asdict()` to crash with `IndexError: tuple index out of range` under concurrent threads (especially during `SSHDatabase.add_host()`).

The fix holds the lock across both execution and row buffering by using a `with` context manager and freezing the result before returning it to the caller if it returns rows.

author: jelitz
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4589.

`external_plugins/context7/.mcp.json` spawns the MCP server with a bare `npx` command. On Windows, `npx` resolves to the `npx.cmd` shim, which Node's `child_process` cannot spawn directly without a shell — it fails immediately with `ENOENT`. Claude Code's MCP client doesn't surface that spawn-level error, so it just times out after 30s instead, making the real cause hard to find.

## Fix

Added `external_plugins/context7/run.js`, a small wrapper that:
- Enables `shell: true` only on `win32` (POSIX behavior is unchanged)
- Builds the command as a single string rather than an args array when using a shell, so Node doesn't emit the `DEP0190` unescaped-shell-args deprecation warning
- Forwards the child's exit code/signal

`.mcp.json` now launches `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/run.js` instead of `npx` directly.

I considered just swapping the config to `"command": "cmd", "args": ["/c", "npx", ...]` (the workaround from the issue), but that would break the plugin on macOS/Linux since `cmd` doesn't exist there. Routing through a Node wrapper keeps a single cross-platform-safe manifest.

## Testing

Ran the wrapper directly on Windows (`node run.js`) and confirmed it launches `@upstash/context7-mcp` cleanly on stdio with no `ENOENT` and no deprecation warnings:

```
Context7 Documentation MCP Server v3.2.5 running on stdio
```

## Scope note

Other external plugins that spawn bare `npx`/`npm` (e.g. `playwright`, `firebase`) likely hit the same issue on Windows. Keeping this PR scoped to `context7` (the plugin from the linked issue); happy to follow up on the others if maintainers want the same pattern applied more broadly.

body:
## Scope

One focused extension to the existing textual no-op guard, rebased on current `main` (`06c069b`). Two files only; no schema, migration, packaging, or generated changes.

A live local-model run ended with a confident future-tense promise — `I'll start by calling write...` — but emitted no structured tool call and finished `stop`. The existing guard catches fenced pseudo-calls, literal tags, and repeated blocks, but not narrated intent.

This change adds a conservative `promised-tool` tell for explicit first-person future action in English and Russian. It runs only in the existing no-tool-call settlement branch. The corrective steer never executes text; it tells the model that promising/describing a call did not run it and asks for a real tool call. Past-tense completion reports and user-facing instructions remain negative cases.

## Validation

- Textual-call tests: **16 passed**.
- Core typecheck: passed.
- Regression fixture uses the exact live failure form (`I'll start by calling write...`).

## Porting recommendations

- Cherry-pick `233adc7` when the downstream tree already has the textual no-op settlement guard.
- Keep detection inside the assistant no-tool-call settlement path. Do not scan user messages and do not execute text that resembles a call.
- Preserve the negative fixtures for past-tense completion and user instructions. They prevent ordinary explanations from causing an extra provider turn.
- When adding another language, add positive first-person future-action fixtures and negative instruction/completion fixtures together.
- If downstream tool names differ, update the known-tool vocabulary without broadening the future-action grammar.
- Run the textual-call suite and Core typecheck. Replay the original no-call response and confirm that exactly one corrective continuation is scheduled.

Likely conflict areas are the textual-call classifier and the runner settlement branch. This change has no database, protocol, UI, or generated-code dependency.

This is intentionally separate from the closed omnibus Linux PR, following the maintainer request for small single-purpose changes.

author: timdebruijn
body:
The bridge read `esp_core_dump_get_summary()` and kept **three** fields out of it. The summary also carries the exception cause, the faulting address, and a sixteen-deep backtrace — read and thrown away.

## What that cost

Trying to diagnose the dump on the EverSolar bridge, its one PC decoded to:

```
0x4037daa9: Cache_Wait_Idle
 (inlined by) Cache_Freeze_ICache_Enable
```

That is the IDF's own cache code, on the panic path — where the *handler* was running, not where the fault was. The one field being reported was the one field that could not answer the question.

`exc_cause` and `exc_vaddr` need **no ELF at all**. "LoadProhibited at 0x00000000" is a null dereference, said in full, before a symbol is looked up. That is the difference between needing a cable and not.

**The dump lives in a flash partition and survives reboots**, so this reads the crash already stored on that bridge — not only the next one.

## Where each field goes, and why not everywhere

| Output | Gets |
|---|---|
| REST | everything, backtrace included |
| MQTT | cause + faulting address only |
| Prometheus | **nothing new** |
| Modbus | unchanged (the present flag) |

**MQTT** gets two short fields so a Home Assistant notification can say *"crashed on a null dereference"* instead of *"crashed"*. The backtrace does not travel: sixteen addresses that never change, republished every diagnostics interval, for something nobody reads there.

**Prometheus gets nothing.** `heliograph_coredump_present` already exists and is the right shape — a 0/1 to alert on. A backtrace is not a time series, and putting the cause in a label would change an existing series' identity for far less benefit than the `phase` label in #104 bought. Today's "every channel reaches every output" rule was about *measurements*; a crash dump is not one, and the reasoning does not transfer.

## Null, never zero

`0` is a real EXCCAUSE (`IllegalInstruction`) **and** a real faulting address, so neither can double as "unknown". `causeKnown` carries that, and `test_cause_zero_is_a_cause_not_an_absence` exists specifically to stop it being simplified away later.

The backtrace is bounded by the array size as well as the reported depth — that depth comes out of a structure that has already survived a crash, and trusting it alone would read past the end of a fixed sixteen-entry array if it were wrong.

## Verification

**823 native tests** (818 + 5 new), covering: cause and backtrace reported without an ELF, cause 0 treated as a cause, a dump without extra info reporting null rather than zero, an unknown cause keeping its number, and the backtrace staying off the MQTT payload.

`check_layering.sh`, `check_web_js.py`, `check_measurement_ids.py`, both firmware targets build clean.

## After merging

Flash the EverSolar bridge and fetch `/api/v1/diagnostics` — the crash from 2026-07-26 should finally say what it was. The backtrace addresses still want the ELF of whatever version crashed for symbol resolution, but the cause and faulting address do not.

Users can start and stop recording from the main menu, see recording status and point counts, recover interrupted recordings, choose a safe unique filename, and share saved tracks. author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [djlint](https://pypi.org/project/djlint) from **1.42.3** to **1.43.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 1.43.1
   ```
   Fix

- `H025` no longer reports the closing tag of a multi-line `<script>` or `<style>` as an orphan - a regression in 1.43.0. A genuinely unmatched `</script>` is still reported.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.43.0
   ```
   Feature

- New `--stdin-filename` option gives content piped in on stdin (`djlint -`) its real path, so `per-file-ignores` matches against that name and linter messages report it. Per-file ignores were previously dead for piped input, since nothing matches the name `-`. Path separators are normalized as they are for files on disk.

 Fix

- An apostrophe inside a template tag nested in an attribute value (`title="{% translate "You don't have permission" %}"`) no longer swallows the rest of the document, which made `H025` report every enclosing element as an orphan. A template tag in a value is now skipped whole unless it holds a `>`, so a quoted literal like `a="{{"` is still left alone.
- A line that starts with a closing tag and ends with a whole tag (`</span>tail<textarea>y</textarea>`) unindents again; everything after it stayed one level too deep.
- A template block tag followed by a whole html tag on the same line (`{% endif %} <td class="x">y</td>`) indents as a block tag again, so `{% endif %}` unindents and `{% else %}` aligns with its `{% if %}`. A line only takes that shape once the tag fits on one line, so reformatting an already formatted file moved it.
- A tag opened after the end of a verbatim block on the same line (`</pre> <span>x`) is tracked again; its closing tag took a level from a tag opened before the block, dedenting that tag's siblings.
- A template control block written across lines is kept that way when it opens against a tag (`<div>{% if x %}`), and the choice is no longer applied to the wrong block. Blocks were paired with the source by position, which does not line up with the expanded html; they are now matched by tag and contents.
- A tag whose `style`, `srcset`, `data-srcset` or `sizes` value was written over several lines is no longer spread over multiple lines and pulled back together on the next run. `max_attribute_length` is now measured against what is written out, not against padding that the rewrite drops.
- A `<pre>` or `<textarea>` opened on a line that also holds a self-contained comment (`<pre>x<!--c-->`) is recognized as opening a verbatim block again. Its contents were re-indented instead of left alone, and the closing `</pre>` gained an indent level on every run - unbounded whitespace growth inside preformatted text.
- A closing tag that starts its line no longer dedents when the tag it closes was opened after text on an earlier line (`text <b>bold` / `</b> tail`). The loss accumulated, so a document repeating that shape drifted further left with each occurrence. A closing tag with nothing to pair against still dedents as before.
- A `<` inside a one-line `<script>`, `<style>`, `<textarea>` or `<title>` no longer counts as a tag when indenting. `<script>var a = '<span>'</script>` left a phantom open `<span>` on the tag stack, leaving everything after it one level too deep.
- An inline element that opens after text on its line and closes on a later line no longer dedents everything that follows it by one level (`text <b>bold` / `more</b> tail` inside a `<p>`) - a regression in 1.40.8. The wrong output was idempotent, so it survived later runs.
- A Go template comment `{{/* ... */}}` is no longer read as a block close tag. It starts with `{{/`, the handlebars block-close prefix, so it popped a block off the stack: `H037` reported `Duplicate attribute found.` for mutually exclusive attributes such as `<a {{if .A}}href="a"{{else}}{{/* c */}}href="b"{{end}}>`, and the formatter unindented the rest of the block. A comment renders as nothing, so `H037` no longer treats one as a template-generated attribute name prefix either.
- A tag that merely touches an ignored block is no longer treated as being inside it. A tag ending exactly where an ignored block starts - such as `{% if x %}{ comment }` - was skipped by the linter, most visibly making `T038` report `End tag has no matching block tag` for a balanced `{% if %}`. Affects every rule that skips ignored blocks (`H025`, `H037`, `H041`, `H042`, `T002`, `T003`, `T027`, `T038`, `T039`) and every kind of ignored block.
- A bare `djlint:off` pragma no longer ignores the tag written immediately before it. `<img>{ djlint:off }` silently dropped every error on that `<img>`, while `<img>{ djlint:off H013 }` correctly reported it - a pragma covers what follows it, not what precedes it.
   ```
   
  
</details>


 

<details>
  <summary>Links</summary>
  
  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/djlint
  - Changelog: https://data.safetycli.com/changelogs/djlint/
</details>

author: ingolf-lohmann
body:
## Purpose

Implements the repository-native event-driven monitor/watchdog adapter requested under Issue #87 and Work Unit RCP-001.

## Event path

GitHub events (`push`, `pull_request`, `issues`, `issue_comment`, selected `workflow_run`, `release`, `create`, `delete`, `repository_dispatch`, `workflow_dispatch`) are normalized into canonical SHA-256-bound Effect Acknowledgement frames. No periodic repository polling loop is used by this adapter.

## Persistence

Each event frame is persisted idempotently on the dedicated `effect-ack-ledger` branch and uploaded as an immutable Actions artifact. Pushes to the ledger branch are excluded from the workflow to prevent recursive triggering.

## Fail-closed semantics

The candidate never infers productive progress merely from activity and hard-codes `pass=false`, `final_pass=false`, and `effect_ack_done=false`. Failed workflow completions yield `BLOCK` with deterministic next effect `INSPECT_FAILED_WORKFLOW_RUN`; other observed events yield `EFFECT_ACK_CONTINUE` and require repository-state refresh.

## Added

- `.github/workflows/qikvrt_event_driven_monitor_watchdog.yml`
- `tools/qikvrt_effect_ack_event_adapter.py`
- `tests/test_qikvrt_effect_ack_event_adapter.py`
- `schemas/qikvrt-effect-ack-event-frame-v1.schema.json`
- `capabilities/monitor-watchdog-effect-ack-v1.json`

## Validation boundary

The test script covers push, successful workflow and failed workflow classification, digest presence, immutable frame creation and no-false-pass fields. A local network-isolated clone attempt could not resolve `github.com`; therefore only GitHub-hosted exact-head checks may establish execution evidence.

This PR is a candidate only. It requires repository evidence materialization, mandatory exact-head gates, first real event-frame persistence, Authority promotion, Mirror synchronization and reciprocal equality evidence before any completion claim.

Refs #87 #153.

## Summary

Completes the base-image CVE remediation started on this branch. The CRITICAL/HIGH Trivy gate (`docker-publish.yml`, `security-scan-scheduled.yml`) now passes with **0 findings**.

### Why ignore instead of bumping the base image

The image was rebuilt with `docker build --pull` against the freshest `python:3.13-slim` (Debian 13.6) and re-scanned with the latest Trivy: **every reported CVE has no fixed package version in trixie** (status `affected` / `fix_deferred`). A base-image bump therefore cannot remediate any of them today — the ignore list is the only option, and every entry carries an `exp:2026-09-15` expiry to force re-evaluation.

### Newly ignored (all NO-FIX in trixie, each with a reachability justification)

| Package | CVEs | Severity | Why acceptable |
|---|---|---|---|
| perl-base | CVE-2026-42496, CVE-2026-8376, CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-57433, CVE-2026-42497, CVE-2026-48962, CVE-2026-9538, CVE-2026-57432 | 4x CRITICAL, 4x HIGH | perl is a dpkg-essential package, never invoked by the Python server |
| libacl1 / libattr1 | CVE-2026-54369, CVE-2026-54371 | HIGH / MEDIUM | requires a privileged process; container runs as non-root `appuser` |
| gzip | CVE-2026-41992 | HIGH | LZH decoder path unreachable, no untrusted archive processing |
| util-linux family | CVE-2026-53615 | HIGH | libblkid partition probing never happens in this container |

### Not ignored

MEDIUM base-image findings (glibc, sqlite3, zlib, bz2, pam, tar, further perl/util-linux issues) remain visible: CI reports MEDIUM informationally with `exit-code: 0`, so they don't gate and staying visible is preferable to widening the ignore list.

author: diegoriccardi1234
body:
## An offer nobody read no longer gets a score

Every failure path used to invent one anyway, by counting words the posting shared with the CV. Once stored, that number is indistinguishable from a model's verdict, and it sorts among the real ones: on a real scan, **7 of the 11 highest-scoring off-target offers had never been read by anything** — a PAYROLL SPECIALIST at 6/10, a DIGITAL COMMUNICATION SPECIALIST at 8/10.

Such an offer is now **unevaluated**: no score, no advice, no match axes, a `non_valutato` flag, and `NULL` in `punteggio_ai` — which in SQL satisfies no `min_score` and sorts last, so an unread posting cannot outrank a judged one. A hard-blocked offer keeps its 3/10: that cap is computed by the app from the ad, not guessed.

- Migration **018** cleans what is already stored (preserving the deterministic caps), because the scan only self-heals a job the day the same posting reappears — which, for an expired ad, never happens.
- New `POST /api/jobs/{id}/analyze` and a **"Re-evaluate with AI"** button: until now an archived job could not be scored at all.
- The scan reports how many offers it left unjudged, why, and what would fix it — mid-run after three in a row, and in the summary. Settings gained a per-provider track record read from `usage_log` (free, no inference).

## Less noise, and it is the user's noise to define

The relevance gate read title+description and fired only on *zero* overlap — a bar no corporate ad ever fails, since "data", "software" and "cloud" appear in all of them. It dropped nothing.

- The **title** now has to name a trade the user practises, and the vocabulary comes from **them** — the terms they search, their CV skills, the roles they declared — not from a list in the app, which would only ever work for the job this app was first written for. Bare role words are excluded, or searching "AI Specialist" would teach the gate that "PAYROLL SPECIALIST" is on topic.
- A **description that talks about the trade throughout overrules a silent title**: "RAI Specialist" at Accenture is a *Responsible AI* role, and one of the best matches in the archive. Threshold measured, not guessed. Short acronyms match case-sensitively — "ai" is an everyday Italian preposition.
- "Candidatura spontanea" forms are dropped (one scored 8/10 — it is not a position); aggregators are flagged, not dropped.

## Measured on the real archive

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| off-domain postings scoring ≥6 | 11 of 47 | **0** |
| offers scored by keyword guess | 7 | **0** |
| LLM calls per analysis | 191 / 36 | **4 / 10** |

Two live scans on the installed database, scored by a local 12B on the user's own GPU: zero unevaluated, zero off-domain.

## Also

- **Two UI regressions**: provider names rendered one letter per line (the "Free" badge added in 1.7.8 pushed a full flex header past its width), and the model picker could not scroll (a grid with no row track).
- **Local models**: VRAM is costed from the quantisation the tag names instead of one flat Q4 coefficient — an FP16 build was offered as fitting a card three times too small — plus suggestions read from Hugging Face and filtered to the user's card, with the exact `ollama pull` command.
- **Quota**: calls to a model on the user's own PC no longer count against the daily cloud budget, and the ceiling is finally editable (it could stop a scan and was writable neither through the API nor from any screen).
- The chat no longer receives `Score: None/10`, which a model reads as a zero.

724 tests, `mypy` and `ruff` clean, i18n parity across five locales.

author: jastinxyz
body:
The account system was unreachable. `/login` existed and worked, but nothing on
the public site linked to it, the `/v1` reference lived only in the GitHub
README, and plans were readable only through an admin route — so a pricing table
wasn't even possible. A developer landing on the site had no way to find out any
of it existed.

## Why a page of the app, not a docs site

It has to be **instance-aware**: it states this deployment's base URL, this
instance's served domains and this operator's plan limits, all read per request.
A static site is built against one deployment and would be wrong for every
self-hoster, and would either ignore the operator's branding or duplicate the
whole theming system.

**One page, not one per endpoint.** A reference is scanned rather than read, so
Ctrl+F beating navigation matters more than tidy sections — Stripe puts ~200
endpoints on one page. Guides get their own pages when there are guides.

**Per-endpoint depth waits for OpenAPI.** Request/response schemas and per-field
types are ~10× this content and every field is a claim about code that can
drift. Hand-writing them for 13 endpoints is a drift machine; depth and
generation are the same decision, so that's `@hono/zod-openapi` first, as its own
PR. Recorded in AGENTS.md so it isn't re-litigated.

The endpoint list is **data, not markup** (`lib/docs.ts`) — adding an endpoint is
adding an entry, and the day this is generated only the source of that array
changes.

## New: `GET /api/plans`

Public and keyless. A plan's limits are what a prospective customer is deciding
on, and hardcoding the numbers this project happened to ship with would be wrong
on every instance but one. It's a price list without the prices.

## Syntax highlighting that costs nothing

Shiki runs during the render, so the browser gets coloured markup and none of the
highlighter — **`/docs` ships less JavaScript with highlighting than the first
draft did without it** (3.58 kB → 2.53 kB). Both themes are emitted as CSS
variables and `globals.css` picks one, so the theme toggle needs no re-highlight
and no second render.

## Funnel

- Inbox header links here, and shows **Dashboard only once there is a session** —
  the inbox works without an account, so an anonymous visitor has nothing to sign
  in for there.
- The dashboard's Quickstart panel points here instead of carrying its own copy
  of the curl samples, which was a second place to keep right.
- `/docs` link in the dashboard sidebar and mobile nav.

## Sidebar follows the reading position

Measured on scroll behind a rAF rather than with an IntersectionObserver:
sections here vary wildly in height, and a short one (Base URL is three lines)
can pass straight through an observer band without ever becoming current.

## Costs, stated plainly

- `/docs` takes the inbox `docs@<domain>`, the same trade `/login` already made
  for `login@`. Worth it for a URL somebody can guess.
- `GET /api/plans` exposes an instance's plan structure to anyone. Intended — it
  is a price list — but a self-hoster with internal-only plans now publishes
  them. Easy to put behind a setting if that ever comes up.
- `shiki` is a new dependency, server-side only.

## Review fixes in this branch

Caught while reviewing: the docs page 500'd because `AccountLink` took a
**function** as a child from a server component, and functions can't cross the
RSC boundary. Also fixed: shiki's own `<pre>` background painted a box inside the
wrapper's, its `tabindex` showed the browser's default focus ring, the copy
button's `z-10` rode over the sticky header, GitHub-specific sign-in copy (the
provider list is configurable), and the domains section now caps at 12 with a
count — community domains are self-service and can grow well past what's worth
printing.

## Verified

`/docs` 200 with the base URL interpolated into every sample, live plans from the
database (Free 10,000/mo · Pro 50,000, retention rendered as "7 days"), served
domains listed, 118 highlighted tokens across 7 blocks, `robots: index, follow`.
`pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass (110 tests); production build
compiles.

Not eyeballed in a browser: the signed-out → signed-in label swap after
hydration, and the dashboard changes (that page is auth-gated, so server HTML is
just the loading state).

**Backend** (`/api/chat`, AI SDK 7): streams UIMessages; eight zod tools (read/createNodes/update/delete/move/rename/history/undoTo) executing server-side through Convex `ops.apply` with `source: "ai"` and ConvexError-recoverable results; ~6k-token depth-first mindmap serializer; thread auto-creation with `x-sprig-thread-id`; assistant messages persist with `operationId` links. Anthropic auth is the **Claude-subscription OAuth token** (`Authorization: Bearer` + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`) — zero API keys; missing token degrades to 503/"AI is not configured". `/new` generation and NodeAiEdit run on the same provider; **groq fully deleted** (actions + package + env).

Verified against installed types, not docs: `instructions`, `inputSchema`, `stopWhen: stepCountIs`, `toUIMessageStreamResponse` onFinish shape, `useChat` v4 surface (no input/handleSubmit/isLoading), `sendMessage` per-call body merge.
