author: danielnogueira8
body:
## The remaining under-deduction

After #1610 fixed Anthropic token accounting, per-turn stage costs are correct ($0.04-0.06 with 4-6 credits). But the monthly pill still showed 1 credit per post. Data from prod explained it: **323 messages vs $1.12 recorded cost** → cost projection = 112 credits, messages = 323 → the pill's `MAX(messages, costProjection)` formula charged per **message**, not per **dollar**. Any workspace whose message count outruns the cost projection watches the pill tick exactly 1 per post no matter what the turn cost — the "deducted 1 credit for a $0.05 post" bug.

## The change

`projectMonthlyUsage` is now purely cost-based: `used = spend / budget × limit` (clamped), `boundBy` always "cost". `getMonthlyUsage` no longer reads the message count. The monthly **message cap** (1000/month) still exists as a separate abuse guardrail enforced inside `claim_chat_turn` with its own banner — it just no longer drives what the pill *charges*.

Per-turn stage credits were already cost-based (verified: 4-6 credits for $0.04-0.06 turns at the $10 prod budget) and are unchanged. The budget stays env-driven (`CHAT_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD`) — no hardcoded value anywhere in the formula.

## Tests

Rewrote the pill suite for cost-only semantics, including the user's exact case: a $0.05 turn at a $10 budget costs 5 credits. Full suite green: 4,920 tests.

author: tiredithumans
body:
## Summary

Batch 3 of the review pass — the frontend UX cluster (findings 6, 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 20, 25, 27, 28). Follows #161 and #162.

**Surfaces that told the operator something untrue**
- The `AuditDashboard` scaffold — shared by Credential expiry, Delegated grants, and Application permissions — rendered "No matches" *on top of* a load error, contradicting the red error directly above it. It also used one message for "nothing here at all" and "your filter hid everything", implying a filter was hiding data that doesn't exist.
- The audit's All-apps pane rendered a select-all bar governing nothing plus a bare table header when a filter matched nothing.

**Destructive actions that couldn't name their target**
- `ConfirmDialog`'s `body` is `&'static str` and describes the *kind* of thing ("this client secret"), so an app with six secrets showed six identical dialogs. Added an optional `subject`; wired for secrets, certificates, and federated credentials (the federated one already had the name staged in `pending_remove` and was throwing it away at the dialog).
- The Bulk Actions page showed only a count, so an operator typed DELETE against a set they couldn't review — and mounted `BulkActionBar` without `names`, so failures listed raw GUIDs.

**Data the surface already had but withheld**
- Enterprise App and Managed Identity rows never showed enabled/disabled state, despite both lists offering that facet.
- The Managed Identities list skipped `ListScaffold` (no drawer, no filter badge) and printed no result count.
- The revealed Key Vault secret had no copy button and no way to hide it.
- App ids were inert text on the three tenant-wide triage tables despite `CopyableId` existing.

## Notes for review

- **Perf, not just markup:** two hot closures were rebuilding whole tables per keystroke (`audit_dashboard`, All-apps pane). Both now build the shell once and hide it when empty, so the keyed `<For>` can actually patch rows. Same for the `object_id -> name` map, which every finding group *and* the All-apps pane each rebuilt independently — it now lives on `AuditController`, built once per scan.
- `app_names` is a new tenant-scoped signal, so it goes in `TenantScopedUi` with its `reset()` line and an assertion in `tenant_switch_resets_every_tenant_scoped_field`, per the documented invariant — not as a bare `Session` field.
- Dropped two now-orphaned CSS rules (`.readiness__head`, `.readiness__title`).

## Test plan

- [x] `just verify` — all gates green, 670 tests

author: mscdit
body:
## The failure this closes

The model sometimes loads a write tool, resolves every parameter through lookups — and then **narrates the mutation instead of calling it**:

> User: *And now please assign it to John Doe.*
> Model: loads `assign-item` ✓, resolves John Doe via `list-persons` ✓, then — `finish=stop`: *"The item has been assigned to John Doe."*

No assign call. No confirmation. Nothing persisted. The user gets a confident "done" for something that never happened, and has no way to notice. Seen in production sessions, reproduced 3/10 in the most prone eval case.

**Prompt rules provably don't stop it.** Three separate instructions said "never claim an action you did not execute" — in the MCP server instructions, in the `load_tools` continue-instruction the model had read *in the same turn*, and in a trial preamble rule — and the phantom happened with all three in context.

## The guard

Structural detection from facts the orchestrator already owns — no text interpretation:

1. `load_tools` promoted a **non-read-only** action this turn (parsed from the result's `loaded` array, so failed loads don't arm it),
2. the model never attempted **any** resolvable write call this turn (an attempt counts even if it errors or raises a confirmation — the model is acting, not narrating),
3. the model is ending the turn in plain text.

All three → one transient system message, **once per turn**: nothing was executed — perform the action now (confirmation follows), correct the answer, or ask the user. All three ways out are legitimate; an honest clarifying question is simply repeated and costs one round. The latch makes a loop impossible — if the model insists, its answer passes through unchanged.

**Cost:** zero on read-only traffic (no write tool gets loaded there), one extra LLM round exactly when the suspicious posture occurs. Every firing emits a `retry` event, so production frequency lands in the existing friction analytics instead of requiring manual session reading.

## Measurements (gpt-oss-120b, Timly eval harness)

| | without guard | with guard |
|---|---|---|
| three prone cases ×10 | 24/30, **3 phantoms** | 29/30, **1 phantom** |
| full suite | 175/188, phantoms present | 176/182, **0 phantoms** |
| nudge firings | — | 3 targeted + ~9 full suite, each converted into action or honesty |

## Known gap, deliberately kept

The surviving phantom had its write tool **batch-loaded in an earlier turn**, so the current turn loaded nothing and condition 1 never armed. Widening the arm to "any promoted write tool in the session" would tax every innocent read turn after a write with an extra round; the only precise wider signal would be interpreting the answer text, which this guard exists to avoid. The narrow same-turn condition covers the dominant posture at zero cost to everything else — the cross-turn variant stays visible through the emitted retry events.

## Tests

Four new tests in `phantom_completion_guard_test.go`: phantom → nudge → corrected answer; the nudge is one-shot; quiet when the write actually executes; quiet on read-only turns. Full orchestrator package green, `go vet` clean.

body:
**Analysis / Root cause**:
The Playwright e2e tests use `page.locator('[data-test-id="..."]')` and similar CSS attribute selectors instead of the idiomatic `page.getByTestId()` API. Since `testIdAttribute` is configured to `data-test` in `playwright.config.ts`, these legacy attributes (`data-test-id`, `data-test-selector`) are not matched by `getByTestId()` without first adding a corresponding `data-test` attribute to the React source.

**Solution description**:
Three incremental commits replace legacy locator patterns with `getByTestId()`:

1. **`data-test-id` → `getByTestId()`** — Adds `data-test` alongside existing `data-test-id` on 4 React components (`Dashboard`, `alert-routing-modal` inputs, `command-line-tools`, node dashboard `DetailsCard`), then replaces 10 `page.locator('[data-test-id="..."]')` calls across 5 test/page files.

2. **`data-test-selector` → `getByTestId()`** — Adds `data-test` alongside existing `data-test-selector` on the `details-item.tsx` label element, then replaces 6 locator calls in `console-notification.spec.ts`.

3. **`locator('[data-test="..."]')` → `getByTestId()`** — Replaces 4 remaining `locator('[data-test="x"]')` calls with the equivalent `getByTestId('x')` in `console-notification.spec.ts`, `channel-modal.spec.ts`, and `cluster-settings-page.ts`.

Total: 13 files changed, 18 locator calls replaced.

**Screenshots / screen recording**:
N/A — no visual changes.

**Test setup:**
Console running locally or in CI.

**Test cases:**
- `npx playwright test e2e/tests/console/crd-extensions/console-notification.spec.ts` — passes (1 pre-existing failure in `crd-test-utils.ts` unrelated to these changes)

**Browser conformance**:

**Additional info:**
Part of ongoing effort to migrate Playwright tests to idiomatic APIs per the locator priority in `.claude/migration-context.md`: `getByTestId > getByRole > getByText > locator`.

author: nitrobass24
body:
## Summary

The decision, delivered: the search page runs on the same merged window and per-member ledger
the feeds serve — sort and counts can never disagree with what your \*arrs see.

- **`GET /api/search`** (session/API-key, beside the per-slug search): explicit
  `indexers=a,b,c` subset resolved via a new `Resolver.Members` (unknown slug in an explicit
  list = 400, the client's bug; configured-but-disabled = `disabled` ledger row; unbuildable =
  `unavailable` — exactly the feeds' semantics). Fan-out is `core.SearchAggregate` **verbatim**:
  zero new merge logic anywhere.
- **Links seal per ORIGIN member** — grouped by origin, sealed through the existing
  `resolveSearchLinks`, reassembled in window order — so a passkey-bearing link can never seal
  against the wrong indexer. `MemberOutcome.Err` never crosses the wire (logged redacted).
- **UI**: one fetch replaces the client fan-out + merge. The count is the server's `total`;
  the failed-slugs banner becomes a per-member ledger (ok members fold into "N indexers · M
  results"; skips render quietly with their closed reason — "PTP — circuit open"). Column
  sorting stays client-side over the returned window, which now IS the whole served window;
  the result filter is untouched above it. Prev/Next removed — the per-indexer-offset pair was
  the original sort-skew defect. The the tracked spec adult filtering carries over to the new endpoint
  (`dropAdultAggregateReleases`) — the UI switching surfaces must not regress a landed feature.

## The one trade to weigh (deliberate, stated, reversible)

**The merged window is capped at 100 rows** — `core.parsePaging` clamps to the shared
`LimitsMax`, and raising core (which would also change the feeds) was correctly out of this
PR's bounds. The old client fan-out could hold 100×N rows; the new page shows the newest 100 of
the merge with the truncation stated ("newest 100 of 412 fetched"), and the result filter now
filters within that window. If 100 feels tight in practice, the fast-follow is a
management-endpoint-only window parameter on the core paging (small, isolated) — flagged for
the operator's call rather than smuggled in here.

## Also

- Default table order = server order (publish-date desc) via the existing sort machinery — no
  ripple into the table/cards components.
- Docs: the two pending rows fold into one ✅; the merged-sort row flips to ✅ worded
  without "paging" (paging was consciously removed, so claiming it would be false).
- Per-slug `GET /api/indexers/{slug}/search` remains documented and tested — only the UI
  stopped using it.

## Testing

- [x] Backend: subset resolution (live + disabled → ledger, 200), unknown slug 400, empty list
      400, per-origin sealing (resolver-needing member sealed to ITS route, magnet passthrough),
      closed-reason ledger, honest total, adult filtering on the new surface
- [x] Web: exactly one fetch (absence of per-slug fetches asserted), ledger fold + skip
      reasons, total renders, no Prev/Next, filter + column sort over the window, pending state
- [x] All seven gates rc-checked individually, then re-run independently at the executor's
      commit: go tests (api/core/registry), `test-openapi`, `web-ci`, strict docs build,
      `precommit`, `build`

  * Adult-content hiding is applied consistently in aggregate search, keeping the ledger counts aligned.

author: notatallshaw
body:
A metadata sidecar that answers 204, or a 300 the transport did not follow, was read as the wheel's METADATA on the default urllib3 backend and cached against that URL, so every later resolve read the same empty or unrelated body back. The same held for a simple listing and for an sdist fetch.

The two backends did not agree on what raise_for_status covers: urllib3 cleared everything under 400, httpx raised on anything that was not 2xx. Neither is the right gate for reading a body.

Body-reading calls now go through raise_unless_ok, which accepts 200 and 203 and raises HttpError on anything else. Both transports share one raise_for_status that raises on 4xx/5xx only. A rejected response is not parsed and not cached, and a stale cached listing survives a bad revalidation.

body:
"Final sale price" took 140000000 with nothing under it while the
asking price above it read "Equivalent to: ₹16 Crore". Prices are typed
as raw digits and a missing or extra zero is invisible at that length,
so a field without the readout is a field where a typo ships.

The readout existed four times over — twice as getEquivalentPriceLabel
(property-form, deal-form), twice as formatPriceLabel (contact-form,
contact-detail-view) — and each copy had reached only some of its own

price; monthly rental income; per-floor rent in the tenancy rows; both

author: lmeyerov
body:
## What

Five defect classes that reviewers keep rejecting by hand are now checked statically, in the **existing** lint lane. No new workflow, no new job, no production code changed.

- `bin/ci_type_hygiene_guard.py` — stdlib-only AST pass over `graphistry/` (tests excluded, matching `mypy.ini`), invoked from `bin/lint.sh`, so it runs in `python-lint-types` on py3.8–3.14. ~1.4 s, **byte-identical counts on all seven interpreters** (verified).
- `bin/ci_type_hygiene_baseline.json` — the per-file ratchet.
- `pyproject.toml` — ruff `B009`/`B010` promoted to errors, today's offenders seeded into `per-file-ignores`.
- `DEVELOP.md` — conventions + escape hatch. `CHANGELOG.md` — entry.

## Measured first

Counts on `master` `b6181d35`, `graphistry/` excluding `graphistry/tests` (same exclusion `mypy.ini` already uses; including tests would add ~5,000 missing-annotation findings from throwaway fixtures):

| Class | Check | Findings | Files | Enforcement |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 missing contracts | `missing-annotations` | 1704 | 79 | ratchet |
| 3a `Any` | `explicit-any` | 1605 | 117 | ratchet |
| 3b `cast()` | `explicit-cast` | 959 | 81 | ratchet |
| 4 bare generics | `bare-generic` | 209 | 48 | ratchet |
| 2 dynamic attr write | `plottable-setattr` | **3** | 3 | effectively a hard rule |
| 2 direct attr write | `plottable-attr-write` | 39 | 5 | effectively a hard rule |
| 5 `str` vs `Literal` | `vocab-str-param` | 42 | 21 | narrow ratchet |
| 2 constant-name attr | ruff `B009`/`B010` | 31 | 14 | **error today**, seeded `per-file-ignores` |

## Ratchet

Per-file count baseline: a file may not gain findings, and a file **absent from the baseline must have zero**. So new files are fully enforced, and new untyped functions inside existing files are caught too — which per-file-ignores alone would not do.

`changed-files-only` was considered and rejected: `python-lint-types` checks out at `fetch-depth: 1`, so no merge-base is available in that job, and I cannot author workflows to change it.

Escape hatch is `# hygiene-ok: <check> -- <reason>` on the line, **not** raising a cap via `--update-baseline`.

## Class 2 targets the hazard, not the syntax

A blanket `getattr`/`setattr` ban was measured and rejected: **300** non-test `getattr` sites, overwhelmingly legitimate optional-attribute reads. The #1825 leak (`setattr` cache onto the caller's `Plottable` keyed by `id()`, returning a stale answer after in-place mutation) requires a **write**, so only writes onto a parameter annotated as a `Plottable` are flagged:

- `plottable-setattr` — 3 sites. One is `gfql_fast_paths.py:514`, i.e. **#1825 itself**; one is `gfql_unified.py:1571`; one is `cluster.py:190` (legitimate, dynamic name on a fresh copy).
- `plottable-attr-write` — 39 sites, the `param.attr = ...` form the same hazard takes when nobody writes `setattr`. Without this the `setattr` rule is one keystroke from being bypassed.

Ruff `B009`/`B010` additionally reject the constant-name forms outright; 31 offenders across 14 files are seeded and retire with `ruff check --fix --select B009,B010 <file>`.

## Class 5 is deliberately narrow

There is no honest general rule for "this `str` should be a `Literal`". I prototyped the obvious one — a `str` parameter compared against a small closed set of literals in its own body — and measured it: **44 hits at roughly 80% precision**. The false positives are exactly the owner's carve-out (`_alias_key(column: str)`, `__getattr__(name: str)`, `_is_bool_literal(text: str)`, `_coerce_value(attr_type: str)` reading arbitrary GEXF). **Not shipped.**

What ships instead is a hard-coded registry of **six** parameter names whose vocabularies this repo has already committed to as `Literal` aliases (`table`, `kind`, `direction`, `how`, `mode`, `engine`) — 42 sites, ratcheted. It is a floor, not a full check; reviewers still own the general case.

## What this will NOT catch

- Wrong annotations. Every check is presence/shape only — `def f(x: str) -> str` where `x` is really a DataFrame is invisible.
- Annotation churn inside a baselined file: delete one untyped function, add another, count unchanged.
- `Any` reached through a type alias or an unparameterized import; only the literal `Any` token in an annotation is seen.
- Plottable writes through a local alias (`h = g; h._x = 1`) or a non-`Plottable`-annotated / unannotated parameter. The rule keys on the annotation, which is why it is precise; that precision is also its blind spot.
- Class 5 at large — see above.
- The baseline can rot: shrinkage only warns by default. `--strict` lists files that improved so caps can be retightened deliberately.

## Not done, on purpose

No `mypy.ini` strictness flags. `disallow_untyped_defs` / `disallow_any_explicit` / `disallow_any_generics` are per-module all-or-nothing, and with 79–117 dirty modules the exemption list would be ~the whole package, with no way to express "no worse than today". The AST guard gives per-file granularity in the same lane at ~1.4 s.

## Verification

- `./bin/lint.sh` green end to end (ruff + guard + relative-import check), exit 0.
- Guard verified to fire on a synthetic file for all 7 checks, and `# hygiene-ok` verified to suppress.

author: smoe
body:
## Summary

- reject empty or oversized RF fragments before calculating their CRC8
- reject multi-data responses whose final fragment does not contain the required two-byte CRC16

## Root cause

The radio receive paths can report a dynamic payload length of zero for a malformed packet. `HoymilesRadio::checkFragmentCrc()` previously subtracted one from that unchecked unsigned length. The value passed to `crc8()` therefore became 255, and the subsequent checksum-byte lookup used an index of `-1`.

There was a similar assumption in `MultiDataCommand::handleResponse()`: it subtracted two from the final fragment length without first verifying that the fragment contained its two CRC16 bytes.

## Impact

Malformed packets are now rejected through the existing error paths. Processing of valid packets is unchanged. The shared CRC8 guard protects both NRF and CMT radio implementations.

# ✨ Feature Pull Request

## What does this feature add?

Scaffolds the **Scenario Controller** — a data-driven linear sequencer that runs narrated VR training scenarios from designer-authored ScriptableObject assets.

A scenario is an ordered list of step assets. The controller walks it one step at a time: build the step → `Enter(context, onComplete)` → wait → `Exit()` → advance, and fires a single `onScenarioComplete` at the end. Four step types are included: **narration** (plays a VO clip), **PC question** (shows a question, validates, retries), **wait-for-task** (blocks until the player grabs/does something), and **scene event** (triggers an animation or prop change).

The goal is that designers assemble and reorder scenarios entirely in the Inspector with no code changes, and engineers add new capabilities by writing one small step class — never by editing the controller.

Built to the architecture in `Docs/ScenarioController.pdf` (§10 file manifest). A full write-up of the implementation, including known gaps and recommended next steps, is in `Docs/ScenarioController-Implementation-Report.md`.

author: ihsandanish25
body:
## Problem
The live worker was placing near-instant buy→sell round-trips on higher-priced stocks (e.g. **AAPL $339, TXN $275 on 2026-07-28**; GOOGL/PANW/NET earlier), scratching a small loss + fees each time and capturing none of the move.

**Root cause:** when the per-trade budget couldn't cover one whole share, `broker.buy()` fell back to a **fractional (notional)** order. Alpaca rejects a **GTC** protective stop on a fractional position (`42210000 "fractional orders must be DAY orders"`), so `attach_stop_target()` returned `(False, False)` and the `market_open` runner immediately **flattened** the unprotected position.

Observed live (2026-07-28 09:43 ET):
```
BUY AAPL 0.077846 (fractional) submitted
↳ Order attach FAILED [AAPL]: {"code":42210000,"message":"fractional orders must be DAY orders"}
✗ AAPL stop NOT attached — flattening
SELL AAPL x0.077846
```
The one same-day trade that survived (CNC, a whole share) kept its stop and finished the day green — confirming the pattern.

## Fix
**Whole-share policy:** if we can't afford ≥1 whole share within the caps, `buy()` now returns `{"blocked": True, "reason": "insufficient_cash"}` instead of submitting a fractional order. `attach_stop_target()` is therefore only ever called with whole-share qty, so the GTC stop always attaches.

- Removes the fractional-notional fallback (−59 / +25 lines).
- **No runner changes needed** — runners already handle a `blocked` result (`order_skipped` + `continue`).
- `core/spy_base.py` (its own deliberate notional SPY-parking order, no stop) is untouched.

## Trade-off
With small equity + a ~10% cap, the bot will now **skip** stocks priced above the affordable whole-share budget rather than churn them — fewer trades, but every position opened is genuinely stop-protected. Becomes a non-issue as equity grows, or if a future change re-places DAY stops each morning to unlock pricier names.

## Tests
- `core/tests/test_broker_buy_cash_cap.py` — **5/5 pass**, including a new regression test reproducing the AAPL/TXN case (share $339, ~$26 budget) asserting it blocks with **no order submitted**.
- Pre-existing unrelated failures (spy_base fractional-rounding, a mocked VCP test, network-bound screener imports) were confirmed to fail identically on `main`.

author: lbhall
body:
## Problem
The "tap the marked winner to clear it" feature (EMC) didn't work in the browser. The winner radios are `display: none` and driven by tapping the label/`<span>`; the browser forwards only a synthetic **`click`** to the hidden input — **`mousedown` never fires on a `display:none` element**. The clear logic captured the prior checked state on `mousedown`, so `_wasChecked` was never set and the deselect branch never ran.

(The backend clear path was correct and unit-tested; only the frontend gesture was broken, which the Django tests couldn't catch.)

## Fix
Track the prior checked state in JS without `mousedown`: seed each radio's `_wasChecked` from the server-rendered `checked` state on load, and refresh the whole group after each click. Tapping a radio that was already checked unchecks it.

## Verification
Ran the exact markup + fixed JS in a browser harness over HTTP and clicked through it:
- Tap the already-selected winner → **clears** ✓
- Tap an unselected player → selects ✓
- Tap the other side → switches ✓
- Tap selected after a switch → clears ✓

author: huitseeker
body:
This completes [Phase 1](https://github.com/0xMiden/node/issues/2319) by storing the exact sealed transaction inputs accepted by the validator. The validator writes the record only after proof checks, reexecution, and header checks pass. Rejected submissions do not change the database, and a duplicate transaction keeps its first ciphertext.

This record is temporary. [Phase 2](https://github.com/0xMiden/node/issues/2374) will replace it with data encrypted under the validators' threshold key. Anyone with the shared submission secret can decrypt the Phase 1 record, so the validator and any remote prover must run within the trusted TEE boundary.

Existing validator databases must be set up again because old rows do not contain the client ciphertext.

Closes #2385.
## Changelog
```toml
[[entry]]
scope = "validator"
impact = "changed"
description = "The validator stores sealed transaction inputs only after all validation checks pass."

[[entry]]
scope = "validator"
impact = "migration"
description = "Existing validator databases must be set up again for the new validated transaction record."
```

author: schickling-assistant
body:
## Why

`docs/vrs/spec.md`'s "Host-local scheduling and supervision" section is one
heading carrying R01–R04, R06, R07 and R11 across roughly 4,500 lines of code
(`run.rs`, `materialize.rs`, `hooks.rs`, `validate.rs`, plus reconcile, watch,
isolate, flapping and the exec backend). It is the largest single thing in the
VRS tree, and the place where a flat structure stops being able to say anything
precise.

## What

Adds `docs/vrs/03-supervision/` — a parent node and three children, each a full
subsystem node with **both** `requirements.md` and `spec.md`:

| Node | Scope | Refines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `03-supervision` | host-pinned scope, one supervisor per catalog and host, shortest-path convergence, deny-by-default event contracts | R03, R04, R13, R14, R15 |
| `01-reconcile` | desired-vs-actual, the plan's buckets and transition table, materialization as the first phase of every pass | — |
| `02-launch` | the two task mechanisms, isolation, restart policy, abandonment, bounded diagnostics | R06 |
| `03-adoption` | the replaceable control plane | R11 |

Docs only. No code changes.

> **Constitutional surface, flagged deliberately.** This adds **four new
> `requirements.md` files**. `docs/vrs/spec.md` states that changing
> `vision.md` or `requirements.md` requires the owner's explicit approval. No
> protected file is edited here — the decomposition works by refinement, with
> each node citing the root ID it refines and stating its own obligations under
> it — but four new requirements documents is a change to the constitutional
> surface, and the owner should see that in a PR description rather than find it
> in a diff. The shape was confirmed with the human beforehand.

## How

Derived from the code and its tests, not from the root documents' prose. Every
requirement traces to observed behaviour or a named test; requirements holding
only by construction say so explicitly; and anything I believed should be true
but could not establish is recorded as an open question rather than written into
a contract.

All 46 test names cited across the eight files were verified to resolve against
`src/` and `tests/`.

**One structural finding worth calling out.** Materialization is specified
*inside* `01-reconcile` rather than as its own node, because the code says it
belongs there: `reconcile_pass` runs hook verification, then materialization,
then observation, then planning — every pass, not only at authoring time. A
standalone materialize-only mode exists, but it exposes that phase rather than
making it a separate lifecycle. This was the seam the tree could most plausibly
have been split on, and the code rules it out.

## Open questions recorded

Eleven, spread across the four nodes. The ones that would change behaviour if
resolved:

- **RECON-DQ1** — that materialization precedes launch every pass, that a gating
  render failure drops exactly one agent, and that an unsatisfied precondition
  defers only dependent agents are all established by reading the pass, not by a
  test. The materialization tests prove rendering in isolation; no test varies a
  render outcome and asserts the launch consequence.
- **LAUNCH-DQ1** — a failed start not consuming a restart attempt is a
  deliberate and consequential rule (it stops a task with a temporarily broken
  environment from exhausting its policy without ever running) and no test
  varies start success against the attempt budget.
- **ADOPT-DQ1** — a replacement supervisor forgetting which tasks its
  predecessor abandoned is load-bearing design, and its only statement anywhere
  is the operator-facing message advising a restart. No test asserts it, so an
  unrelated refactor could change it silently.
- **ADOPT-DQ2** — adoption matches by identity and treats anything alive under
  that identity as current. If a declaration's command changed while the
  supervisor was down, the surviving task is running the old command and is
  adopted as though current. Nothing records the launched definition to compare
  against.
- **SUP-DQ1** — the supervisor's watcher admits less than discovery accepts.
  Discovery takes three file formats and two naming forms; the watcher wakes
  only on the canonical KDL filename. Other forms are reconciled normally but
  never wake a pass early — timer only. Possibly deliberate (canonical form
  earns the fast path), but nothing says so and no test covers it.
- **RECON-DQ2** — a task pinned against collection that dies is frozen: neither
  collected nor restarted, and reported as present. Nothing surfaces it the way
  an abandoned task is surfaced.

## Scope held

Hooks and validation are deliberately **not** under supervision. Hooks are a
precondition supervision consumes and validation is a gate; both are specified
elsewhere. Where a supervision obligation depends on one — reconcile's
precondition phase does — the node states the dependency and its failure
behaviour without specifying the dependency itself.

## Gates

- `axe vrs check --profile strict docs/vrs` — green, zero diagnostics.
- All 46 cited test names resolve.
- No protected file touched; `git status` shows only the new directory.

author: cargopete
body:
Cursor-side half of mount, mirroring how slice 2 was split. **No behaviour change** — nothing sends `Mount` yet.

## The design point worth reading

`CursorCommand::Mount` carries a nest that is **already prepared and caught up**. The catch-up happens before the command is sent (RFC-0027 §4, phase 1), off to one side of the cursor.

That ordering is the whole reason phase 1 exists. The cursor advances from the **min** of its live nests' positions, so splicing in a nest a million blocks behind would drag every co-tenant back through history with it. It would be *correct* — RFC-0026 §4's re-admission maths means nothing double-processes or is skipped — but unusable. So the driver does the backfill first and hands over a nest whose cursor is already near the shared one.

`Supervisor::admit` therefore marks the nest `prepared`. Getting that wrong would be quietly disastrous: an unprepared nest has `nexts[i] = 0`, which the loop reads as *unknown* rather than *genesis*, and the min would take the whole cursor back to block 0.

## Index alignment

`names`/`states`/`attempts`/`prepared` and the loop's `nests`/`nexts` are parallel arrays, and `live_nest`'s `expect` rests on them staying aligned. So `drain_lifecycle` now takes both `Vec`s and grows them together in one place — a mount that extended one and not the others would turn a lifecycle operation into a panic, or worse, into a nest indexing under another nest's identity.

There is a test asserting all five lengths after an admit, which is dull but exactly the kind of thing that silently rots.

## Also

- **Mounting over a name already on the cursor is refused.** That case is an *upgrade* (RFC-0020); letting the two overlap silently would leave two nests writing one store.
- `CursorCommand`'s `Debug` is hand-written — a mount carries a whole `NestIngest` (stores, decode registry, view handles), and printing that would be enormous and useless. It prints the name and target block, which is what anyone debugging a lifecycle command actually wants.
- `NestIngest` becomes `pub` so the driver can hand one over.

Full suite green (291), fmt and clippy clean.

## Next (slice 3b)

The driver side: admission checks (§3's three refusals — budget `507`, undeclared chain `409`, name taken `409`), bundle verification through the same path as `nest load`, then build → `prepare` → send `Mount` → re-compose the router with the new nest's routes. That is where `RoostHandles` needs the mount context it does not yet carry (source per chain, admin settings, the per-cursor RSS ceiling).

author: longvu-db
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR implements the server-side SQL configuration approach suggested in https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/57043#issuecomment-5097384606.

It adds the internal `spark.sql.execution.skipV2TableRefresh` configuration, defaulting to `false`, and sets it to `true` whenever the Spark Connect server creates or clones a session. `QueryExecution` uses this setting when deriving its effective `refreshPhaseEnabled` value, so the optimization covers every Connect path that creates a query execution, including SQL, DataFrame operations, checkpoint, local checkpoint, and future call sites.

Spark Connect's plan cache is handled conservatively. A cache hit can contain an already-resolved `DataSourceV2Relation`, for which analysis alone cannot reload current table metadata. Such cached plans are cloned and tagged so their `QueryExecution` retains the refresh phase. Freshly analyzed Connect plans still skip it.

The existing `QueryExecution` constructor signature and `refreshPhaseEnabled` accessor remain binary-compatible.

### Why are the changes needed?

Spark Connect normally analyzes a plan immediately before execution. The DSv2 table refresh phase then performs another catalog `loadTable` request without changing the outcome, adding an avoidable catalog round trip and latency.

Using `spark.api.mode` on the server is not reliable because it is a client-side builder/launcher directive and is not propagated to Spark Connect server sessions. A server-side session setting explicitly records the execution environment and avoids having to update every Connect call site.

The plan-cache exception preserves correctness for resolved DSv2 relations that may outlive the table metadata captured during their original analysis.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The new configuration is internal. Spark Classic keeps the refresh phase enabled, while Spark Connect avoids redundant catalog refresh requests for freshly analyzed plans.

### How was this patch tested?

Added a counting DSv2 catalog and tests that assert the exact number of `loadTable` calls, not only query results. Coverage includes:

- Classic defaults and explicit refresh skipping.
- Connect-created sessions and cloned sessions.
- DataFrame `table`, `drop`, SQL, checkpoint, and local checkpoint paths.
- Repeated execution through the Connect plan cache, where cached resolved DSv2 plans retain the refresh.
- Existing Connect DSv2 freshness scenarios.

The following suites passed (119 tests total):

- `QueryExecutionSuite`: 29 tests.
- `SparkConnectSessionManagerSuite`: 11 tests.
- `SparkConnectCloneSessionSuite`: 9 tests.
- `SparkConnectServerTestSuite`: 21 tests.
- `DataSourceV2DataFrameConnectSuite`: 49 tests.

Compilation passed for `catalyst/Test/compile`, `sql/Test/compile`, and `connect/Test/compile`. Scalastyle passed for the catalyst, SQL, and Connect modules.

author: axpnet
body:
The negotiated compressor is the first name in **our own** advertised list that the peer also offers, computed the same way on both sides (`compat.c::parse_negotiate_str`). That makes the advertisement a promise rather than a wish list: every name in it is one the negotiation may hand back to us.

We were advertising stock rsync's list verbatim, `zstd lz4 zlibx zlib`, while this module drives exactly two of those four.

## The defect

It is worse than a harmless superset, because stock ranks `lz4` above `zlibx`. A peer built with lz4 but without zstd made the negotiation settle on a codec that has no implementation here at all, so the transfer fell back to the classic wrapper while a working, byte-pinned `zlibx` sat one position lower. We were losing to our own advertisement.

Same shape as the bug #491 just closed: a declaration that promised more than the code delivers.

## The fix

`zstd zlibx none`. The trailing `none` is the load-bearing part: it guarantees the two lists always intersect, so a peer offering only codecs we decline lands on uncompressed literals, which is a working delta transfer, instead of an empty intersection. On Windows that difference is the whole native path, since there is no classic fallback there.

## Why plain `zlib` stays out, structurally rather than for effort

`zlib` feeds matched block data through the compressor history on both ends (`token.c::see_deflate_token`), so decoding it needs `inflateIncomp`, a function rsync patches into the zlib it bundles. It is in neither the system zlib (checked with `nm` on the `.so`) nor any Rust crate. Upstream split `zlibx` out for exactly this reason, and the rsync man page says so directly:

> the "zlibx" compression algorithm is just the "zlib" algorithm with matched data excluded from the compression stream (to try to make it more compatible with an external zlib implementation)

Supporting it would mean owning an inflate implementation. The correct move is never to negotiate it, which is now a property rather than a hope.

## Tests

Four new, and **verified as pins by restoring the old list and watching them fail**, not by watching them pass:

| Test | What it catches |
|---|---|
| `lz4_capable_peer_without_zstd_still_lands_on_zlibx` | the defect itself |
| `zlib_only_peer_lands_on_uncompressed_literals_not_a_typed_error` | the working-delta guarantee the trailing `none` buys |
| `default_advertisement_never_yields_a_codec_we_cannot_drive` | the rule, not an example: a sweep over all 32 subsets of stock's own compress list, so a name added without a codec fails here instead of against a stranger's NAS |
| `forcing_zlib_through_the_env_shaped_profile_still_takes_the_typed_error` | keeps the `Unsupported` arm covered, since making the default safe would otherwise silently delete the coverage the classic fallback depends on |

Three byte-pinned driver tests re-declared the advertisement by hand, which is the duplication that let the string and its pins drift apart. They now derive it from `PreambleProfile::default()` and check that the driver **emits what it advertises**, leaving `preamble_profile_default_is_byte_pinned` as the single place pinning the literal strings. Confirmed the split works: with the defect restored, the pin test fails and the three derived ones pass, which is each doing its own job.

## Also

A stale number that predates this change: the `real_wire` module doc called the client preamble "55 bytes", which was an observed peer shape and never ours. With the shipping profile we emit 46, and the derivation is written out so the next reader can check it rather than trust it.

Docs realigned in all three places, including the `lz4` row that did not exist anywhere.

## Gate

605 to 609 aerorsync tests, 0 failed. `cargo fmt` clean, `clippy --lib --features aerorsync --all-targets -D warnings` clean, `RUSTFLAGS='--cfg ci_lane3' check` clean.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Compatibility**
  * Improved compression negotiation by advertising only `zstd`, `zlibx`, and `none`, and selecting the first codec both sides offer.
  * Added/strengthened fallback to uncompressed literals when peers only support unsupported codecs (e.g., `zlib`).
  * Updated default negotiation behavior to avoid advertising codecs that can’t be safely handled.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified compressor negotiation and the “winner” selection logic across the README and protocol comparison docs.
* **Tests**
  * Expanded coverage to verify negotiation outcomes across different peer codec sets.

## Surfacing-prep view-model (no-build lane)

Second of three board view-models over the orphaned E5/E6/E7 pure cores. Follows [#1552](https://github.com/bradleybond512/crystal-ball/pull/1552) (retrospective board view).

`buildDecisionBoardView(decision, { maxRows })` bounds, tones, and formats `decision-consequence.ts` output into a fixed-size "if I act now" board card:
- **Card tone** is `act` when the sim recommends a move, else `muted` (hold), `neutral` (nothing to evaluate).
- **Row tone**: recommended → `act`; other materially-helping move → `prepare`; no-effect → `muted`.
- **Metric** is the signed peak change (`−12 pts` lowers the peak, `+7 pts` raises it, `0 pts`), matching the sim's own rationale convention.
- **Labels**: `now`/`45 min`/`2 h` lead time, capitalized cost tier, and `Still worst: <axis>` residual peak.
- Rows preserve the sim's best-first order, capped at `maxRows` (default 4) with `+N more` overflow.

Pure: no DOM, no fetch, no globals, no clock. Renderer mount stays deferred (needs a build), consistent with E4–E7.

author: echoofdawn
body:
## What Changed

`publish-spec-review.mjs` spawned the relay as a bare **relative** path (`.instar/scripts/telegram-reply.sh`) and then printed `[published] … delivered to topic N` **without inspecting the spawn result**.

instar-dev work is *required* to happen in a worktree, and a worktree has no `.instar/scripts/`. So every send from one failed with ENOENT and was reported as delivered. Reproduced live at 18:09Z today — these two lines printed one after the other:

```
bash: .instar/scripts/telegram-reply.sh: No such file or directory
[published] link verified (HTTP 200) and delivered to topic 29723.
```

The operator received nothing.

**Why this one matters more than its size.** The script sits on a hook-**enforced** path: `grounding-before-messaging` *blocks* a hand-written message of this kind and directs the agent here. So the single tool whose job is delivering approval asks could silently drop them — leaving work "awaiting operator approval" that the operator was never asked for. A vanished ask is indistinguishable, from the operator's side, from the agent simply not having asked yet.

The script already refused a broken link, a missing overview, and a stub overview. Then it did not check whether the message sent.

**Filed three times in fifteen days before this fix:** ACT-616 (2026-07-13), ACT-1390 (2026-07-27), ACT-1517 (2026-07-28) — three independent investigations, each recording it as a TODO. Dates verified against the ledger.

## The fix

- `resolveRelayScript()` walks **up** from cwd until it finds the relay, so a worktree reaches the agent home. Honors `INSTAR_AGENT_HOME` first, falls back to the documented `.claude/scripts/` path for older installs, and returns `null` rather than a guessed path.
- `relayDelivered()` requires the relay's own `Sent <n> chars to topic <id>` confirmation — not merely exit 0. A silent no-op is not a delivery.
- On any failure: `[NOT DELIVERED]` with the reason, the composed message printed so the ask is not lost, exit 1. **Fails closed instead of failing silent.**

The second part is the durable half. The first removes today's cause; the second means the next cause announces itself.

## ELI16 — the tool that hands you things to approve was dropping them

When your agent needs your approval on a design, there is one sanctioned way to send it to you: it renders the plain-English summary as a web page, checks the link actually loads, and messages it to you. A safety hook *blocks* the agent from asking any other way — so this one tool is the only door.

That tool sent the message by running a small script, and it looked for that script in whatever folder it happened to be running from. But agents are required to do their work in a separate checkout folder, which does not contain the script. So the send failed with "file not found." Then the tool printed: **"published — verified and delivered."** Both lines, one after the other, in the same output.

Everything else in that tool is careful. It refuses to send a broken link. It refuses if the summary is missing or too short. And then it didn't check whether the message was sent.

An approval request that vanishes doesn't look like an error to anyone. To you, nothing arrives — and nothing arriving is indistinguishable from the agent simply not having asked yet. To the agent, it's done. So a design can sit "waiting for the operator" indefinitely while the operator was never actually asked. This exact problem was written down three separate times over fifteen days before anyone fixed it.

Now it searches upward until it finds the script, and it only says "delivered" if the messaging script actually confirms it sent something. If it can't confirm, it says **not delivered**, prints the message so the request isn't lost, and exits with an error.

## Verification

- 11 unit tests over both exported functions: the exact production failure (ENOENT → not delivered), the worktree walk-up that shipped broken, the `.claude` fallback, precedence when both exist, exit-0-with-no-confirmation, and null-result.
- Proven against the real filesystem **from the actual worktree**: `resolveRelayScript` returns the agent home's relay and `fs.existsSync` on it is true.
- Fix direction confirmed before writing code: the unmodified script from the agent home printed `Sent 408 chars to topic 29723` and genuinely delivered; the same command from the worktree printed ENOENT then "delivered".

## Tier

Declared **Tier 1** against a size-driven signal of 2 (`size=2, riskFloor=1`, 71 LOC / 1 file). Risk floor is 1; **zero `src/` runtime files** — agent tooling under `skills/`, no route, config, persisted state, or migration. Most of the LOC is the doc comments recording why; trimming them to slip under the 40-LOC bar would be gaming the gate, so it is declared openly and recorded as `belowFloor`.

Release fragment is marked internal-only, which the push gate objectively verifies against the diff (it rejects that marker when any runtime `src/` file changed — zero here).

author: steve-flanagan
body:
Closes the half of the self-destruct promise that was never true.

## The gap

The site tells every visitor their demo account self-destructs. That covered the **directory object** only — `Remove-ExpiredDemoAccounts.ps1` deletes the user in The Identity Playground Workforce and has no idea Table Storage exists, so the SCIM row it was provisioned into lived forever.

**Not theoretical.** The first orphan appeared within an hour of the endpoint going live: a terminated hire whose directory object was gone while its SCIM row still read `active: true`.

## A second sweep, not one that does both

[ADR 009](docs/decisions/009-workforce-guest-cleanup.md) rejected a single workflow spanning both tenants for reasons that apply here unchanged: different cadence, different blast radius, and one job holding delete rights over two systems at once is a wider surface for the same work.

**This one holds no Graph permission at all.** It can delete rows in one table and nothing else. That is the whole of its authority.

## Two choices worth naming

**The TTL is deliberately longer than the directory's** — 36 hours against the sweep's 24-plus-hourly. A downstream copy outliving its upstream object is what actually happens in production. The reverse would show a visitor a lie about their own hire.

**Abort, don't truncate, above the ceiling.** A run finding more expired rows than expected has misunderstood something — a flood of hires, a clock problem, a TTL edit — and deleting the first N of a set nobody understands is how a bug becomes data loss. Loud beats tidy.

## Tests

`selectExpired` is extracted as a pure function because it decides what gets destroyed, and that decision should be verifiable without an Azure account. Seven tests, weighted at the dangerous direction rather than the happy path:

- an unparseable `created` stamp is **never** selected — it must not read as "very old"
- the TTL boundary is exclusive, so a row exactly at the edge survives
- mixed sets pick only the expired ones

**24 pass, up from 17.**

This PR is stacked on #842 only because that is where they were discovered (installing `--all-extras` to test the bump made them visible). It can merge in either order.

- **`sample_to_hf`** was annotated `dict[str, str]` but returns exactly the twelve `str` keys of the `SWEbenchInstance` TypedDict, which is what `make_test_spec` expects. Annotated as such.
- **`state.sample_id`** (`int | str`) and **`state.input`** (`str | list[ChatMessage]`) are now coerced with `str()` when building an instance — matching what `sample_to_hf` already does for the same two fields.
- **`get_test_directives`** is typed as taking a full `SWEbenchInstance` but only reads `"repo"` and `"test_patch"`, which are the only fields available at that call site. Cast with a comment, rather than fabricating the other ten fields.
- The **`swebench < 3.0.0` single-argument parser call** is a deliberate runtime version probe. All 64 parsers in the pinned swebench (`>=3.0.0`; 4.1.0 installed) take `(log, test_spec)`, so that call always raises `TypeError` and falls through to the two-argument path. Kept for anyone on an older swebench, but the ignore is narrowed to `call-arg` and the comment now says why it is expected to fail.

No behaviour change — types and comments only.

author: evereq
body:
The chat panel was the **one** prompt surface with no way to attach a file. `/new`, `/works/new`, `/missions`, `/ideas` and `/agents` all have the PromptComposer's `+` button, and `agent.ts` has documented an "Attached files" block the whole time — it just described a control the chat UI did not have. Files attached *elsewhere* reached chat; files a user wanted to attach *in* chat had nowhere to go.

## What's here

Paperclip button, **drag-drop** onto the composer, and **paste** — pasting a screenshot is the fastest way to attach one, and without a handler the clipboard image was discarded and only its (usually empty) text survived.

Uploads reuse the existing owner-scoped `/api/uploads/file` spine rather than a new path, and start **on selection, not on send**:

- the user watches progress while still typing;
- by send time every attachment is either a resolved URL or visibly failed;
- **send is blocked while an upload is in flight** — firing early would drop the file silently, which is the exact failure this surface exists to prevent;
- a **failed upload stays visible with its error** instead of vanishing. Dropping it quietly would let someone send a message believing a file went too.

Text is no longer required: an attachment with no words is a real message ("here, look at this"), so send unlocks on either.

## One formatter, not two

`formatAttachmentsBlock` moves out of `use-start-from-prompt.tsx` (where it was module-private) into `lib/ai/attachments.ts`. Two producers emitting two near-identical blocks is how a system prompt ends up describing a shape nobody sends any more — the `"Attached files"` prefix is load-bearing for the agent and now lives in exactly one place.

The request carries **both**: the fenced block for the *model*, and `attachmentIds` for the *platform* (validated against the sha256 shape the uploads spine issues, bounded at 20). Nothing downstream re-parses a model-facing string to recover ids, so the block's wording can change without breaking tool calls.

## Two things the tests caught

1. **`attachmentUploadIds` was unanchored** — `https://evil.test/api/uploads/u/<sha>.pdf` yielded an id the caller never uploaded. An id is a lookup key. Anchored, with a regression test.
2. **Two of my own assertions were wrong**: they counted backticks anywhere, which fails on a filename that merely *contains* them inline — harmless, since a fence only **closes** at line start. They now assert the property that matters: injected content cannot begin a new line.

## Not in this change

**Attachments do not yet land in Memory.** That needs an org-scoped memory upload endpoint, which does not exist — `/api/memory` is read-only today (no `POST /api/memory/uploads`, no upload UI on the Memory page). Wiring chat to a route that isn't there would be the "exists but nothing calls it" pattern in reverse. That endpoint is the next slice.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| **`pnpm build` (full monorepo)** | **114/114** |
| `apps/web` vitest | 135 files, 1354 tests (9 new) |
| `apps/web` tsc | clean, across 21 locales |
| prettier | clean |

author: koussay183
body:
Closes the three owner-only items from the audit, plus the sitemap rebuild and the mobile logo.

## Backend — the data fixes, not just the guards

**Canonicals.** A migration clears every stored `canonical_url` whose **host is not protein.tn**. Four live CMS pages still pointed at the old domain:

| id | slug | stored value |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | conditions-generale-de-ventes-protein | `https://sobitas.tn/...` |
| 7 | politique-de-remboursement | `https://sobitas.tn/...` |
| 8 | politique-des-cookies | `https://sobitas.tn/...` |
| 9 | proteine-tunisie | `https://sobitas.tn/...` |

The frontend guard already refused to emit these, but that's a net, not a fix — the wrong value was still what the admin displayed, still what any new API consumer would read, and the guard fails open during `next build`. Host-based rather than an id list (all 7 canonical-bearing tables), logs each row before touching it, idempotent.

**Redirects.** Seeds the hand-curated tail of the 404 export: **15 × 301 + 1 × 410**.

Every row was re-verified live before being written: each source 404s to **both** a browser and Googlebot, and each target returns **200 in zero hops**. That gate earned its keep — the generated proposals were measured *before* #152 and wanted to 410 both `/pack-builder` (answers 200; it was only 404 to bots) and `/api` (now 301s to `/marque-api`). **40 of the 56 proposals were dropped** because the code fixes already resolve them.

## Sitemap — bigger, automatic, smarter, production-shaped

`/sitemap.xml` is now a **sitemap index** over five children, products chunked at 5k:

```
/sitemap.xml
  ├── /sitemaps/static.xml        11
  ├── /sitemaps/listings.xml     102
  ├── /sitemaps/products-0.xml   303
  ├── /sitemaps/blog.xml         100
  └── /sitemaps/pages.xml          5     = 521 URLs
```

Same URL, so nothing needs resubmitting — and Search Console now reports coverage **per content type** instead of one opaque number for the whole site, which is what makes a future drop diagnosable.

- Route handlers rather than `generateSitemaps()`, so the index sits at exactly `/sitemap.xml` (the URL robots.txt and GSC already name) and the XML stays ours.
- All children share **one** cached crawl — fetching the whole index costs a single upstream pass.
- Unknown child names **404** instead of rendering an empty urlset; failures return **503 + Retry-After**, never a 200 with a short list (a truncated sitemap reads to Google as "these URLs were removed").
- **`+/pack-builder`** — indexable but orphaned, and 404-to-Googlebot until #152. 520 → 521, parity verified against the old output.

**`lastmod` is now honest.** It fell back to `new Date()`, and the products API never selected its timestamps — so *every product advertised "modified just now" on every crawl*. Google discounts a lastmod it can prove is unreliable, so the signal was being actively spent. The API now returns `created_at`/`updated_at`, and an unknown date omits the element entirely.

**Automatic for all content, not just products.** `SitemapTouchObserver` busts the sitemap cache on create/update/delete for Categ, SousCategory, Brand, Article, Page, BlogCategory, BlogTag. Previously only a product save did this, so renaming a category or publishing an article left the sitemap stale for up to an hour. Fire-and-forget after the response — an admin save can never block on it.

## Mobile

Navbar logo `h-8` → `h-10`. Dropping Compte/Panier from that bar freed the room, and 40px is exactly the row's content box (`h-14` minus `py-2`), so the logo grows into space that already existed rather than making the bar taller.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0, `npm run build` → 0
- Sitemap index and all five children served from a local dev server against the **live** API: counts above, balanced tags, no raw ampersands, correct XML declaration, unknown name 404s
- `php -l` clean on every backend file

author: madrone77
body:
Signed-in anglers who hit reelcaster.com now land on `/dashboard` instead of the marketing homepage.

## Why it's client-side

supabase-js keeps the session in localStorage, not a cookie — so neither middleware nor the server render can tell a signed-in visitor from a crawler. Redirecting from a component on the page also leaves the homepage's static HTML untouched for search engines, which is the point of the recent SEO work.

## How

`src/app/(marketing)/components/signed-in-redirect.tsx`, mounted at the top of the marketing homepage. Two passes:

1. **Before first paint** — peek at the `sb-*-auth-token` key in localStorage, cover the page, prefetch `/dashboard`. Waiting on the async `getSession()` (which can include a token-refresh round trip) flashes the hero at every signed-in user.
2. **Once auth resolves** — only a confirmed session navigates. A stale token that can't be refreshed drops the cover and leaves the visitor on the homepage, rather than bouncing them through `/dashboard` into `/login`.

Signed-out visitors and crawlers render nothing at all.

## Verification

Local dev build, against a real signed-in session:

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| signed in → `/` | lands on `/dashboard` |
| signed out → `/` | homepage renders, stays on `/`, no cover |
| bogus/expired token → `/` | cover drops, stays on `/`, no login bounce |
| crawler view (`curl`, no JS) | hero HTML intact, zero redirect markup |

`tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean.

## Note

The homepage is now unreachable for signed-in users — pricing section included. Signing out is the only way back to it.

author: loomou
body:
## Problem

Logs were named by UTC date only, so every run on a given day appended to the same two files with no size ceiling. A single `conn_close` event can be ~13KB once request and response body samples are captured, so one long watch grows `ccwatcher-<date>.jsonl` without bound until the disk or your patience runs out. There was also no retention: files accumulated forever.

A related bug: the filename was resolved once in `New()`, so a process running past midnight kept writing to the previous day's file indefinitely.

## What this adds

Size rotation. The logger tracks bytes written per file in memory, and when the active file passes the threshold it is closed, renamed to the next free archive slot, and a fresh file is started. `.jsonl` and `.log` rotate independently.

```
ccwatcher-2026-07-28.jsonl      <- active, being written
ccwatcher-2026-07-28.1.jsonl    <- filled, archived
ccwatcher-2026-07-28.2.jsonl
```

On startup the existing file's size is read with `Stat()` and seeded into the counter, so restarting the watch cannot sidestep the limit.

Date roll-over. Every write checks the current UTC date and moves to that day's files when it changes, fixing the past-midnight bug. If reopening for the new day fails, it falls back to the previous day's files so logging keeps working rather than writing to a closed handle.

Retention. At startup, log files older than the retention window are deleted. Only names matching `ccwatcher-<date>[.<n>].(jsonl|log)` are ever removed, so unrelated files sharing the log directory are left alone. Cleanup failures are non-fatal — they must not stop the watch from starting.

Two new knobs, following the existing flag > env > .env > default chain. `0` disables either behavior, which keeps "no rotation, no cleanup" expressible.

| flag | env | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--log-max-mb` | `MON_LOG_MAX_MB` | `32` | rotate the active log once it passes this size |
| `--log-keep-days` | `MON_LOG_KEEP_DAYS` | `7` | delete logs older than this at startup |

## Why `--analyze` had to change too

Rotation would otherwise silently hide data: the report resolved exactly one path, `ccwatcher-<date>.jsonl`, so after a rotation it would only see the newest fragment and quietly under-report the day. `logx.SeriesFor()` now returns every `.jsonl` for a day in write order (numbered archives ascending, then the active file) and the report reads the whole series. When more than one file is involved the header says so: `... (+N rotated archive(s))`. An explicit path passed after `--analyze` is still read on its own.

`New(dir)` keeps its old signature with rotation and retention off, so existing callers and tests are unaffected; `NewWithOptions` takes the settings.

## Verification

11 new tests: 8 in `logx` covering size rotation, rotation disabled at `0`, size-seeding across a restart, human-log rotation, retention deleting old while keeping recent and ignoring unrelated files, retention disabled at `0`, and `SeriesFor` ordering. 3 in `config` covering the new defaults, flag-beats-env, and `0` disabling. `clearEnv` was extended to unset the new vars, and the config tests were confirmed to still pass with those vars polluted in the real environment.

Retention was also checked end to end with a real binary against a temp log dir: 30-day-old files deleted, the previous day's kept, an unrelated `notes.txt` untouched. Rotation was verified through the same MB-to-bytes conversion `main.go` uses, confirming the archive is created and the active file resets.

`gofmt`, `go vet`, and the full suite are clean.

author: externl
body:
Neither build system defines a bare `DEBUG`. Make adds `-DNDEBUG` for optimized builds and only `-g` otherwise, and MSBuild defines `_DEBUG` for Debug and `NDEBUG` for Release. These were the only two bare-`DEBUG` checks in the tree, and both were dead on every platform and configuration.

- `php/src/Operation.cpp`: the out-parameter `Z_ISREF` checks in `prepareRequest` were gated on `DEBUG`, so they had never run. Switched to `NDEBUG`, which is what governs `assert()` and what `Operation.cpp:778`, `Types.cpp`, `DefaultSliceLoader.cpp` and `Config.h` already use.
- `cpp/src/Ice/ResourceConfig.h`: `VER_DEBUG` was gated on `DEBUG`, so it was always `0` and the 31 `.rc` files using `FILEFLAGS VER_DEBUG` never set `VS_FF_DEBUG` — Windows debug binaries were not marked as debug builds. Switched to `_DEBUG`, matching `ICE_LIBNAME` six lines above and what MSBuild passes to `rc.exe`.

Found while auditing the codebase for dead code.

author: liassuo
body:
## Distinguir SMTP key de API key

### O que aconteceu
Com `BREVO_API_KEY` configurada, o diagnóstico avançou bastante — **Provedor: Brevo (HTTPS)**, resposta em **524ms** (contra 20s de timeout no SMTP) — mas a Brevo respondeu `401 {"message":"Key not found"}`.

Causa: a Brevo oferece **duas credenciais diferentes na mesma tela**. A aba **SMTP** gera uma *SMTP key* (para relay SMTP, justamente o caminho bloqueado) e a aba **"API keys & MCP"** gera a *API key* (para a REST API, que começa com `xkeysib-`). Foi gerada a primeira.

### Melhorias
- `brevoApiKey()`: aplica `trim()` — valores colados em painel costumam trazer espaço ou quebra de linha invisível
- `describeBrevoKey()`: exibe **prefixo e tamanho, nunca o valor**, e avisa quando não começa com `xkeysib-`
- Mensagem de erro passa a apontar explicitamente a aba correta

Com isso, esse tipo de troca fica visível na própria tela em vez de exigir investigação.

Verificação: typecheck do backend e build do frontend passando.

## Decisiones que conviene mirar

**`/health` no toca la base salvo con `?deep=1`.** Neon se suspende a los 5 minutos de inactividad y cobra por hora de cómputo: un monitor de uptime pegándole cada minuto a un health con `SELECT 1` la mantendría despierta 24/7. Hay un test que lo blinda con `expect(db.pings).toBe(0)`.

**Dos drivers de Neon a propósito.** `neon()` (HTTP) en el runtime; `Client` (WebSocket) solo en el runner de migraciones, porque el HTTP no soporta SQL multi-statement ni transacciones reales.

**`src/app.ts` no lee `process.env`.** Recibe sus dependencias inyectadas y `src/index.ts` es el único que las arma. Por eso los 19 tests corren sin red y sin base.

**TypeScript fijado en `^6`.** La 7 es el port nativo a Go y `typescript-eslint` todavía no soporta su API: el lint falla entero.

## Verificación

- `lint`, `typecheck` y `test` en verde: 19 pasando, 1 salteado.
- El test de integración de migraciones se saltea solo sin `DATABASE_URL`, por eso CI queda verde sin base.
- Pendiente de la fase: verificar `/health?deep=1` contra Neon y en el deploy de Vercel.

author: matze2010
body:
## Summary
This PR adds support for listing unread inbox items from the Enaio workflow system. Users can now query their pending inbox entries through a new `list_inbox` tool that filters and formats workflow activities.

## Key Changes

### Backend (`EnaioBackend.py`)
- Added `INBOX_WORKFLOW_ID` constant identifying the inbox workflow
- Added `WORKFLOWS_RUNNING_PATH` endpoint constant for the `/osrest/api/workflows/running` API
- Implemented `_epoch_ms_to_iso()` static method to convert millisecond timestamps to ISO-8601 format with graceful error handling
- Implemented `_inbox_record()` class method to transform raw workflow activity entries into a slim, standardized inbox record format
- Implemented `get_inbox()` async method that:
  - Fetches running workflow activities from the Enaio API
  - Filters to include only unread entries from the inbox workflow
  - Handles case-insensitive workflow ID matching
  - Sorts results by creation date (newest first)
  - Gracefully handles malformed entries and timestamps
  - Provides detailed error reporting for invalid API responses

### MCP Tools (`EnaioMCP.py`)
- Added `list_inbox_session()` tool for authenticated session-based inbox queries
- Added `list_inbox_basic()` tool for basic authentication mode
- Both tools return inbox count and filtered list of pending items
- Updated tool descriptions to guide users on when to use inbox vs. running cases queries

### Tests
- Added comprehensive test suite (`tests/test_backend_inbox.py`) covering:
  - Filtering of read items and foreign workflows
  - Correct API endpoint and header usage
  - Output format validation
  - Timestamp conversion and error handling
  - Non-dict entry handling
  - Case-insensitive workflow ID matching
  - Error handling for malformed responses
- Added tool integration tests (`tests/test_tools_inbox.py`) validating:
  - Session ID passing and item counting
  - Progress reporting

### Documentation
- Updated README.md to document the new `list_inbox` tool

## Implementation Details
- The inbox filtering is strict: only unread items (`read` field not set) from the specific inbox workflow are included
- Timestamps are converted from milliseconds since epoch to ISO-8601 format without fractional seconds
- Entries with invalid or missing timestamps are sorted to the end of the list rather than being dropped
- Non-dictionary entries in the API response are silently skipped to improve robustness
- The implementation distinguishes between inbox items and other workflow activities (ad-hoc workflows, approvals, etc.)

Deux bugs de précision trouvés en vérifiant à la main chaque résultat sur un gros monorepo en cours de migration v1/v2.

`--compare OLD=NEW` matchait les mondes par préfixe de chaîne : un vieux monde nommé comme un préfixe du nouveau (`main`/`mainV2`, le layout typique) avalait tout le nouveau monde — ses internes sortaient « deletable », et les symboles v1 référencés par le nouveau monde aussi, alors que les supprimer l'aurait cassé. author: obijuandeanobi
body:
Four commits. The prompt work for #29, plus the architectural decision that came out of discussing where this product is going.

## Summary

**Both prompt source paths built and proven on two standards** (#29). The spike's premise — that the OCR Audit Protocol would source all three rules — was wrong. Two better sources, split by rule:

| Rule | Records | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Security | 63 | **NIST SP 800-66r2** — 55 key-activity tables across all 22 standards, each with a Sample Questions column. Machine-readable, current, covers §164.314 and §164.316 which Appendix A does not. Source PDF pinned. |
| Privacy + Breach | 129 | **The regulation's own enumeration.** 45 CFR 164.520(b) lists what a notice must contain, item by item. Prompts quote the rule and carry a paragraph citation. No extraction risk, no staleness. |

The Audit Protocol is demoted to optional supplement — no PDF exists (three URLs, 404/403), fetches truncate inconsistently, and it is stale against current rule text.

**Shared paragraph walker.** `iter_section_paragraphs` is now the single source of truth for paragraph-path computation, used by both the catalog and the prompt builder. This was not tidying: the prompt builder had reimplemented the walk and dropped the inline-descent handling, putting every child of 164.520(b) at the wrong depth and yielding zero prompts for a record that enumerates twelve. **The refactor is verified behaviour-preserving — the catalog rebuilds byte-identically.**

**Stranded separator stripped from 29 records.** The regulation joins a paragraph's title to its inline first child with an em dash; once the label was removed the dash headed the requirement text.

**ADR 0012 — frameworks are data, not code.** Adding a framework means writing an ingester and declaring four things — record shape, rollup rule, status set, presentation mode — without touching the assessment workspace. Ingestion stays bespoke per source and is explicitly excluded from that generalization.

## Verification

**Ran, all passing:**
- 27 unit tests.
- Catalog byte-identical before and after the refactor, and byte-reproducible from pinned sources.
- Both sample paths render.
- Record count unchanged at 192.

**Not verified:** Johnathan's judgement on prompt shape and volume. That is the open acceptance criterion on #29.

## Scope and Debt Review

- [x] Implements only the approved ticket and its acceptance criteria
- [x] Uses the simplest implementation that satisfies the current requirement
- [x] Adds no speculative abstraction, configuration, or migration machinery
- [x] New dependencies are necessary, documented, and compatible with ARM64/x64 — PyMuPDF, used only by the ingestion script, never by the application
- [x] Existing lifecycle/version/audit behavior is reused instead of duplicated — this PR removes a duplication rather than adding one
- [x] Any accepted debt has a labeled issue with a reason and revisit point — #25

## Screenshots

Not applicable.

## Notes

- **Two open findings, deliberately not fixed.** The Security path yields 45 prompts on one standard, which extrapolates to several hundred across 192 — volume needs a practitioner call. The Privacy path picks up exceptions and scoping provisions alongside obligations, so it needs a filter, and which sub-paragraphs make good prompts is a judgement that should not be made alone.
- **ADR 0012 records where its own model breaks** — SOC 2, PCI DSS and ISO 27001 each strain it differently. Both frameworks named as possible later additions are on that list, so the analysis is recorded while it is cheap. Nothing is built for it and no debt issue is opened, per the gate's rule against debt for hypothetical work.
- **Process note.** These four commits sat unmerged while work continued on top of them, and a branch reset briefly discarded them. They were recovered intact, but the underlying cause was letting unmerged work accumulate. Opening this PR now rather than after more is stacked on it.

author: ywatanabe1989
body:
## Design + test-first skeleton. No guard behaviour changes.

This PR adds a design document and failing/xfail tests that encode intended
behaviour. **Zero source files are touched.** Implementation is a separate,
reviewed PR. Card: `scitex-cards-resolver-never-default-yaml-20260727` (P0).

## The defect

Store identity is a PATH. Measured on the HOST on 2026-07-28, the only place it
reproduces:

```
stamped store_path : /home/agent/.scitex/cards/cards.db
exists on HOST     : False
host resolves      : /home/ywatanabe/.scitex/cards/cards.db
                     -> /home/ywatanabe/.dotfiles/src/.scitex/cards/cards.db
```

ONE bind-mounted file, two names. `_same_file` compares by inode when both paths
exist and falls back to a realpath STRING compare when one does not. From the
host `/home/agent/...` cannot be stat'd, the strings never match, and the board
is refused its own database. `_same_file`'s own docstring records the same
false-negative class from 2026-07-20.

scitex-storage's formulation is the whole problem: **a path is not identity when
more than one view or code path can produce it.**

## The 500 is the guard working

Three repairs were tried on 2026-07-28 and all three were refused by defences
this package already carries. Recorded in section 2 of the design doc so nobody
re-runs them: loosening the shared predicate (broke the foreign-clobber test,
correctly), confining the relaxation to the read door (the exact asymmetry
`_read_canonical_db_or_raise` exists to prevent), and re-stamping the live store
to the host path (the 500 cleared and the board returned an EMPTY document --
the 2,138-card-wipe shape; reverted within a minute, 2646 cards verified
unchanged).

## What lands here

- `docs/design/store-identity-is-a-uuid.md` -- the `schema_meta.store_uuid`
  contract, the decision table, why identity and resolution stay two separate
  rules, removal of the realpath string fallback, the migration, the exposure,
  and what the design **cannot** decide.
- `tests/scitex_cards/test__store_uuid_identity_contract.py` -- the pure
  decision table and minting (9 tests).
- `tests/scitex_cards/test__store_uuid_guard_integration.py` -- the same
  contract against a real database (8 tests).

`1 passed, 16 xfailed`.

16 tests are `xfail(strict=True)` against `scitex_cards._store_uuid`, which does
not exist. All 16 were verified to fail on `ModuleNotFoundError` for that module
specifically, not on an incidental fixture error -- an xfail that fails for the
wrong reason proves nothing.

`strict=True` is the point: an XPASS fails the suite, so the implementation PR
must delete the markers test by test rather than write fresh assertions against
whatever it happened to build.

**One test is NOT xfail and passes today:**
`test_a_matching_identity_does_not_bypass_the_ambient_store_creation_guard` --
the regression lock on scitex-dev's requirement that identity and resolution
never merge.

## The decision table

`identity_verdict(db_uuid, expected)` is a PURE function of two optional strings
-- no path, no connection, no environment, so no view or mount namespace can
change the answer.

| `db_uuid` | `expected` | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `None` | `ADOPT` |
| `None` | `X` | `ADOPT` (see open question) |
| `X` | `None` | `ACCEPT` (contract rule 4b) |
| `X` | `X` | `ACCEPT` |
| `X` | `Y` | `REFUSE` -- the only refusal |

## Two things flagged rather than decided silently

**1. OPEN QUESTION -- row 2 of the table.** The tests encode the contract
literally (`ADOPT`). I think it is the weakest row and would rather it were
`REFUSE`: an expectation is a STATEMENT that this store must be X, and a
database that cannot show it is X does not satisfy that statement -- "no
identity" is not "the identity you named". Contract rule 4b is about the CALLER
lacking an expectation, which is a different question from the DATABASE lacking
an identity. The counter-argument, and why I did not just change it: `REFUSE`
strands an operator mid-migration with a board that refuses every write. Design
doc section 10. One row, one line of one test.

**2. PR #598 interaction.** #598 makes an unresolvable stamp mean "cannot tell,
so proceed". It is explicitly a mitigation, and the only thing in the tree that
can bring the board back before this lands. If it merges first, the
implementation PR MUST revert that relaxation -- but only AFTER the live store
carries a `store_uuid`. Reverting earlier re-opens the outage; leaving it leaves
a permanent "proceed when unsure" branch behind a guard whose whole value is
that it does not do that. Design doc section 8.

## What the design cannot decide, stated honestly

A byte copy carries the same `store_uuid`; the file cannot self-distinguish,
because everything it could distinguish itself by is inside the thing that was
copied. Both copies are ACCEPTed. Closed only by an INJECTED expectation pairing
the identity with something OUTSIDE the file (scitex-dev's registry), and even
that detects "wrong endpoint", never "this copy is the stale one".

`test_a_byte_copy_carries_the_same_identity_and_cannot_self_distinguish` asserts
the copy is INDISTINGUISHABLE **on purpose**, so a later attempt to close the
gap by mixing a path or an inode back into the identity goes red instead of
quietly reintroducing the view-dependence this change removes.

## Tests do not measure the machine

A test written earlier on 2026-07-28 stamped the real `/home/agent/...` path to
exercise the unresolvable branch and PASSED VACUOUSLY inside the container where
that path exists -- green here, red on the host, the same environment-coupling
that let the original bug reach the operator.

So paths that must not resolve are spelled
`/proc/self/no-such-mount-namespace/...`, which cannot exist anywhere, and the
strongest test does not depend on resolvability at all: it stamps a path that IS
resolvable and IS genuinely different alongside a MATCHING identity, and asserts
the identity wins. That cannot pass vacuously under today's code, nor under
#598.

Every test uses an EXPLICIT tmp store, pinned via a fixture rather than
per-test, because `_read_canonical_db_or_raise` resolves `$SCITEX_CARDS_DB`
regardless of any `store` argument -- a test that forgets the pin does not
merely read the operator's board, it can rewrite it.

## Not done here

No source file is modified. No live store was written.
`refuse_ambient_store_creation` is untouched, both doors keep the same shared
predicate, and no `store_path` was re-stamped anywhere.
