author: filipexyz
body:
## Objective

Prevent exhausted runtime recovery from being sent through user-facing channel transport, while keeping the failure actionable for operators. Also preserve agent capabilities when an internal prompt uses a reset session's retained chat binding only as its reply destination.

## Problem

- Exhausted event-loop recovery used the normal response subject and retained the failed replay queue.
- The retry limit was fixed in code.
- A derived reply surface could be mistaken for an unresolved external actor after a session reset.

## Solution

- Suppress channel responses when event-loop recovery exhausts, drop the failed replay queue, and retain technical detail in runtime trace and log events.
- Create an urgent deduplicated local inbox item and publish `ravi.inbox.system.runtime_recovery_exhausted` for operator automation.
- Read the retry ceiling from `RAVI_RUNTIME_EVENT_LOOP_MAX_RESTARTS` (default `2`; `0` disables replay).
- Distinguish prompt-provided authority surfaces from session-derived reply surfaces.

## Practical impact

- External chats no longer receive infrastructure failure text from this recovery path.
- Operators get an actionable inbox/event signal and subsequent messages can start cleanly.
- Session reset retains the agent's configured tool capabilities for internal prompts.

## What does NOT change

- Actual external prompts without a resolved contact still fail closed.
- The default recovery budget remains two attempts.
- Normal user-facing failures and successful recovery behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run test`
- `bun src/ci/run-quality-gate.ts` with the PR file set
- `bunx markdownlint-cli2 docs/start/configuration.mdx`
- Repository pre-push checks

## Risks

- The exhausted turn is intentionally not replayed again after the configured limit; the next inbound message starts from a clean queue.
- Operator event delivery still depends on the configured NATS and trigger path; the local urgent inbox item remains the durable signal.

## Rollback

Revert commit `38dcc621` to restore the previous recovery and authority-resolution behavior.

## Follow-ups

None.

author: noan98
body:
## 概要

TLS/SSL 設定 (#520) の既知ギャップだった「実 TLS サーバへのハンドシェイク検証 (CA 検証失敗時のエラー表面化を含む)」を CI で実走できるようにします。既存の env ゲート方式 (未設定ならスキップ) を踏襲しています。

## 変更内容

- `src-tauri/tests/tls_integration.rs` (新規) — `NOOBDB_TEST_MYSQL_TLS_URL` / `NOOBDB_TEST_POSTGRES_TLS_URL` / `NOOBDB_TEST_TLS_CA` でゲートされる統合テスト。各ドライバ 4 件・計 8 件:
  - `require` で接続成立
  - `verify_ca` + 正しい CA で接続成立
  - `verify_full` + 正しい CA で接続成立 (証明書 SAN に `127.0.0.1` を含めホスト名検証もカバー)
  - `verify_full` + CA 未指定でのエラー表面化
- `scripts/ci-setup-tls-db.sh` (新規) — openssl で自己署名 CA + サーバ証明書を生成し、mysql-server / postgresql (ランナーにプリインストール済み) を TLS 必須 (`require_secure_transport=ON` / `hostssl` のみ許可) で別ポート (3307/5433) に起動
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `rust (test)` ジョブに TLS DB セットアップの background ステップを追加 (sshd セットアップと並列)
- `CLAUDE.md` — TLS 統合テスト方針セクションを実装後の状態に更新

## CI 配備方式の選択理由

既存のサービスコンテナ (平文 MySQL/PostgreSQL) は変更せず、独立した TLS 必須インスタンスを別ポートに立てる方式を採用しました。サービスコンテナはジョブ内で生成した証明書を後から渡せず、`services:` 構文では起動引数 (`-c ssl=on` 等) も上書きできないためです。既存の SSH トンネル統合テスト (#331 の `ci-setup-sshd.sh`) と同じ「apt パッケージを直接構成する」実績あるパターンで、ci.yml の変更を最小限に抑えています。

## テスト (ローカル、TLS サーバ無し環境)

- `cargo test --test tls_integration` → 8 件すべてスキップ経路で ok (コンパイル成功)
- `cargo test --lib` → 338 件 pass (既存への影響なし)
- `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` → pass

Closes #795

author: innercoder78
body:
### Motivation

- Telegraph-derived titles were sometimes corrupted by an overly permissive slug cleanup that stripped only part of a numeric suffix (e.g. `3126-Inferno-07-28-4` became `Inferno-07` → `Inferno 07`).
- When a Telegram message included both a `.docx` filename and a matching Telegraph link the parser preferred the full Telegraph-derived report and discarded the more trustworthy `.docx` filename title.

### Description

- Constrain Telegraph suffix stripping to plausible month/day patterns with an optional trailing collision suffix so date-plus-collision endings like `-07-28-4` are removed but legitimate trailing numbers (e.g. `Catch-22`) are preserved (`src/shadow_slave_monitor/parsers.py`).
- When a message node contains both a matching `.docx` document candidate and a Telegraph candidate for the same chapter, merge them into a report that uses the `.docx`-derived title and the Telegraph URL (while preserving candidate ordering, deduplication, and chapter selection).
- Add focused regression tests covering the reported problematic slugs, ordinary date suffixes, legitimate numeric titles, document-title precedence, Telegraph fallback behavior, and unchanged earlier Telegraph parsing behavior (`tests/test_parsers.py`).

### Testing

- Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_parsers.py' -v` and the 7 new parser regression tests passed.
- Ran the full test suite with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and all tests passed (46 tests total).
- Ran static checks and bytecode compilation with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m compileall -q src scripts` and `git diff --check`, both of which succeeded.

body:
# Pull Request

## Description

Fixes an early-morning negative array slicing bug in `fetchAirQualityByCoords` within `src/services/airQualityService.js`. When querying air quality data during early morning hours (`idx < 23`), `startIndex` evaluated to a negative integer (`idx - 23`), causing JavaScript `slice()` to count backwards from the end of the array rather than starting at `0`. This resulted in corrupted AQI trend arrays and `undefined` pollutant lookups.

---

## Related Issue

Closes #372

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] UI/UX Improvement
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] Performance Improvement
- [ ] Accessibility

## Cosa è già successo

La potatura del lotto 27 **è stata applicata su `main`** (commit `75e7c6b`): i tre file vivi della memoria sono passati da **1.068.042 a 267.885 byte** (−75%), con tutto lo storico in `90-Memoria-AI/Storico/` e nessuna riga persa.

Questa PR porta solo i due pezzi che **sono codice** e che il pre-commit giustamente non lascia passare su `main`.

## I due pezzi

**`cervello/peso-contesto.json`** — i tetti scendono al nuovo peso, con un **margine dichiarato del 25%**.

Senza margine, `--aggiorna` avrebbe messo il tetto pari al peso esatto — e la prima riga scritta in DECISIONI l'avrebbe sfondato. Un guardiano che suona a ogni scrittura legittima viene spento entro la settimana, che è esattamente il difetto che questi lotti curano. Il margine è il respiro fra una potatura e la successiva, non un permesso a crescere: il tetto resta un cricchetto che scende.

```
STATO.md             97.768 → tetto 122.210
AZIONI-IN-ATTESA.md  59.289 → tetto  74.111
SALA-OPERATIVA.md   110.828 → tetto 138.535
DECISIONI.md        508.955 → tetto 636.194   (append-only, esente dalla potatura)
```

**`cervello/test/il-costo-della-memoria.test.mjs`** — la prova post-potatura pretendeva un totale sotto 600 KB **includendo `DECISIONI.md`**, che è append-only ed esente dalla potatura: faceva fallire una potatura perfettamente riuscita. Adesso misura i **tre file potabili**, che sono quelli su cui il lotto agisce. Metro sbagliato, non fix sbagliato — ed è il quarto metro storto di questo lotto.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

The repo had no test tooling at all, so every JS module sat at 0% coverage. The least-covered (only) JS is `script.js` (menu, `aria-current`, smooth scroll, footer year) and the inline tab controller in `metodo_5d.html`; both are now covered by Vitest + jsdom.

Coverage of `script.js` after this PR: **100% lines / 98.4% statements / 94.1% branches / 100% functions** (the two uncovered branches are unreachable guards: the redundant `!mobileToggle || !mainNav` check inside `setMenuState`, and `targetId ? ... : null` for a matched `a[href^="#"]`).

Two testability details worth knowing:

- `script.js` is a side-effectful `DOMContentLoaded` script, not a module with exports. `tests/helpers.js` re-imports it per test via `vi.resetModules()` and intercepts its `DOMContentLoaded` registration so the callback can be invoked directly:
  ```js
  document.addEventListener = (type, listener) => { if (type === 'DOMContentLoaded') onReady = listener; else add(type, listener); };
  vi.resetModules(); await import('../script.js');
  onReady(new Event('DOMContentLoaded'));
  ```
  Dispatching a real `DOMContentLoaded` instead would re-fire every previous test's listener on the shared document and double-bind handlers (menu toggling twice per click).
- The `metodo_5d.html` tab logic is inline in the page, so the test extracts `<script>` blocks without `src` from the HTML and evaluates them against the page body — no HTML changes required.

Also added: `npm test` / `npm run test:coverage`, a `tests` GitHub Actions workflow, and `.gitignore` for `node_modules/` and `coverage/`. No production code was modified.

author: lefarcen
body:
## Why

The beta feed cannot be published to any more. Both attempts tonight died at `Prepare beta metadata`:

```
[release-beta] packaged base version 0.16.1 must be strictly greater than latest stable 0.16.1
[release-beta] beta metadata.json baseVersion 0.16.1 does not match betaVersion 0.16.2-beta.144
```

The first is waivable with `force`. The second is not: this afternoon `0.16.2-beta.144` was published using an explicit `release_version` override while every manifest on this branch still read `0.16.1`, which left the published `metadata.json` self-inconsistent. Any later build validates that file and refuses.

This is my own mistake coming back — the override produced a version number the repo could not substantiate.

## What changed

`0.16.1` → `0.16.2` in the **same 18 manifests** the release bot touched in `23f9fcaac` (`chore(release): bump main to 0.16.2 ahead of stable 0.16.1`). Nothing else. Two test files mention `0.16.1` as fixture data (`WhatsNewPopup.test.tsx`, `packaged-launcher-update-loop.test.ts`); that commit left them alone and so does this one.

After this, `0.16.2-beta.145` is consistent with its own metadata and `force` is no longer needed for the base-version check.

## What users will see

Nothing directly. It unblocks publishing dogfood betas from this branch with a version number that does not go backwards — the auto-resolver currently proposes `0.16.1-beta.1`, which is behind the `0.16.2-beta.144` already circulating.

## Surface area

- [x] Root `package.json` / workspace manifests
- [ ] UI
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Contracts
- [ ] i18n

## Notes for the reviewer

This raises the branch only; `main` remains at `0.16.1` and is untouched. If the intent is instead to bump `main` on the normal release cadence, close this — but then tonight’s beta cannot be published with a forward-moving version.

author: viniciusborgeis
body:
Closes #50

The 0.1.0 publish failed for all 29 packages, and the log said only this:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')
    at isAlreadyPublishedError (.../changesets-cli.cjs.js:880:17)
```

That is changesets reading a field off an error shape it did not expect. The
cause underneath: npm provenance is on, and provenance requires a `repository`
field pointing at the repository doing the build. Not one package had one.

The token was never the problem. #49 added an `npm whoami` check to the release
workflow and it came back `viniciusborgeis`, which is how this was found.

## What changed

Fixing only `repository` would still have published 29 packages in a poor state,
because none of the rest was there either.

| field | why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| `repository` | provenance refuses to sign without it |
| `files` | without it npm ships everything not ignored |
| `description` | the npm page is otherwise blank |
| `license` | npm shows the package as unlicensed |
| `homepage`, `bugs` | no way back to the source or the issues |
| `author`, `keywords` | attribution, and being findable at all |
| `publishConfig.access` | a scoped package is private by default |

Each description is taken from the blockquote its README already opens with, so
the npm page and the repository cannot drift apart.

The published tree is `dist` and `src` with the tests excluded. `src` stays
because every exports map carries a `development` condition pointing into it,
and publishing a manifest that refers to files that are not there is worse than
the few kilobytes it saves.

## Effect on the tarball

`npm pack --dry-run` on `@venn-lang/cli`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| test and source files with no business shipping | 80 | 0 |
| total files | everything not ignored | 73 |
| package size | not measured, larger | 471 kB |

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (the lockfile still matches)
- [x] `pnpm -r --sort run build` (0 errors)
- [x] `pnpm -r run typecheck` (0 errors)
- [x] `pnpm lint` (clean, same 2 pre-existing warnings)
- [x] `pnpm test` (1315 passing, 214 files)
- [x] All 29 packages carry every field, and each `repository.directory` matches
      its own path on disk
- [x] `npm pack --dry-run` ships no `.test.ts` or `.suite.ts`
- [x] No em dash anywhere

## Checklist

- [x] A test covers the change, and it fails without it (not applicable: this is
      package manifest metadata, verified by `npm pack` and the assertions above)
- [x] Public API has JSDoc (no API changed)
- [ ] A changeset is included (not needed: 0.1.0 is already versioned on main
      from #40 and remains unpublished, so this goes out under that same number)
- [x] Documentation is updated (each description now mirrors its README)

## State right now

Still nothing published: every `@venn-lang/*` name returns 404. `0.1.0` is free
and goes out under that number. #49 should land first, since it is what lets the
action find the token at all.

author: jasisz
body:
Four producer-side changes; the Lean wall is untouched (zero files under aver-cert/assets/wall/).

- Refuse fragment plans for functions whose parameters, return value, or locals use the bare i64 representation. The plan lowerer assumes carrier structs; on a bare signature it would emit invalid wasm. Not reachable end-to-end today (bare promotion requires a self-recursive shape that plan bodies cannot have), so this is a fail-closed guard with a unit test documenting why.
- Inline single-use let bindings when building fragment plans. `y = o; match y { ... }` now produces the same plan as `match o { ... }`. Strictly limited: exactly one use counting nested blocks, initializer must itself be planable, comparison operands must still resolve to a parameter read, multi-use bindings stay unplanned.
- Render the generic fragment bridge for any source arity. Previously two `panic!`s fired at arity 3+; `aver compile --certify` crashed on an exported three-parameter Int/Bool function. The Lean side was already arity-generic.
- Enforce the kernel's plan-block shape invariants (contiguous node ids, root last) in the producer's `finish`, so future producer bugs degrade to uncertified instead of failing late in the kernel.

Verification: both new fixture packages fully replay in the kernel (`aver cert verify`: letnamed 3 certified exports, arity3 1 certified export); plan-vs-MIR equivalence suite extended with the new shapes; 9 new producer unit tests incl. negatives (multi-use let, computed comparison operand, payload binder, bare-slot guard); goal matrix and MIR floors unchanged; spot-checked example packages byte-identical; fmt and clippy clean on the CI feature matrix.

author: pureween
body:
### Description of Change

Removes `.github/CODEOWNERS`, whose only entry is currently invalid:

```text
* @dotnet/dotnet-maui-reviewers
```

GitHub's CODEOWNERS errors API reports this owner as unknown because the team has **Read** access to `dotnet/maui` (`pull: true`, `push: false`). GitHub requires teams named in CODEOWNERS to have explicit Write access, so the line is ignored today.

This does **not** remove an effective review gate:

- `MAUI protection` independently continues to require one approving review.
- Its `require_code_owner_review` setting has no matching valid code owner today, so removing the rejected file preserves the current effective behavior.
- There is no fallback CODEOWNERS file elsewhere in the repository.
- No repository automation reads this file; the only text references are generic content embedded in generated workflow lock files.

The entry was introduced in #16682 on August 10, 2023 to auto-request the MAUI reviewers team. Repository team permissions are not stored in git, so it is not possible to determine from public history whether the team had Write access then and lost it later, or whether the entry was invalid from the start.

Removing it makes the repository configuration accurately reflect its current behavior and prevents a future team-permission change from unexpectedly activating code-owner enforcement and blocking automation.

A separate repository-settings cleanup can turn off the currently ineffective **Require review from Code Owners** checkbox. That settings change is intentionally not represented as code in this PR.

Related context: #36875

### Issues Fixed

None; repository policy cleanup.

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

`creating-product-tours` never shows up in `wizard skill list`. Its `config.yaml`
has no `cli:` block, and `generateCliEntries()` in `scripts/lib/build-phases.js`
filters on `allSkills.filter(s => s.cli)` — so it never reaches `cliEntries` in
`skill-menu.json`, which is the only thing `wizard skill list` prints. The skill
runs fine if you already know the id; it just can't be found.

## Why

Product tours is sunsetting, and `npx @posthog/wizard@latest skill creating-product-tours`
is now the recommended path for people who want to build tours themselves. Support
has been handing out the exact id because the listing doesn't have it — two tickets
in the last eight days, one from a customer migrating off a paid guides vendor.
Wizard telemetry shows no traffic reaching the skill at all.

## Changes

- `context/skills/creating-product-tours/config.yaml`: declare `cli: role: skill`.
  It picks up an entry at build time and `skill list` shows it on the next release,
  with no wizard change needed.
- Fix the contributor docs that made the omission look correct. `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  claimed skills with no `cli:` block "default to the `skill` role" and were
  "discoverable via `wizard skill list`" — they aren't; they get no entry at all.
  Same wording corrected in `AGENTS.md` and the two doc comments that repeated it.
- Add a regression test asserting the real config produces a browsable entry.

## What I checked while in here

Every other skill missing a `cli:` block is deliberately unlisted: sub-skills a
flow pulls in (`posthog-best-practices`, the `integration-v2` steps), skills
fronted by a wizard-native command (`data-warehouse-source`, `web-analytics`,
`self-driving`), or internal test fixtures (`quack`). `creating-product-tours`
was the only standalone, user-facing one silently absent, so this is a one-line
fix rather than a sweep.

Not covered here: the support macro still uses the deprecated `--skill <name>`
flag instead of the `wizard skill <name>` positional — that lives outside this
repo and needs a separate update.

## Verification

`pnpm test` (138 passing) and a full `pnpm build`, confirming the entry lands in
`dist/skills/skill-menu.json`:

```json
{ "skillId": "creating-product-tours", "role": "skill", "displayName": "Creating product tours" }
```

Rendered as `wizard skill list` would print it:

```
  creating-product-tours                  wizard skill creating-product-tours   Build an in-app product tour that guides users through a feature...
```

author: atassis
body:
Following up on the Chess to Peano scoping discussion (#3414), this is the
uncontroversial first slice: tests whose only purpose is to run a design through
Chess when a Peano test of the same design already exists.

Nothing here loses coverage of a design or a configuration. Each deleted test has
a Peano counterpart in the tree that runs the same Makefile parameters on the same
device, so the only thing dropped is a second compile of the same thing through
the backend we are moving away from. No production code changes, no new tests, no
extra device runs.

### programming_examples/basic (12 lit files)

| deleted | Peano test that already covers it |
| --- | --- |
| `matrix_vector/tests/run_makefile_chess.lit` | `run_makefile.lit` |
| `matrix_vector/tests/run_strix_makefile_chess.lit` | `run_strix_makefile.lit` |
| `single_core/tests/run_makefile_chess.lit` | `run_makefile.lit` (both all defaults) |
| `single_core/tests/run_makefile_bf16_chess.lit` | `run_makefile_bf16.lit` |
| `single_core/tests/run_strix_makefile_bf16_chess.lit` | `run_strix_makefile_bf16.lit` |
| `single_core/tests/run_strix_makefile_bf16_emulated_chess.lit` | `run_strix_makefile_bf16_emulated.lit` |
| `whole_array/tests/run_makefile_chess.lit` | `run_makefile_4_col.lit` (`n_aie_cols?=4`) |
| `whole_array/tests/run_makefile_bf16_chess.lit` | `run_makefile_bf16.lit` |
| `whole_array/tests/run_strix_makefile_bf16_chess.lit` | `run_strix_makefile_bf16.lit` |
| `whole_array/tests/run_strix_makefile_bf16_emulated_chess.lit` | `run_strix_makefile_bf16_emulated.lit` |
| `vector_scalar_mul/run_makefile_chess.lit` | `run_makefile.lit` (superset, adds `int_bit_width=32`) |
| `vector_scalar_mul/run_strix_makefile_chess.lit` | `run_strix_makefile.lit` (superset) |

I compared the resolved Makefile variables rather than the file names, so the
mapping accounts for defaults: `whole_array/run_makefile_chess.lit` passes no
`n_aie_cols`, which resolves to 4, matching `run_makefile_4_col.lit`.

### test/npu-xrt (3 directories)

`add_one_cpp_aiecc_xchesscc`, `add_one_func_link_with_chess` and
`add_one_scale_func_link_with_chess`. Their counterparts `add_one_cpp_aiecc`,
`add_one_func_link_with_peano` and `add_one_scale_func_link_with_peano` test the
same feature on the same devices through Peano/lld, as the file headers say
("End-to-end test for func-level `link_with` (Chess/xbridge backend)" against
"(Peano/lld backend)"). The only substantive difference I found between the pairs
is an unused `%c8 = arith.constant 8 : i64` in the Peano copy.

### Evidence

From the CI run on the base commit `a079d8b0a87` (run 30278176623, all checks green),
on both device runners:

* Each of the 15 Peano tests listed above passed on its matching runner and was
  correctly Unsupported on the other. Neither device suite reported a single
  FAIL or TIMEOUT, and none of the 15 carries an `XFAIL` marker, so "a Peano test
  already covers it" is a green test rather than a skipped one.
* The tests I am deleting were live, not dead weight: they ran and passed too.
  That is the point, they were running the same designs a second time through
  Chess.

Their measured cost in that run was about 1535s of device-runner time, 911s on
`aie2-4col` and 624s on `aie2p-8col`. That is a lower bound, since the log only
times the 64 slowest tests per job and `add_one_cpp_aiecc_xchesscc` falls outside
that.

### What I deliberately left alone

`single_core/tests/run_strix_makefile_chess.lit` and
`whole_array/tests/run_strix_makefile_chess.lit` look like the same pattern but
are not. Each runs its example with all defaults on npu2, and no Peano test covers
that configuration: the npu2 Peano tests for single_core all pin different
parameters, and for whole_array they cover 1, 2 and 8 columns plus 4 columns at
i8, but not 4 columns at i16/i32. Deleting those would drop a configuration rather
than a backend, so they want converting to Peano instead. I can send that
separately with the device run attached.

The `block_datatypes` examples still need Chess and are untouched, and I left the
`use_chess` plumbing in `makefile-common` and the designs alone so this change
stays purely subtractive and easy to revert.

### One question while I am here

The discussion says Peano is the default, but `aiecc` still has
`--xchesscc`/`--xbridge` at `cl::init(true)` and CMake defaults `AIE_COMPILER` and
`AIE_LINKER` to `XCHESSCC`. `%backend_flags` only steers tests onto Peano when
Chess is absent, so on a Vitis-equipped runner the 62 tests that invoke a bare
`%aiecc` still go through Chess. Is flipping those defaults something you would
take, or is the Chess-when-present default deliberate for now? Happy to prepare it
if it is wanted, though it needs your CI to validate.

author: pineapple40
body:
## Summary

A complete local, paper-trading day-trading platform for US equities/ETFs — Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript strict mode, PostgreSQL/Prisma, Redis, Docker Compose. Simulated market data and a simulated broker throughout; **no real money and no real broker are involved anywhere**, and live trading is hard-disabled in code (not just a config toggle).

Built in 14 logical-stage commits (see commit history): scaffold → schema/migrations → auth → market data → broker/risk engine → dashboard/watchlists/charts/order ticket → journal/analytics → strategy builder/backtesting → paper strategy runner → alerts/admin/audit → tests + CI → docs/deployment prep.

## What's included

- Auth: registration, email verification, password reset, optional TOTP MFA, account lockout, Redis-backed rate limiting, role-based authorization (trader/admin)
- Provider-neutral simulated market-data feed (deterministic, reproducible candles + live quotes)
- Simulated broker: MARKET/LIMIT/STOP/STOP_LIMIT orders, matching engine, idempotent submission, long-only position/P&L accounting
- Server-side risk engine (pure, unit-tested): max risk per trade, daily/weekly loss lockout, exposure limits, required stop-loss, min reward-to-risk, market-hours gating, and more — every decision audited
- Dashboard, watchlists, candlestick charts (lightweight-charts) with SMA/EMA/VWAP/RSI overlays, scanner, order ticket, and a working emergency-stop trading lock
- Trading journal + performance analytics (win rate, expectancy, profit factor, drawdown, CSV export)
- No-code rule-based strategy builder + event-driven backtesting engine (no look-ahead bias, next-bar-open fills, commission/slippage/spread modeling, Sharpe/Sortino)
- Paper strategy runner (background worker) running strategies live through the same risk-checked order path as manual trading, with a kill switch
- Alerts + in-app notifications (deduplicated, cooldown-based)
- Admin panel: user management, feature flags, searchable audit log

## Verification (fresh clone, this session)

- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run test` (Vitest) — **77/77 passing** (indicators, risk engine ~20 rule cases, strategy evaluator, backtest engine, data-generator determinism, password strength, full order-lifecycle + auth integration tests against real Postgres)
- `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright) — **9/9 passing** (registration, login success/failure, protected-route redirect, watchlist CRUD, real rendered chart, risk-rejected order, filled order, resting-order cancel)
- `npm run build` — succeeds
- `npm start` (production server) — boots; `/api/health` and `/api/ready` both healthy; login + account fetch verified via curl

GitHub Actions CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs all of the above against Postgres/Redis service containers on every push/PR to this branch.

## Docs

README, `PROJECT_STATUS.md` (running log of decisions/assumptions/limitations), `ARCHITECTURE.md` (Mermaid diagrams + rationale for non-obvious choices), `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md`, `docs/COMPLIANCE_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`.

## Try it locally

```bash
cp .env.example .env
npm install
npm run docker:up && npm run db:migrate:deploy && npm run db:seed
npm run dev
```
Demo logins: `demo@probable-disco.local` / `Demo!Trader123` (trader), `admin@probable-disco.local` / `Demo!Admin123` (admin).

## Known limitations / not built in this pass

See `PROJECT_STATUS.md` for the full list — highlights: journal file attachments have no storage backend, no SMS/push notification provider (email/in-app only), no admin-initiated lock on *another* user's account, and live trading requires a compliance/acknowledgement flow that is intentionally not implemented (see `docs/COMPLIANCE_CHECKLIST.md`).

author: reyzartz
body:
Ports the Fastify/TypeScript server to Go and restructures the repo to mirror [Reyzartz/cha-ching](https://github.com/Reyzartz/cha-ching).

Behaviour is unchanged. The edge-trigger state machine, the schedule ⇄ cron bijection, the browser mutex and the storage guarantees are ported 1:1, and the whole Node test suite came with them.

## Layout

```
breckr/
├── Makefile  Dockerfile  docker-compose.yml
├── client/          ← packages/dashboard, now a standalone npm root
└── server/          go.mod, main.go
    └── internal/{api,app,config,middleware,migrations,routes,store,utils}   ← cha-ching's packages
        + {types,browser,executor,notifier,runner,scheduler}                 ← what breckr needs beyond CRUD
```

`internal/{api,app,config,middleware,migrations,routes,store,utils}` are cha-ching's packages, same names and roles. The rest exist because cha-ching's domain logic lives in its stores and breckr's does not — the cron registry, the CDP driver and the edge-trigger runner have nowhere else to go.

npm workspaces and `@breckr/shared` are gone. The contract now lives in `server/internal/types`, with `client/src/types/index.ts` mirroring it as declarations — no generator, just two files that have to agree, pinned together by the json tags.

## Stack

chi + chi/cors, `robfig/cron/v3`, go-rod, goose, `modernc.org/sqlite`.

The SQLite driver is pure Go, so the binary builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and the runtime image is bare alpine — the Node image needed Debian trixie purely to satisfy better-sqlite3's prebuilt binary. Compose still runs one app container plus the browser; the server serves the dashboard build from its own origin, so there is still no CORS and nginx stays optional.

**Migrating an existing database needs no action.** goose applies the schema at boot, every table is created `IF NOT EXISTS`, so the first run against a Node-era `data/monitor.db` just stamps the version.

## API change

Successful responses are now `{"data": ...}`; failures stay `{"error": ...}` at the top level with a `field` on validation failures. `client/src/apis/client.ts` unwraps the envelope, so nothing downstream knows it exists. Field names and types are otherwise byte-identical.

## Verification

- `make test` green — 8 test files ported, including the `FromCron(ToCron(s)) == s` round trip and the edge-trigger state machine through every delivery outcome. Each test gets its own database under `t.TempDir()`, so nothing runs serially any more.
- Booted against a copy of a real `data/monitor.db`: goose stamped the version without touching a row, both tasks loaded, one armed.
- Responses diffed field-for-field against the Node server. All error paths carry `field` — a duplicate ID renders against the ID control in the form, not as a page banner.
- All five extraction kinds driven through Lightpanda, plus a real `run-now` firing exactly once on false→true and staying quiet after.
- Dashboard exercised on both the served build and the Vite dev proxy: create, toggle, run-now, filter, paginate. No console errors.

## Three things worth a closer look

**The websocket is dialled directly** rather than through rod's `ControlURL`. rod keeps its own socket private, and cancelling its context stops the event loop without closing the TCP connection — against Lightpanda, which spawns a thread per session, that leaks until it answers every new connection with `MaxThreadsReached` and goes permanently unreachable. `browser.go` owns the socket so it can close it, including when a run outlives its timeout and the pool mutex has already been released.

**Teardown disposes the browser context instead of closing the page.** Lightpanda can take ~47s to answer `Target.closeTarget`, and the pool mutex is held for all of it. Disposing the context is 3ms, takes the pages with it, and on Chrome is what stops a per-run context leaking after we disconnect.

**`count` evaluates `querySelectorAll(...).length` in the page.** rod's `Elements()` rejects the `NodeList` Lightpanda returns, and this is one round trip rather than one per match.

Device emulation is also off — a monitor reads a value out of the DOM and has no use for a viewport or a spoofed user agent, both of which Lightpanda answers with a `not_implemented` warning.

## Unrelated fix

`ScheduleField.tsx` passed `color="default"` to brake-ui's `Button`, which is not a valid `ButtonColor` — unselected weekday chips rendered unstyled, and it was the one thing blocking `npm run typecheck`. They are `"secondary"` now. Happy to change the colour if you'd rather it looked different.

author: vicvalch
body:
## Summary

Consolidates PMFreak onto a single, honest, evidence-derived onboarding journey. Retires the legacy fabricated-readiness wizard as a reachable onboarding surface and removes the PMO-before-Project routing gate that forced every new/PMO-less user through it.

**⚠️ Updated after review.** The initial version of this PR modeled onboarding as only 4 coarse states and returned "active" as soon as a single Project existed, collapsing "Project exists", "a real task exists", and "Command Center is active" into one state — see **§ Correction pass** below for the fix. All feedback items are resolved.

**Backlog IDs addressed:** `PMF-001`, `PMF-002` (`docs/audits/pmfreak-post-merge-backlog.json`)

**Ratified canonical onboarding decision** (was `PENDING` in `docs/audits/pmfreak-remediation-decision-brief.md` §22, now recorded there — no other decision answer was touched):

> The PR #547 evidence-derived onboarding model is canonical. The legacy wizard is retired as a reachable onboarding system. Project creation must not require prior PMO or Command Center creation. Onboarding progression derives from real persisted state.

**Prerequisites verified merged into `main` before this work began:** `PMF-003` (#557), `PMF-003B` (#558), `PMF-004` (#559, commit `7a8a8d4`).

## Legacy system retired

- `src/components/pmfreak/activation/getting-started-flow.tsx` (+ its two private subcomponents `ActivationProgress.tsx`, `AIActivationTransition.tsx`) — computed fabricated readiness/completion scores from string-length arithmetic, shipped hardcoded fake evidence templates, disabled "Create Project" behind a PMO-first tooltip.
- `src/app/api/getting-started/route.ts` — persisted the fake templates as real `operational_memory` rows, had a `loadDemo` fictional-project seeding branch, wrote the forbidden `onboarding_completed` boolean.
- `src/app/api/onboarding/route.ts` — a second, entirely dead (zero callers) route that wrote the same forbidden flag.

`/workspace/setup`, `/getting-started`, `/onboarding` remain registered protected routes (so bookmarks don't 404) but now render nothing — each redirects to the real, currently-derived canonical destination via a shared helper (`src/lib/auth/legacy-onboarding-redirect.ts`), never a hardcoded legacy route.

## Routing-layer gate removed

The decision brief's independent verification (§5/§11) found the wizard's disabled button was the *weaker* instance of PMF-002 — the real, undocumented gate lived in `resolveOnboardingState`, which checked `pmos` **before** `projects`, and in Edge middleware (`proxy.ts`), which enforced this via a stale JWT `onboarding_completed` boolean claim *before* the DB-derived resolver ever ran.

- Edge middleware makes **no** onboarding-state decision anymore — `(protected)/layout.tsx` (DB-derived) is the *sole* redirect authority.
- `resolveOnboardingStateFromJwt` (the boolean-authority shortcut) is deleted outright.

## Correction pass — state authority reconciliation

Product review correctly identified that the routing authority (`resolveOnboardingState`) and the PR #547 evidence-derived `workspace-activation` engine (`src/lib/workspace-activation/*`) had overlapping, unreconciled semantics: the engine already computed `execution_started` and richer stages for the checklist UI, but routing never consulted it and instead returned `active` as soon as any Project existed.

**Fix — one evidence source, not two machines:**

- `resolveOnboardingState` now calls `collectWorkspaceActivationEvidence` (the PR #547 engine's own evidence collector) directly for `projectExists`/`taskExists`/`pmoExists`, instead of running its own separate queries. `evaluate-workspace-activation.ts`/`activation-rules.ts` are **unmodified** — zero risk to the canonical, heavily-tested checklist engine.
- `OnboardingState` gains `needs_task` and `execution_started`, reusing the engine's own vocabulary (`execution_started` is the literal `deriveActivationStage` already returns for that evidence shape) rather than inventing new terms.
- `active` now strictly means **Command Center is active** (a real, PMF-004-backed `pmos` row exists) — independent of task existence, since `activateContextAction` can create a Project + PMO together without a task ever existing first.
- Two boolean *views* over the one state, not two machines: `isOnboardingComplete` (true only for `active`) drives post-auth landing; `hasWorkspaceAccess` (true for `needs_task`/`execution_started`/`active` alike) drives the persistent route gate — preserving "a Project may exist before Command Center activation" (ADR-PMF-006) without re-gating the whole app behind full activation.
- `needs_task`/`execution_started`/`active` all redirect to `/command-center` — the same surface that already hosts the evidence-derived first-task and activation CTAs (`WorkspaceOnboardingPanel`/`CommandCenterEmptyState`, unchanged). States remain distinct in the `OnboardingState` value itself; only the destination is shared, which is the explicitly-permitted design.
- **Login/signup session-visibility investigation:** `signup/actions.ts` and `api/login/route.ts` previously called `getAuthUser()` (cookie-backed) immediately after sign-up/sign-in to resolve the post-auth destination — a real assumption about same-request cookie propagation. Rather than trying to prove that assumption (not achievable in this sandbox), it was **eliminated**: both flows now build identity directly from `data.user` (the sign-in/sign-up response itself), and `resolveOnboardingState`'s parameter type was narrowed to the minimal `{id, email}` it actually needs — no cookie read anywhere in this call chain.

Full detail, before/after comparison, and pre-correction failure evidence in `docs/audits/remediation/pmf-001-002-canonical-onboarding-honest-activation.md` §21.

author: ranhassid17
body:
Phase 5 of [`PLAN.md`](../blob/master/PLAN.md). FunnelIQ is now usable by a person rather than by `curl`.

## The security shape

The browser holds **only** the public anon key and the session token Supabase issued it. The API verifies that token server-side and keeps the service-role key.

`/api/config` serves the public values **from the environment at runtime**, so no key is committed to the repo. There's a test asserting the service-role key can never appear in that response — leaking it would make Row Level Security decoration, since it bypasses RLS entirely.

## Session handling — the part the brief grades

- A logged-out visitor is redirected to `/` **before any panel renders**
- `onAuthStateChange` drops the user back if the session ends, rather than firing doomed requests
- Sign-out clears the session and returns to the login screen
- A page refresh preserves the session (supabase-js persists it)

## Panels

Every work package, plus one that isn't in the brief:

| Panel | Package |
|---|---|
| Campaign lifetime | 2 |
| Upsell likelihood | 3 |
| Super-customer score (0–100 gauge) | 4 |
| Follow-up dropout (bar chart, best/worst highlighted) | 5 |
| Pre-launch profit + budget simulator | 6 |
| Campaign comparison | spec-required |
| **Models in service** | — |

That last one shows each model **beside its naive baseline**, tagged `beats baseline` or `ties baseline`. The two targets where boosting only ties are visible **in the product**, not buried in a report. If the tool tells you it's using a group mean, that's the honest thing for it to say.

The budget table flags extrapolated scenarios and greys their numbers — 1 × ₪50,000 renders as `extrapolated` and is excluded from the recommendation.

## Choices worth noting

**Hand-written, no build step.** The surface is small, and one dependency-free stylesheet is easier to audit for the thing that matters: that no privileged credential reaches the client.

**Every label says CAMPAIGN.** One row is one advertising campaign, so a customer-level reading of any number on this page would be a category error. Each prediction response carries that caveat inline.

**Static mounts last**, so API routes and probes resolve first.

## Verification

Against live Supabase:

```
GET /                 200  <title>Sign in · FunnelIQ</title>
GET /dashboard.html   200  <title>Dashboard · FunnelIQ</title>
GET /static/app.js    200
GET /api/config       url ok · anon key 208 chars · service key present: False
GET /api/campaigns    401  (still gated)
```

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` → clean
- `pytest -q` → **110 passed** (was 107)

## Not verified

I have not driven the login flow in a real browser — that needs a user account in your Supabase project, which I'm not creating without your say-so. The **Create account** button on the login screen does it self-serve.

author: delivstat
body:
## Bug

A pipeline could not receive an input payload. `swarmkit pipeline emit` (and `POST /pipelines/signal`) enqueue `{"kind":"start",…,"input":…}`, but the controller's `_start` read only `graph` + `tag` and **dropped `input`** — `SagaState` had no field for it. The run-stage seam then built every stage's input purely from prior artifacts, so the **first stage always ran on an empty string** and the payload never reached the pipeline. A pipeline is expected to be driven by an incoming payload (a requirement, a webhook body, a document handle); losing it is a correctness bug.

## Fix (runtime 1.120.0)

- `SagaState.input` — persisted (new `pipeline_saga.input` column; threaded through `create()` on the `SagaStore` protocol + both `InMemorySagaStore` and `SqlSagaStore`; survives restarts).
- `_start` stores the start event's `input`.
- Run-stage seam (`_stage_input`): the **first** stage is seeded with `saga.input`; **downstream** stages thread the prior artifacts as before. The `correlation_id` stays available (it's the run's `thread_id`), so a pure "fetch by correlation id" stage still works.
- `GET /pipelines/sagas/{id}` returns `input` so the CLI/UI can show what seeded a run.

The orchestrator stays content-free — it threads only the opaque `input` string + artifact references.

## Tests
- `test_first_stage_is_seeded_with_the_pipeline_input_payload`
- `test_downstream_stage_uses_upstream_artifact_not_the_input`
- `test_start_event_input_is_persisted_on_the_saga` (round-trips a fresh `SqlSagaStore`)
- Full runtime suite green (1577 passed); ruff + mypy clean.

## Deferred
Downstream selection is still "all prior artifacts". A per-stage `consumes` declaration (which upstream artifact(s), and whether to re-read the payload) with ordered selection is the follow-up — documented in the design note.

Design note updated with a "Fix: pipeline input payload (was dropped)" section.

## What

## Why

The statement justified the finding on execute-path grounds and noted *"no upstream fix available (affects nltk <= 3.9.4)"*. That is now stale:

A container re-scan therefore sees the patched version and no longer flags CVE-2026-54293, so the `not_affected` exception is no longer needed. `nltk` is added to the header's "fully remediated / intentionally excluded" note for the record.

body:
## 이메일 전수조사 결과

라이브 export **2,000행**(활성·tier1 우선) 실측.

### 품질은 문제 없습니다

| 검사 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 형식 오류 | **0** |
| 마스킹(`*`) | **0** |
| 플레이스홀더(example/wix/sentry) | **0** |
| 뉴스룸 계정(press@ 등) | **0** |
| 중복 이메일 | **0** |

역할계정(`info@` 등) 22.4%는 B2B 접촉엔 오히려 적합하고, 개인 웹메일 38.8%는 소상공인 대행사 특성상 정상입니다.

**⇒ 문제는 품질이 아니라 양입니다** — 이메일 2.5% / 전화 99.4% / 사이트 15.5%.

### 이메일은 오직 사이트 크롤에서만 나옵니다

**"사이트 없이 이메일만 있는 행 = 0"**. 즉 사이트를 못 찾으면 이메일은 구조적으로 0입니다.

- 사이트 310 → 이메일 49 = **크롤 전환율 15.8%**
- `local`(지도): 사이트 13.7% / 이메일 **1.0%**
- `webkr`(웹문서): 사이트 100% / 이메일 **69.0%**

## 결함 — 크롤 예산의 22.9%가 못 여는 문에 쓰이고 있었습니다

사이트 보유 행의 **22.9%**가 `instagram` · `blog.naver` · `cafe.naver` · `youtube` · `facebook` · `pf.kakao` · `soomgo` 같은 **플랫폼 URL**입니다. 크롤해도 업체 이메일이 나올 수 없습니다.

보강 레인은 `realSite()`로 걸렀지만 그게 **`enrich-lane` 내부 클로저**라 수집 레인은 같은 판정을 쓸 수 없었고, `website IS NOT NULL`로만 뽑아 그대로 크롤했습니다.

`LIMIT 15`라서 **진짜 사이트가 슬롯을 뺏깁니다** — 예산과 슬롯 이중 낭비입니다.

## 수정

`realSite` + `PLATFORM_URL_SQL_EXCLUDE`를 `contact-enrich` **SSOT로 승격**(enrich-lane의 로컬 정의 제거, 동작 동일) → 수집 레인은 SQL 선정 단계에서 제외 + JS 최종 판정(서브도메인 변종 차단).

## 자동수집 영구성 — 구조적으로 안전 확인

- 게이트 ON: `collect` / `storeinfo` / `commerce` / `localdata` / `nps`
- cron 매시간
- **lease는 5분 TTL** — 크래시로 해제를 못 해도 자동 만료됩니다(영구 잠김 불가)

⚠️ 단 `collect` 레인이 17:00 회차를 건너뛴 흔적이 있습니다(15:01 → 다음 없음). 오늘 배포가 3회 겹친 구간이라 배포 블립일 가능성이 크지만, 다음 세션이 한 번 더 확인해야 합니다.

## 🔴 제가 틀렸던 것 정정 — 서브리퀘스트 천장은 50~63이 맞습니다

앞서 *"수집 레인이 예산 110으로 80회 성공했으니 천장은 110보다 높다"*고 했는데 **틀렸습니다.**

그 레인은 fetch 오류를 `.catch(() => null)`로 삼켜서 **한도를 넘어도 조용히 빈 결과**가 됐을 뿐입니다 — 바로 그 blindness를 #816에서 고쳤습니다. 근거 자체가 무효였습니다.

실측이 답을 줬습니다: 보강 레인 학습 상한이 63 → **50**으로 내려갔습니다(`budget_total: 50`). 이는 백오프 `floor(spent*0.8)`가 발동했다는 뜻 = **실제로 한도를 맞았습니다.** CLAUDE.md의 "무료 = 50" 기술이 대략 맞습니다.

다만 **#813 덕에 `processed`가 5 → 10으로 2배**가 됐습니다(회복이 풀려 캡이 63까지 올라간 구간의 효과). 앞으로 캡은 50↔63 대역에서 진동하며 진짜 천장을 스스로 측정합니다.

**⇒ 유료 전환($5/월) 판단 근거가 이제 실측으로 섰습니다** — 건당 비용을 더 줄이거나, 유료로 한도를 올리거나.

## 검증

- `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` → **0 에러**
- `npx vitest run` → **214 files / 2,808 tests pass**
- 크롤쿨다운 / 캡레인격리 / sql bind·column 가드 → GREEN

author: nedtwigg
body:
## Why

WATCHING was a per-Session toggle, so the bell had to be re-enabled on every new pane running the same program. But the thing you want to be alerted about is a *program* — `claude`, a test runner, a build — not a particular tab.

## What changed

**WATCHING is now a property of the command.** You keep an app-global, persisted set of watched command names; a Session runs the output/silence monitor exactly while its foreground command's first word is in that set. Enable it while `claude` runs and every `claude` pane watches, now and later; turn it off anywhere and the rule is gone everywhere. There is no per-Session enable and no per-Session mute, so `PersistedAlertState.watchingEnabled` is gone too.

With nothing running there is no rule to key on, so the bell changes nothing and opens the alert dialog to say so. The dialog gained the per-command rule switch plus a list of every watched command with a remove control — the only place a rule set on a since-closed pane can be found.

### Two behaviors this forced

- **A ring must outlive its monitor.** Watching switches off the instant the watched command exits, usually the same instant the ring was raised, so the WATCHING ring moved out of `ActivityMonitor` into the entry. Removing a *rule* still silences the ring; a command merely ending does not.
- **WATCHING now outranks `COMMAND_EXIT_ARMED`** in the status projection. A watched command is by definition running, so the old precedence would have masked the monitor's busy/quiet states for the whole run.

### Simplification

`alert-manager.ts` 719 → 596 lines, `alert.md` 283 → 201, while both gained the new model. Deleted: the duplicated bell transition table (one copy now, in the renderer), `AlertManager.dismissOrToggleAlert`, `toggleAlert`/`disableAlert`, two platform methods net, and the legacy watching-status inference in `seed()`. `startCommandExitWatch` and the terminal-state reducer now share one `resolveCommandStart`.

### Playground fake shell

`TutorialShell` never reported command boundaries, so no playground pane had a command to key on — including the pane hosting the tutorial that teaches the feature. It now emits the same `OSC 633` sequences a real integrated shell does (`A`/`B` around the prompt, `E` + `C` on launch, `D` on exit). Every pane reports its program, so the bell works everywhere.

## Known limitation

WATCHING needs a shell that reports command boundaries, so `cmd.exe`, `fish`, and any shell where integration injection did not take no longer get it. Routing the renderer-side keystroke fallback into the manager would buy those shells a worse version of the feature at the cost of a second command-tracking path. Stated plainly in `alert.md` rather than left implicit.

## Tutorial

The desktop alert section was rebuilt around the new model (6 steps → 9, adding the rule spreading across panes plus the two tracks that had no coverage before). **It is knowingly in a middling state** — it teaches the mechanics but not the attention model, which is the actual idea. `TUTORIAL_MOCKUP.md` is a working draft for that rework; it lands in a follow-up PR.

## Verification

`pnpm test` (1280 tests), `pnpm lint:specs`, and `build:vscode` all pass. Driven end-to-end in the desktop playground: one bell click lights every pane running that command; the dialog shows the rule switch and removable rule list; the ring fires on silence and leaves a TODO; `OSC 777` and command-exit both ring without a rule; the bell at a prompt opens the "nothing is running" dialog and creates nothing.

Not exercised by hand: VS Code (the one host where `AlertManager` is cross-process and the rule set arrives by `postMessage`) and a real integrated shell in standalone.

author: shibaji7
body:
## Summary

The coverage-omit block had grown to **18 entries**, most of them pure \`raise NotImplementedYetError\` stubs. Those are already handled by the line-level rule in \`[tool.coverage.report]\`:

\`\`\`toml
exclude_lines = [
    "raise NotImplementedYetError",
    ...
]
\`\`\`

so the file-level omission was **redundant**. Worse, it created a maintenance chore — every time a stub grew into real code, the maintainer had to remember to remove the file from the omit list or the new code would silently escape measurement.

## Changes

- **Trim the omit block from 18 to 3 entries.** Kept only:
  - \`_version.py\` — trivially uninteresting (version literal),
  - \`earth/unstructured_3d.py\` — will grow into real physics in stages,
  - \`solver/sparse.py\` — same story.
- **Raise \`fail_under\` from 75 → 80 %.** Measured coverage after the cleanup + smoke-import test lands at **89.19 %**, so 80 % leaves ~9 % headroom.
- **Add \`tests/unit/test_smoke_imports.py\`.** Two tests:
  - \`test_every_submodule_imports\` — walks every submodule via \`pkgutil.walk_packages\` and imports it. Catches import-time regressions (a stub with a broken import would sit undetected until first call).
  - \`test_walk_finds_expected_families\` — sanity-check the walker reaches every top-level family.

The smoke test does double duty: it defends against import breakage AND exercises the stub-file import lines that were previously masked by the omit block, keeping overall coverage healthy after the trim.

## Coverage delta

| | Baseline (\`main\`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage | 84.57 % | **89.19 %** |
| \`fail_under\` gate | 75 % | **80 %** |
| Passing tests | 117 | 119 (+2 smoke) |

## Rationale for keeping the three omit entries

- **\`_version.py\`** — one-line version string. Nothing to cover.
- **\`earth/unstructured_3d.py\`** — reserved API for a full FD MT solver. Real implementation will land over multiple PRs; partial coverage during that development would fluctuate wildly and either mask real gaps or noise up the report.
- **\`solver/sparse.py\`** — same story for sparse-solver plumbing.

Everything else (all the pure-stub \`raise NotImplementedYetError\` files) is now under the line-level exclude and gets its import lines counted by the smoke test.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pytest tests/unit/test_smoke_imports.py -v\` — 2/2 pass
- [x] \`pytest --cov=src/geopulse --cov-report=term\` — 119 pass, 89.19 % coverage, fail_under=80 % gate satisfied
- [x] Reviewer: nothing behavioural changed; the only risk is that some CI job pins on the exact old \`fail_under\` value or the exact omit list — quick grep of \`.github/workflows/\` confirms no such pin

## No conflicts

Only \`pyproject.toml\` is touched, in a small region (the coverage block). Merges cleanly against every other open PR (they all edit different lines in the coverage-omit block; when this lands and shortens that block, their omit-list edits become obsolete no-ops — trivial to resolve).

author: automateip
body:
## Summary
- Raise the transitive `mcp` (Python MCP SDK) floor to `>=1.28.1,<2` via `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies` in `pyproject.toml`, resolving `mcp` from `1.26.0` to `1.29.0`. Fixes 3 high-severity `mcp` SDK advisories.
- `mcp` is a transitive dependency pulled in via `fastmcp`/`fastmcp-slim`, which only floors `mcp>=1.24.0` - so the earlier `fastmcp>=3.4.1` bump (#369) didn't lift it on its own. This PR adds the targeted constraint needed, following the same floor+ceiling pattern already used for `cryptography`.
- The `<2` ceiling explicitly excludes `mcp 2.0.0` (a same-day major redesign, released the same day this constraint was added) - out of scope for this CVE fix.
- `starlette` (`1.3.1`) and `fastmcp`/`fastmcp-slim` (`3.4.4`) are unchanged. No other package in `uv.lock` drifted. No `.py` files changed.

## Why this needed extra scrutiny
`mcp` v1.27.1 modified output-schema generation code ("catch PydanticUserError when generating output schema, pydantic 2.13 compat") - this touches the exact code path that broke `trigger_automation`/`start_workflow`'s union return type (`StartWorkflowResponse | StartAgentResponse`) in a prior real incident (#356/#361, where a live platform run - not unit tests - caught the bug). This bump was treated with the same rigor as that incident's lesson demands.

## Test plan
- [x] `make ci` - 2519 passed, 99% coverage held, bandit 0 issues
- [x] Confirmed resolved versions: `mcp==1.29.0` (not `2.0.0`), `starlette==1.3.1` and `fastmcp==3.4.4`/`fastmcp-slim==3.4.4` unchanged, no other package drifted
- [x] Statically inspected the raw generated `output_schema` JSON for `trigger_automation`/`start_workflow` - confirmed structurally correct `anyOf` union with proper `$defs`, no leaked raw type, no `PydanticUserError`
- [x] Ran the full test suite with `-W error::DeprecationWarning` to confirm no new WebSocket/wsproto deprecation warnings (mcp 1.28.0 added these) - clean pass, not masked by repo's `filterwarnings` config
- [x] **Live integration test** against `itential-se-poc-dev01.trial.itential.io`: clean server startup, all 68 tools/13 service plugins registered with no schema-generation exceptions. Triggered a real workflow automation end-to-end - valid `StartWorkflowResponse` returned, followed by a successful `describe_job`. Confirmed identical shape/success against `devel` HEAD (pre-bump, `mcp==1.26.0`) via a worktree comparison for the same payload.

### Known gap in this testing (not a regression, tracked separately)
Could not live-verify the `StartAgentResponse` branch of the union - all 3 agent-type automation routes tried on this platform returned a live `400 Bad Request`, even with well-formed, schema-matching payloads. Confirmed via the same `devel`-HEAD worktree comparison that this 400 is **pre-existing and unrelated to this bump** (identical failure with `mcp==1.26.0`). The schema-generation risk this PR was actually flagged for is a static, at-registration-time property of the union type, and was verified two ways (static schema inspection covering both branches + a clean live registration of all tools with zero exceptions), so this gap doesn't block the fix itself. Root cause of the 400s is untriaged and tracked as its own follow-up.

author: frivonikoma
body:
## What this PR adds

Builds on #362. Two things: (1) a second signaling module (**AMPK**) run through the same
three-control pipeline, and (2) a **phylogenetically-controlled, strategy-stratified redesign** of the
long-lived-vs-short-lived contrast, applied to both the AMPK and SIRT6 panels. All result docs are
marked as technical checkpoints, not validated biological claims.

### 1. Species-panel expansion (`config.py`)

`SPECIES_REGISTRY` grows from 11 to 33 target species, grouped for a convergent-divergent design via
three name lists (`_BMAL_NAMES` / `_ELLSM_NAMES` / `_REFERENCE_NAMES`) and derived
`BMAL_SPECIES` / `ELLSM_SPECIES` / `REFERENCE_GROUP_SPECIES`:

- **ELLSM** (extremely long-lived small mammals): 3 independent mole-rat lineages + 2 independent bat
  lineages (*Myotis*, *Rhinolophus*).
- **BMAL** (body-mass-associated long-lived): elephant + whales (blue/sperm/beluga) + white rhino —
  the first large-bodied stratum with real ortholog coverage in this project.
- **Reference**: 12 phylogenetically broad "typical lifespan-for-size" species (primates, rodents,
  carnivores, ungulate, eulipotyphlan, marsupial).

Categories keep existing `LONG_LIVED`/`SHORT_LIVED` machinery working (BMAL/ELLSM → `LONG_LIVED`,
reference-typical → `SHORT_LIVED`); the analysis grouping is by the `*_NAMES` lists. Species without
ortholog coverage simply drop out at scoping. No change to default command behavior; full test suite
(2078) and mypy pass.

### 2. Results

**Motivation.** Recent comparative work argues mammalian longevity is *convergent via divergent
strategies*: ELLSM show intensified selection for cellular maintenance / DNA repair; BMAL show
genome-wide relaxed selection with constraint on cell-cycle & DNA-repair, with limited overlap.
If true, **pooling all long-lived species cancels signal** — motivating stratified contrasts
(ELLSM-vs-Reference, BMAL-vs-Reference, BMAL-vs-ELLSM) against a phylogenetically broad reference.

**AMPK module (energy sensing).**
- Pooled 5×4: 0/30 interfaces survive BH-FDR. One lead — AMPKα2–β1 (`5iso`) — passed nominal
  significance *and* clean raw convergence but **collapsed under NEGATOME** (a clean demonstration of
  why that control is load-bearing).
- Stratified (5 BMAL × 5 ELLSM × 12 Reference): **0/28, 0/29, 0/27** survive FDR. The 12-species
  phylo-broad reference **dissolves the 5iso lead** (p 0.029 → 0.078), confirming it tracked rodent
  phylogeny — the design working as intended.

**SIRT6 module (DNA repair) — the decisive test.** This is the pathway where the model predicts an
ELLSM-specific signal. Stratified **ELLSM-vs-Reference is null: 0/25 FDR** (min q = 0.34); BMAL-vs-Ref
0/25; BMAL-vs-ELLSM 0/25 (min q = 0.099). The predicted positive does not appear.

**Bottom line.** Two pathways × two designs × three controls → robust panel-wide nulls. The
interface-divergence hypothesis is not supported. The negative **localizes to the method**: per-residue
ESM-embedding L2 divergence at a PPI interface is a different quantity than the lineage-specific
selection intensity (dN/dS-type) those comparative studies detect, and does not capture it at this
panel size. The one persistent crumb across all designs is **Ku80/8ag5**, nominally long-ward every
time but never surviving FDR or convergence — a candidate for an orthogonal (site-level dN/dS) look,
not a hit here.

Method validation holds throughout: hundreds of (interface, species) rows show significant interface
localization (BH q < 0.05) and the shuffled-mask control sits at ≈ 1.00 — the nulls are not
power/artifact failures.

### Result docs

- `docs/results/2026-07-28-ampk-module-5x4/` — AMPK pooled 5×4 (lead rescued by NEGATOME).
- `docs/results/2026-07-28-ampk-convergent-divergent-stratified/` — AMPK stratified (lead dissolves).
- `docs/results/2026-07-28-sirt6-convergent-divergent-stratified/` — SIRT6 stratified (decisive null).

### Reproduce

```bash
# AMPK
uv run select --candidate-set ampk_pilot --count 20
uv run orthologs && uv run embed && uv run analyze
# SIRT6
uv run select --candidate-set sirt6_dna_repair --count 20
uv run orthologs && uv run embed && uv run analyze
```

Stratified contrasts + BH-FDR + convergence are computed from `data/output/enrichment.parquet` over
the ELLSM / BMAL / Reference groups defined in `config.py`.

### Notes for reviewers

- No change to default behavior; `data/output/*` and `data/interim/*` remain gitignored — only the

author: allens
body:
Surfaced by a real backup logging this mid-run:

```
@smithy/node-http-handler - [WARN] a request has exceeded the configured 30000 ms requestTimeout.
Init client requestHandler with throwOnRequestTimeout=true to turn this into an error.
```

Chasing the warning turned up the bigger problem underneath it.

## The hang fix never worked

[ADR-0065](https://github.com/allens/s3cab/blob/main/docs/adr/0065-s3-client-request-timeouts.md)
set `requestTimeout: 30_000` on the S3 client and described it as a socket **inactivity** limit.
It isn't one. `@smithy/node-http-handler` has three distinct options:

| Option | What it actually does |
| --- | --- |
| `socketTimeout` | Idle limit. Destroys the request, rejects with `TimeoutError`. **What we wanted.** |
| `requestTimeout` | Cap on **total** request duration. **Logs a warning and lets the request continue**, unless `throwOnRequestTimeout` is also set. |
| `connectionTimeout` | Connect phase only. |

We set `requestTimeout` and `connectionTimeout`, and never `socketTimeout`. So there was **no idle
timeout at all**, and the one thing we did set only warned. The infinite hang ADR-0065 was written
to kill has been fully live the whole time — a backup that loses its network mid-upload still
parks forever.

The warning above is the second symptom: because it caps *total* duration, any object legitimately
taking over 30 s on a slow uplink trips it, printing straight to the console mid-backup, past
s3cab's own output discipline (ADR-0010).

Upstream names the trap in its own type docs — *"because `requestTimeout` was for a long time
incorrectly being set as a socket idle timeout, users must also opt-in for request timeout thrown
errors"* (`@smithy/types`, `NodeHttpHandlerOptions`). It once **was** the idle timeout; the rename
left the old name meaning something else.

**`throwOnRequestTimeout: true` is rejected as the fix.** It would make the second symptom fatal —
failing a perfectly healthy large upload for the crime of being slow, the opposite of the goal.
Only `socketTimeout` distinguishes "slow" from "dead".

## The test is replaced, not adjusted

The old assertion was *"both timeouts are set and non-zero"* — which is exactly **how this shipped
green**. `requestTimeout` was non-zero throughout and never broke a single hang. A value-shaped
assertion can't notice that an option's *meaning* changed underneath it.

It now points the real client at a loopback server that accepts a request and then goes silent,
and asserts a `TimeoutError` arrives instead of a hang. Crucially it builds that client from
`clientConfig()`'s own handler **keys**, shortening only the durations — so a revert to
`requestTimeout` fails here rather than in someone's backup. Verified by doing exactly that:

```
✖ fails a silent connection instead of hanging on it (5014ms)
  AssertionError: a silent connection must raise a TimeoutError, not hang
  actual: Error: the request hung: no idle timeout ever fired
```

With the fix it rejects in ~530 ms. Loopback only — no bucket, no network, so it sits in the unit
tier.

`connectionTimeout` keeps a value-only assertion: a connect that never completes needs a blackholed
address, which isn't hermetic. Noted in the test.

## Also

ADR-0065 gets a Correction section rather than a quiet edit — the original Decision was wrong, and
the reasoning that produced it ("any bounded non-zero value achieves it") is worth leaving visible
next to what it missed.

Gate clean locally: `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, 734 tests.

author: tylercschneider
body:
## Context

`event_engine` does not define events — `event_engine-event_definition` does. The runtime only ever consumes a compiled catalog. But the class holding a parsed catalog entry was named `EventEngine::EventDefinition::Schema` and lived at `lib/event_engine/event_definition.rb`, borrowing authoring vocabulary for a runtime object.

That name was not merely misleading, it was load-bearing in the worst way: **both gems shipped `lib/event_engine/event_definition.rb`**. In any host using both, the definition gem won `$LOAD_PATH` and `event_engine`'s copy never loaded. `EventDefinition::Schema` in `EventSchemaJsonLoader` silently resolved to the definition gem's `Schemas::Schema` instead.

Verified in a scratch Rails app before this change:

```
loaded:  event_engine-event_definition/lib/event_engine/event_definition.rb
Schema:  EventEngine::EventDefinition::Schemas::Schema
```

`event_engine`'s own suite never saw this, because it does not install the definition gem — so it only ever exercised the branch where its own class wins.

## What changed

- `EventEngine::EventDefinition::Schema` → `EventEngine::CatalogEntry`
- `lib/event_engine/event_definition.rb` → `lib/event_engine/catalog_entry.rb`
- Call site in `EventSchemaJsonLoader` and all test references updated

Nothing named `event_definition` remains in `event_engine`.

## Verification

Pure rename — no behaviour change. Suite green: 129 runs, 167 assertions, 0 failures.

Confirmed in a scratch Rails app with both gems installed:

```
collides on event_definition.rb? false
CatalogEntry owner:  event_engine/lib/event_engine/catalog_entry.rb
loader builds:       EventEngine::CatalogEntry
```

## Note on size

38 files, but 36 are mechanical test updates of the constant name. A rename cannot be split — a partially renamed constant does not load. Size exception agreed in advance.

## Follow-up

`process_type` is retained as a member here to keep this PR behaviour-neutral. It should be dropped once #245 lands, since the rules file then owns that decision and nothing reads it off the entry.

author: gaoflow
body:
A `string` equal to a null token (`~`, `null`, `Null`, `NULL`) is emitted as a plain scalar, so it deserializes back to `null` even when the target is `string` — the serializer emits output its own deserializer reads as a different type (#493).

```csharp
var s = new SerializerBuilder().Build();
var d = new DeserializerBuilder().Build();
d.Deserialize<string>(s.Serialize("null")); // returns null, not "null"
```

`TypeAssigningEventEmitter` now quotes a string scalar whose plain form matches the exact set `NullNodeDeserializer` treats as null, so it round-trips. Only that set is quoted — `nUll`/`nullish` stay plain — and actual nulls are unaffected (still emit bare `null`). It is the same set `WithQuotingNecessaryStrings` already quotes, applied unconditionally for the null tokens because, unlike bool/number look-alikes, they lose data even for a `string` target.

Tested: the four tokens round-trip as scalars and dictionary values, look-alikes stay unquoted, and real null still emits bare.

author: dmnyc
body:
## Summary
The Following count on a profile showed **0** on every visit and filled in a moment later — and sometimes stayed at 0 for good. Two separate defects produced the same symptom.

**Shows 0, then fills in.** `ProfileViewModel.start()` already reads `FollowsCache` to decide `youFollow`, but left `followingCount` at its `0` default until the kind-3 relay query returned. `ProfileView.statRow` renders that value directly, so the stat read as a fresh load of the follow list rather than a cached value updating quietly. It's now seeded from that same cache read, and `loadContacts` overwrites it when the relay copy lands.

Only the count is primed — deliberately not `followingPubkeys`. That array gates whether `loadFollowingProfiles` re-fetches contacts, so priming it would let the Following *tab* render a stale cached list and mark itself loaded without ever consulting a relay.

**Sticks at 0.** `loadContacts` races `loadTargetWriteRelays` inside the same task group, but builds its relay set via `queryRelays()`, which folds in `targetWriteRelays` — still empty at that point. For a profile whose kind-3 lives only on its author's own write relays, that first attempt searches the wrong servers and finds nothing. Nothing ever re-runs it: `start()` is one-shot behind `hasStarted`, and the header has no pull-to-refresh. So the count stayed at 0 for the life of the screen.

It now retries once the write relays are known. Kept concurrent rather than serialized — awaiting the kind-10002 lookup up front would delay the entire header by up to its 8s timeout, trading a wrong count for a slow screen. The retry is guarded on `followingPubkeys.isEmpty`, so it's a no-op whenever the first attempt succeeded.

## Test plan
- [x] Builds clean on Simulator
- [x] Verified on Simulator: Following renders `1.1k` at t+300ms and is unchanged at every sample through t+17s — no 0, no visible fill-in
- [ ] Open a profile that previously stuck at 0 (kind-3 published only to the author's own write relays) and confirm the retry resolves it
- [ ] Open the Following tab and confirm it still lists the full set — the tab must fetch from a relay, not render the seeded cache

## Notes
Scope is the **Following** count. **Followers** is a remote-only count via `NostrArchivesClient` with an `∞` placeholder and no local cache to seed from, so it still populates on load; giving it the same treatment would need a new persistence layer rather than a one-line seed.

author: jeremydmiller
body:
Closes #3680.

## The "flake" was real durable message loss

`DurableReceiver.ProcessReceivedMessagesAsync` checked `_latched` **before** calling `Envelope.MarkReceived`. The latched branch then persists each envelope to the durable inbox as a safety net — but on an envelope that never went through `MarkReceived`, `Status` is still the enum default (`Outgoing`, the first member of `EnvelopeStatus`) and `Destination` is null.

Both are filter columns for inbox recovery:

- `CheckRecoverableIncomingMessagesOperation` selects `where status = 'Incoming'`
- `LoadPageOfGloballyOwnedIncomingAsync` selects on `received_at` (= `Destination`)

so the rows were written in a state **no recovery sweep on any node can ever see**. A null `Listener` also made the latched branch skip its `Listener.DeferAsync` nack, so the broker copy was not requeued either — and when the listener restarted, the broker's redelivery hit `DuplicateIncomingEnvelopeException`, which acks and drops.

Net result: genuine message loss under a *durable* inbox any time a circuit breaker trip latches the receiver mid-flight.

## Evidence

Log reading dead-ended (zero `[Error]` lines; zero "Issuing a command to recover" lines across 358 durability sweeps — the rows were invisible to the query). What settled it was gating `TeardownResources()` behind an env var and querying the leftover schema directly:

```
before:  1191 rows Handled + 9 rows status='Outgoing', received_at=NULL   test times out at 3m
after:   1200 rows Handled, 0 orphans                                     test passes in 16.5s
```

Reproduced 3/3 runs locally on `durable_and_not_parallel.the_circuit_breaker_should_trip_and_restart`. Note that #3680's premise that this only fails on CI was wrong — it fails locally on the first run.

## Changes

- **Move the `MarkReceived` loop above the `_latched` check** in `ProcessReceivedMessagesAsync`, so the safety-net row is written as a recoverable `Incoming` row addressed to the listener. This is the fix.
- Defense in depth in `receiveOneAsync`'s latched branch: never persist an inbox row with a default `Outgoing` status or a null `Destination`.
- `RecoverIncomingMessagesCommand` / `ListenerInboxRecovery` both reassign rows to this node and *then* hand them to the listener. A failed hand-off (the agent nulls its receiver on a circuit trip) left the rows owned by a live node, which only orphan-release-for-a-dead-node would ever undo. Release them back to any node so a later sweep retries. **This one is a hazard found by inspection in the same code path, not the observed root cause above.**
- Un-skips the test that #3680 disabled.

## Verification

Full `CircuitBreakingTests` suite (the `CICircuitBreaking` CI job): **24/24 passed, 0 skipped**, 3.5 min, net9.0.

This is the second time a "flake" in this test has turned out to be genuine message loss (after #3137) — which is a good argument for never tuning its timeout.

author: spectraqc
body:
## Summary
Of the 601 unsourced assertions the audit found, 427 (8 profiles) have no source document in the corpus at all and are fully blocked on SQC-1936. The other 174 (8 profiles) had a real, locatable source document — this PR reconciles those, plus r128_audio (a 9th profile added after the original audit, also had a real source: EBU R128 itself).

Every field was resolved by actually reading the cited source PDF (Dropbox `Broadcast/Specs` + `Broadcast/Standards` corpus), never by guessing:
- **Literally stated** → `method:"literal"`, exact quote recorded.
- **Cites an external standard by name without restating the number** (e.g. "per EBU R103") → `method:"model"`, noted as such.
- **Reasonably derivable from stated facts** (e.g. duration tolerance = one video frame at the document's own stated frame rate) → `method:"model"`, flagged for human review.
- **Structural/self-referential** (`id`, `name`, `structure.type` describing UMDP's own modeling) → `method:"model"`, `source:"n/a"`, honest note.
- **Genuinely untraceable** → the field is **removed** from the profile, never guessed. UMDP already models absence; omitting a field is legal, asserting an unsupported one is not.
- **Actually contradicted by the source** → corrected in the profile and recorded `state:"contradicted"` — but only when confident. A few genuinely ambiguous contradictions (see below) are flagged in commit messages rather than silently "corrected."

**9 of 17 profiles now pass `tools/validate.py`'s SQC-1947 gate** (up from 1 — `clearcast_commercials` was already done in a prior commit on this branch). The remaining 8 are the SQC-1936-blocked set and are unchanged.

**Real defect found and fixed**: `rte_hd` is the profile SQC-1946 was filed over, citing two known timecode errors as the motivating example (`bars_start` off by 90s, `black_start` off by 2 frames). Found and corrected both, plus two more in the same section (`bars_duration_seconds` was attached to the wrong table row; `sync_plop_window`'s end time was off by a frame). This is the system working exactly as intended.

**Confirmed suspicion**: `dpp_uk_hd` and `bbc_uhd_x1` both had a block of `assets.video.quality.*` / `assets.audio.quality.*` fields (blockiness, dead-pixel count, ghosting, etc.) that read like SpectraQC's own internal QC-engine thresholds rather than broadcaster-spec values. Confirmed against the actual DPP/BBC/AMWA documents — they only make qualitative statements, never these specific numeric thresholds — and removed (19 fields across both profiles) rather than force a citation onto engine-internal defaults.

**Also fixed**: two provenance records in `orf_hd` from the earlier SQC-1935 backfill pass that claimed `method:"literal"` for values (`16`, `235`) that don't actually appear in the source document — verified directly, downgraded to `model` to match the profile's own `rgb.min`/`rgb.max` fields (same underlying EBU R103 citation-by-name).

## Flagged for a human ruling (not silently resolved)
- `bbc_uhd_x1.constraints.video.pse_standard`: asserts `ITU-R BT.1702-3`; only `BT.1702-2` found in any cited doc.
- `dpp_uk_hd`: loudness tolerance (profile 0.5 vs DPP QC Guidelines ±1 LU) and `audio.sync.max_drift_ms` (profile 40 vs DPP QC Guidelines ±10ms).
- `r128_audio`: loudness tolerance (profile 0.5 vs current R128-2023's ±1.0/±0.2 LU — 0.5 matches only a 2014-vintage prior edition per the standard's own changelog).
- `orf_hd.governance.sourceSpec`: points at an ARD (not ORF) URL — may be intentional (ORF explicitly follows joint ARD/ZDF/ORF guidelines per its own notes) rather than a copy-paste bug, so left alone.

Each is called out in its commit message with the exact source quote so a human reviewer can rule quickly.

- [x] Schema syntax check (`Draft202012Validator.check_schema`) still passes
